items.name: Castigation
entries: You may spend your Action and one Warlock spell slot to empower your weapon to its limits, punishing those who defy the Will's action through you. You instantly perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, dealing 4d12 piercing damage on a hit and dealing additional piercing damage equal to the sum of Sinking count on the target with your current Poise count times two. The target's AC is reduced by 5 for this attack.

items.name: Decapitation
entries: You may spend your Action and one Warlock spell slot to momentarily sever another's soul from their body, shattering it with a force that governs the world around you. You perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, dealing 5d8 slashing damage on a hit and causing the target to suffer a further 4d6 force damage at the start of their next turn alongside having them deal only half of any damage they would deal in any attack, spell or otherwise until the end of their next turn.

items.name: Eradication
entries: You may spend your Action and one Warlock spell slot to channel the Will directly, creating a number of mechanical arms that swing down from the heavens to crush any creature of a choice within 120-ft. of you. Any target within reach must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC, suffering 6d10 bludgeoning damage and being knocked Prone on a failure or only suffering half that damage on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Rooster
entries: {@i "Is that it?! Where are the rest? Where?! I ain't stopping 'till- [inhales] ... Fine... Keep it down. I've got to keep this down... or I won't get to fight another day."}

Barbarians following the Path of the Rooster have been permanently changed by a powerful magic likening their appearance and instincts to those of the same animal. Usually members of the Heishou Packs, these Barbarians are commanded by the highest payers or strongest authorities, the ones holding the leash of their Packs, to wreak havoc and destruction upon their enemies. In the Forgotten Realms, these Barbarians are usually part of a gang of bandits hired for their lust for battle, unafraid to die in combat as long as they can take out one more enemy. You were born, or transformed, to fight until your last breath.

entries.name: Peck 'Em
entries: {@i "Ya-hah! Now are the rest? Where?! I ain't stopping 'till there's no more of 'em to peck... For to keep this down... or I won't get to fight another day!"}

Your body has been altered to sport powerful feathers made to boost your aggression despite damage to yourself. You gain resistance to fire damage, and once per short rest you can use a Reaction when you would take fall damage to negate that damage instead, as long as you didn't fall more than 100 feet.

entries.name: Bloody Storm of Blades
entries: {@i "Ah... and here I thought I'd manage to keep it cool all day today."}

You do not simply rage, your fury and lust for battle boil and spill over like an erupting volcano. While you are raging, once per turn when you hit an attack, you gain 1 count of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. Additionally, you gain 1 count of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} when you score a critical hit, when you attack a creature with half or less of its total hit points, or when a creature dies or falls unconscious within 15 feet of you.

While you have counts of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, your attacks also deal 1 count of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to the target and 2 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to yourself. While you have counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you won't stop raging even if you haven't attacked a hostile creature or taken damage, and you add +1 to your rage damage bonus for every 2 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} you have on yourself, to a maximum of +3.

subclassFeature.name: Flame Rooster's Death Defiance [炎鳥不死戦]
entries: {@i "Roosters crow only when the lord holding our leash commands us to."}

Roosters never die, they're simply out of breath, ready to recover and burst back into the fight like a living inferno. If your hit points drop to 0 or you become {@condition Unconscious}, you can use a reaction to immediately deplete all of your counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or half the counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a creature within 15 feet of you and lose the {@condition Unconscious} condition, recover 1 hit point and gain {@dice 1d10} temporary hit points for each count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} depleted this way. After this, you can immediately start Raging and move up to your movement speed towards a creature to perform an attack roll. If you score a critical hit or reduce the creature to 0 hit points with this attack, you gain an additional {@dice 1d10} temporary hit points.
You can use this feature once, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest. Upon reaching level 14, you can use it twice.

subclassFeature.name: Mutilating Talons
entries: {@i "Listen... I did this for you instead of indulgin' my fighting urges. Remember, that, yeah?"}

Your feathers have grown more fierce, are burning hotter, and you can't wait to dispense all of that fury on your enemies. While you have counts of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you now deal 2 counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to the target and 4 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to yourself. While you have 4 or more counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on yourself, your {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} applies thrice its amount as {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on enemies. If you have {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} or counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you get to do an extra attack once per turn. For each consecutive attack that you hit on the same creature this turn, you deal an additional {@dice 1d6} fire damage to them as long as you have counts of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodflame Massacre [血炎亂舞]
entries: {@i "Hah, what's that? You lot haven't had your fill just yet, either...? Fine! Come and get me!"}

The oil you use to ignite your sword is now coursing through your veins, and every single part of you is itching to start a conflagration. While you're raging, you can use a Reaction when you take Fire damage to immediately make an attack against a creature within reach. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.
Whenever you bring a creature to 0 hit points after an attack, you can immediately walk up to 15 feet and make another attack roll against a creature within reach.

entries.name: Rooster's Rampaging Blades Under the Ensanguined Heaven.
entries: Once per long rest, as an Action you can take when you have half of your hit points or less, you open your wings and coat your weapons and yourself in flammable oil, gaining 4 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. You can reach each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere around you without spending movement speed. You can make a number of attack rolls against them equal to half the count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on yourself. Your weapon damage dice for all of these attacks is {@dice 1d4} fire damage, but you can still apply your Rage bonus to them. If you reduce a creature to 0 hit points this way, your damage dice becomes {@dice 1d6} for the duration.

subclassFeature.name: Gamefowl Martial Archetype
entries: Most Fighters live for fighting, simple as it may be, but none embody the vital need for pure, unadulterated violence as the Gamefowl Martial Archetype, defined by being an opportunistic and usually battle-crazed bundle of blades who craves nothing more than a good fight.

By using a special technique to ignite their blades in oil and then spark that with their victim's blood, they turn the battlefield into a searing inferno as they rush around, seeking not the greatest fight possible like a grandious warrior wanting glory, but like a mad rooster needing to feed on the greatest amount of battles possible, being proficient at finalizing creatures and heading onto the next as soon as possible.

In realms such as Fâerun, they are found as a Mercenary Group with the same namesake as the Archetype, a bunch of warriors with barely any hierarchy, only waiting to be leased by whatever lord of the land they aimlessly wander into so they can incur the wrath of their flock onto some poor target.

entries.name: {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Sword
entries: Through a rare technique you've managed to procure an efficient way to enchant your blade to ignite when soaked in blood, turning it into oil to fuel your violence. While you have a free hand you gain one count of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} whenever you deal damage to a creature that has below half its Maximum Hit Points. You also gain one count of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} whenever a creature is knocked {@condition Unconscious} or is killed within 15-ft of you.

While you have {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you may easily coat your swings into a pure blaze, causing you to deal an additional {@dice 1d6} fire damage per count of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} and also inflict two times your {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on melee weapon attacks, You may have up to three counts of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} at any given time, losing one whenever you deal damage to a creature and at the end of combat.

entries.name: Battle Roosting
entries: In the high tide of battle you may wish to fan the flames so a fight is brought straight to you, disregarding your safety just for more violence. As a Bonus Action during your turn you may let out a battle-crazed screech, causing all creatures around 30-ft of you to have Advantage on attacks against you. Furthermore, when you do this you deal additional damage on melee weapon attacks equal to the target's {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks, for a maximum amount equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The type of this additional damage is the same as your weapon's.
These effects last until the start of your next turn and you may use this feature an amount of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus (Rounded Down) per Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Rooster's Flight
entries: Through magical mutations that have pinions grow upon your arms to aid with your movement or special training that have you feel as if you could fly, you have achieved a point where your movement is leagues above the usual person. You gain Proficiency in Athletics, or Expertise if you were already Proficient in this skill. Furthermore, as a Reaction to when you would take fall damage you may attempt to catch yourself on any footholds on walls nearby or to soften your fall as you can by attempting an Athletics Skill Check with a DC that equals 13 + 1 for each 10-ft you fell. On a Success, you take no damage from falling.

subclassFeature.name: Fuel My Rampage
entries: You have become a fearsome, opportunistic beast. Whenever you knock a hostile creature {@condition Unconscious} or kill them, you may spend your Reaction to move up to your base movement speed towards a creature within reach and perform a melee weapon attack against them if able. In addition you are healed by half a roll of your Second Wind ability when you land a Critical Hit against a hostile creature, knock them {@condition Unconscious} or kill them.

subclassFeature.name: Headless Fowl
entries: Death's door has now been a far thought in your head, barely considered even as you stand by it - Your desire for more always fueling your will to move foward to the next fight, no matter what. When you would be knocked {@condition Unconscious}, once per Long Rest, you instead suffer the {@condition Headless Fowl [无头鸡]|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} condition.

While in this state you have Disadvantage on any Saving Throws and Skill Checks, but may still move as your body acts upon its instincts looking for more fights. Whenever you inflict {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on another creature, you deal one more count of the condition and you deal an additional damage die on every melee weapon attack, with its damage type being the same as your weapon's. You must roll a Death Saving Throws at the end of your turn and automatically regain half your Maximum Hit Points if you pass three Death Saving Throws, however instead of taking damage when a creature would deal any to you, you instead fail one Death Saving Throw per creature, per turn. You may benefit from Fuel My Rampage while like this.

subclassFeature.name: Rooster's Battle Techniques
entries: You've developed and mastered techniques using your {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Sword that would make a normal person easily burn themselves from mishandling. These techniques can be used by spending two {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} during your turn, and you can only benefit from one at any given turn. They are as follows:

items: {@b Pecking Storm.} You spend a Bonus Action to perform half your total attacks you may perform during your turn (Rounded Down) as extra melee weapon attacks against a target within reach.

{@b Overwhelm.} You spend your Action to deliver a particularly powerful strike with your blade, sinking it into the target and burning them from the inside out. You perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, on a hit they suffer 6 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and suffer {@dice 1d6} burn damage per count they are currently suffering from, to a maximum of {@dice 12d6}. This attack ignores Resistance to fire damage and treats Immune creatures as if they were only Resistant instead.

{@b Rooster's Flight.} You spend your Action to perform up to your maximum amount of attacks' worth of melee weapon attacks against creatures within your reach, moving up to 15-ft in a direction of your choice every time you do so. When you move this way, creatures have Disadvantage on Opportunity Attacks against you.

subclassFeature.name: True Battle-Craze
entries: Upon going near your breaking point, you only feel more at ease for breaking other's. While at or below half your Hit Points, you gain the following effects:

items: You deal an additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on every attack.
You gain an additional {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} when you would gain it.
You deal two additional weapon damage die on attacks.
You are considered Proficient on Wisdom, Intelligence and Charisma Saving Throws against spell effects.

subclassFeature.name: Lifestew Domain
entries: {@i "Salutations!!!!!! I implore thee to try this soup!!!!"}

None are more warm-hearted and kind than the ones who follow the Lifestew Domain, focused on hailing the ancient {@creature Basillisoup|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Basillisoups}'s word of keeping anyone and everyone well fed through cold winters and harsh famines alike. A member of the Lifestew Domain usually starts out working to aid in their soup-kitchen bases, yet adventures call to them like a second nature, looking both for new ingredients they can bolster their order with or hungry mouthes to taste the delights of Dragonstew!

In some realms such as Faerun, the clerics of this domain ride along the sword coast in their mighty chariot-train pulled by the very divine beasts that they consider so beloved, aiding any settlement they come across and bringing a happiness unlike no other to the festivals of the world, being sought after to calm down and pacify even the most starve-crazed monsters and bandit groups, one of their main tenets being that all creatures deserve to be well-fed in the end.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

entries.caption: Lifestew Domain Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell animal friendship}, {@spell catapult|XGE}
3rd
{@spell Aganazzar's scorcher|XGE}, {@spell flaming sphere}
5th
{@spell elemental weapon}, {@spell Leomund's tiny hut}
7th
{@spell dominate beast}, {@spell polymorph}
9th
{@spell awaken}, {@spell conjure elemental}

entries.name: Dragonstew Kitchen
entries: Among the countless cookbooks you've memorized and holy precepts that were gotten to an art, you've also attained the skill to unite both in the divine objective of keeping a belly fed. As such, you know a ritual to summon a {@item Basillisoup Ladle|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} that you're proficient in during a long rest, which remains with you until its destroyed, lost or you summon another one, where the old one vanishes. You may use this Ladle as a holy symbol.

Furthermore, you've also mastered the art onto preparing enchanted food to give poor souls their deserved nourishment no matter what; Whenever you deal fire damage to a friendly creature who has the {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} condition, they instead ignore fire Resistance or Immunity and heal the target by half the damage dealt, as they have a chance to consume the food flying at them.

A creature may benefit from this only once per turn. When you apply {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} through a Ladle ( By attacking with it or using it to cast your Cleric Spells ), they are instead healed by half the hit points they would suffer as per the Condition's fire damage.

entries.name: Sanctified Cook
entries: In a kitchen you are a ruler, the kitchen utensils being your noble knights to serve as you will. You gain proficiency in Cook's Utensils and during a short rest you may prepare a feast for your allies, be it a good old Dragonstew or even varying with a Dracopie, either ways your delicious food grants them the {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} condition until the next short or long rest, alongside a number of {@dice d4} temporary hit-points equal equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down. These temporary hit-points last until {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} wears off.
Upon reaching 6th level your cooking improves, causing a {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature to gain Resistance against the Fire and at 12th level, Cold damage as well.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Summon Stew Cauldron
entries: With a chattering incantation you summon forth a huge soup cauldron that occupies a 5-ft an space thats within touch range of yourself, blessed to fulfil your duty of cooking. Once per combat, any friendly creature may spend their bonus action to drink from its glorious soup while within 5-ft of it, recovering an amount of {@dice d8} hit points equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, and gaining the {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} condition, if they didn't have it already. Whenever a hostile creature or one you deem unworthy attempts to drink from the cauldron, they take the same amount they would be healed for as fire damage.
While within 5-ft of the cauldron you may spend your bonus action to add a Magical Ingredient to the brew, as described on the list below:

items: {@b Grilled Ginger.} A specially spicy pepper that teems with flickering flames. A creature who ingests this peppery brew deals an additional stack of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} when they hit an attack, for up to 2 times per turn. This lasts as long as they are {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

{@b Life Lettuce.} Crunchy and makes you feel fresh as a newborn leaf. A creature who ingests this alleviating brew is instead healed by an amount of {@dice d8} hit points equal to the Lifestew Cleric's proficiency bonus.

{@b Guiding Guarana.} This ingredient is famous for how its refreshing, calming the mind to focus on what it needs to. While {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} a creature who ingests this brew may add a {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to their skill checks. After doing so, they can only add this bonus again after failing another skill check.

{@b Brutal Beef.} Hard to chew and extremely juicy, this ingredient packs a punch by itself. A creature who ingests this thick brew has advantage on Strength Saving Throws and ability checks. This lasts as long as they are {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

{@b Monster Mash.} This is undescribable but a great remedy to poison. A(n unlucky) creature who ingests this (???) brew instantly vomits. this clears their body of any poisons or non-magical diseases currently affecting them. If the ingesting creature was suffering from the poisoned condition, they may choose to instead hold the vomit in, performing an melee ranged attack they are proficient in choosing a target creature within 5-ft of them as a free action during the end of their turn. On a hit the target takes {@dice 3d4} poison damage and gains the poisoned condition instead.

entries: You may add a Magical Ingredient an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per long rest, rounded down. The cauldron has an amout of hit points equal to 10 * your level in Cleric and an AC of 13 + your proficiency bonus. When it would be reduced to 0 hit points, the iron cauldron crumbles to dust while the soup explodes violently, forcing any creature within a 15-ft radius to pass a Dexterity Saving Throw equal to your cleric Spell Saving Throw or suffer {@dice 4d8} fire damage and 4 stacks of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
This cauldron may be drawn from an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, becoming inert and empty after all uses are consumed.

subclassFeature.name: Spice of Life
entries: The noses of cooks long past have been reached by your delightful cooking and they have chosen to give you the blessing of special ingredients to create a True Dragonlife Stew, a magnificent meal meant for the servants of the Lifestew that has a chef transcend their mundane existance and become akin to the mighty {@creature Basillisoup|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. As an action you may take once per long rest, you produce a True Dragonlife Stew and consume it, gaining the {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Condition and the effects of the following ingredients while you have it:

items: {@b Jesty Jallapeños.} You gain a breath weapon as a great fire starts swirling in your gut! You may spend your action to spew fire in a 30-ft cone in any direction, having any creature within this range have to perform a Dexterity Saving Throw, suffering {@dice 5d8} fire damage and 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a failure or half the damage and half the stacks on a success. After using this feature you must roll a {@dice d6} at the start of your next turns only, regaining the ability to use it upon rolling a 5 or a 6. If you were poisoned and consumed a stew with Monster Mash, this Saving Throw becomes a Constitution Saving Throw and in addition to other effects any creature who fails also becomes poisoned for one minute, being able to re-attempt this Saving Throw at the end of their turns.

{@b Clawing Crawfish.} Great draconic claws morph from your fingers and a tail sprouts from your lower back! You gain natural weapons in the form of claws and a tail, the former dealing {@dice 2d4} slashing damage on a hit and having the finesse traits while the latter deals {@dice 1d12} bludgeoning damage and has the reach trait.

{@b Thick Tomatoes.} Your legs transform to be durable and powerful, springing with each step. You gain an additional 10-ft of walking speed and proficiency with the Athletics skill, or expertise if you were already proficient.

{@b Careful Carrots.} Your eyes gain a yellowish tone and slit pupils, becoming fully draconic. You gain advantage on Perception skill checks, can't be surprised and can see Invisible creatures as if they were colorless sillouettes over the world.

entries: Furthermore, you may throw one of these ingredients into your Stew Cauldron as a bonus action on your turn, granting any friendly creature who drinks this it's associated effect. This counts to the amount of times you may throw an ingredient in, and you may add a Spice of Life ingredient once per long rest. If you are knocked {@condition Unconscious} you lose the effects of your True Dragonlife Stew as your stomach becomes upset from not being to enjoy its grace fully.

subclassFeature.name: Meal of a Lifetime
entries: You've learnt how to become the best chef possible, a true believer and follower of the Lifestew. As such, you gain the following:

items: You may throw up to two ingredients from your Spice of Life feat into your Stew Cauldron per long rest instead of one.

When you consume your True Dragonlife Stew, you may dedicate a portion of it to the great {@creature Basillisoup|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Basillisoups}. Because of the greatness you've achieved with the pieces of food you make, a mighty {@creature Basillisoup|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} appears on the same square as you, having you ride it valiantly into battle. It takes it's turn alongside yours in Initiative, where you may have it move as a free action and spend your action or bonus action to command it to take one of its own. You may spend your reaction for it to take a reaction of its own when triggered.

subclassFeature.name: Soldato Tuttofare Roguish Archetype
entries: {@i "... I failed to complete my duties. This is but a punishment I deserve."}

Stern, rigid and hierarchical. That is the life of any Rogue who has become a Soldato Tuttofare - A foot soldier meant to do anything and everything asked by their superiors in whatever great organization they have found themselves in, be that carrying ammunition to dishing out horrible gashes in cost-effective close-quarters combat.

These are obedient people, for better or worse - Unrelenting in their rulekeeping to a fault, but they often tend to hold themselves to the same standards as they do others, being second to none in reliableness to those who have managed to stand at their side literally and figuratively.

In worlds such as that of Faerun, a Soldato Tuttofare Rogue might find themselves serving in the Zentharim as one of its many agents, or in others such as that of Keybreak they are one of the many, many people vying for a higher position in one of the Ringed Cities' megacorporations' military forces.

entries.subclassFeature: Under the Thumb of Greater People|Rogue|PHB|Soldato Tuttofare|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|3

subclassFeature.name: Under the Thumb of Greater People
entries: {@i "I listen carefully to every order I'm given. I... just look to the ground to not risk staring at my superiors straight in their eyes."}

There's a great organization you have joined, and you've been elected an acceptable enough cadet to be imparted with particular training toward attaining a certain role within the faction. Choose between the Ammunition Tributary and Warden of Respect features to gain one of them:

subclassFeature.name: Ammunition Tributary
entries: {@i "Let's get ready... Before our superiors with even higher authority have to intervene..."}

You've been taught - No, you've had the rules etched to your very brainstem lest it is removed. You are to distinguish between bullet types, know how to produce them when asked to and when to spend them yourself. You are proficient in Firearms and may, once per turn after triggering a {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue|PHB|1}, draw from your Reserves by rolling on the following table:

entries.caption: Ammunition Types
rows: Armor Piercing Rounds
Attack rolls made with this ammunition consider the target's AC as if it were one number lower.
Flame Rounds
Damage rolls made with this ammunition deal fire damage and inflict {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half of the user's proficiency bonus.
Frost Rounds
Damage rolls made with this ammunition deal cold damage and cause the target to suffer a stacking -1 modifier to their attack rolls until the start of the user's next turn.
Shock Rounds

Damage rolls made with this ammunition force the target to make a Strength check against a DC equal to 8 plus your Dexterity modifier plus your proficiency bonus, suffering {@damage 2d8} an additional thunder damage and being pushed back 10-ft. on a hit.

entries: After doing so, you immediately Reload your currently wielded firearm with the resulting ammunition type. It counts as an amount of bullets appropriate to your currently wielded weapon's Reload property.

These ammunition types have their effects take place whenever you hit a creature on an attack made with them, for an amount of attacks equal to the remaining bullets before you need to reload as per the Reload property.

Additionally, you have been imparted with the knowledge of how to make the most of any ammunitions gunpowder, causing your ranged weapon attacks to inflict an amount {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half the damage die they would deal, to a minimum of one.
Upon reaching 5th level you may toss that Ammunition toward another creature within 30-ft. of you, instantly Reloading their weapon with the rolled ammunition instead.

subclassFeature.name: Warden of Respect
entries: {@i "... Anyone in The Thumb has to know how to wield bayonets. Nothing like the sharp blade and the hard stock of a rifle in situations when we can't use ammunition."}

The way of the bayonet has been sliced into your memories, every movement and way to swing it - You know it. You also know how to best attach them to ranged weapons, requiring only a Dagger or similar light weapon to add onto a ranged weapon over a short or long rest.

When you attach a bayonet to a ranged weapon, you may also use it as a melee weapon you are proficient with. This weapon has gains the finesse property and retains the two-handed property if it had it, dealing a dice one step lower than the weapon's ranged damage dice (Such as a ranged weapon that deals {@damage 1d6} would deal {@damage 1d4}, an {@damage 1d8} would become an {@damage 1d6} and so on.) of a damage type of your choice between slashing or piercing damage.

You do not suffer Disadvantage on ranged attack rolls while a target is within 5-ft. of you when using a weapon with a bayonet and inflict {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the amount of damage die you would roll on a weapon attack hit.

Upon reaching 5th level your footwork has also improved to keep some distance between you and your target, increasing your AC by one until the start of your next turn whenever you hit a creature with melee weapon attacks. Your AC is increased by an additional point for the duration whenever you use your {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue|PHB|1}.

subclassFeature.name: Downcast Gaze
entries: {@i "I have to... try my best to uphold the perfect manners and etiquette."}

Those above you are the only ones allowed to look up to the sky, you've taken that to mean that you also must keep sure of the presence of all that dwell on the ground beside you, granting you Proficiency in the {@skill Perception} skill. Additionally, that exceptional precision has made it so that whenever you trigger a {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue|PHB|1} you can also trigger a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Thruster Compression Bullets
entries: {@i "Daring to breathe when you haven't even followed the underboss's command? Now that's quite discourteous."}

There is a special kind of ammunition that runs through your organization, Scorch Propellant Round, a kind of which you have just been trust to carry around and use at your own discretion - Of course, with the possibility of upper sight regarding it as unnecessary, so think well when spending these bullets. You have an amount of Scorch Propellant Round equal to your proficiency bonus, being able to resupply half of them at a short rest and all over a long rest. You may use them according to the 3rd level feature you have chosen, as per the following:

entries.name: Ammunition Tributary
entries: You have learned how to use these Scorch Propellant Round on your ranged fire, being able to instantly replace a regular bullet and spend one such Round before rolling a ranged weapon attack on your turn.

When you do so, the bullet's propellant systems supercharge the shot, causing it to easily pierce through any targets in a line equal to the short Range of your wielded weapon. You make one ranged weapon attack roll once, counting the result against all targets within reach and dealing damage to any whose AC you'd beat, also inflicting {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus. You may then choose to convert the targets current count into {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

Additionally, you may roll an additional ranged weapon attack and take the lower result to target any additional creatures that would be within a line equal to your long range. On a hit you deal half that {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count instead. If you would deal {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue|PHB|1} damage this way to multiple creatures, you only deal half that damage instead.

entries.name: Warden of Respect
entries: You have learned how to use these Scorch Propellant Round on to further the impact and speed of your melee swings, being able to instantly chamber and spend one such Round before rolling a melee weapon attack on your turn.

Whenever you do so, your weapon flares in flame as it swings through the air, dealing an additional amount of d8 fire damage and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half your proficiency bonus. You may also choose to convert the targets {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count into {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} as well.

Additionally, whenever you hit a creature with this attack you may immediately spend another Round to make an additional melee weapon attack against the same target benefitting from the same bonuses. You may do so until you perform a total amount of attacks equal to half your proficiency bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Class and Respect
entries: {@i "I'm a Soldato Secondo, you know...? It's about time I moved away from ammo cleaning duty to something more important, like ammo carrying duty for the esteemed Capos."}

You've managed to be recognized as a decent enough soldier to reach a higher rank within your organization, benefitting from all the little amenities that can come with - But also being granted the great deal of importance to deliver orders to others in a clean and concise manner.

You may spend your Bonus Action to give an Order to a friendly creature within 30-ft. that can hear and understand you, granting them an {@dice 1d6} bonus modifier to their next skill check. You may also do so as a Reaction whenever they are about to make a skill check. You may use this feature an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

This has also been ingrained through the very act of teaching, allowing you to spend a long rest teaching another creature that can understand you on tactics regarding a Skill you are Proficient in. They gain Proficiency in that skill until your next long rest. If you grant them Proficiency in the same skill six times in a row, they become permanently Proficient with that skill. (A creature may only gain proficiency in a only a single skill like this.)

subclassFeature.name: L'ascesa del Vice-capitano
entries: {@i "Hierarchy is absolute for the Thumb. To us, it's as natural as the fact of nature that spilt blood only flows downwards, not up."}

Hardly just some soldier anymore, you've managed to reach a position of some importance within your organization - A trusted steward to actual captains, a high-achiever between your ilk or even simply a dreadfully good shot. Upon reaching this level, you gain a Feature equivalent to the Feature chosen at 3rd level and may do the following during your turn:

entries.name: Custode della Regola.
entries: You are both beholder and beholdent of the Rules of your organization, and also the acting executor of every single line. Once per long rest you may spend your Action to rally your comrades, granting all creatures of your choice within 60-ft. that can understand you a +2 bonus modifier to hit and double that value to damage rolls until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Summary Judgement
entries: {@i "Obey the orders issued by your superior unconditionally, and do not question the intentions of your superior. Kill if you're told to kill, and die if you're told to die."}

The trust put upon you is something that would crush the stature of those which are lower than you, the implicit recognition of the Bosses that you are the one whose judgement will be performed upon the bodies of all that illicit quick punishment. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your experience and discipline has made any gun in your hands seem like it were a higher grade than it really is. You consider any ranged weapon you are wielding to deal magical damage for the purposes of bypassing Resistances and they are also considered to be at least a +2 Weapon, if it was any lower than that.
Whenever you take the Take Aim Bonus Action, your next ranged weapon attack gains a +2 bonus modifier to hit and is considered a Critical Hit on a dice result of 19-20.

Any time you would roll on the Ammunition Tributary table, before you roll you may choose to instead choose to draw the Round of your choice. You may do so an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Ferrous Discipline
entries: {@i "Not even the Thumb, one of the Five Fingers sitting at the apex of the Backstreets, can just waste bullets willy-nilly... Some just stick to raw strength, though"}

Most of your subordinates still rely solely on their allotted rounds to finish their work, but you've become more self reliant despite the fact that you're allowed an even greater amount of ammo. Your bayonet fighting rips through the battlefield better than most bullets, and you have come a long way into being a threat to your underlings - for its hard for them to keep their eyes away. You gain the following:

items: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.

Your nasty bladework has become an urban legend amongst your subordinates. You consider any melee weapon you are wielding to deal magical damage for the purposes of bypassing Resistances and they are also considered to be at least a +2 Weapon, if it was any lower than that.
Whenever you would make a melee weapon attack you may choose to instantly move up to 10-ft. in any direction of your choice without spending additional movement, provided you will reach a target.
You have an additional 4 Scorch Propellant Rounds.

In the case you are ever without a weapon, your fists have become quite the reliable tool, calloused enough to hit like pure iron and counting as natural melee weapons that you are proficient with. These have the Finesse and Light properties and deal {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage on a hit, and although they cannot benefit from your Round they deal an 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit.

subclassFeature.name: Beast of the Black Forest
entries: {@i In iustitia confidimus, ad nostram protectionem et poenam eorum qui nobis audent laedere.}

The Beast alone remains after darkness fell unto the Black Forest, a far-away place in any world that some regard as a demiplane where a child may become lost in when trying to travel through the woods at night, while others see it as the place seen deep within a bloody puddle left where no other person is.

Nevertheless, it seeks for a grim "protection" of all things living, offering to take a handful of the lost fools who wander into its woods under its sky-covering wings, turning them intoWarlocks of the Beast of the Black Forest, who become afflicted with the same agony over all the existing evil that surrounds the world.
A Warlock of such an Otherworldly Patron must take the following Oath in recognition of their service to a greater ordeal:

items: {@i "None shall lose their way under my witness."} Whenever a creature would cause another to become {@condition Charmed}, {@condition Frightened} or otherwise under the effects of an enchantment spell.
{@i "No evil deed shall go unpunished for as far as my wings reach."} Whenever a creature would cause another to become {@condition Unconscious}, be killed or suffer a Critical Hit.
{@i "No failure to uphold the greater good will be missed by my justice."} Whenever a creature fails a saving throw.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: {@i "Then, in the middle of all the chaotic cries, someone shouted:'It's the beast! A big, scary monster lives in the black, dusky forest!'"}
The Beast of the Black Forest lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell.The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

entries.caption: Black Forest Pact Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell detect evil and good|PHB|Detect Evil and Good}, {@spell dissonant whispers|PHB|Dissonant Whispers}
2nd
{@spell phantasmal force|PHB|Phantasmal Force}, {@spell Tasha's mind whip|TCE|Tasha's Mind Whip}
3rd
{@spell bestow curse|PHB|Bestow Curse}, {@spell blinding smite|PHB|Blinding Smite}
4th
{@spell dominate beast|PHB|Dominate Beast}, {@spell phantasmal killer|PHB|Phantasmal Killer}
5th
{@spell commune|PHB|Commune}, {@spell geas|PHB|Geas}

entries.name: Relicary of the Lost Guardians
entries: {@i "Why do they commit sins, knowing it's wrong?"}

You have been granted the blessings of the Beast, being able to call upon them at a time of need. \As an action during your turn you may summon the following three Relics of the Black Forest, symbols of the Beast of which you can, as part of this action, touch and become attuned to for the next minute.They are as follows:

entries.caption: Relics of the Black Forest
rows: Weight of Justice

A blunt greatsword wrapped in black feathers and bandages alike. It is a {@item Greatsword|PHB} of which you have proficiency using, yet it counts as if it were dealing slashing, bludgeoning and piercing damage instead of slashing por the purposes of eploiting Vulnerabilities and ignoring Immunities of its targets. While attuned to this weapon you gain an additional 10-ft. of movement and an extra attack as part of the {@action Attack} action. Upon reaching 10th level in Warlock this weapon also counts as if it dealt force damage.
Lamp-Lit Eyes

A billowing overcoat of black feathers covered in swirling yellow eyes. You gain a +1 bonus modifier to your AC and {@skill Perception} checks while attuned as described below, also being able to spend your reaction when you are hit with an attack or when you are targetted by a spell to force the creature who incurred this reaction to pass a Charisma saving throw or become Enchanted by you. An enchanted creature is {@condition Charmed} by you and must spend all their movement speed during your turn to move closer to you, no matter what harm might be in the way.
All-Devouring Stomach

You gain an internal organ that devours violence and ill-intent, but it is not a thing for an unbeastly body to bear, causing you to have a -2 negative modifier to hit and to damage rolls while attuned. However, you ignore these negative modifiers when targetting a creature that has dealt damage to you during their last turn until the end of your next turn, instead dealing an additional damage die of the same type as your attack's on a Critical Hit. Furthermore, you deal a Critical Hit against such targets on a dice roll of 19-20.

entries: Each relic grows in power in tandem with you, becoming greater when you reach certain levels in Warlock:

items: Weight of Justice becomes a +1 magical weapon when you reach 6th level, +2 when you reach 10th level and +3 when you reach 16th level.
Lamp-Lit Eyes grants a further +1 bonus when you reach 6th level, another at 10th level and a further one at 16th level.

All-Devouring Stomach deals an additional damage die and your Critical Hit dice roll becomes a 18-20 at 6th level, another damage die and a Critical dice roll of 17-20 at 12th and a last damage die at 16th level, alongside a Critical on a roll of 16-20.

entries: You can do this once per long rest, needing to spend a Warlock spell slot any other time you wish to do this.You may only become attuned to one of the Relics at any given time, and they vanish after becoming attuned to one or after one minute, if attuned.

entries.name: Sacrifice to a Beast
entries: {@i "If I kill the creatures first, then no one would be killed by the beast!"}

Much as your master has given part of itself to become what it is today, so have you to do its bidding, be that done in a manner of solidarity or as the steep cost of becoming a Warlock of the Beast.When you first choose this Otherwordly Patron you must choose from the following three sacrifices, also gaining boons from the Beast:

entries.caption: Sacrifices to the Beast
rows: Instinctus

{@b Sharpened Beak;} You gave away your innocence, having a permanent -2 modifier to your Charisma score. You, however, have had this dreary break shape you into something closer to beast than human as well, being able to manifest a Natural Weapon you are proficient in whenever you take the {@action Attack} action. This weapon can be a Talon or a Wing, both being wreathed in black feathers. Your Talons deal {@damage 2d4} slashing damage and have the finesse property while your Wings deal {@damage 1d10} bludgeoning damage and have the Reach property. Furthermore, as a reaction to when a creature would hit you with a melee attack you may perform a melee weapon attack against them using a Beak weapon. This Beak is also a natural weapon you are proficient in, except it uses your choice of Constitution or Charisma as an attack modifier and deals half your proficiency bonus' worth of {@damage 1d12|d12} piercing damage.
Inspectio

{@b Illuminate the Dark.} You gave away your eyes, becoming permanently {@condition Blinded}. You, however, gain a Dark Lantern that is bound to your soul, being indestructible and capable of illuminating a 60-ft. area centered on itself. It must be carried with one free hand yet also functions while set down, provided you are bathed by its light. All other creatures of your choice gain Darksight within the light's radius and you ignore the effects of the {@condition Blinded} Condition whenever being targeted by another creature's attack or when you are attacking another creature within the light. You also gain Blindsight of 30-ft. centered on the Lantern.
Repressio

{@b Broken Balance.} You gave away part of your inherent humanity and capability to see things as they are. A silvered scale has either been lodged as if wing addornments to your shoulders or you bear the tattoo of one covering the area from the back of your neck to your upper back. Whenever a creature you can see or hear breaks one of the tenets described in this subclass' flavour text, it suffers from an invisible weight bearing down their backs, gaining a negative {@dice 1d6|d6} modifier on their next roll. A creature does not need to know your tenets for this to trigger. You are also subject to this effect, except it lasts until the end of your turn if in combat.

entries: Your sacrifice cannot be undone unless you participate in the killing of the Beast of the Black Forest.

subclassFeature.name: Skewed Justice
entries: {@i "Its scale would never neglect the weight of even the smallest sin."}

You may spend your bonus action and a spell slot to channel the Beast's overwhelming desire for all's "Safety" through your body, instantly gaining double your proficiency bonus' worth of Mark of Sin. Mark of Sin is a counter that is transferred once to other creatures whenever a certain trigger is met, allowing you to have special effects against them, as follows:

entries.caption: Marks of Sin
rows: Whenever you are hit my a weapon attack.

The triggering creature suffers a Mark of Punishment. A creature with counts of this effect suffers an additional {@damage 1d10|d10} force damage whenever you hit them per Mark of Revenge they are suffering from, then removing all Mark of Punishment count.
Whenever you witness a creature within 60-ft. of you killing another

The triggering creature suffers a Mark of Justice. You gain a bonus modifier to attack and damage rolls against a creature suffering from Mark of Justice equal to its count, to a maximum of +3. This count is reset to zero when the creature dies or combat ends.
Whenever you witness a creature within 60-ft. of you cast a spell

The triggering creature suffers a Mark of Darkness. Creatures suffering from this effect cannot target you for spell attacks or force you to make a saving throw against their spells, losing one count whenever they cast a spell targeting at least one other creature.

subclassFeature.name: Toll of Guardianship
entries: {@i "I heard terrible things happen to any creature that enters the forest."}

The Beast has long whispered in your ears to remember that all sacrifices are made in search of the greater good, and even if a little blood is spilled it will never compare to the death of all you hold dear.As a reaction to whenever a creature you can see or hear within 60-ft. of you would suffer damage, you may move towards the nearest empty space within 5-ft. of them and perform a weapon attack or spell attack against the source of that damage. On a hit, you don't deal damage to the source, instead parrying their attack with the side-effect of your own overwhelming force hurting the one you were trying to protect, having them instantly suffer {@damage 2d8} damage of your attacks damage type.This damage increases to {@damage 3d8} when you reach 14th level in Warlock.

subclassFeature.name: Twilight Bringer
entries: {@i "Those who endure until the last moment shall reach an apocalypse for themselves..."}

The Beast has become pleased with your devotion, pleased enough to grant you its direct help. Once per long rest when you take an action to summon from your Relicary of Lost Guardians you may instead summon three Eggs of the Black Forest each appearing at the closest unocupied space at the end of three 60-ft. lines spaced as a triangle centered from you.These eggs grant you their relics for the next minute until they are broken by another creature.They are as follows:

items: {@b Punishing Egg.} This chair-sized egg is small and has 40 hit points, with an AC of 8.Whenever it is hit, the egg has a fleshy maw appear from its cracks and perform a melee weapon attack using your spell attack modifier against the creature who hit it, dealing {@damage 2d12+4} piercing damage on a hit.

{@b Just Egg.} This barrel-sized egg is medium and has 80 hit points, with an AC of 12.Whenever it is hit, the egg rings out a hollow noise that surrounds a 30-ft. radius around it, forcing all creatures withinn reach or suffer 120 force damage divided between each creature who failed this saving throw.

{@b Watchful Egg.} This bear-sized egg is large and has 120 hit points, with an AC of 4.Whenever it is hit, the creature who hit it must pass a Charisma saving throw against your Spell Save DC or become Enchanted until the end of their next turn, being forced to spend all their movement speed moving away from the egg.

entries: If you break the eggs yourself, their relics do not vanish early. If you break all three eggs you may then spend your action to call upon a portal to the Black Forest as an action, making its doorframe appear within an unnocupied space of your DM's choice within 120-ft. of you.When you are within 5-ft. of this doorframe you may spend your action to open the door and let the beast appear for but a moment.

When you briefly open the doorframe, the sheer force emanating from the Beast covers a 160-ft. radius centered around the doorframe, causing every single creature within this reach to try a {@dc 20} ( Or your Spell Save DC, if it is higher ) Wisdom Saving Throw or have their minds raked by nightmares and visions of the Beast's inception, having them become {@condition Blinded} and {@condition Deafened} for the next minute, also suffering {@damage 18d8} psychic damage, or half on a success. Children and other pure-hearted beings are immune to these effects, instead becoming {@condition Blinded} until the end of your turn as bandages cover their eyes, a manifestation from the flicker of the Beast's original goal still being present.You can only do this once per long rest.

Otherwise, you may spend your action to fully open the door, causing the Beast of the Black Forest to appear, wishing to cleanse the world of sin. It works to destroy the nearest living creature or settlement that isn't you for as long as you don't attack it. If you defeat the Beast, you permanently gain its three Relics and are attuned to all of them, also recovering the sacrifice you have done as part of your Sacrifice to the Beast feature.The Beast uses the {@creature tarrasque|MM|Tarrasque} stat block.

subclassFeature.name: Cheerful Spirits
entries: {@i "T'was but another jolly holiday night. That the Cheerful Spirits came out to bring fear and delight. Through gifts, plentiful and wondrous. Their dear patrons would find their lives quite disastrous."}

Warlocks of the Cheerful Spirits follow the harrowing whims of a multitude of different souls, being granted a single gift-bag with a myriad possibilities for chaotic delight. Of course, they are also provided with a handful of co-worker gnomes that will do their best to fulfil whatever is needed to bring out the cheer in people!

The lifes of these Warlocks is beset by an undecisive magic that always keep them on their toes, usually either forcing badness unto them directly or having them become closed off in a last ditch attempt to endure their supernatural holiday calling.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Cheerful Spirits lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

entries.caption: Cheerful Spirits Pact Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell chaos bolt|XGE|Chaos Bolt}, {@spell grease|PHB|Grease}
2nd
{@spell Nathair's mischief|FTD|Nathair's Mischief}, {@spell pyrotechnics|XGE|Pyrotechnics}
3rd
{@spell create food and water|PHB|Create Food and Water}, {@spell sleet storm|PHB|Sleet Storm}
4th
{@spell confusion|PHB|Confusion}, {@spell fabricate|PHB|Fabricate}
5th
{@spell animate objects|PHB|Animate Objects}, {@spell awaken|PHB|Awaken}

entries.name: Fine Gifts For All!
entries: You have made a pact with a number of discordant, dissonant and dishevelled spirits who only care for whimsy and merriment, being granted an artifact from them all. This artifact is a Cheerful Giftbag made from patchwork and conflicting feelings alike, usually taking the appearance of a large burlap sack covered in ribbons and chimes, or any other appearance of your choice. This Giftbag has the same properties as a {@item Bag of Holding}, except you can also pull Giftboxes out of it which contain mysterious presents for your use.

As an action during your turn you may draw a Giftbox from the bag and either open it as part of that same action, gift it to a creature within 5-ft. of you or toss it anywhere within 60-ft. of you. If you gift it to an unwilling creature, it must pass a Wisdom saving throw against your Warlock Spell DC or be compelled to accept the gift, dropping whatever it is holding if it doesn't have a free hand. After you decide to keep, give or throw a Giftbox like this, roll a {@dice 1d8|d8} to determine its effects when opened as per the following table:

entries.caption: Mystery Gift Box of Heck Effects
colLabels: Mystery Gift Box of Heck Effects
rows: Gnomic Helpers

A gaggle of four Gnomes jumps out of the Giftbox and each one rushes toward a creature of your choice within 30-ft. of the Giftbox. That creature gains an additional {@dice 1d4|d4} bonus modifier to their rolls until the end of your next turn, where they pop into confetti.
Gift Within a Gift

There is a box within the box, roll {@dice 1d4}. On a 1, there is a {@item Potion of Healing}. 2 has a {@item Potion of Growth}. 3 has a {@item Potion of Flying} and a roll of 4 has a {@item Potion of Mind Reading}.
Modern Classic

Its a round, dark and very volatile bomb. All creatures within 15-ft. of the GIftbox must pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer {@damage 1d6} + your proficiency bonus' worth of {@damage 1d8|d8} piercing damage. On a success, they only suffer half that damage. Structures and objects not being held or worn suffer double this damage.
Gnomic Raiders

A gaggle of four Gnomes with weapons emerge from the Giftbox, attacking the nearest creature within 60-ft.. You perform a number of spell attack rolls against that creature equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down. On a hit, they deal {@damage 2d4} + your Charisma modifier slashing damage. This damage cannot be non-lethal and on killing a creature, the Gnomes overtake the corpse until the end of the next Round. Upon that time passing, roll a {@dice 1d4|d4}. On a roll of 1, the body is made into a surprisingly cute trinket ( as per the Player's Handbook Trinket Table ) . On a roll of 2, it becomes a +1 weapon of the DM's choice. On a roll of 3, it becomes a +1 armor of the DM's choice. On a roll of 4, it becomes a +1 magic focus. Any magic items created like this rot away after one day.
Yuletide Howls

The box is actually a music box, playing a loud cacophony of holiday tunes that covers a 30-ft. area around itself. All creatures within reach must pass a Wisdom saving throw against your Spell Save DC or become frightened of it until the end of their next turn. Creatures {@condition Frightened} this way may re-attempt this Wisdom saving throw at the end of their next turns.
You

The gift grows a toothy candy-cane maw and attempts to eat the nearest creature within 10-ft. of it. That target must pass a Dexterity saving throw or become {@condition Grappled} and {@condition Restrained} inside the box until the end of your next turn. While suffering these Conditions, the target creature gains Resistance against all damage types.
Buddy-Ship
Its pure holiday cheery magic! You and up to your proficiency bonus' worth of creatures within 30-ft. of you gains a +1 bonus modifier to their Saving Throws for the next minute.
Santata's Big Surprisese!

A gigantic, muscular and dry arm bursts out to sucker punch the nearest target within 15-ft. That target must pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer an amount of {@damage 1d12|d12} bludgeoning damage equal to your proficiency bonus, or half on a success. Also on a failure the target is pushed up to 15-ft. in a direction of your choice.

entries: You may also forgo rolling by spending a Warlock spell slot, being able to choose the exact effect instead. You may pull a gift from the bag this way an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, restoring spent uses after a short or long rest.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: This ability and subclass as a whole is incredibly chaotic, and a way to mitigate it if the player and GM concur on doing so is by allowing the player to roll the {@dice 1d8|d8} for effect and then being able to decide if they wish to keep, give or throw their gift. Another option is treating the low-level character as someone who doesn't know much about the gifts yet and is getting familiar with them, being able to roll before deciding how to act after seeing each effect happen or reaching 4th level first.

entries.name: Infinite Gifts
entries: Happiness can come in many ways, and the Cheerful Spirits have blessed your very touch to contain and spread holiday cheer. You gain proficiency in land Vehicles and through the course of a long rest you may enchant one to gain a fly speed equal to its movement speed for the next 24 hours, as it is infused with sheer holiday cheer. Furthermore, you also gain proficiency in the Performance skill.

subclassFeature.name: Gnome's Help-ome!
entries: The Cheerful Spirits are always watching! And they are always happy to help you and your fellows. Whenever you would become {@condition Unconscious} or afflicted with a condition that would cause you to be have your movement speed reduced to 0-ft., a gaggle of gnomes emerges from the Giftbag and rushes to aid you move, having you always maintain at least half your walking speed. If you would be {@condition Grappled}, they do not help you move, instead coming out to attack the creature Grappling you repeatedly. At the end of your turns, you may perform one melee spell attack against that creature, dealing {@damage 2d4} + your Charisma modifier damage on a hit and granting you advantage on your next skill check against being {@condition Grappled}.

subclassFeature.name: Neverending Holiday Madness
entries: The mischief and love placed into selecting the gifts of your Giftbag has been multiplied manifold by your devotion. When you roll in the Fine Gifts For All! table, you may choose to roll another {@dice 1d8|d8} in accord to the result, causing an effect from the corresponding table to trigger. ( Ex: Rolling a 1 on the first {@dice 1d8|d8} would cause you to roll another {@dice 1d8|d8} on the Gnomic Helpers table. )
All these tables may be found at the end of this document.

entries.caption: Gnomic Helpers Effects
rows: A gnome waddles out wearing an aerodynamic armor set beset with spikes. It walks up to one creature of your choice within 30-ft., of whom may spend their reaction to kick the gnome towards another creature within 60-ft, dealing {@damage 2d4} + your proficiency bonus' worth of piercing damage on a hit.

Four stylish gnomes waddle out of the bag toward you and up to 3 other creatures of your choice, addorning you in resistant clothes that grant temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus times 3.

A gaggle of bearded gnomes jump out and use their holiday magic to bolden a creature of your choice within 30-ft. of you. The next spell that creature casts until the end of your next turn is done so at one higher level, such as a 1st-level spell being cast at 2nd while still spending a 1st-level spell slot.

A gaggle of gnomes come out with stretchers to move one willing creature of your choice within 60-ft. toward another unnocupied space within the same range of you. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

A gaggle of gnomes rushes toward a creature of your choice within 60-ft., acting menacing to extort them for whatever they have. The target must pass an {@skill Insight} check against your Spell Save DC of be forced to give the gnomes whatever it is holding in their hands. The gnomes then may move it to any other stop within 60-ft. or give the items to you.

A gaggle of gnomes comes out carrying cookies and milk, eating them and returning to your Giftbag at the end of your next turn. Any creature within 5-ft. of them may attempt a Grapple check against the gnomes ( they use your modifier ) to steal their snacks, eating them as part of the same action and having {@dice 3d4+3} of their hit points restored. A creature may also attempt an {@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation} against the gnomes for the same effect. ( Against your Spell Save DC. )

A sick gnome waddles out toward the nearest creature within 15-ft. of the giftbox and vomits rainbows on them before being knocked {@condition Unconscious} for the next {@dice 2d8} hours. The target must pass a Constitution saving throw against your Spell Save DC or become {@condition Poisoned} for the next minute. When the gnome wakes up, it walks back to you and enters your giftsack no matter how far you are, as long as you are within the same plane of reality. Otherwise, it becomes sad and sits in place until able to return home.

A thermonuclear gnome waddles out toward the nearest creature within 15-ft of the giftbox. It explodes. Any creature within 15-ft. of the gnome must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC or suffer an amount of {@damage 1d8|d8} poison damage equal to double your proficiency bonus.

entries.caption: Gift Within a Gift Effects
rows: {@item Wings of Flying} are within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
A bottle of {@item Sovereign Glue} is within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
{@item Pipes of Haunting} are within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
A {@item Periapt of Health} is within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
A Pipe of Bubbles is within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
A {@item Necklace of Fireballs} is within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
A pair of {@item Gloves of Missile Snaring} is within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.
A {@item Robe of Stars} is within the giftbox. The first creature to pick them up may instantly become attuned to them.

entries: All these items still become snow after one minute.

entries.caption: Modern Classic Effects
rows: The bomb deals fire damage instead of piercing and all spaces within its radius are lit on fire until the end of the next round. Any creature who starts or ends their turn inside this fire suffers {@damage 2d4} fire damage.

The bomb deals cold damage instead of piercing and all spaces within its radius are frozen over until the end of the next round. Any creature who moves into or within a frozen space must pass an {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics} check or fall {@condition Prone}. The DC for this check is 14.

The bomb deals acid damage instead of piercing and all spaces within its radius are soaked in an acidic puddle until the end of the next round. Any creature who starts or ends their turn inside this fire suffers {@damage 2d4} acid damage.

The bomb deals necrotic damage instead of piercing and all spaces within its radius are coated in graveyard grime until the end of the next round. Any creature who moves into or within this area must pass a Dexterity saving throw or have their feet grabbed by a spectral hand, which causes them to lose 15-ft. of movement until the end of their turn. The DC for this saving throw is 14.

The bomb deals poison damage instead of piercing and all spaces within its radius are lit on fire until the end of the next round. Any creature who starts or ends their turn inside this fire suffers from the {@condition Poisoned} condition until they end their turn outside of this area.

All spaces within the bombs explosion radius are covered by caltrops until the end of the next round. Any creature who moves within that area suffers 2 piercing damage per 5-ft. of movement spend within the area.
The bomb deals thunder damage instead of piercing and its radius is extended by 10-ft..
The bomb deals radiant damage and all creatures who fail its saving throw must pass a Constitution saving throw ( {@dc 14} ) or be {@condition Blinded} until the end of your next turn.

entries.caption: Yuletide Howls Effects
rows: Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, it is assailed by visions of dreadful direwolves which cause them an inability to focus. While {@condition Frightened} this way they cannot take the Aid action and have a negative modifier to any rolls made as a Reaction. This modifier is equal to your proficiency bonus.

Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, they feel as if a biting cold wind swept through them, having them shiver and treat all terrain as difficult terrain for as long as they are {@condition Frightened}.

Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, they feel their extremities freezing to the point of frostbite, instantly suffering 4 times your proficiency bonus' worth of psychic damage.

Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, an illusory gnome jumps off of the box with a spooky mask, forcing them to spend all their movement speed moving away from the box at the start of their next turn.

Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, they start having illusions of being a giant turkey drumstick. While {@condition Frightened} in this way, whenever they recover hit points they must pass a Wisdom saving throw or perform a melee weapon attack against themselves as a reaction, as they desperately feel the need to take a bite of a nice-looking meal.

Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, they see an illusory gnome jumping over their face and scurrying over their body, having them become {@condition Prone} at the start of their next turn.

Whenever a creature would become {@condition Frightened} by this giftbox's effects, a deep paranoia settles into the creature's mind, as if they forgot to buy presents at the last second. They automatically fail any {@skill Perception} or Investigation checks while {@condition Frightened}.

Instead of playing a cacophony of songs, the music box instead only plays one jolly tune of your choice. All friendly creatures within 60-ft. that can hear gain advantage on their next Wisodm saving throw for the next minute.

entries.caption: Gnomic Raiders Effects
rows: The raiders have extra-sharp weapon, dealing {@damage 1d6|d6s} instead of {@damage 1d4|d4s}.

The raiders have laced their weapons with something foul, dealing acid damage instead of slashing and causing the target to suffer a -1 negative modifier to their Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws per each hit suffered. This modifier recedes by 1 at the end of each of their next turns.

The raiders come out but instantly enter their holiday-mandated break time, remaining on the space of the giftbox for the next minute. They are not agressive but instantly become incensed if any creature moves within 5-ft of them or performs an attack within the same range. Upon becoming incensed, the gnomes perform three melee weapon attacks as per the original Gnomic Raiders effect against the triggering creature, except they deal {@damage 3d8} slashing damage per hit attack. After attacking or if the time passes, they leave back into your Giftsack.

Before attacking the raiders attempt to jump their target, forcing them to attempt a Strength saving throw against your Spell Save DC. On a failure, they are knocked {@condition Prone}. On a success, the gnomes are shaken off and have disadvantage on their attack rolls against the target.

The more civilized gnomes hop out this time, carrying crossbows to attack instead of their usual junk. You may choose for them to target any creature of your choice within 60-ft. of the Giftbox. They deal piercing damage instead of slashing.

This gaggle of gnomes decided to not be hurtful today, instead waddling in search of being annoying as can be. Their target must pass a number of Wisdom saving throws against your Spell Save DC equal to the amount of attacks they would originally perform. For each failure the target suffers a -1 negative modifier to their attack rolls, with this negative modifier diminishing by one at the end of each of the target's subsequent turns.

The gnomes come all carrying one big weapon together, performing a single attack as per the original effect's rules against their target. On a hit, the target creature takes {@damage 8d8} plus your Charisma modifier's worth of bludgeoning damage and is knocked {@condition Prone}.
The gnomes are incredibly focused today. If they kill a creature as part of the Gnomic Raider's original effect, they make it so the item produced never melts.

entries.caption: You Effects
rows: The box's fangs are horridly jagged, also dealing {@damage 4d8} piercing damage on a failed saving throw or half that damage on a success.

The box instead hopes only to protect until the next winter, making it so the creature inside becomes immune to all damage types except force. Furthemore, they remain {@condition Grappled} for up to the next minute and may spend a free action to break free.

This gift drank bad milk during the holidays and suffers horrible indigestion, spitting the creature out towards any other of your choice within 60-ft. You roll a ranged spell attack against the target and on a hit, the target and the originally {@condition Grappled} creature suffer {@damage 2d10} bludgeoning damage if the {@condition Grappled} was of small size, {@damage 4d10} if they were normal sized and {@damage 6d10} if they were large. Furthermore, the {@condition Grappled} creature also becomes {@condition Prone}.

This gift is filled with a horrible toxic liquid. A creature {@condition Grappled} by the box suffers {@damage 3d4} acid damage when initially {@condition Grappled} and at the end of their next turn. It does not benefit from the box's Resistance to damage for this acid damage.

The box doesn't want to be the gift at all, running 30-ft. away with the {@condition Grappled} creature towards a random direction. To determine that direction, roll a {@dice 1d8|d8} where 1 is North, 2 is Northeast, 3 is East and so on.

The box is disgusted by whatever it eats, quickly spitting it out after Grappling the creature with a bundle of vomit and spit. The creature has their movement speed halved for the next minute or until they can submerge themselves in a liquid to wash off.

The box is confused as to the logistics of interplanar travel, being teleported upwards by {@dice 1d8} times 20-ft. and then vanishing, leaving the {@condition Grappled} creature to fall. If this would cause the box to be teleported into a solid surface, it instead teleports to the nearest unnocupied space below the surface.

The box is a portal to a demiplane which houses the Cheerful Spirits whom love scaring people, causing them to also be {@condition Frightened} of you for the next minute, being able to attempt a Wisdom saving throw against the same DC at the end of their subsequent turns.

entries.caption: Buddy-Ship Effects
rows: This magic is dictated by a freaky battle-loving Spirit, also granting this bonus to attack rolls.
This magic is dictated by a nurturing family Spirit, also granting this bonus to it's targets Armor Class.
This magic is dictated by a feisty and hurried Spirit, also granting an additional 10-ft. of walking speed to it's targets.
This magic is dictated by a particularly battle-liking Spirit, also granting this bonus to attack rolls!

This magic is dictated by an old, ancient and long-lived Spirit, making it so the bonus gained by the original effect lasts for the next minute. If any other effects are gained by another Spirit, they also last for the same duration.
This magic is dictated by an experienced and tale-weaving Spirit, granting a +2 bonus modifier instead of +1.

This magic is dictated by you and your friends true friendship. Each creature blessed by this gains a {@dice 1d4|d4} bonus modifier they may grant to another creature as a reaction to when they perform any roll. This {@dice 1d4|d4} lasts for up to the next minute, whereafter the feeling just settles down in their hearts.

This magic is dictated by pure disgust and hatred towards whatever you are facing, making it so it's target creatures deal an additional {@damage 1d4|d4} damage when attacking. The damage's type is equal to the attack's original damage type.

entries.caption: Santata's Big Surprisese! Effects
rows: INSTEAD: A giant leg kicks at the nearest target! On a failed save the target is flung back an additional 15-ft. and if they come in contact with another creature or wall, they suffer an additional {@damage 3d8} bludgeoning damage.
INSTEAD: A giant hand smacks down at the nearest target! On a failed save, the target isn't flung back, instead being knocked {@condition Prone}.

INSTEAD: An ovesized ( and beardy ) face appears and screams at the target! This effect deals thunder damage instead of bludgeoning. On a failed save the target also becomes {@condition Deafened} for the next minute.
INSTEAD: A giant sack is flung at the nearest target! On a failed save the target takes an additional {@damage 2d12} bludgeoning damage.

INSTEAD: A giant pair of fingers jab at the nearest target! On a failed save they suffer piercing damage instead of bludgeoning and become {@condition Blinded} for the next minute if they rely on their eyesight alone.
INSTEAD: A pair of giant hands clap at the nearest target's head! On a failed save the target also becomes {@condition Deafened} for the next minute.

INSTEAD: A torrent of gifts pour out of the giftbag. Instead of Santata's Big Surprisese!'s original effect, you roll a number of ranged attack rolls equal to your proficiency bonus against targets you can see within 60-ft. of you. On a hit, roll on the Fine Gifts For All! table and that gift opens targetting the hit creature. On a miss, nothing happens.

INSTEAD: An oversized ( and particularly hairy ) face bites at the nearest target! On a failed save the target is also {@condition Poisoned} for the next minute, being able to attempt a Constitution saving throw at the end of their subsequent turns against the same DC. While {@condition Poisoned}, the creature feels as if they were drunk ( if able ), like a great deal of alcohol was transfered into their bloodstream.

subclassFeature.name: Purvey The Marvelous Christmas Tree!
entries: Your devotion to the spirits of holidays long past and to come have bore fruit in the greatest gift of all, granting you your choice of the following benefits which must be chosen when reaching 14th level in Warlock:

items: When you take the {@action Help|Aid Action} you may spend one of your Warlock Spell Slots to grant the target your choice of a temporary Spell Slot ( Up to 5th Level ) or grant them an Additional Attack as part of the {@action Attack} action or Reaction. These last until the start of your next turn.

Items created by the Gnomic Raiders Giftbox also have special chemicals applied to them. They never rot. You may also have the Gnomes make Uncommon items of your choice, as long as you have been Attuned to the item before. These items can only be gifted to other creatures willingly and without a transaction, they can't be sold or traded for other items or they will instantly become a pile of snow, as the Spirits frown upon such greedy endeavours over the holiday spirit.

The Cheerful Spirits grant you an allowance of gold, to which you can instantly spend to take out a non-magical item out of your Giftbox. It is of pristine condition and always wrapped in colorful ribbons. This item fades into snow after a week and the allowance you are granted is of 100 GP on a short rest and 500 GP on a long rest.
