Any surplus value left over is instantly spent on eggnog during a short or long rest, which grants you and all friendly creatures who spent the long rest with you advantage on their first Charisma check until the next long rest.

entries: Furthermore, you can ask them for help in a pinch. Once per long rest you may spend your Action to pour out gifts from your Giftbag, rolling your proficiency bonus' worth of {@dice 1d8|d8} on the Fine Gifts For All! table. You may do so targetting yourself or a willing creature within 5-ft. When you do so, the target may choose to activate any of the Giftboxes effects as part of your Action to pour them out or on a subsequent turn by spending their bonus action. These gifts automatically activate if combat ends.

subclassFeature.name: Silent Sniper Ranger Archetype
entries: You have trained since a young age how people think, where they expect an attack from, and how to hide from the most perceptive of targets. The weather is your constant ally to conceal your advances, and your performance as an archer excels beneath the rain and the snow. You are from a group of assassins that always completes their contracts, lest your own life be taken prematurely from you.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: You learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Silent Sniper Spells table. Each spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.

entries.caption: Silent Sniper Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell create or destroy water|PHB|Create or Destroy Water}
5th
{@spell alter self|PHB|Alter Self}
9th
{@spell call lightning|PHB|Call Lightning}
13th
{@spell ice storm|PHB|Ice Storm}
17th
{@spell scrying|PHB|Scrying}

entries.name: Snipe - Archery
entries: {@i "Rain pelts awake hearts."}

You know how to operate in any kind of weather, and even pebbles on the street can be efficient weapons to someone with your experience. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Stealth} skill, and if you already have proficiency in it, you gain expertise instead. Additionally, you gain proficiency with improvised weapons.

As a bonus action until the start of your next turn, you can double the range of all ranged weapons you are holding. Additionally, all weapons you are holding gain the thrown property if they don't already have it, with a range of 30/90 feet. When you hit an attack with a weapon while in this state, it deals an additional {@damage 1d8} piercing damage and 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to creatures that can't see you.
If it's raining or snowing, you gain advantage on {@skill Stealth} checks while outside or while experiencing the weather.

entries.name: Glimmering Bow [弓閃]
entries: {@i "Alleyways puddle with steps."}

Learning to focus on your target and aim for hours on end is the first thing any competent sniper learns - your bow must be treated not as a tool, but as an extension of your own body. You have 4 Snipe arrows. If one of them is lost or destroyed, you can reconstruct them during a long rest. You can choose to use one of your Snipe arrows instead of the usual ammunition when shooting with a bow. If you use a Snipe arrows instead of another arrow, you gain the following effects:

items: If you would have disadvantage on the attack roll due to distance, you instead do not have disadvantage as long as you haven't moved for 1 minute or longer.
For each 100 feet of distance from the target that you are, you add {@damage 1d10} piercing damage to the arrow, to a maximum of {@damage 4d10}.

Instead of immediately attacking, you may focus on your target, aiming your arrow at them but not moving from your position. You gain 2 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} per turn you spend aiming without moving, to a maximum of 8.
If it's raining or snowing, the arrow becomes untraceable back to where you shot it.

subclassFeature.name: Retaliating Maneuver
entries: {@i "The rest is silence."}

Even after being detected, you have learned to quickly take advantage of the situation and return to the shadows. When a creature successfully detects you while you are hidden, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against that creature if it is within your weapon's range. After the attack, you can move up to 15 feet without provoking opportunity attacks, and you may immediately attempt a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check to hide again if you have cover or concealment.
If it's raining or snowing, you apply the Snipe - Archery damage and {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} bonus to that reaction attack even if the creature can see you.

subclassFeature.name: Straight-Line Wind
entries: {@i "Nock the arrow, pull, loose-it punches through the target, felling it."}

You have honed your arrows to pierce and not be easily removed, becoming a powerful dent in any enemy's armor. When you successfully hit an enemy using a Snipe Arrow as ammunition, it suffers 1 count of the {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} condition. Additionally, whenever you use a Snipe Arrow, you immediately gain 2 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} before the attack and you deal {@damage 2d8} additional piercing damage if the creature can't see you instead of the {@damage 1d8} additional damage from Snipe - Archery if the attack hits.

If it's raining or snowing, when you hit a creature that has one or more {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} stacks, your attack scores a critical hit on a lower {@dice d20} roll equal to the number of {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Lodged Arrows} the creature has (For example, a creature with 3 {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is critically hit on a roll of 17 - 20). When you score a critical hit this way, all {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Lodged Arrows} are destroyed.

subclassFeature.name: Pierce Heaven
entries: {@i "The pelting raindrops shroud the falling arrows, and they will die in the downpour without knowing what killed them."}

Mastering control over the elements is what classifies you as a sniper that stands out among the rest, showcasing your incredible skill and unparalleled ability. While you are focusing your aim with the Snipe arrows, you can see up to 1 mile away with no difficulty, able to discern even fine details as though looking at something no more than 100 feet away from you. Additionally, even if you are {@condition Incapacitated}, {@condition Paralyzed}, {@condition Petrified}, {@condition Stunned} or {@condition Unconscious}, you can still make an attack roll as long as you were focusing an attack with your Glimmering Bow [弓閃] feature.

Once per long rest, you can cast the {@spell control weather|PHB|Control Weather} spell without spending a spell slot or material components by shooting a magical arrow into the skies. However, if you cast it this way the casting time is an action, it is a concentration spell that lasts for 1 minute and the change to the weather is instantaneous.
If it's raining or snowing, you may use a bonus action to gain the {@condition Invisible} condition until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Abraxas Chariot Martial Archetype
entries: {@i "Every now and then, I find myself thinking back... to the days I spent aboard that bus. Those memories... might be the only things that keep me going in the days to come.."}

There are many children who walk upon the world, no matter which. Yet there is a differential present within those that one day will grow to embody the Archetype of the Abraxas Chariot, those that rush through the fine line between the world of light and the world of darkness - Having come to accept the necessity of others and the orders that uphold the world while not denying or shying away from the fear that lingers through every shadow one may see, welcoming the wholeness of oneself.

Despite that, they are often born in wartorn lands, where conflict has forced them to suffer through vile events that have scarred not only their bodies but their minds, often forcing them to pick up a weapon at first for defense against having their innocence broken, yet soon after raising it toward protecting and nourishing their own world between.

At their best, they are brilliant leaders who descend like angels wherever their feet touches the ground, while at their worst they may be cruel as a devil and even be considered flippant about the most horrible things. In either way, their good and bad goes hand in hand, as is the true mark of those who look upon Abraxas for guidance.

entries.name: Historian's Note: Making an Abraxas Chariot...
entries: Many of these subclasses themes involve war and a violent conflict, yet you need not concern yourself to being forced upon that niche to create a character who still fits its mold - Consider instead other types of conflict that may have shaped your character, such as that of having the paradigms of their life crack open and leave them in search of a new balance to order their own being around, or a conflict of ideals that can be either a form of inner turmoil or with an outsider. The possibilities are vast as to where to take the flavour of this subclass, and we do hope you enjoy that process as much as we did creating it!

entries.name: Abate the Smoke
entries: {@i "I, too, once sought the answer from knowledge."}

So much has come and gone, yet you still remember your roots - spread deep through Wartorn land and fed by the blood left in your wake. Your place in the world is self-driven, blowing past the obstacles in front of you with a force that only one raised in conflict could boast. When you reach this level, you gain the following:

items: You have felt the weight of your blade in your hands many times, memorized it truly was no more than an extension. Whenever hit with a creature with a weapon attack you also inflict {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half your proficiency bonus. Whenever you deal a Critical Hit or a Posture Critical Hit, you inflict the same {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count an additional time.

Whenever you kill a creature, you gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus. Additionally, you gain 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever you first hit a creature during your turn.

Your attacks are dispelling forces in their own might, cutting through 30-ft. lines of gale whenever you perform an attack roll. This manifests either as a general wind or a specific cut, that being slicing through and rendering clear any smoke within 15-ft. long cone in a direction of your choice whenever you perform an attack roll.

entries.name: Rough-hewn Path
entries: {@i "It invaded the mind and clouded the judgement of the victim."}

Your upbringing wasn't the best, but it made you become something near that regarding your skills to keep living another day. You gain Proficiency in the {@skill Survival} skill, or Expertise if you were already Proficient in it.

subclassFeature.name: Guerrilla Tactics
entries: {@i "Though now, I've come to realize that knowledge holds no real answers."}
You have come to wield the stress of duelling against something much greater than you with prowess, developing a handful of techniques to ensure your success no matter where your halberd falls upon:

items: {@b True Decapitation Deathblow.} While having at least 6 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, you may use your Action to perform a melee weapon attack roll against a target within reach, dealing an additional damage die and inflicting one additional {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count for each extra attack you would be able to perform during your turn. You deal a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20, before any modifiers. This does not trigger effects such as that of a {@item vorpal sword|DMG|Vorpal Sword}. If you kill a hostile non-summoned creature this way you gain double the {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count you would gain as per your Abate the Smoke feature.

{@b Excision of Sacrifice.} As a Reaction to when you would successfully pass any Saving Throw or similar effect that would cause you to suffer half damage, you may deliver a staggering counter-blow that cuts through any onslaught. You and a number of other creatures of your choice suffering this Saving Throw suffer no damage, or half the damage that would be dealt if they failed this Saving Throw themselves. This number starts at 0 and you may spend 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count to increase it by one, to a maximum number of chosen creatures equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

{@b Lend My Inner Ear to Myself.} As a Bonus Action, you may consume 4 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count to quell your inner turmoil, calling upon everything you went through to live another day - After all, what is a better comrade than you? You instantly end any negative Conditions afflicting you. If you could not use a Bonus Action during your turn because of an external effect, you can still use this specific Bonus Action.

entries: You may use these skills an amount of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus per short or long rest. Alternatively, upon reaching 9th level you may spend an use of your {@classFeature Indomitable|Fighter|PHB|9} feature to utilize one of these techniques without counting toward your limit per short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Withstand the Snow
entries: {@i "Survival was reserved only for those who learned to accept the Smoke as part of their daily lives."}

For those who hail from the same homeland as you living long is a rarity, yet something that you somehow have managed to do, and in doing that your mental resistance has been sharpened to something unlike what most others possess. You gain Proficiency in Wisdom saving throws, Resistance to Psychic and Poison damage and any Disease or Poison you are suffering from ends after one minute.
Additionally, whenever you use your {@classFeature Indomitable|Fighter|PHB|9} Feature, you instantly recover half the damage taken during the previous turn, rounded up.

subclassFeature.name: Between God and the Devil
entries: {@i "Some called him the Green Damnation, while others called him the Green Deliverance."}

You have become something which threads the centerpath between extremes - a liminal space between what once was and what will be - of good and evil - of so much yet so little. Your prowess is shown right upon arrival - An Ordeal that floods any area of battle in a single feeling, chosen whenever you roll first Initiative during combat:

items: {@b Dawn of Damnation.} Whenever you inflict {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a critical you inflict 2 additional count as well and whenever you achieve a Posture Critical, you gain one {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count. On a Critical Hit, this attack considers a targets damage Immunity as if they were only Resistant to the damage dealt, and Resistance as if they weren't Resistant as well.

{@b Dawn of Deliverance.} You gain 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} at the start of your turns and whenever you get a sum of 8 count, you gain one {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count. On a Critical Hit, all friendly creatures within 30-ft. of you gain 4 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. The same happens whenever you Stabilize a friendly creature or protect another creature with any effect such as the {@spell sanctuary|PHB|Sanctuary} spell or with using the Protector Fighting Style.

entries: As you perform better and better in combat, your prowess coalesces into a plume of your own shade - {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} that swirls, and surrounds your body, matching that of your inner world.

While you have {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} during the Dawn of Damnation, you deal an additional 2 damage on weapon hits per count instead of suffering it. While you have {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} during the Dawn of Deliverance, you suffer 2 less damage whenever you would suffer damage instead of suffering it, to a maximum reduction equal to half the total value of damage being taken.
You only lose {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count at the end of combat, but may only hold a maximum of 5 at any given time.

subclassFeature.name: Unrestrained Ripples of the Future to Come
entries: {@i "Let me show you the singular teaching that has shaped my life."}

The road to reach inner peace was or even still is hard and tenuous, however your efforts have come to bear fruit - your techniques flourishing into a knowledge of the world that only few can truly claim to have. As such, you may, once per long rest, coat your weapon in a manifestation of your very soul. You do so by spending your Bonus Action while you have at least 3 {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count. While encased this way, your weapon attack hits deal an additional {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and the effect lasts for up to a minute.

While benefitting from this, you may replace your True Decapitation Deathblow technique with a use of your Branches of Knowledge. When you do so, you perform a melee attack weapon against one target creature within reach, inflicting 12 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and an amount of {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count equal to your current count. All other hostile creatures within a 30-ft. radius of you must also pass a Wisdom saving throw or suffer the same amount of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count, or half on a success. You may choose to trigger {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the main target instantly after performing this attack. Other effects of Deathblow apply to this attack.
Additionally, after attempting to hit a creature with your Branch of Knowledge, flip a coin:

items: {@b On a result of Heads,} you delve into the world of fears and insecurities, of secrets and all things that make you stronger toward peril. You suffer Vulnerability against psychic damage and deal an additional point of damage per {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count until the end of combat.

{@b On a result of Tails,} you delve into the world of order and strong morals, of comfort and authority that strengthen your resolve toward danger. You gain Immunity to psychic damage and reduce any damage you take by a value equal to your {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count until the end of combat. Furthermore, after flipping this coin your maximum {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} increases to 10 until your next long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Shrimply Delicious Bard College
entries: Bards of the way of Shrimply Delicious Soda are the very model of a happy go-lucky sort of guy/guyette, breathing in the cold sea breeze and cracking open a delicious can of soda to share with their allies. Those who were privy to the secrets of Canned Wellcheers or even in some worlds invented the drink themselves can easily reproduce it, spreading its unique value to the realms as their rightful duty. In the Forgotten Realms, the College of Canned Wellcheers is a known estabilishment in the Sword Coast, gracing Neverwinter, Luskan and particularly Waterdeep with its nectarine substance, their bards working both on marketing and production of the soft beverage. In Eberron, there are still tales of the magical drink that was divised to end the great war, and all wars on the planet. Those were hoaxes, yet the drink is still pretty good.

entries.name: Canned Caroller
entries: You've essentially mastered the art of producing a good old can of Canned Wellcheers, as such you gain proficiency in Brewer's Supplies. In addition you cannot get the jingle out of your head. Ever.

entries.name: Cheery Sips
entries: You've always got a can or two laying on you just to be the most reliable. When you you grant a creature Bardic Inspiration, the creature who benefits from it also restores hit points equal to the amount rolled, as they sip down on the Soda.

entries.name: Can Toss
entries: In addition to all else, you may expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration die to, as a bonus action, toss another creature a can of your soda, which, if willing, they drink immediatedly. You may choose which flavor of soda to toss, with each having a different effect: Cherry. The vibrant cherry flavour of Wellcheers heals the soul and brings out the best in people.

When consumed, the creature who has done so heals for {@damage 2d8} hit points, healing an additional d8 at 5th level, and another one at 10th level, and an last additional d8 at 15th level. Regular. Canned Wellcheers regular flavor bolsters its irregularized and often rampant dosage of caffeine.

Upon consumption, the creature who has done so gains a bonus equal to half their proficiency modifier to their next Saving Throw. This bonus is increased to their proficiency modifier at 5th level and double that amount on 10th level. Grape.

The most popular and rarest flavor of Wellcheers is popular for a reason, when imbibed, the imbibee gains {@dice 1d8} temporary hit points and benefits from a +1 to their next Saving Throw. Upon reaching 5th level, the drink grants an additional d8 in temporary hit points and a +2 for Saving throws, a third d8 and a +3 to Saving Throws upon reaching 10th level and a total of {@dice 4d8} temporary hit points and a +4 to their next Saving Throw when reaching 15th level. Any cans produced this way lose their effects after one minute, as the drink goes flat.

subclassFeature.name: Secret Formula: Tropical Takeaway
entries: Upon reaching 6th level, you've devised one of your best creations yet, a flavor of Canned Wellcheers that can put even Shrimp to sleep just from how calming it is, being the first drink ever to boast negative levels of caffeine. As an action, you may force-feed this drink to another creature within 60-feet of you through a well timed Can-Toss, effectively casting the {@spell sleep|PHB|Sleep} spell at 3rd level at them, with the addition of if they don't fall asleep and the {@spell sleep|PHB|Sleep} roll was above half their current hit points, they are {@condition Drowsy|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. A {@condition Drowsy|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature is more succeptible to sleep, with any following rolls of the spell being considered double the result.

In addition they suffer a -5 to their perception checks, as they are just too sleepy. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, restoring its uses on a long rest. The {@spell sleep|PHB|Sleep} spell cast through this ability is instead upcast at 4th level when you reach 10th level in this class, then at 5th level when you reach 14th level in this class and finally at 6th level when you reach 18th level.

subclassFeature.name: Express Area of Impact Delivery
entries: You've only now realized how volatile a shaken up can of WellCheers can be. As such, you may expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and your action to shake up and toss a can on any space within 60-feet of you. When reaching a surface, it explodes, the soda engulfing a 15-foot radius of that point, with its effect depending on its flavour, which you select when you use this action.

Minty Breeze. An upgrade on the Cherry flavour, it refreshes anything and everything! All creatures within radius are healed by {@damage 3d8} hit points and gain a +1 to Saving Throws until the end of your next turn.
Oceanic Rage. What do you do when someone is a mean Shrimp? Exactly, you blow them up to high heaven.

All creatures within the Delivery's radius must pass a Dexterity Saving throw or take {@damage 4d8} acid damage, or half on a success. Marshmellow Cushions. All creatures around the radius must make a Constitution Saving throw, creatures who fail this saving throw suffer as if the {@spell sleep|PHB|Sleep} spell was cast at 2nd level on them, falling asleep if the treshold beats their current hit points, or becoming {@condition Drowsy|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} if it is higher than half their current hit points.
Despite the flavour used, the area covered by the Delivery is covered in sticky soda, being considered hard terrain.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Turbulence
entries: Emotions are at the forefront of all life, the happiness of its beginning, the many, many varied feelings thorough its longevity and the sadness or even peace at its end, it all comes and goes, and a Paladin of Turbulence is one to embrace and nourish them all, be it in the name of many gods or for the sake of the simple right to feel. In the forgotten realms, there are no Orders of Turbulence, instead there are quixotic knights roaming around all of Faerun who have adopted the similar tenets of Turbulence, enjoying bringing all who makes them raw around the very realm. In the drowsy lands of Ravenloft, a Paladin of Turbulence might be one more equipped to deal with the droughts of will and bouts of sadness, yet always remain ontop, persevering and aiding to persevere through the many hard times ahead.

entries.name: Tenets of the Turbulence
entries: The vast majority of Paladins of Turbulence hold the following Tenets in their heart:

items: Wear your heart on your sleeve.
Always be genuine with what you do.

entries.name: Today's Look
entries: Starting from when you choose this subclass, every daybreak you may choose between what is appropriate for your character or roll {@dice 1d4} and define what type of feeling is particularly turbulent within you today. These feelings can encompass many others, such as Wrath also accounting for frustration or annoyance, Elation to being particularly inspired or Apathy to being extremely focused. During the day, important events may shift your Look to something else, the DM says when and what it changes into. As an example, a dragon eating your legs would turn you from Elation to probable Sorrow or Wrath.

rows: Sorrow
Elation
Wrath
Apathy

entries.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed according to the last emotion used in Passionate Emotions or Coagulate the Feelings.

entries.caption: Oath of Turbulence Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell snare|XGE|Snare}
{@spell grease|PHB|Grease}
{@spell hellish rebuke|PHB|Hellish Rebuke}
{@spell silent image|PHB|Silent Image}
5th
{@spell blur|PHB|Blur}
{@spell suggestion|PHB|Suggestion}
{@spell heat metal|PHB|Heat Metal}
{@spell calm emotions|PHB|Calm Emotions}
9th
{@spell slow|PHB|Slow}
{@spell thunder step|XGE|Thunder Step}
{@spell fireball|PHB|Fireball}
{@spell counterspell|PHB|Counterspell}
13th
{@spell arcane eye|PHB|Arcane Eye}
{@spell hallucinatory terrain|PHB|Hallucinatory Terrain}
{@spell storm sphere|XGE|Storm Sphere}
{@spell polymorph|PHB|Polymorph}
17th
{@spell wall of light|XGE|Wall of Light}
{@spell awaken|PHB|Awaken}
{@spell maelstrom|XGE|Maelstrom}
{@spell commune|PHB|Commune}

entries.name: Channel Divinity
entries: When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

entries.name: Passionate Emotions
entries: You focus on attuning even more with the emotions that currently have their reigns on you, gaining Expertise for one minute with certain skills depending on your current Look, as described below:

rows: Sorrow
{@b Paranoia.} {@skill Insight} and {@skill Investigation}.
Elation
{@b Overjoyed.} {@skill Persuasion} and {@skill Performance}.
Wrath
{@b Enraged.} {@skill Intimidation} and {@skill Athletics}.
Apathy
{@b Focused.} {@skill Perception} and {@skill Stealth}.

entries.name: Coagulate Feelings
entries: You fully embrace the feeling that lays deep in your heart at the moment, letting it out in a flurry of emotions. You gain the following abilities depending on your current emotions:

rows: Sorrow

{@b Whirlpool of Sadness.} As an action you may let out the waterfalls of your tears out, magically becoming greater and greater in size as you wallow. Any creature within 15-feet of you must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or be pulled to the nearest unnocupied space within 5-feet of you, as the torrent of tears draws them closer. You gain advantage on attacks against those creatures until the end of your next turn.
Elation

{@b Joyful Rush.} As a bonus action on your turn, a gale of your elation swirls around you and all friendly creatures within 15-feet of you, gaining an additional 10 feet of movement speed until the end of their next turn, also gaining advantage on the first attack of their turn for that duration.
Wrath

{@b Rapture in Hatred.} As a part of your attack action, you may let out a mighty roar and engulf your weapon in the flames of your rage. Your next hit deals an additional {@damage 4d8} fire damage on a hit, or half if you miss, as the heat is still unbearable. This value increases by an additional D8 on each level you'd gain a feature in this subclass.
Apathy

{@b Icy Focus.} As a bonus action, you steel your resolve and with a deep breath end both the {@condition Charmed} and {@condition Frightened} condition on yourself, gaining immunity to them until the end of your next turn. In addition, for this moment of focus, you land a critical hit on a roll of 19 or higher, before any modifiers.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Turbulence
entries: Starting at 7th level, you start imposing your feelings on the world around you much like a tulpa. Your Paladin's Aura gains the following effects according to your current look:

rows: Sorrow

{@b Dreadful Aura.} All creatures of your choice must make a Charisma Saving Throw when they enter your aura or become {@condition Frightened} of you until they leave, as a crawling paranoia washes over their thoughts.
Elation

{@b Ecstatic Aura.} All creatures of your choice inside your aura feel more energetic to go through life, gaining the benefits from the {@spell guidance|PHB|Guidance} spell. They may only use this benefit every other roll.
Wrath
{@b Murderous Aura.} All hostile creatures inside your aura take an additional amount of radiant damage equal to your proficiency bonus, as your rage makes open tears open even more fiercely.
Apathy
{@b Unimpressed.} All friendly creatures inside your aura take less damage equal to your proficiency bonus, as every blow seems to strike more lazily.

subclassFeature.name: Embrace Emotional Flow
entries: During the day, your emotions shifting have become a force to be reckoned with by themselves. When you reach 15th level, when your Look changes, you may spend your reaction to let the energy of the shifting emotions out, with the following effects:

rows: Sorrow

{@b Tearful Wails.} You let out all the pent up sadness in your soul with a single scream. All hostile creatures around a 15-feet radius around you must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw or have disadvantage on attacks against you until the end of your turn, as they are staggered from the sudden outburst.
Elation

{@b Inspiring Confidence.} Your sudden jollyness is infectious. Choose one friendly creature within 30-ft of yourself you'd like to inspire. That creature gains the effects of the {@spell bless|PHB|Bless} spell, they hold Concentration for its normal duration yet this concentration doesn't count against other concentrated spells.
Wrath

{@b Biting Anger.} The rage inside you bursts out in a powerful blow, you perform an attack with advantage against a creature within reach. On a hit, it has the benefits of a 2nd-level Divine Smite, without spending any spell slots.
Apathy

{@b Snap of Stability.} For a moment, you reclaim your calm in a moment of no bursting feelings, the focus giving you an opening to quickly cast one of the spells gained from your Oath Spells table at 3rd level without spending a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Enlightened Saint
entries: You've achieved a higher state of being through your mastery of your very own emotions. Starting at 20th level, your turbulence has died down, letting your mind become unshackled for true serenity. You can now change your current Look with a bonus action and you now have two Looks' effects actives at the same time, as your mind can easily adapt to a place between the both of them. When you would use Coagulate Feelings, you may choose two of its effects to enact during a single action. Evolving also as a spiritual guide, you can better aid creatures through their own emotions, granting you Expertise in the {@skill Persuasion} skill and allowing you to choose which of your Auras of Turbulence are active on each creature that is affected, such as choosing for one to benefit from the Sorrow Aura while another benefits from Elation. Your Aura is no longer locked to follow your Look of the day, yet other creatures may still only benefit from one of them. You may only change your Look every other turn.

entries.name: Designer's Note on Today's Look!
entries: It is suggested for the sake of truly embracing turbulence to allow yourself to be taken by the whims of the dice when you can, instead of always choosing which emotion is more convenient at any given time. The option to choose instead of trusting the dice is mainly given with the intention of better allowing a character to not become dissonant mechanically from how they are in roleplay, and should be used with that in mind.

subclassFeature.name: [Anonymous Roguish Archetype]
entries: You came and you will do your gruesome job, and you won't be remembered for it, but instead by only the terror of your work. Anonymous Rogues are a force to be reckoned with, known both for how unknown their whereabouts and personal details are and for how horrendous their assassinations can become, holding a flourish unlike anything the public could ever imagine before.

entries.name: Anonimity
entries: Your identity is a closely guarded secret, and you with to keep it like that for as long as you can. At 3rd level, you gain proficiency in {@skill Deception}, or expertise if you were already proficient in the skill. In addition to that, you can don or doff costumes in an incredibly fast time, also knowing how to make the most of it.

You gain a bonus to Charisma and Dexterity checks to blend in while wearing a disguise equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down. Aditionally, when a feature from this subclass calls for a Saving Throw, you use your Anonymous DC, which is equal to: 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus.

entries.name: To Make // Irrecognizable
entries: Upon reaching 3rd level, you're already used to turning a slab of meat into a surgeon's worst nightmare. When you reduce a creature below one hit point, you may use your reaction to mangle their corpse beyond recognition or salvation. If they somehow survive, they maximum hit points are reduced by one roll of your Sneak Attack die, only being restored by a Restoration spell or greater means. Upon reaching 13th level and using this feature, the damage instead is only recoverable through the means of a Greater Restoration spell or similarly higher level spells.

Additionally, upon doing this, a sense of despair washes over any creature that was able to see the horrible act. Any creature that can see the scene must pass your a Wisdom Saving throw against your Anonymous DC. On a failure, they must either roll a d4 or have the DM choose the most appropriate reaction of theirs to the scene:

entries.caption: Irrecognizable
rows: {@b Blind Rage.} Some are still thinking about a fallen friend, and are overtaken by the need of revenge for such atrocities. The creature gains advantage on their next attack, yet all attacks against it have disadvantage until the end of your next turn.

{@b Silent Sorrow.} To become shaken is a natural reaction, a failure for the brain to respond. The creature has a penalty to their {@skill Perception} and to their Wisdom Saving Throws until the end of your next turn that equals half of your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down.
{@b Bodily Reaction.} They just can't breathe in the scene, puke billowing out their mouth. The creature takes a number of d8 poison damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Paralyzing Fear.} No movement, like a deer caught in headlights. The creatures movement speec is reduced by 5 times your Proficiency Bonus until the end of your next turn.

entries: A creature can only be affected by this feature once per turn, and creatures with immunity against being {@condition Frightened} have advantage on this saving throw.

subclassFeature.name: Make a Scene // Elsewhere
entries: A good killer is one that knows when to aid a friend in need, or to have an useful tool help you later. Upon reaching 9th level, you've acquired a knack to making a scene while not being directly involved with it. You may do so as an action, the way you do this differs from scenario from scenario, such as swiftly unscrewing a pork from a merchants cart and causing a ruckus on the market, or throwing a spider onto a guards armor with them noticing way too late. You make a {@skill Deception} skill check with advantage against a DC your DM checks to cause this chaos, which may be decided following the Dungeon Master's Guide's example of levels of difficulty in a check.

On a success, you and any friendly creatures of your choice within a 15-feet radius of you gain advantage to their next rolls as if you had granted them the Help action. On a failure, roll a d4 for a Disaster to happen:

entries.caption: Distraction Disaster Table
rows: {@b Accidents Happen.} Oh no, something exploded or fell right on your face. You and all creatures within a 10-feet radius of yourself must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer a number of d10 bludgeoning damage equal to your proficiency bonus, or half on a success.

{@b Suddenly, Fire.} Something has caught fire, and of course it is quickly spreading. An area of 15 times your Proficiency Bonus becomes difficult terrain as its engulfed by an inferno. Any creature who enters this area or ends their turn in it suffers {@damage 1d8} fire damage.

{@b Too Much-Too much!} All the chaos around you all doesn't help, instead having the contrary effect. All the creatures that would be chosen to benefit from this instead have disadvantage on their next roll.
{@b Nothing..?} Nothing happens. Except that one person of the DM's choice notices it was you who did this act.

subclassFeature.name: Flourish of Panic
entries: Sometimes all you want to do is not just to kill a creature, but to maim them to your hearts content, drawing in attention from your barbarisms like a maestro conducting an orchestra. Upon reaching 13th level, you may perform the Flourish of Panic action instead of a Sneak Attack. The same restrictions of Sneak Attack apply and you may use this action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining expended uses on a long rest.

Flourish of Panic. Instead of delivering only one swift strike to destroy a foe, you instead draw the pain out by swiftly hitting them where it hurts the most, joints, the face, shallow cuts on the fingers - anywhere. When you do so, you perform an attack for each dice of your Sneak Attack, dealing your normal weapon damage plus {@dice 1d8} of the same damage type on a hit.

Every other hostile creature must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw or have their next roll reduced by a negative modifier equal to the number of times you've hit your original targets. After rolling any dice except for damage dice, this negative modifier is reduced by one, until it becomes zero, as they are slowly recovering from the shock of such a scene. Creatures who are imune to being {@condition Frightened||frightened} have advantage on this Saving Throw.

subclassFeature.name: The Neverseen
entries: Upon reaching 17th level, your prowess to hide yourself is so heightened that you have learnt how to wear another's skin with ease. Not literally, not in most parts, at least. After killing a humanoid ( Or human-like, such as an Angel celestial ) you may spend a long rest studying their body and make prosthetics to don a costume of the dead person.

You also impeccably are able to imitate their mannerisms and habits, as you can infer them from seeing them at their rawest before death. You have advantage on any Charisma checks to pass yourself as the dead creature, in addition you gain half your Proficiency Bonus as a bonus modifier to any skill checks that the dead person was proficient and you are not, as you push yourself to achieve a perfect disguise, so no one may gaze upon your true skin.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Dream Ender
entries:
{@i "The Family will be well-cared for... after all, the onus always fell on me to provide for what you abandoned."}
Too long have the dreams of foolish idealists ensnared the hearts of your Family and tricked your brethren into serving for the promise of a unified tomorrow. Those dreamers preached and traveled thoughout the lands to share a gospel that was lauded in gold by humans, yet drenched in sweat and tears from your tortured kindred. You have decided to take responsibility and declare a clear and defined end to this perverse goal. Your brothers and sisters are not to toil endlessly for the comfort of humankind. Vampires, {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiends}, they were birthed with desires and necessities much like humans, however, their numbers falter and plunge them down the food chain. Your very presence aims to tip that scale by shattering the pointless dreams of those selfish utopians and awake the masses to their true purpose in life.

entries.name: Tenets of the Dream Ender
entries: {@i "... Hold your tongue; I will no longer tolerate any more ingenious ideas. I've wasted enough time entertaining those cloud-chasing ruminations."}
A Paladin who upholds the Oath of the Dream Ender has promised to end foolish ideals before they take root, and cut down those that are already poisoning the minds of their fellows.

items: {@b Take What Is Yours.} Do not let different systems of morality dictate the well-being of yourself and your brethren. Drink, for the world is your share.

{@b Free Your Kindred.} All Vampires and {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiends} bound to the yoke of hunger and subservience must be liberated. Unchain them, for the streets are yours to rule.
{@b Protect the Family.} You must never let harm come to those your mantle of blood covers, those you deem family. Shield, for they depend on you.
{@b End Foolish Dreams.} Never allow thoughtless ideals to grow and fester. Crush any notion of unity with those that wish you harm beneath your heels. Slay, for this pain begets truth.

entries.name: Oath Spells
entries: {@i "I shall bear the responsibility for everything."}
You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed in the Oath of the Dream Ender Spells table. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how oath spells work.

entries.caption: Oath of the Dream Ender Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell hunter's mark|PHB|Hunter's Mark}, {@spell inflict wounds|PHB|Inflict Wounds}
5th
Exsanguinate, {@spell Melf's acid arrow|PHB|Melf's Acid Arrow}
9th
{@spell haste|PHB|Haste}, {@spell vampiric touch|PHB|Vampiric Touch}
13th
{@spell compulsion|PHB|Compulsion}, {@spell freedom of movement|PHB|Freedom of Movement}
17th
Blossoming Carmilla, {@spell conjure volley|PHB|Conjure Volley}

entries.name: Guide's Bloodfeast
entries: "For the Family..." Long have you suffered for their joy, but now, their blood is a living fountain of power for you and your allies. Whenever you inflict a creature with counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, an equal amount of Bloodfeast is added to your party's pool. Bloodfeast is a party-wide resource used to fuel a number of skills, including your own.
The party's Bloodfeast is reduced to 0 during a long rest.

entries.name: Hardblood
entries: {@i "From this impalement..."}

You have learned to fasten your enemies' demise into a resistant coat and a lance of hardened blood for battle. You gain Hardblood whenever you spend Bloodfeast equal to the same amount spent. The requirements you must meet for each rank and their effects are described in the table below:

entries.caption: Hardblood
rows: 3rd

You have a long Lance made of hardened blood which you can wield with a single hand even if not mounted, and if lost or destroyed you may recreate it during a long rest without spending materials. It acts as your spellcasting focus and applies 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to any creature that you damage while wielding it.
I
3rd
Your Lance now applies 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead of just one. Additionally, your speed increases by 10 feet.
II
7th

Your Lance now deals {@damage 2d6} piercing damage and an additional {@damage 1d8} slashing damage to bleeding enemies, and it applies 3 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead, as well as counting as a +1 arcane focus and weapon. Additionally, your AC increases by 1.
III
15th

Your Lance now deals an additional {@damage 1d12} slashing damage to Bleeding enemies, and it applies 4 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead, as well as counting as a +2 arcane focus and weapon. Additionally, your speed increases by 20 feet instead. Whenever you score a critical hit, you gain temporary hit points equal to the amount of Bloodfeast your party holds plus the amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts on the target (maximum 30).

entries.name: Channel Divinity
entries: {@i "... shall it cascade."}
You gain the following Channel Divinity options. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how Channel Divinity works.
"... shall it cascade." You gain the following Channel Divinity options. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how Channel Divinity works. Enough Is Enough.

As an action, you immediately make a melee attack against a creature within range. You can spend up to 10 Bloodfeast, gaining an additional +1 for the attack roll for each 5 Bloodfeast spent. If your current Bloodfeast count was 0, you can choose to apply 6 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on yourself instead.

If the attack hits, you apply 4 additional counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target, and heal Hit Points equal to half the amount of damage this attack dealt. Variant Hardblood Arts 6 - Whip. This Channel Divinity option substitutes Enough Is Enough once you witness the suffering other {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiends} or Vampires go through when suppressing their needs in an attempt to live among humans; or if there's a Kindred Domain Cleric in your party.

As an action, you immediately make a melee attack against a creature within range. You can spend up to 15 Bloodfeast, gaining an additional +1 for the attack roll for each 5 Bloodfeast spent. If your current Bloodfeast count was 0, you can choose to apply 6 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on yourself instead.

If the attack hits, you apply 4 additional counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target, and heal Hit Points equal to half the amount of damage this attack dealt. Additionally, for 1 minute or until you dismiss it as a bonus action, your Lance transforms into a Whip. This Whip retains all Hardblood properties your Lance would have, except its damage dice increases from {@dice 1d4} to {@dice 1d6} at Rank I, {@dice 1d8} at Rank II and {@dice 1d10} at Rank III, and can attack up to 3 creatures as long as they're standing 5 feet next to each other, or 2 creatures as long as they're standing 10 feet next to each other.

Laughters Will Subside. As a bonus action, apply {@condition Shimmering|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to target creature within 30 feet of you. For a minute, they also gain advantage on {@skill Intimidation} ability checks.

Variant Hardblood Arts 15 - Build up to Finale. This Channel Divinity option substitutes Laughters Will Subside once you witness vampires or {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiends} being objectified or needing to don masks, wear make up or hide who they are in any way to escape the wrath of other creatures; or if there's a College of Lifeblood Bard in your party. As a bonus action, apply {@condition Shimmering|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to up to 2 target creatures within 30 feet of you.

For a minute, they also gain advantage on {@skill Intimidation} ability checks. Additionally, for 1 minute or until you dismiss it as a bonus action, your Lance transforms into a Parasol. This Parasol retains all Hardblood properties your Lance would have, except its damage changes to {@damage 1d8} piercing damage and increases from {@dice 1d8} to {@dice 1d10} at Rank I, {@dice 1d12} at Rank II and {@dice 2d6} at Rank III, and you can use a reaction when a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack to divert the attack's target to you, and increasing the damage dice by 2.
This damage cannot be diminished in any way, and you generate an amount of Bloodfeast equal to the number of damage dice used plus half your proficiency bonus modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Aura de Sangre
entries: "Blood must continue to flow, to sate more of my family..." You exude an intense sanguine aura that makes your allies' blood boil. Creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you gain +1 to their AC and +1 to their attack rolls if they're below half their hit points or have counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Whenever they kill a hostile creature, they gain a number of d4s in temporary hit points equal to half your proficiency bonus modifier.

Additionally, whenever a creature within 10 feet of you that is friendly to you falls to 0 hit points or dies, you gain {@condition Responsibility|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Let All Blossom Free
entries: {@i "Let us see if humans can continue to insist on such 'righteousness' were they plagued by the same yearning that ails us."}

Your blood empowers your kin to be freed from all shackles of this world. You can spend Bloodfeast equal to the amount in the Conditions table below to immediately cure that condition from a creature within 30 feet of you:

entries.caption: Conditions
rows: {@condition Blinded} (Must not be missing this body part)
{@condition Charmed}
{@condition Deafened} (Must not be missing this body part)
5 (for each point of Exhaustion)
Exhaustion
{@condition Frightened}
{@condition Grappled}
{@condition Paralyzed}
{@condition Poisoned}
{@condition Prone}
{@condition Restrained}
{@condition Stunned}

entries: Additionally, there is a desire on your blood to continue the family and protect those you have sired. As an action, you can bite into a willing creature, transforming them into a {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} after a minute. The creature's race becomes {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} (Tome of Oblivion), and they become your immediate Kindred. Your Kindred are naturally inclined to listen and obey your demands, as if under the {@condition Charmed} condition, however, you cannot utter commands that would directly harm them, as you wish for their safety and protection as their sire. Instead of two, {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiends} you sire this way can choose up to 3 Blood Arts, but they must consume blood from a living creature at least once per day or take {@damage 2d6} Psychic damage that cannot be resisted or healed in any way.

entries.name: Variant Hardblood Arts 8 - Split Apart.
entries: Once you witness vampires or {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiends} having completely lost their minds due to the hunger and the repression of their base instincts, turning into murderous, psychopathic beasts; or if you have a Bloody Barber Artificer in your party, this ability becomes available. As a bonus action for 1 minute or until you dismiss it as another bonus action, your Lance transforms into a giant pair of scissors. These scissors retain all Hardblood properties your Lance would have, except their damage changes to {@damage 1d6} slashing damage and increases to {@damage 2d4} at Rank I, {@damage 2d6} at Rank II, and {@damage 3d8} at Rank III. Additionally, after hitting a creature with your pair of scissors, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or become {@condition Restrained} by bloody threads until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: I Shall Impale
entries: "So drink, drink with abandon, for that is the only dream this existence has permitted us." You ascend to the position you were always meant to hold, manipulating the blood around you to create an unbreakable lance to guide your kin. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute: As a reaction, if a creature within 30 feet of you would be reduced to 0 hit points due to {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} damage, instead you take a number of d4s in {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} damage equal to half their {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, and they recover Hit Points equal to that damage, afterwards losing all stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, You gain a +5 bonus to {@skill Perception} checks made to notice creatures that are missing Hit Points. Additionally, if you have inflicted {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a target, you always know where it is as long as it is within 1 mile of you and still has counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

Whenever you apply counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a creature, they immediately take the damage after the attack but do not lose any counts that round. Ascendant Hardblood Arts - La Sangre. Once you become the only one capable of leading the Vampires or {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiends} forward, once you are certain of your position and will in this world and are chosen as their guide by at least three other relevant {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiends}, you gain these additional benefits: As a reaction when a hostile creature within 30 feet of you takes {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} damage, you can heal another creature within 30 feet of you by double that amount.

Whenever you hit with an attack, you apply 1 additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. When you kill a creature that was Bleeding, you generate 10 Bloodfeast. As an action, you can empower your lance and immediately use all of your movement speed to move in a straight line and force every creature of your choice within that line to roll a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC.

If they fail, they take {@damage 5d12} piercing damage and {@damage 5d12} necrotic damage, they gain 4 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and are pushed back towards the end of your lance, becoming {@condition Restrained||restrained}. On a success, they only take half the damage and half the count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, As a reaction to when a creature {@condition Restrained||restrained} this way is hit by an attack, you can spend 30 Bloodfeast to make them vulnerable to all damage types until the end of that round. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.
Designer's Note

subclassFeature.name: Fangripper Ranger Archetype
entries: "{@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiends} are not only vile, they're also very persistent. So~ we should make sure we have everything ready to take them on, right?" It is true that one trait shared between many rangers is their specialization towards a specific type of quarry, but this truth is the boldest and most dogmatic when it comes to the Fangrippers, who dedicate their lives to destroying the scourge that are bloodsuckers.

Wielding impressive arsenals of their own design, the Fangrippers prowl about in search of all the uglies that go bump in the night, {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|bloodfiends}, vampires or any other type of shapechanger, all with the objective of ending them.

Wherever they may be found, they are usually seen in groups, armed to the teeth and knocking on doors with the friendliest demeanor for the living, saving all their pent up hatred for those that have abandoned life itself.

entries.name: Additional Favored Enemy
entries: You've collected enough about the leeches of your world, as such you gain the benefits of Favored Enemy towards a new type of favored enemy: Shapechangers. These include Vampires, Changelings, Werewolves and other Werebeasts. In general, monstrous beings who keep their true nature hidden are considered Shapechangers, except for Fey. When in doubt, the DM holds final ruling about what is and isn't considered a Shapechanger.

entries.name: Cheerful Hunt's Focus
entries: When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn it into a deliberate wound. The damage is halved, and you suffer twice the number of the attack's damage dice in {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} counts.
While suffering from Bleed, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist being {@condition Grappled||grappled}.
You have advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist having a weapon removed from your grip.
You have advantage on Wisdom saving throws made to resist being {@condition Frightened||frightened} or {@condition Charmed||charmed}.
Whenever you deal damage, the target suffers {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Rupture} counts equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.

entries: You can use this reaction once per short or long rest, twice beginning at 8th level, and three times beginning at 14th level.

entries.name: Arms of the Hunt
entries: At the end of the day, you can't deal with abominations with the common weaponry you see everyday, Instead you gather a variety of resources to employ in your crusade against the dark, gaining a pool of Preparation Die that you may spend during a Long Rest to prepare any of the following items:

entries.caption: Arms of the Hunt
rows: Antitoxin
Any Horror Trinket from Van Richten's Guide to Ravenloft or similar useless bauble
Caltrops (20)
{@item Grappling Dart|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}
{@item Stake|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} (6)
{@item Bonecrusher Hammer|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}
Net
{@item Styptics Bag|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}
{@item Sanctified Canister|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}
{@item Vein Splitter|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}
{@item Vial of Silver Water|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}
{@item Aromatized Incense Burner|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}

entries: At the start of a long rest, if you had any unused item you break them down for scraps, as you've got to make the most of each piece you have. Additionally, these items are usually scrapped together or have already seen their fair share of use and have to be rebuilt, causing merchants to be wary of buying them.

subclassFeature.name: Hunting Manual - Practical Uses 101
entries: There are a number of tricks that any good hunter must learn to employ to further their goals, afterall, you're only a regular person when compared to a beast of blood. As such, you've learnt how to make the most of your limited resources, gaining the following uses for your Arms of The Hunt through spending an action:

entries.caption: Practical Uses 101
rows: Antitoxin

Inject. You may use your Bonus Action to administer Antitoxin to yourself or to a creature within your melee reach, instantly ending the {@condition Poisoned||Poisoned} condition on them and causing the target to be Resistant to poison damage until the end of their next turn.
Horror Trinket

Spook. As a Bonus Action you may immolate the Horror Trinket as an Effigy, forcing up to your Proficiency Bonus' worth of creatures within 60-ft that can see you to pass a Wisdom Saving Throw or become {@condition Frightened||Frightened} of you for up to one minute. You gain a bonus modifier to {@skill Intimidation} Skill Checks against creatures {@condition Frightened||Frightened} like this equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature {@condition Frightened||Frightened} this way may re-attempt this Saving Throw at the end of their turns, ending the condition on a success.
Caltrops

Wedge. Whenever a creature would take damage because of your Caltrops, they also suffer an additional {@damage 2d6} piercing damage and two {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Rupture} Count.
{@item Grappling Dart|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}

Pull-Through. When the {@item Grappling Dart|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Grappling Dart} is lodged into a creature you've hit that is of your size or Larger, or is an Object that weighs more than you, you may spend your Bonus ACtion to pull yourself to be within the closest unoccupied 5-ft space from the target.
{@item Stake|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} (6)

Twisting. As a Reaction taken after you deal damage using a Stake, you may choose to twist the piece of wood and cause the target to trigger {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} up to half your Proficiency Bonus' worth of times, rounded down, removing {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count in accord.
{@item Bonecrusher Hammer|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}
Veincrush. Makes it so the target can't recover Hit Points for the amount of turns equal to your Proficiency Modifier.
Net

Laminate. Your net is laced with a special coating that makes it easily cut when put under strain, causing any creature that tries to break free from the net to suffer 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} on a Failure.
{@item Styptics Bag|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}
Imbibe. When used, the {@item Styptics Bag|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Styptics Bag} also heals the target for {@dice 2d4 + 2} hit points.
{@item Sanctified Canister|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}

Aimed Throw. You know how to use the explosion to direct creatures away on the right angle. When you throw the grenade and it explodes, you may choose to have the detonation forcefully push any creature who fails the Saving Throw in a 15-ft line of your choice.
{@item Vein Splitter|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}

Gouge. When you would trigger Hemorrhaging while using this weapon, you may spend your Reaction to quickly draw out the pain inflicted to either scratch at a creature's eye or sink into their ear, causing them to be respectively {@condition Blinded||Blinded} or {@condition Deafened||Deafened} until they are cured of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding}.
{@item Vial of Silver Water|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}

Accessorise. You may don this item not as a charm but as the weight at the end of a whip or another melee weapon's pommel as a Bonus Action, causing any damage you deal with the adorned weapon to also deal an additional {@damage 2d4} radiant damage against Shapechangers and Undead creatures, yet the Vial breaks if you receive or deal a Critical Hit. You may spend an Action to retrieve the Vial out of the weapon.
{@item Aromatized Incense Burner|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}

Combust. Your Incense is particularly strong, making it so that the 30-feet area around the Incense Burner also becomes Heavily Obscured to any Undead or Shapechanger creature. This area increases by 5-ft at the start of your turns and lasts for up to one minute or until you are knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}. Furthermore, any Undead or Shapechanger creature who starts or ends their turn inside this area instantly suffers {@damage 1d4} radiant damage.

entries: You may use this feature for an amount of times equal to your Proficiency Modifier, regaining half the spent uses at a Short Rest or all spent uses on a Long Rest. Despite the nature of the original item, such as a weapon being used, it is always consumed or destroyed after use, as you wring out all its usefulness at once. The DC for any Saving Throws mentioned in this table is equal to your Ranger Spell Save DC.

subclassFeature.name: Jolly Old Hunter
entries: With time and experience so comes the strengthening of bones broken numerous times. You gain Advantage on Constitution, Wisdom and Intelligence Saving Throws. Furthermore, you may push your body beyond its limits to change a failed Saving Throw into a Successful one, also taking no damage if you still would. Whenever you do this you suffer one Point of Exhaustion and may do so up to an amount of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Hunting Manual - The Secret Trades
entries: You have become quite the Hunter, learned in their ways and nimble with their thoughts on how to take down the befanged threat. So much so, that you've learnt how to become a threat yourself. Upon reaching 15h level you may choose one of the following weapons to have as your Signature Weapon, a weapon of which you have trained painstakingly to become a monster with:

entries.caption: Signature Weapons
rows: {@item Serrated Hand-axe|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Serrated Hand-axe}

While wielding a Serrated Edge, you are an unstoppable menace, gaining the following effects: Once per turn you may choose to suffer only half the damage you would take from an attack, shrugging it off as one of your many lacerations. Furthermore, you deal an additional {@damage 2d8} slashing damage with {@item Serrated Hand-axe|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Serrated Hand-Axe} attacks and always inflict 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed}, inflicting two additional counts instead of one when triggering Hemorrhage. You also deal double any damage rolled against structures and objects that are not being worn or wielded.
Steel-Tipped Whip

You have made some modifications to your whip, using a specific alchemical formula to make any Steel-Tipped Whip you wield to be considered as a Silvered Weapon that deals an additional {@damage 3d4} radiant damage against Undead and Shapechanger creatures, of which cannot recover hit points after being dealt damage this way until they bask into complete darkness for 12 hours. Furthermore, you may use your Whip to cause other creatures to fall {@condition Prone||Prone} by forgoing dealing damage when you would hit them, also inflicting 6 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Rupture} Count on the target.
{@item Stake|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}

You're a monster when it comes to pinning the monsters of night down and bleeding them dry. You may treat {@item Stake Crossbow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Stake Crossbows} as if they had the Light property in place of Heavy and Two-Handed. Furthermore, when you spend your Bonus Action to attack with them, you fire three stakes without any additional ammo cost, being able to perform a ranged weapon attack to the same or another target. At the end of your turn, if you have hit one target with Stakes at least thrice, they must pass a Constitution Saving Throw against your Ranger Spell Save DC (Or 8 + your Dexterity Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or become {@condition Restrained||Restrained} until the end of your next turn on a failure. A creature who fails this Saving Throw automatically succeeds it on the next time it is forced to attempt it. You also inflict 2 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Rupture} whenever you hit an attack while using Stakes. When you do so, you do not trigger {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Rupture}'s effects or reduce its Count.
{@item Vein Splitter|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}

You have dabbled into the arts of potioncrafting, or more specifically: poisoncraft. As a Bonus Action during your turns you may douse a {@item Vein Splitter|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Vein Splitter} with this poison, which forces a creature that takes damage from it to pass a Constitution Saving Throw (DC 8 + your Dexterity Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or be {@condition Charmed||Charmed} by you until they stop {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} or is knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}. While {@condition Charmed||Charmed} in this way, the creature is under effect of your choice of illusion from the {@spell major image|PHB|Major Image} or {@spell phantasmal killer|PHB|Phantasmal Killer} spells as if you had cast them and only the {@condition Poisoned||poisoned} creature can perceive it. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, restoring spent uses on a Long Rest. You may use your Signature Weapon for your Practical Uses 101 ability an amount of times before it breaks equal to your Proficiency Bonus, also fixing and recreating it during a Long Rest without the need to spend extra resources.

subclassFeature.name: Flamespout Artificer Specialist
entries: "What'd I say, big sis? I said I'd return to burn it all down."

The life of an artificer isn't an easy one, much less the one of a person who has had their life burn down around them. Those who specialize in the Flamespout have grown to believe one theory above all the rest: That flame will be the only salvation for their soul, not for an afterlife or grander reward, much less greater good; All they wish for is their peace again.

A Flamespout artificer specializes in producing copious amounts of combustion to lay waste unto anything within their path, setting out in a burning crusade of their own making. They save no fuel until their job is done. Flamespout artificers are often misfits and people abandoned by their world no matter the setting, usually having lost all they ever had in one way or another, and with no way to revert that loss they turn into making sure that the price of their suffering is paid by all of those that have wrongfully crossed their path.

entries.name: Convictions in Flame
entries: Hope is akin to a candle's fire, despite its ephemerality it still grants safety amidst the dark. This is something that you've learnt well, and as such your obsession with flame has led you to better implement it in your weapons.

You gain proficiency with Gauntlets and during a long rest you may choose to perform maintenance on weapons you are proficient with to have them be able to deal fire damage instead of their initial damage type, provided they dealt Slashing, Piercing or Bludgeoning damage before. You choose which damage type to deal when you would deal it, as you coat your weapon in burning fuel or shove it off.

Additionally, this constant burning has you deal one stack of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} whenever you would cause fire damage with a weapon attack. This increases to two {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} when you reach 8th level and three upon reaching 16th level. You may only benefit from this up to an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per round, rounded down.

entries.name: Flamespout Spells
entries: You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the table below. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don't count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

entries.caption: Flamespout Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell burning hands|PHB|Burning Hands}, {@spell hellish rebuke|PHB|Hellish Rebuke}
5th
{@spell aganazzar's scorcher|XGE|Aganazzar's Scorcher}, {@spell flaming sphere|PHB|Flaming Sphere}
9th
{@spell erupting earth|XGE|Erupting Earth}, {@spell fireball|PHB|Fireball}
13th
{@spell fire shield|PHB|Fire Shield}, {@spell wall of fire|PHB|Wall of Fire}
17th
{@spell dawn|XGE|Dawn}, {@spell flame strike|PHB|Flame Strike}

entries.name: Drink in Flame
entries: The beauty of darkness being lit is one that your heart finds confidence in, a source of fuel to move forward. As such, you gain a bonus modifier to Wisdom Saving Throws for each {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning} creature within 20-ft of you, up to a maximum equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

If there are four or more creatures {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning} within that range, you also gain half your proficiency modifier's value (rounded down) as a bonus to attack rolls.

entries.name: Workshop Bathed in Fuel
entries: Your Firefist Engine holds Igniter Fuel equal to 10 times your proficiency bonus. You can use that fuel for the following features:

entries.name: Pre-Heated Gasoline
entries: As a bonus action, spend Igniter Fuel to heat the engine. The next time this turn you deal fire damage, apply 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count per 4 Igniter Fuel spent. A creature that succeeds on a saving throw against the initial fire damage suffers half as many Burn counts, rounded down.

entries.name: Fuel Detonation
entries: As an action, spend 2 Igniter Fuel per {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count on a Burning creature and make a melee weapon attack against it. On a hit, the attack deals an additional {@damage 1d8} fire damage per Burn count on the target.

entries.name: Burning Grounds
entries: As an action, spend Igniter Fuel in multiples of 4 to coat a radius of 5 feet per 4 fuel spent. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. The area is difficult terrain for other creatures. Whenever one creature in the area suffers Burn, every other creature in it suffers half as many Burn counts, rounded down. The zone lasts until a creature uses its action to extinguish a 10-foot radius or running water washes the fuel away.
You regain all Igniter Fuel when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Until the Last Drop
entries: When your Igniter Fuel is below half its maximum, it becomes Overheated Fuel. Spending Overheated Fuel on a Workshop Bathed in Fuel feature adds the corresponding effect below:

entries.name: Blazing Gasoline
entries: For every 4 Overheated Fuel spent, Pre-Heated Gasoline's Burn lasts 1 additional turn without being halved at the end of that turn.

entries.name: Complete Devastation
entries: When Fuel Detonation hits, each other creature within 10 feet of the target must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking the same fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The original target then loses all Burn counts.

entries.name: Live Fire Zone
entries: A creature other than you that starts or ends its turn in Burning Grounds takes {@damage 1d8} fire damage and suffers 1 Burn count per 4 Overheated Fuel spent. The number of d8s is reduced by one at the start of each of your turns until the fire is extinguished.
If spending fuel takes you below half your maximum, only the fuel spent after crossing that threshold counts as Overheated Fuel.

subclassFeature.name: Emergency Measures
entries: Sometimes a quick decision is needed to keep on burning, and you've made sure that your Firefist Engine is adaptable for that. As a bonus action during your turn you may choose to have your Engine tap onto a magic item you're attuned to's magic power to convert it into fuel. The item becomes inert and loses its magical properties until the next short rest and you regain Igniter Fuel based on its rarity:

entries.caption: Emergency Measures
rows: Uncommon
Rare
Very Rare
Legendary

subclassFeature.name: A Lone Firefly's Path
entries: The fire in your heart has not dimmed and will keep on fighting as long as you can have more lights around you, having burned enough to turn your Firefist Engine into a near perfect creation. When you spend any Fuel, the fire damage you deal ignores a target creature's Resistance to fire damage and considers Immune creatures to only be Resistant instead.

Additionally, you may spend your bonus action or a reaction when you would become {@condition Charmed||Charmed}, {@condition Frightened||Frightened} or suffer any Enchantment spell effects that you are aware of you may spend 5 Igniter Fuel to set yourself ablaze, suffering 6 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} Count and immediately ending the condition or effect. While burning this way, all your Fuel is considered Overheated Fuel. You may do this an amount of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down, regaining spent uses on a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Lordship
entries: The Oath of Lordship is one rarely taken, and those who dare to do it lightly simply do not make it out alive. To be a lord one must know how to answer the fundamental questions of what a World needs, and how to deliver results in that pursuit, commanding their fellows with a strong conviction for all, no matter the cost, also following these principles:

entries.name: Lead With Justice.
entries: Be fair towards those you judge, weighing all they may have done and what they still have to contribute.

entries.name: Show Your Power.
entries: Reject no duel, never be happy in the backseat of a fight; Instead be headstrong in your pursuits, no matter how violent they might be.

entries.name: Be Brazen and Undaunted.
entries: No matter what tactics you may employ, know that to truly be a Lord you must not fear exposing yourself and your truths.

entries.name: Share Knowledge.
entries: Others must understand the grandiosity of your pursuits, so they as well may one day reach enlightenment.

entries.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed.

entries.caption: Oath of Lordship Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell guiding bolt|PHB|Guiding Bolt}, {@spell sanctuary|PHB|Sanctuary}
5th
{@spell see invisibility|PHB|See Invisibility}, {@spell silence|PHB|Silence}
9th
{@spell beacon of hope|PHB|Beacon of Hope}, {@spell intellect fortress|TCE|Intellect Fortress}
13th
{@spell dominate beast|PHB|Dominate Beast}, {@spell freedom of movement|PHB|Freedom of Movement}
17th
{@spell conjure volley|PHB|Conjure Volley}, {@spell wall of force|PHB|Wall of Force}

entries.name: I Carve The Path of a Lord
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity as an Action to prepare a grand attack while being assisted by a friendly creature within 60-ft of yourself, you perform a melee weapon attack against a target creature within reach and deal your weapon's damage die plus a number of d8 radiant damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Immediately after, one friendly creature of your choice within range performs a Melee or Ranged attack against the same creature with Advantage, regardless if you miss or hit. The friendly creature you chose may also choose to cast a spell against the same target, for a Spell Level equalling half their highest Spell Slot Level known, rounded down. (Ex: A Wizard with access to 5th Level Spell Slots may only cast up to a 2nd Level Spell, or only Cantrips if they only know up to 1st Level Spell Slots.)

entries.name: The Lord of All Beasts
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity as an Action to augment your and your fellows' resolve toward a shared goal, granting you and a number of willing creatures within 30-ft of you equalling your Proficiency Bonus an additional modifier to their Skill Checks for the next minute or until you are knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}. This bonus is equal to half your Proficiency Modifier, rounded down.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of a Lord
