entries: Your pure, unadulterated presence forms into a magical aura that expands around you as you breathe, bolstering your allies' resolve in unique ways. A friendly creature within 10-ft of you gains one of the following benefits according to their class:

entries.caption: Aura of a Lord
rows: Artificer
The Artificer adds half of your Charisma Modifier to their Flash of Genius bonus.
Barbarian
The Barbarian has an {@dice 1d4} reduction to any damage they take while within the Aura.
Bard
Whenever a creature would benefit from the Bard's Bardic Inspiration die, they also gain an additional {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier.
Cleric

As long as the Cleric or a creature they are targeting are within your Aura, the Clerics spells either deal an additional {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage on a hit or failed Saving Throw or heal for an additional {@dice 1d6} hit points when healing another creature.
Druid
The Druid gains two rolls of your Divine Smite die as Temporary Hit Points when they enter Wildshape. Those last until they are reduced to 0 or the Druid leaves Wildshape.
Fighter
The Fighter is healed by an additional amount equal to two rolls of your Divine Smite die when they use Second Wind.
Monk
The Monk may use an additional Unarmed Attack during their Flurry of Blows.
Paladin
Other friendly Paladins gain an additional Divine Smite damage die.
Ranger
The Ranger deals an additional d8 radiant damage against their Favored Foe.
Rogue
The Rogue gains one additional Sneak Attack damage die.
Sorcerer
The Sorcerer gains a 1 point Metamagic cost reduction while within your Aura. The cost for using a Metamagic Option cannot go below 1 Metamagic Point spent.
Wizard
The Wizard's spells are upcast to be one level higher (If able) if you spend one of your spell slots to empower theirs, doing so when they would cast a spell but you don't spend a Reaction to do so.
Warlock: Blade
The Warlock has a bonus modifier to hit creatures as long as either are within your Aura while wielding their Pact Weapon. This bonus equals half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down.
Warlock: Chain
The Pact Familiar may perform an attack without the Warlock needing to sacrifice one of their own attacks to do so, provided that either the Warlock or Familiar are within your Aura.
Warlock: Talisman
The Warlock gains an additional bonus to their Talisman re-rolls equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down.
Warlock: Tome
The Warlock gains a bonus to hit creatures with Cantrips while they or the target are within your Aura. This bonus equals half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down.

entries: If a creature within your aura doesn't have a class, it benefits to the closest fitting effect as per your DM's choice, and unless the DM decides so, summoned creatures do not gain any benefit from this. If a player is Multiclassing, they choose which of their classes to benefit from this at the combat's start.
Furthermore, you may spend your Reaction in the following situations to directly order and advise friendly creatures within the aura:

items: {@b Lordsguard.} As long as a creature has another friendly creature within 5-ft of them and either is targeted by an attack, you may spend your Reaction to give one of them an Assist Order. When you do so, the creature defends the other as best they can, imposing Disadvantage on the attacking creature's attacks until the end of their turn. When your Aura is upgraded, you also grant the target a bonus modifier to their AC that equals half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down. This lasts until the start of the defended creature's turn.

{@b Exalted Command.} As long as a creature is able to hear you, you may spend your reaction when they would perform an attack, but before rolling, to order them to perform an Exalted Attack instead. When they do so, they add half your Charisma Modifier to hit and on a hit, deal half your Divine Smite's damage die of Divine Damage, rounded down.

subclassFeature.name: Lone Stand on the Crimson Garden
entries: The struggles of battle and scars of many past events have shaped your road, yet through it all you remain with your head held high and proud. As such, it is much harder for you to fall than most, only becoming a tougher opponent as a fight goes on: You deal an additional d8 divine damage on your melee attack and spell attack hits for each 20 Maximum Hit Points you have missing from your total to a maximum of {@dice 5d8}.

Furthermore, once per month you may instantly revive yourself when you would die, healing half your Maximum Hit Points and ending any Conditions on yourself. If you do so outside of combat or after it ends you instantly suffer 5 points of Exhaustion after reviving, as crystallized blood sprouts around your limbs like the scales of a dragon from the sudden manifestation of your power.

subclassFeature.name: Absolute Path of Paved Ambitions
entries: You have become the splitting image of a powerful Lord, leading on your fellows in battle with unparalleled might and shaping the world to your vision. You gain the following benefits:

items: The reach of your Aura of a Lord increases by 5-ft at the end of your turn if you have not moved from the space you started your turn in. Furthermore, you gain Advantage on Strength Saving Throws and Skill Checks against being moved while your Aura has increased reach. Your Aura of a Lord may increase in this way for a maximum reach of 60-ft and resets when you move or are moved.
Whenever a creature you can see is killed or knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious} within 60-ft of you, you gain an additional use of your Reaction until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Despair Domain
entries: {@i "I look down? Nah, it's gotta be the E.G.O gear... Or, maybe it's just the night getting me all sentimental. Yeah... you know how it is."}

Not all clerics of the Despair Domain chose this calling. While there is a congregation of cultists that worship gods of trickery, disaster, and tragedy, some, if not most, of the ones chained by their domain are people that have lost it all and have had their mind and soul consumed by despair. If at every waking moment your only thoughts are related to a tragedy you suffered, you are a devotee of the Despair Domain.

Clerics and chosen ones of the Despair Domain have their lives filled with grief and a sense that their future will not be long. However, they are possibly some of the largest sources of hope in the universe, both for themselves and for others. As dark and thick as despair may be, there always remains a meager thought that it might one day be cleansed by the light of the coming day. The larger the tragedy befallen one of the Despair Domain, the grander their revival could be.

Essentially, clerics and chosen ones of the Despair Domain are constantly switching from sinking down and being mired in thoughts of defeat to standing proud and rising to conquer their demons with a radiant glow of hope flowing from them.

entries.name: Despair Domain Spells
entries: {@i "E.G.O Corrosion rate... acceptable... Probably."}
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

entries.caption: Despair Domain Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell arms of Hadar|PHB|Arms of Hadar}, {@spell sanctuary|PHB|Sanctuary}
3rd
{@spell spiritual weapon|PHB|Spiritual Weapon}, {@spell warding bond|PHB|Warding Bond}
5th
{@spell beacon of hope|PHB|Beacon of Hope}, {@spell conjure barrage|PHB|Conjure Barrage}
7th
{@spell death ward|PHB|Death Ward}, {@spell phantasmal killer|PHB|Phantasmal Killer}
9th
{@spell conjure volley|PHB|Conjure Volley}, {@spell hallow|PHB|Hallow}

entries.name: The Sword Sharpened with Tears
entries: {@i "All I had left was a hollow, weathered pride..."}

Uncertain of your place in the world, whether a warrior of hope or a knight of despair, you still try to radiate what you believe in to your allies. You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor, and you always have a Blessing/Despair counter, which can have a maximum value equal to your proficiency bonus and a minimum equal to the negative value of your proficiency bonus. If your Blessing/Despair counter does not change for 1 minute, it shifts 1 point toward 0: a positive value decreases by 1, and a negative value increases by 1.

While the value of your Blessing/Despair counter is greater than 0, you are in Blessing Mode. Any creature that attacks you while you are in this mode gains 1 count of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} per attack. Additionally, when a creature within 15 feet of you other than yourself is targeted by an attack, you can use your reaction to give that creature a bonus to its AC equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down. This bonus lasts until the end of the round.

While the value of your Blessing/Despair counter is lower than 0, you are in Despair Mode. Any creature you hit with a weapon or a spell gains 3 counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Additionally, if you miss an attack roll against a creature with {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, you can use your reaction to roll again.
As a bonus action, you can perform a Hollow Wail to raise or lower your Blessing/Despair counter by 2. It also changes under the following circumstances:

entries.caption: Blessing/Despair Counter
rows: When you heal another creature.
When a friendly creature becomes {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}.
When you deal a critical hit.
When you suffer a critical hit.
When you succeed on a saving throw.
When you fail a saving throw.
When a creature fails a saving throw you forced it to make.
When a creature succeeds on a saving throw you forced it to make.

entries: Your Blessing/Despair counter resets to 0 when you finish a long rest.

entries.name: The Knight's Sanctuary
entries: {@i "The Knight of Despair still dwells in her past glories, just like her sisters."}

As you cry on the battlefield, your teardrops transform into stars that float around you, forming constellations of weapons that remind you there is still a battle to be fought. At the start of your turn in combat, or once per turn by using a bonus action, if you are in Blessing Mode, you gain 1 count of {@condition Protecting Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. When a creature within 30 feet of you is attacked, you can use your reaction to spend all your counts of {@condition Protecting Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, reducing the damage by {@dice 1d8} for each count spent. If you spend 6 counts of {@condition Protecting Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} this way, the damage is reduced to 0.

entries.name: Faded Faith.
entries: At the start of your turn in combat, or once per turn by using a bonus action, if you are in Despair Mode, you gain 1 count of {@condition Piercing Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. When a creature within 30 feet of you deals damage to another creature, you can use your reaction to spend all your counts of {@condition Piercing Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, adding {@damage 1d6} cold damage to its damage roll for each count spent. If you spend 6 counts of {@condition Piercing Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} this way, the damage ignores resistance and immunity.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: With the Power of Justice
entries: {@i "As mandated by chivalry, foul play is strictly forbidden in combat; however, mercy should also not be expected."}
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to summon forth the constellations from your tears, turning them into physical swords that surround you and protect your allies.

As a bonus action, if you are in Blessing Mode, you can lift your holy symbol and become surrounded by starry swords. For 1 minute, when a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see is hit by an attack roll, you can use your reaction to force one of your swords to pierce you. The creature takes only half the damage from the attack, and you take the other half. This damage ignores your resistance and immunity.

entries.name: With the Tear-Sharpened Sword
entries: As an action, if you are in Despair Mode, you can lift your holy symbol and choose a number of creatures within 30 feet of you equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one creature). Sharp swords surround the chosen creatures, pointing toward hostile creatures. For 1 minute, when one of the chosen creatures hits an enemy with an attack roll, it can use its reaction to be pierced by one of the swords, taking {@damage 2d8} cold damage that ignores resistance and immunity and causing the creature it hit to take the same amount of damage.

subclassFeature.name: Whispers of the Betrayed Knight
entries: {@i "As with sorrow, perhaps sharing the burden will blunt the edge."}

The injustices you have suffered do not end, and tears continue to flow from your face, bringing with them magic and a few blessings. Twice per turn, whenever you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you is hit by a hostile creature, you gain 1 count of Deep Tears. You can have a number of Deep Tears equal to twice your proficiency bonus, and you can use a bonus action to spend them according to the Deep Tears table. All counts of Deep Tears disappear when you finish a short or long rest.

entries.caption: Deep Tears
rows: Choose a creature within 30 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, its attacks apply 2 additional counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
You gain resistance to a damage type of your choice until the start of your next turn.
Choose a creature within 30 feet of you. It gains {@dice 2d6} temporary hit points until the start of your next turn.
Choose a creature within 30 feet of you. Whenever it rolls damage before the start of your next turn, it may change the result of one damage die to its maximum value.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Strike
entries: {@i "There are times in life when one may shed tears over the littlest things."}

You gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} psychic damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeature.name: Arcana Pierce
entries: {@i "Tears fall like ash, embroidered as if they were constellations."}

You have reached the culmination of your suffering and guilt, and as your swords pierce you, they bring forth all manner of emotions that flood and mold the battlefield with their crushing weight. As an action, you gain {@condition Sharpened by Tears|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Tear-Sharpened}. Then, if you are in Blessing Mode, as part of the same action, choose a number of creatures within 30 feet of you equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one creature). If a chosen creature made an attack roll on its previous turn, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, your swords pierce it, and it becomes {@condition Restrained||restrained} until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, it is not restrained, but it gains 2 counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Arcana: Tear and Pierce
entries: If you are in Despair Mode, you instead immediately cast {@spell spiritual weapon|PHB|Spiritual Weapon} without expending a spell slot. If you expend a spell slot, the spell is cast at 5th level regardless of the slot's actual level. While you are concentrating on this {@spell spiritual weapon|PHB|Spiritual Weapon}, all your spell attacks apply 2 additional counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Slithering One Sorcerous Origin
entries: {@i "I did everything as I was told... I was fiercely loyal... so why wasn't it me?"}

The Heishou Pack are a group of mutant assassins and combatants, each assigned to a different branch themed after the Chinese zodiac. Those of the Si Branch follow the way of the Serpent, making use of elastic arms and poison to quickly steal from and assassinate their targets.

You are blessed with serpentine features, which could be due to a yuan-ti ritual, a certain poison your mother was afflicted by, a snake-like ancestor, or even a special transformative medicine applied to you. Either way, your body has undergone changes, becoming long and thin. Additionally, you have an affinity for poisons and the natural magic present in the world, able to attune to it similarly to how a druid would.

The Heishou are a mercenary group, owing loyalty to no one except their lord, who is the latest person to have hired a specific branch. As a member of the Si Branch, you might be a hired assassin on a mission, a beast of violet scales trying to escape your leash, or simply an assassin waiting for a new lord to hire you and take you to battle.

subclassFeature.name: Slithering Magic
entries: {@i "Sun's up, gotta keep m'lord updated. Fuhu, he's gonna love me for it."}

You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Slithering Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it does not count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be an evocation or transmutation spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list.

entries.caption: Slithering Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell longstrider|PHB|Longstrider}, {@spell ray of sickness|PHB|Ray Of Sickness}
3rd
{@spell pass without trace|PHB|Pass Without Trace}, {@spell spider climb|PHB|Spider Climb}
5th
{@spell hypnotic pattern|PHB|Hypnotic Pattern}, {@spell vampiric touch|PHB|Vampiric Touch}
7th
{@spell evard's black tentacles|PHB|Evard's Black Tentacles}, {@spell grasping vine|PHB|Grasping Vine}
9th
{@spell contagion|PHB|Contagion}, {@spell mislead|PHB|Mislead}

subclassFeature.name: Heishou Mutation [Si]
entries: {@i "Once I took the Si Bolus, I lost most of my sense of taste... But hey, I can still enjoy the texture."}

Your limbs were modified by a special medicine to stretch farther than is usual for humanoids. You can stretch your arms up to 5 feet beyond their normal length, allowing you to interact with objects and creatures at a distance, and your melee weapon attacks have the Reach property. This distance increases to 10 feet at 6th level, 30 feet at 14th level, and 60 feet at 18th level. Additionally, you have resistance to poison damage.

subclassFeature.name: Serpent Glint
entries: {@i "It's disgusting and ugly, isn't it? It gets worse with time. I'm going to be like the other snakes, like the other beasts of the Heishou Pack... becoming numb to everything."}

As your mutations improve, your animal characteristics become more prevalent with each spell conjured. Whenever you use Metamagic, you gain 2 stacks of {@condition Serpent Arm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

Additionally, when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you have advantage on the roll, as you use your arms to grab onto something and pull yourself out of harm's way.

subclassFeature.name: Snake Fang
entries: {@i "Didya see that? Doubt ya did... A crooked snake whips faster than the speed of sound, you know."}

You can hasten your serpentine transformation and reap the benefits of your monstrous future. As a bonus action, you can spend one or more sorcery points to magically transform your body for 10 minutes. For each sorcery point you spend, you gain one of the following benefits of your choice, which lasts until the transformation ends:

items: You gain blindsight out to 30 feet, as you activate the heat vision of a serpent.
You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

Whenever you hit an enemy with a spell that deals poison damage, it suffers 2 stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Your spells ignore resistance to poison damage, and when you reach 18th level, they also ignore immunity to poison damage.

Your head morphs into that of a large, poisonous purple snake. As an action, you can make a melee spell attack against a creature within 30 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 5d8} poison damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer 3 stacks of {@condition Deathrite Venom|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

subclassFeature.name: Serpent's Mortal Flurry
entries: {@i "You won't find a better snake for this job~"}

Your transformation into a serpent is almost complete, as you feel your veins slither and tremble beneath your skin. As an action, you transform both arms into myriads of purple serpents, then stretch them toward a point you choose within 60 feet. Each creature of your choice in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 6d8} poison damage and is {@condition Restrained|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} until the start of its next turn. If it had neither resistance nor immunity to poison damage, it is {@condition Paralyzed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers 2 stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, but is neither paralyzed nor restrained.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 4 sorcery points to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Chronocrush Arcane Tradition
entries: Wizards of the Crushbound Arcane Tradition are oddballs among oddballs, obsessed with compressing the very concept of time into the palm of their hand to use much like a battery, unleashing its potential to hasten themselves or the world around them just as they slow it by extracting this precious metaphysical concept.

They are most often a subsect of the Chronurgy school of magic, specializing in a practical and direct reapplication of time as a resource and procuring as much knowledge as they can within this niche of the arcane sciences.

Crushbound wizards are few and far between in any realm, usually hermits in search of higher knowledge about the concept of time. They are often drawn to adventure either to search for it or to apply their widely insane theories in field practice, with little regard for the consequences of compressing time, as they see it as simply another source of energy.

subclassFeature.name: Crushbound Metronome
entries: Chronurgy's lineage of arcane traditions can be very specific at times, and you have studied the ways of compressing and compounding a series of moments into a smaller form fit for your hand, to use in any way you wish. Coupling that with a metronome-like technique to conduct your spells, you have begun mastering the ways of the Chronocrusher, gaining the following benefits:

entries.name: Accumulating Time
entries: At the start of each of your turns, you gain 1 count of {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, a magically contained string of compacted time you can use to empower yourself. You can also use your action to gain 4 counts of {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, or your bonus action to gain 2 counts. When you successfully cast {@spell counterspell|PHB|Counterspell} against a creature, you gain 2 counts as well.

entries.name: Metronomic Quality
entries: Beginning on the first turn in combat, you switch between tempos of attack and defense in the way you weave spells. Odd-numbered turns are Tick turns, while even-numbered turns are Tock turns.

entries.name: Tick (Odd Turns)
entries: The flow of your spells focuses on the everlasting destruction in the passage of time. As a bonus action, you can spend up to twice your proficiency bonus in {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to gain a bonus to either your next spell attack roll or your spell save DC equal to half the number of counts spent, rounded down. This effect lasts until the end of your turn. Furthermore, whenever you deal damage with a wizard spell, you inflict 1 additional point of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Tock (Even Turns)
entries: The flow of your spells dictates a mechanical, rigid defense that cannot be easily meddled with, just as time itself. As a bonus action, you can spend up to twice your proficiency bonus in {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to gain a bonus to your AC equal to half the number of counts spent, rounded down. This bonus is reduced by 1 each time a creature hits you with an attack. Furthermore, you gain a bonus to Dexterity saving throws equal to half your Intelligence modifier, rounded down.

subclassFeature.name: Time-Guarded Memory
entries: The knowledge of time and history are intrinsically linked, as awareness of one helps determine the state of the other. You gain proficiency in the {@skill History} skill. Whenever you take or receive the {@action Help} action, the creature making the aided roll gains an additional bonus equal to the helper's proficiency bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Advanced Decompression
entries: You have furthered your means of using the time you compress, putting it through advanced uses as needed. You gain access to the options in the Time Decompression table.

entries.caption: Time Decompression
rows: Physiological Rewind
5 per Turn Rewound (maximum 15)

As an action, you unwind your body, restoring your hit points to what they were one turn before for every 5 counts of {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} spent, to a maximum of rewinding three turns for 15 counts. Once you use this option, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Re:Cast
Twice the Spell Slot's Level

You can spend {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to cast a spell you have cast previously during this combat without expending a spell slot. The cost equals twice the spell slot level you use. For example, casting {@spell magic missile|PHB|Magic Missile} at 2nd level costs 4 counts of {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.
Hasten

As a bonus action, you decompress an abundance of time onto a friendly creature within 60 feet of you, granting it the positive effects of the {@spell haste|PHB|Haste} spell until the end of its next turn.
Quick Wind

As a bonus action, you quicken the next spell you cast. A casting time of 1 minute becomes 1 action, a casting time of 10 minutes becomes 1 minute, and a casting time of 1 hour becomes 10 minutes. You cannot use ritual spellcasting with this option.

entries: Furthermore, the first time during a combat that you knock a creature {@condition Unconscious|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or kill it, you can use your reaction to absorb and compact its time, gaining a number of {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} counts equal to its proficiency bonus. This does not work on summoned creatures, such as those spawned from a Bag of Teeth.

subclassFeature.name: Indefinite Compression
entries: The act of compressing time could end catastrophically if mishandled, yet you have conquered that fear and learned the perfect means of handling such a fragile energy source indefinitely. Your {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count does not degrade below your proficiency bonus while you are out of combat.

Furthermore, during a long rest you can compress one spell into a small lightbulb, which can be crushed to cast the stored spell. The spell must be of 3rd level or lower, and any creature holding the lightbulb can use a bonus action to crush it and cast the spell. You can prepare a second lightbulb at 14th level and a third at 18th level. When you finish a long rest, the stored time in any previously prepared lightbulbs dissipates, causing them to lose their magical properties.

subclassFeature.name: Full Temporal Release
entries: There is a point where the pure, distilled disruption of time itself becomes like a bomb, and you have mastered how to weaponize it. Once per long rest, you can use your action to perform Crushbound Past.

entries.name: Crushbound Past
entries: You unleash a stream of temporal disruption from your hand like a gigantic laser in a 90-foot-long, 30-foot-wide cone in a direction of your choice. Each hostile creature in the area must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d8} force damage, suffers 4 points of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, and then suffers a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers half as much {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, rounded down.

Before unleashing this attack, you can spend up to 40 counts of {@condition Accumulated Past|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to empower it. You inflict 1 additional {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for every 2 counts spent. For every 10 counts spent, {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}'s damage die increases by one step, such as from a d4 to a d6 and then to a d8, and your spell save DC increases by 1 for this attack. After the attack, you suffer one level of exhaustion, plus one additional level for every 10 counts spent.

subclassFeature.name: Marksman Otherworldly Patron
entries: A warlock who makes a pact with the Marksman is ready to put their life on the line for one simple thing: power, even if they must ultimately pay the final cost.

The Marksman is a deity focused on hunting its targets with ever-perfected precision, infusing a fraction of its ability into magic bullets given to its warlocks, usually in exchange for their lives after a certain number of bullets have been used. The Marksman is usually found in a setting as a serious and cold patron, murmured about through the back alleys of large cities where a person goes missing every other day.

subclassFeature.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Marksman lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

entries.caption: Marksman Expanded Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell compelled duel|PHB|Compelled Duel}, {@spell hunter's mark|PHB|Hunter's Mark}
2nd
{@spell cordon of arrows|PHB|Cordon Of Arrows}, {@spell magic weapon|PHB|Magic Weapon}
3rd
{@spell lightning arrow|PHB|Lightning Arrow}, {@spell sending|PHB|Sending}
4th
{@spell locate creature|PHB|Locate Creature}, {@spell phantasmal killer|PHB|Phantasmal Killer}
5th
{@spell conjure volley|PHB|Conjure Volley}, {@spell steel wind strike|XGE|Steel Wind Strike}

subclassFeature.name: Marksman's Smoking Pipe
entries: Your patron has granted you a replica of one of its prized possessions, a smoking pipe from which you can inhale to sharpen your senses greatly. If this magical item ceases to be in contact with you, it teleports to your hand or the nearest available space, such as inside a backpack you are wearing. As a bonus action, you can take a drag from the pipe, gaining {@dice 1d4} + half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, in {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

While out of combat, the smoke aids you in sharpening your senses, granting a bonus to {@skill Perception}, {@skill Investigation}, and one skill of your choice with which you are proficient, chosen when you gain this feature. The bonus equals half your current {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, rounded down, to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus. You choose when to add this bonus, and all {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on you is removed after a successful roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, and regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Bullets
entries: {@i "The vows of your contract are clear - pull the trigger and shoot to kill, for your bullet shall never miss its mark."}

As the main benefit of your pact with the Marksman, you receive a magical ranged weapon called a Marksman's Weapon that serves as the instrument of your will. You can summon or dismiss this weapon as a free action, and it takes the shape of a two-handed ranged weapon of your choice, such as a bow or rifle. It uses the statistics of a {@item longbow|PHB|Longbow}, with which you are proficient. While wielding it, you can cast {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} by expending one of your warlock spell slots.

This weapon comes loaded with a revolving chamber of seven Magic Bullets, each engraved with a number and increasingly potent magic. At the start of combat, the First Magic Bullet is always slotted. Once per turn, you can rotate the chamber to select a higher-numbered bullet, such as moving from the First to the Fourth, but you cannot move from a higher-numbered bullet to a lower-numbered one. When you cast {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Magic Bullet Fire} while a Magic Bullet is slotted, the spell gains the corresponding effect:

entries.caption: Seven Magic Bullets
rows: The 1st Magic Bullet
A creature within range takes force damage equal to your warlock level, or half as much on a successful saving throw.
The 2nd Magic Bullet
A creature that fails this saving throw is {@condition Incapacitated|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} until the end of its next turn.
The 3rd Magic Bullet

The width of the spell's line increases by 10 feet, and the line becomes 30 feet longer. A creature that fails this saving throw suffers 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and has the damage it deals reduced by half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, until the end of your next turn.
The 4th Magic Bullet
Whenever a creature that fails this saving throw takes damage before the end of its next turn, it suffers 1 count of {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.
The 5th Magic Bullet
A creature that fails this saving throw has its AC reduced by half your proficiency bonus until the end of your next turn.
The 6th Magic Bullet

All creatures within range must repeat this saving throw once for every combined 7 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count among all targets before the spell was cast. A creature that fails one of these saving throws takes {@damage 2d10} force damage and suffers 3 counts of {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} instead.
The 7th Magic Bullet

A creature that fails this saving throw takes a number of {@damage 1d10 + 1} force damage rolls and suffers a number of {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} counts equal to your warlock level. It is vulnerable to force damage for this attack and until the end of your turn. A creature automatically fails this spell's saving throw unless it expends a Legendary Resistance. You take the same damage and {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count, which cannot be reduced by any means.

entries: When you cast {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Magic Bullet Fire}, the chamber automatically rotates to the next bullet, if able. At 6th level, you can cast {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Magic Bullet Fire} at 1st level without expending a spell slot. At 14th level, you can instead cast it at 2nd level without expending a spell slot.

If you die because of the Seventh Magic Bullet and are returned to life by any means other than {@spell true resurrection|PHB|True Resurrection}, you return with 5 levels of exhaustion, which can be reduced only one level at a time by finishing a long rest.
Any expended Magic Bullets are recreated when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Close Quarters Combat
entries: Sometimes preserving a bullet might be the right shot, and you have learned that your Magic Bullets are not truly spent when not fired from your Marksman's Weapon, only unleashing a fraction of their power otherwise. You have developed your own form of close-quarters combat using your Marksman's Weapon in melee. It counts as a martial melee weapon with which you are proficient, you can use Charisma for its attack and damage rolls, and it deals {@damage 2d6} bludgeoning damage and 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit.

As a bonus action, you can prepare to empower your next hit with the Magic Bullet currently in the chamber. When you next hit, the target must make a Dexterity saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 2d4} force damage and suffers the corresponding effect from the Close Quarters Magic Bullets table. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effect unless the table says otherwise.

entries.caption: Close Quarters Magic Bullets
rows: The 1st Magic Bullet
You deal extra force damage equal to half your warlock level, rounded down, or half that amount on a successful save.
The 2nd Magic Bullet
On a failed saving throw, the target can take only one of a bonus action or a reaction on its next turn.
The 3rd Magic Bullet

On a failed saving throw, the target suffers 3 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and a penalty to its attack rolls equal to half your proficiency bonus until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it suffers only 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.
The 4th Magic Bullet
All hostile creatures within 5 feet of the target must make the same saving throw or suffer the same base effect.
The 5th Magic Bullet
On a failed saving throw, the target has its AC reduced by 2 until the end of your next turn.
The 6th Magic Bullet
This attack is repeated up to three times, once for every 3 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on the target.
The 7th Magic Bullet
This attack deals {@damage 4d8} force damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much on a successful one, but you take the same damage dealt.

entries: The effect is determined by the bullet currently in your Marksman's Weapon's chamber. You cannot benefit from the effect of a bullet that has already been fired until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Request Work
entries: The connection between a warlock and their patron is ultimately one of exchange, including a constant exchange of information. You can request aid from your patron for one of the following effects, using each effect once per short rest:

items: As an action, you cast {@spell locate object|PHB|Locate Object} or {@spell locate creature|PHB|Locate Creature} without expending a spell slot.

As a bonus action, you ask your patron to fire a bullet in your stead. Choose a space within 120 feet of you. A magical circle forms there and casts {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} at 4th level without expending a spell slot. A creature whose challenge rating is lower than twice your warlock level automatically fails the spell's saving throw. This counts as you casting the spell.

You ask your patron one question, which it answers to the best of its ability, provided you are in good standing with one another. Its knowledge may be limited, and it might refuse to respond truthfully or at all, at the DM's discretion. This question may naturally lead into a conversation if your patron desires.

entries: When communicating with your patron, it may willingly materialize as a figure of smoke from your Marksman's Smoking Pipe. It can hear and be heard by creatures within 60 feet of the pipe.

subclassFeature.name: Perfected Marksmanship
entries: Your eyes have been engraved with your patron's magic, evolving to become unerring in their coordination with your hands. When you cast {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, a creature automatically fails its saving throw unless it expends a Legendary Resistance. Furthermore, when you reach 18th level, you can always choose which Magic Bullet to fire, regardless of which one is currently in your Marksman's Weapon's chamber.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Burning Jade
entries: Monks of the Way of the Burning Jade train with a special tool called a Pyrojade, a round bracelet made from magical jade that ignites on command. Monks of this path train specifically to become immune to the magical fire this tool creates.

They are capable fighters in any situation, but especially in a pinch. Their fighting style revolves around never standing still, confusing their opponents through constant movement, and then striking with a fiery fist.

Monks of this path tend to be relaxed and friendly, even while fighting. They enjoy taking care of other people, especially if that means cooking for them. However, they also possess a burning, valiant soul that will not smolder until they see their dreams accomplished.
{@i "Thy bladed instrument poseth little threat to me, amigo. Mine virescent pyrojade shall melt it to nothingness ere it doth me harm!"}

subclassFeature.name: Virescent Pyrojade
entries: You carry two round jade bracelets made from a magical material called pyrojade. If you lose them, you can procure a new set in any city or monastery that follows your way by spending a long rest doing so. While wearing these bracelets, the first attack you hit with on each of your turns inflicts 1 stack of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. At 11th level, it inflicts 2 stacks instead. Additionally, you gain the following abilities:

items: As a bonus action, you can spend 1 ki point to heat a weapon. Until the start of your next turn, it deals fire damage instead of its normal damage type and inflicts 1 stack of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever a creature hits with it.

As an action, you can spend 3 ki points to make a grapple check against a creature within your reach. On a success, you melt one nonmagical weapon, piece of equipment, or tool of your choice that the creature is holding or wearing, destroying it.
As a bonus action, you can spend 1 ki point to ignite a flammable object you can touch that is not being worn or carried.

As a bonus action, you can spend 2 ki points to make an attack roll against a creature within your reach. On a hit, roll a number of Martial Arts dice equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down. The creature takes fire damage equal to the total and suffers a number of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks equal to the number of dice rolled.

As an action, you can spend 3 ki points to melt a section of a nonmagical wall you are touching, creating a 5-foot-diameter hole. The wall must be made from a meltable material such as stone, wood, or metal.

subclassFeature.name: Fa Jin
entries: {@i "The virescent pyrojade burneth."}

Once per turn after you hit a creature with an attack, you can either inflict 1 point of {@condition Nerve Strike|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} on the target or gain 2 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. At 11th level, you can use this ability twice per turn.
You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Featherstride Technique
entries: {@i "'Tis an emergency, hm? Do know that it shall cost thee a tad more!"}

Your training through serious and casual environments has helped you hone a diverse arsenal of skills that aid you in surviving both official tournaments and tavern brawls. You gain the following abilities:

items: If you are within 5 feet of a stationary object at least 10 feet tall, such as a lamp post or tree trunk, you can use a bonus action to swing around it and launch yourself in a 30-foot line. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failed save, it is pushed to the end of the line and takes a number of Martial Arts dice in damage equal to one for every 10 feet traveled, with a minimum of one die. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and is not moved.

If you are holding a weapon or object, you can use an action to slam it into a creature within your reach. The creature must make a Constitution saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failed save, it suffers 3 stacks of {@condition Nerve Strike|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} and takes damage equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effect. The damage increases to four rolls at 11th level and five rolls at 17th level.

When a creature attacks you while you are adjacent to a wall or vertical surface at least 5 feet tall, you can use your reaction to evade by running along the wall. You gain a bonus to your AC against that attack equal to 1 for every 10 feet of the wall's height, to a maximum of +3. If the attack misses and the attacker is within your melee reach, you can make one melee weapon attack against it as part of the same reaction. You then land in an unoccupied space behind the target, if one is available.

When you successfully deflect a ranged attack using Deflect Missiles, you burn the missile before throwing it back as part of the same reaction. If it hits, it inflicts 2 stacks of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries: You can use these abilities a total number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest. If you have no uses remaining, you can spend 2 ki points to activate one of them.

subclassFeature.name: Virescent Flame Soup
entries: {@i "Thou should have imagined that there would be a hidden dragon lurking somewhere amongst the shadows, hm?"}

Once per long rest, you can prepare a hot bowl of noodle soup. As a bonus action, you can drink it or have a willing creature within 5 feet drink it. The creature gains 4 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Until the end of its next turn, whenever it scores a Posture Critical Hit, it gains one additional bonus action, which must be used before the end of its next turn.

Alternatively, as a bonus action, you can spill the steaming soup on a creature within 5 feet. It must make a Dexterity saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failed save, it suffers 6 stacks of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, 2 stacks of {@condition Nerve Strike|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, and damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die. On a successful save, it suffers half as many stacks of each condition and takes no damage.
Once used in either way, the soup is expended and cannot be used again until you prepare another after finishing a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Blinding White Dawn
entries: {@i "Thou mayest know me as Don Quixote, Fixer of the third Section of Cinq Association East!"}

Your Pyrojades are fully energized and can create concentrated fire strong enough to melt anything it touches. As an action, choose a point you can see within 80 feet. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw against your ki save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 10d10} fire damage, suffers 8 stacks of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, and becomes {@condition Frightened||Frightened} of you until the end of its next turn. While frightened this way, it must immediately use its reaction, if available, to move as far from you as possible, provided it can see you. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers half as many {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks, with no additional effect.
Any nonmagical item, equipment, tool, or structure in the sphere is burned or melted and destroyed. The area becomes difficult terrain as the structures liquefy.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Shadow Rabbit Roguish Archetype
entries: The Heishou Pack are a group of mutant assassins and combatants, each assigned to a different branch themed after the Chinese zodiac. Those of the Mao Branch follow the way of the Rabbit, using short hops and agility to secure victory on the battlefield.

Heishou warriors carry magically infused talismans that help them perform superhuman feats while slowly changing each branch member to gain the physical powers of its animal. Members of the Mao Branch commonly grow rabbit tails and eventually lose their feet to black rabbit paws.

The Heishou are mercenaries who owe loyalty only to their lord, the latest person to hire their branch. As a member of the Mao Branch, you might be an assassin on a mission, a beast of black fur trying to escape its leash, or a combatant waiting for a new lord to lead you into battle.

subclassFeature.name: Partial Mutation Training
entries: You can help your allies accompany your speed on a hunt. As an action, you provide a speed talisman to one ally. For 1 hour, its speed increases by 10 feet, after which the talisman burns away. At 13th level, you can provide two talismans to one or two allies. Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Additionally, as a bonus action, you can jump a number of feet equal to five times your proficiency bonus without provoking opportunity attacks. You can use this ability once and only while your speed is greater than 0. You regain the expended use when you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Blinkstep
entries: When you take the {@action Dash} action as your action, your feet temporarily morph into rabbit paws, granting you 3 stacks of {@condition Strider Mao|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. As part of the same action, you can use your remaining movement and make a melee weapon attack against a target you can reach. On a hit, the target suffers 1 stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. After the attack, you can jump up to 5 feet away from the target without provoking opportunity attacks.
You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: As Written
entries: The Mao Branch knows that speed equals strength and has vowed to become the fastest. Immediately after you use Blinkstep, choose one creature you can see within your reach. If its speed is lower than yours, it suffers 1 stack of {@condition Deathrite Haste|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

Additionally, your instincts draw closer to those of a rabbit, allowing you to carve a path through the earth. You gain a burrowing speed of 30 feet, but can burrow only through nonmagical, nonsolid materials such as dirt, sand, clay, or soft earth. You leave behind a 5-foot-wide tunnel through which other creatures can crawl or use as three-quarters cover.

subclassFeature.name: Mutation [Mao]
entries: Your mutations become more lasting. You retain {@condition Strider Mao|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} points for up to 1 minute while in combat or 1 hour outside combat, after which all remaining points are lost. While you have at least 1 point of {@condition Strider Mao|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you have advantage on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) and Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) checks.

subclassFeature.name: Curse-Engraved Sword
entries: You gain proficiency with greatswords if you do not already have it, and greatswords have the Finesse property for you. Whenever you hit with a melee attack using a greatsword, you can use one of the following reactions:

entries.name: Strider Unleashed
entries: Each creature of your choice in a 15-foot line directly in front of you must make a Dexterity saving throw against a DC equal to 10 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d6} bludgeoning damage and suffers 2 stacks of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. On a successful save, it takes the damage but suffers no additional effect.

entries.name: Runic Explosion
entries: The creature you hit must make a Constitution saving throw against a DC equal to 10 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier. On a failed save, it takes {@dice 1d6} damage for each stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} it currently has. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage, rounded down.

subclassFeature.name: Moonshadow Warden Martial Archetype
entries: Moonshadow Wardens are mercenaries who use both blade and talisman to perform swift and deadly acts in the name of a lord, ruler, or boss. They roam the land with antique teachings of bladework and old rituals, taking work as protectors and hunters while forgoing cumbersome defenses in favor of overwhelming agility and force.
In worlds such as Faerun, they are higher disciples of the Heishou Pack, Mao Branch, using their knowledge to protect their brethren and carry out their lord's orders.

entries.subclassFeature: Blade Wreathed in Heavenly Authority|Fighter|PHB|Moonshadow Warden|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|3

subclassFeature.name: Blade Wreathed in Heavenly Authority
entries: During a long rest, you can apply a series of talismans to a weapon with which you are proficient, transforming it into a Weapon of Heavenly Authority. The weapon deals only half the damage rolled with it after adding all modifiers, but inflicts 1 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on every hit. While you wield it, it gains the Light property and loses the Two-Handed and Heavy properties.

Whenever you deal damage with the weapon, you gain 1 stack of {@b Tianjiu Star's Blade}, to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus. When using the weapon for two-weapon fighting, you can spend your bonus action during your Attack action to make one additional attack with it, then resume any attacks you could still make.
The {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} inflicted on a hit increases to 3 at 8th level and 4 at 14th level.

subclassFeature.name: Trained Under Moonlight
entries: You gain proficiency with calligrapher's supplies and choose one of the following options:

items: {@b Amidst Shadows.} You gain proficiency in the {@skill Stealth} skill.

{@b Under Moonlight.} You gain a cumulative +1 bonus to {@skill Perception} checks for each friendly creature within 10 feet of you, to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus. You gain the same bonus to your passive Perception, but its maximum equals twice your proficiency bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Swiftfeet Protection
entries: When a friendly creature is hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to spend any number of {@b Tianjiu Star's Blade} stacks and move up to 10 feet toward it for each stack spent. If you arrive within 5 feet of the creature, the attack targets you instead, potentially becoming a miss if its attack roll does not hit your AC. You then make a melee weapon attack against the original attacker, inflicting 2 additional {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a hit.

You gain a bonus to your AC equal to the number of {@b Tianjiu Star's Blade} stacks spent until the end of the attacking creature's turn. If you spend at least 2 stacks, your counterattack also inflicts {@condition Deathrite Haste|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} on a hit. If you spend at least 3 stacks, it also inflicts {@condition Deathrite Fissure|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

subclassFeature.name: Over the Moon
entries: When you take the {@action Dash} action, you gain 3 stacks of {@condition Strider Mao|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. During that action, you can jump in a straight line up to your speed and make a melee weapon attack against a creature along the distance traveled. Opportunity attacks made against you during this movement have disadvantage. On a hit, the target suffers 3 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, and this attack does not reduce its {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} value if it triggers the condition.

If you would hit a wall during the jump, you can use your bonus action to press against it and gain 20 additional feet of movement until you touch the ground, allowing you to wall-jump. You have advantage on any Athletics check required by this feature.
Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you finish a short rest.

subclassFeature.name: Sleeping Beasts Rise
entries: During a short or long rest, you can grant yourself and a number of friendly creatures equal to your proficiency bonus a Talisman of Haste, which becomes inert when you next finish a short or long rest. A wearer adds 10 feet to the length of its jumps and adds your proficiency bonus to its Athletics and Acrobatics checks. When a wearer rolls initiative, the talisman activates and grants a bonus to the roll equal to your proficiency bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Traceless to Sight and Sound Alike
entries: At the start of your first turn in combat, or when you hit a creature using your Swiftfeet Protection reaction, you can make a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check contested by each hostile creature's passive Perception. When you take the Attack action while hidden, you are not revealed and do not trigger {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}'s extra damage until the last attack that hits during your turn. Each earlier attack that would have triggered {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead inflicts 1 additional stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Midnight Storm
entries: Once per long rest, you can use your action to perform Midnight Storm. Make every attack you could make with the Attack action against one creature, then make one additional weapon attack against it for each {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stack it has. These attacks do not trigger {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}; each hit instead removes 1 stack, pushes the target 5 feet directly away from you, and moves you the same distance to remain within 5 feet of it. If one of these attacks hits, you have advantage on your next attack roll during the turn.
You can also use Midnight Storm in place of the attack made as part of Over the Moon. Once you use Midnight Storm, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Grudgekeeper Otherworldly Patron
entries: {@i "...I don't care that we failed. It's my failure, not the Middle's. And the Middle always pays its debts."}
The Grievance is a living concept represented by groups united as a family, not necessarily through blood, but through kindred ideals and care for one another.

Warlocks who follow the Grudgekeeper personally rectify everyone who has wronged their kin or ideals, granted power by their betters or a great deity to act in their stead. Such a warlock will stop at nothing to aid their siblings, carrying a heavy bound tome that empowers their every movement, granting them magic instead of ink and the force to do what they must.

The Grudgekeeper takes many forms across different worlds, from a far-reaching cult acting as brigands and gangsters to the servants of a grand war-profiteer whose chains spread across the land. Either way, a Grudgekeeper pays their dues and lives to cross names from their list.

subclassFeature.name: Unforgiving, Unforgetting
entries: You perfectly recall information about any creature you have perceived bad-mouthing, obstructing, or otherwise slighting you or a friendly creature. While confronting such a creature, you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks against it and can use Charisma instead of Wisdom for those checks. Furthermore, when you make a {@skill Perception}, {@skill Investigation}, or {@skill Survival} check to track a transgressor, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.

subclassFeature.name: Tome of Grudges
entries: You carry a grand leather-bound Tome of Grudges granted by your family. It is a magic item and acts as an arcane focus for your warlock spells. You can summon or dismiss it as a free action. During a long rest, the Tome can break down and absorb another arcane focus as magical ink, destroying that item and gaining its properties. You can benefit only from the last arcane focus destroyed this way.
When a creature takes certain actions against you or your fellows, you become Offended and gain Offense Points, which can be spent in the following ways:

items: You can spend Offense Points to cast a warlock spell you know without expending a spell slot. You cannot upcast the spell, and its level cannot exceed your proficiency bonus. The cost equals the spell's level + 2 Offense Points. You can cast a spell this way a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.

As an action, you can spend 5 Offense Points to Write 'Em All Down. Choose a number of creatures within 60 feet equal to your Charisma modifier and curse them with a {@b Vendetta Mark}. Whenever you hit a marked creature while it is within 60 feet, it takes an additional {@damage 1d4} psychic damage. The number of additional d4s increases by one whenever the creature Offends you, to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus. The mark ends when you or the marked creature becomes {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}, or after four turns. A creature cannot gain another Vendetta Mark while it already has one.

When a creature within 30 feet hits you with an attack, you can spend 2 Offense Points to use the Payback With Interest reaction. Make a melee spell attack against the attacker. On a hit, it takes {@damage 1d10} force damage plus a number of d6s of psychic damage equal to the number of damage dice rolled by the original attack.

entries: You gain Offense Points when you perceive one of the following acts within 60 feet through sight or hearing:

items: {@b Aggression Offense.} You gain 2 Offense Points the first time during a turn that a hostile creature damages you.
{@b Beatdown Offense.} You gain 2 Offense Points the first time during a combat that a friendly creature falls {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious}.
{@b Grievous Offense.} You gain 5 Offense Points when you or an ally suffers a critical hit.
{@b Disrespect Offense.} You gain 2 Offense Points whenever you or an ally is forcibly moved, such as by being shoved or by the {@spell thunderwave|PHB|Thunderwave} spell.

entries: You can have a maximum number of Offense Points equal to twice your proficiency bonus. They are reduced to 0 when combat ends.

subclassFeature.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Grudgekeeper lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

entries.caption: Grudgekeeper Expanded Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell absorb elements|XGE|Absorb Elements}, {@spell ceremony|XGE|Ceremony}
2nd
{@spell gift of gab|AI|Gift of Gab}, {@spell zone of truth|PHB|Zone Of Truth}
3rd
{@spell crusader's mantle|PHB|Crusader's Mantle}, {@spell sending|PHB|Sending}
4th
{@spell locate creature|PHB|Locate Creature}, {@spell phantasmal killer|PHB|Phantasmal Killer}
5th
{@spell geas|PHB|Geas}, {@spell wrath of nature|XGE|Wrath of Nature}

subclassFeature.name: Partybringer
entries: As a bonus action, you can spend 2 Offense Points to summon a magical instrument that plays on its own, usually a spectral boombox carried over your shoulder. Each friendly creature that can hear it within 30 feet gains a {@dice 1d4} bonus to attack rolls and saving throws. Whenever one of those creatures deals damage, it deals an additional {@damage 1d4} thunder damage; you instead deal an additional {@damage 2d4} thunder damage.

At the start of each of your turns, you must spend 2 Offense Points as a free action to continue the music, or the instrument vanishes and the effect ends. At 12th level, the bonus to attack rolls and saving throws increases by 1, affected creatures deal {@damage 2d4} additional thunder damage, and you deal {@damage 3d4} additional thunder damage. At 18th level, the radius increases to 60 feet, and all thunder damage dealt through this effect is doubled against wooden, metal, and crystalline structures and objects.

subclassFeature.name: Waiting for Vengeance
entries: You begin each combat with 3 Offense Points. When an enemy Offends you, you can inflict it with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. When you target a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} with an attack, you gain a bonus to the attack roll equal to half your current Offense Points, to a maximum of +4, and deal additional psychic damage equal to your current Offense Points.

Additionally, your Grudge Points are no longer removed after combat. You can retain a maximum number equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, and they are reduced by 1 each hour. You can spend 1 Grudge Point to add +2 to a failed ability check, potentially turning it into a success as you push through to correct your grievance.

subclassFeature.name: Party Crashout
entries: Whenever a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is killed, you recover one warlock spell slot. This can occur a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, per short rest.

Whenever a creature suffers {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} for the first time, rageful duty grants you a surge of power. Whenever you deal damage, you deal an additional {@damage 3d6} psychic damage. This bonus diminishes by {@damage 1d6} at the end of each of your turns.

When a creature bearing {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} or a Vendetta Mark is knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious} for the first time in combat or killed, you can use your reaction to Boast. Up to three creatures of your choice can add your Charisma modifier to the first attack roll they make before the end of their next turn.
You gain the following additional uses for Offense Points:

items: You can spend 3 Offense Points to inflict {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} on a creature within 60 feet even if it has not Offended you.
Once per combat, you can recharge one use of a Mystic Arcanum spell by spending Offense Points equal to that spell's level + 4.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Grievance
entries: Barbarians of the Path of Grievance never forgive and never forget. They remember every slight committed against them and other members of their clan, and will go through all ordeals necessary to see the perpetrators of such crimes be thoroughly punished. They are armed solely with their fists and with magic tattoos given to them after they exact final vengeance, with the purpose of making them stronger. The more tattoos in your skin, the higher your ranking at the clan.

In the Forgotten Realms, the city of Waterdeep has grown restless with fear over a criminal group comprised of people that follow this way of life. Known as the Half, because none of their members are complete without each other, the Barbarians that stem from this family are known for being swift deliverers of vengeance over the smallest injuries and remarks raised against their own.

In the universe of Project Moon, the Middle is one of the Fingers, and, consequently, a Star of the City. They record all injustices made against their members in a book, repaying not in kind, but in cruelty, everything done against them tenfold. Members of the Middle see each other as a family, and would die for the honor of their brothers and sisters.

subclassFeature.name: Loyalty
entries: Starting on level 3, you can roll {@dice 1d6} in place of the normal damage of your Unarmed Strike, which now also count as Heavy Weapons. When you hit a creature, you can choose to make them roll a Constitution saving throw against your Tattoo save DC or be pushed back 5 feet.

During combat, the enemy that dealt the most damage to you or your allies this round gains a {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. This lasts until the end of the next round, or until you fall {@condition Unconscious}. If no enemy has dealt damage this turn, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is given to the enemy that last attempted to attack you or an allied creature. If two enemies dealt the same amount of highest damage, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} goes to the latest enemy that dealt this damage. Outside of combat, whenever someone rolls an ability check to hurt or damage your character or their reputation, they will also gain a point of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until your next short rest. If combat is initiated right after an instance of this by rolling an initiative check, then the enemy with the highest initiative roll gains {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until the end of the first round of combat. Whenever you hit an enemy with a stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, they gain 1 stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
Additionally, you gain proficiency on Painter's Supplies for the sake of carving magic tattoos on yourself and others.

subclassFeature.name: Checking the Book
entries: Every barbarian in the path of grievance carries magical tattoos that empower them in fights and allow them to deal devastating blows to their enemies and the enemies of their family. Also on level 3, you engrave two tattoos of your choice on your body, from among the tattoos described below, and each time you gain a level in this class, you can replace one tattoo you know with a different one from this feature, as they need a constant flow of magical ink, not permitting all of them to be active at once. When you reach certain levels in this class, you learn additional tattoos, as shown in the Tattoos Known table.

Whenever you finish a long rest, you can engrave one of your known tattoos onto a willing creature or reactivate one with magical ink. Your tattoo remains active on that creature until you finish a long rest, after this, the magical ink ceases to have effect unless you activate it again. Any Tattoo can be engraved and activated, as long as it is known to you. Allied creatures can count levels from any class for the sake of using your level-restricted Tattoos.

entries.caption: Barbarian Tattoos Known
rows: 3rd
6th
10th
14th

entries: The tattoos shown at the bottom of this document are available to you when you learn a tattoo. If a tattoo has a level requirement, you must be at least that level in this class to learn the tattoo. If a tattoo requires a saving throw, your Tattoo Magic save DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier.

subclassFeature.name: A Just Vengeance
entries: Your family has only empowered you further, and the more enemies you strike down, the more benefits you reap for your loyalty. Once you reach 6th level, your Unarmed Strike damage dice changes to {@dice 1d8}. Additionally, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, choose one of the two options below:

entries.name: Brush it Off.
entries: Gain temporary hit points equal to a roll of your Unarmed Strike damage dice plus your rage bonus.

entries.name: Ready to Write.
entries: Gain a +1 bonus for your attack and damage rolls for the duration of the combat against enemies with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.
Your Unarmed Strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

subclassFeature.name: Favoritism
entries: You are finally starting to ascend in the family, growing from a common runt to a person of some respect. Once you reach level 10, your Unarmed Strike damage dice changes to {@dice 1d10}. Additionally, whenever a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is killed, the creature that last attacked you or an ally this combat gains a stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

Whenever an allied creature within 30 feet of you is hit by a hostile creature, the allied creature with least HP gains a +1 bonus to their ability checks, attack rolls and saving throws until the end of their next turn, to a maximum of +3.

subclassFeature.name: Multifold Retribution
entries: The family has finally recognized your skills, and given you a position worthy of your power, which demands respect from all people. Once you reach 14th level, your Unarmed Strike damage dice changes to {@dice 1d12}. Additionally, as a reaction when a creature within 30 feet of you attempts to cast a spell, take a bonus action, a reaction, a legendary action or a mythic action, you may use your speed to run up to them without provoking opportunity attacks and perform an attack roll. If you hit, the creature's action and spell slot is spent and lost. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

Whenever you enter your Rage, a burst of purple energy flames explode from your Tattoos, covering your entire body in a menacing aura, signaling you have entered Rageful Vengeance. During Rageful Vengeance, you have all benefits from a normal Rage, with the addition of:

entries.name: Right In the Solar Plexus.
entries: As an action, which can be taken as part of your attack action when you hit a creature or an object, you get to end all magical effects currently affecting that object or creature, and if the creature is shape-shifted, it reverts to its true form. If the magical effect is of 7th-level or higher, you must roll {@dice d20} + your Con modifier against the caster's save DC, dispelling the effect on a success. If the magical effect doesn't need to be activated, and is instead constantly active, like a Monk's Timeless Body, the suppression only lasts for a minute. You can use this ability once per Rageful Vengeance.

entries.name: Watch Your Back!
entries: As part of your attack action, you can force the enemy to roll a Charisma saving throw against your Tattoo save DC. If they fail, they become surprised by your might, recognizing their inferiority, and your second attack immediately grapples the creature on a hit. You have advantage attacking a creature surprised this way. Immediately after grappling them, you may throw them on a 30 feet line in any direction. They take {@dice 1d10} bludgeoning damage for each 10 feet traveled. If they hit another creature or an object this way, they instead take double the dice in damage and what they hit takes half that damage, being pushed along with it to the end of the line if possible. All creatures that took damage this way fall {@condition Prone}. You can use this ability once per Rageful Vengeance.

entries.name: Swear Vengeance.
entries: Whenever you successfully hit a creature with all available Unarmed Attack actions in your turn, they become {@condition Panicked|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until the end of their next turn.

subclassFeature.name: College of Lifeblood
entries: Members of the College of Lifeblood decided to add a spice to their shows and parades that no other Bard would morally consider - which makes their craft more special than any other. They fearlessly draw from cruelty, violence and fear to paint the crowds in unforgettable shades of crimson. White blood and guts, they lead a march of masks, parasols and colorful dresses that change the lives of any towns and villages they visit forever.

Their parasols have a special mechanism which allows them to both draw and expel blood quickly through its end tip, which they use to sign their works and paint vibrant pictures of carnage. They always carry masks with themselves to add to the mystery of whoever is behind it, as well as to avoid the ones focused on maintaining the law.

Bards of this College want to spread joy, in their own twisted sense, throughout the realms, but they also want to be the lead as they do so - the one that vaunts always in front of the bloody promenade. The centerpiece, and the brightest jewel. Let your jealousy and the envy of others burn as you rise as the main character of life's spectacle.

subclassFeature.name: Parade's Bloodfeast
entries: The vital fluid that flows out of the creatures you pierce serves as fuel for your {@skill Performance} and the parade which it conducts. Whenever you inflict a creature with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks, an equal amount of Bloodfeast is added to your party's pool. Bloodfeast is a party-wide resource used to fuel a number of skills, and when you use it to fuel your own abilities. The party's Bloodfeast is reduced to 0 during a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Hardblood Thorn
entries: You can use a parasol as a spellcasting focus for your bard spells. This parasol is the perfect tool to easily channel blood from your enemies to you, and vice versa. You gain Blooming Thorns with your Bloodfeast, which gradually grows in power the more blood you spend. The requirements you must meet for each rank and their effects are described in the table below:

entries.caption: Blooming Thorn Ranks
rows: 3rd

If your parasol is lost or destroyed, you may recreate it during a long rest without spending materials. It is a martial weapon you are proficient with, deals {@dice 1d8} piercing damage, and can use Charisma for its attack and damage rolls.
I
3rd

Whenever you apply stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to a creature, you add twice that amount of Bloodfeast to your party's pool. Once per day, you can cast {@spell Melf's acid arrow|PHB|Melf's Acid Arrow} with your parasol without material components. Instead of dealing its additional {@dice 2d4} acid damage, it applies 2 stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. You can also spend a spell slot of 2nd level or higher to cast this version as though it were prepared.
II
6th

Your parasol deals {@dice 2d8} piercing damage. As a bonus action, you can open it to grant yourself and a creature directly behind you half cover. Whenever you are hit by a melee attack, the attacker gains 1 stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. The parasol counts as a +1 arcane focus and a +1 weapon.
III
14th

Your parasol deals {@dice 2d10} piercing damage plus {@dice 1d8} piercing damage against enemies with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Whenever you apply stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you add three times that amount of Bloodfeast to your party's pool and regain hit points equal to the Bloodfeast acquired. It counts as a +2 arcane focus and a +2 weapon. On a critical hit, you can heal yourself or a creature within the weapon's reach for up to twice the target's {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks.

subclassFeature.name: Lead of the Parade
entries: As the centerpiece, you must know how to draw attention and awe from your peers, allowing the envy and jealousy to fester in their hearts and turn that into aggressive power. You gain expertise in the {@skill Performance} skill if you didn't already have it.

As a bonus action, you can choose a creature that you can see in front of you and roll a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check against their presence DC (CR + 10). If you pass, whenever {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} is applied to them until the start of your next turn, that number +1 is applied instead. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

Additionally, whenever you hit a creature with a damaging spell or it fails a saving throw, they gain 1 stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and 1 stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: In Finely Ground Mistfall
