entries: As an action, you get to raise your parasol in front of you and spin it, releasing a sharp storm of blood crystals in a 15 foot Cone. Every creature in this Cone must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, they take {@dice 2d10} piercing damage and gains 2 stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. On a successful save, they take only half the damage and suffer no additional effects. If a creature that failed the saving throw was also the successful target of your Lead of the Parade ability, creatures attempting to hit them gains a +1 bonus to their attack and damage rolls on their first attack against them until the start of your next turn.

After a creature uses Bardic Inspiration, as a reaction, you may walk up to 15 feet and use this ability. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: The Finale
entries: You have finally become the master of the parade, rivaled by none and adored by all. Once you use your Lead of the Parade ability, you can choose up to three creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you to gain a stack of {@condition Festive Fever|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. If you choose three creatures, they will each gain a stack of {@condition Festive Fever|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}; if you choose two creatures, you can choose which one of them gains two stacks while the other gains one; if you choose one creature, they will get all three stacks.

Additionally, when a creature uses your Bardic Inspiration on their attack roll and successfully hits because of it, they inflict 2 stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Kindred Domain
entries: The weight of a pious soul is a heavy one to bear, yet Clerics who follow their Kindred will do so without complaint, weaving their own blood drawn from self-flaggelation to wash away the sins of their fellows, no matter what terrible pain they may have to endure. Kindred Domain clerics can come in a grand amount of variety, some using literal blood, sweat and tears to fuel their holy rituals, others channeling their own soil to aid others, and some even taking the pain of their fellows literally; Yet one thing connects them all, the need to bear a cross in the name of those they love. In the Forgotten Realms, most Gods who value companionship may hold the Kindred Domain, yet in particular some scant few followers of Lathander take the mantle of Kindred Clerics, attempting to hold onto their own virtue while lifting their fellow worshippers, no matter how much this vision of perfection may cost them. In other worlds such as Eberron, the Kindred Domain sometimes isn't held by those who have faith in a God, but those who have faith in themselves and who beckon the faith of others, roving warlords and those who wish for more power to their own, willing to endure such suffering to reach it.

subclassFeature.name: Priory's Bloodfeast
entries: Starting at first level, your misericordious hands have dipped into the blood of the sinful, and with them you may flagellate evil as you see necessary.

Whenever you may inflict a creature with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks, an equal amount of Bloodfeast is added to your party's pool. Bloodfeast is a party-wide resource used to fuel a number of skills, and when you use it to fuel your own abilities. The party's Bloodfeast is reduced to 0 during a long rest.
Additionally, your relationship to the purifying nature of pain has left you tougher than most. Whenever you gain a level in this class and at first level you gain an additional maximum hit point

subclassFeature.name: Bloodied Hands
entries: Also when entering this Divine Domain, the weight of sin that you must carry pools around your fingers and hardens into devastating tools of purification. You gain Bloodied Hands with your Bloodfeast, which gradually becomes fiercer the more blood you spend. The requirements you must meet for each rank and their effects are described in the table below:

entries.caption: Bloodied Hands Ranks
rows: 1st

You have a metallic holy symbol that acts as stake, if lost or destroyed you may recreate it during a long rest without spending materials. It is a martial weapon you are proficient in and it deals {@dice 1d6} piercing damage.
1st

Your Bloodied Hands seep into the symbol, forming a bloody whip to inflict salvation unto others. This weapon gains Reach and deals an additional {@dice 1d4} piercing damage to {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} creatures.
6th

The blood weeps further from between your fingers. Your weapon now deals {@dice 2d6} piercing damage plus {@dice 2d4} piercing damage to {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} creatures. When you hit a target with a melee attack while using this, you regain two hit points. Additionally, this weapon counts as a +1 Holy Symbol and a +1 Weapon.
12th

Your sinful hands will never be fully washed away from the red that coats them. Your weapon now deals an additional {@dice 3d4} piercing on {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} creatures, and has a reach of 10 feet, also healing 3 hit points on a melee hit. It counts as a +2 Holy Symbol and a +2 Weapon. On a Critical Hit with this weapon, you may heal yourself or a creature within the weapon's reach for up to two times the stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on target.

entries: This table's effects do not stack, any changes to the weapon are as described.

subclassFeature.name: Self-Destructive Dedication
entries: Finally, upon choosing this Divine Domain, you may use the righteousness behind your brutish actions to fuel you onward in flagellation. When you deal melee damage to another creature, you may choose to remove {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks from yourself and transfer them to the target. The number of stacks you may transfer is up to half your Proficiency Modifier, rounded down. In addition, you may strike your whip against your own flesh as a bonus action to steel your resolve. You suffer an amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} equal to your Proficiency Modifier, and gain the same value as a bonus modifier to Wisdom Saving Throws for as long as you are {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding}. You may use this feature an amount of times equal to your Wisdom Modifier.
In your dedication, you may also spend the blood spilt by your hands to fuel Bloodarts, horrifying works of hemomancy. They are as follow:

items: Once at the start of your turn you may spend 2 Bloodfeast as a free action to heal yourself by {@dice 1d8} hit points. You may spend additional 2 Bloodfeast to heal additional {@dice 1d8} hit points, to a maximum amount of die healed equal to your Proficiency Modifier.

As a bonus action you may ready an attack empowered by your hunger, by doing so and spending 2 Bloodfeast you may give yourself advantage on your next attack against a creature suffering {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. This creature suffers an additional amount of your weapon's damage type equal to the amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks they are currently suffering.

You may spend 3 Bloodfeast and an action to channel a vicious rage, causing you to scream and attempt to goad others into committing sins you can punish. When you do so, all creatures within 15-ft of you must pass a Charisma Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC or be goaded. A goaded creature has a bloody rage also overtakes their senses, be more inclined to target you as the source of their rage until the end of their next turn. Goaded creatures gain advantage to hit you and disadvantage to hit other creatures. Creatures immune to being {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened} succeed in this Saving Throw instantly.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Sacrifice for the Family
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to raise your Holy Symbol high above your head and call upon the necessary sacrifices of your fellows for a grander good. As an action, you may send a wave of blood crashing down a 30 foot radius around you. All creatures within reach must pass a Constitution Saving Throw or have the blood leave gashes down their bodies, causing them to suffer half your Proficiency Modifier (Rounded Down) of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and the same value of slashing damage. If a creature fails this Saving Throw while having less than half their hit points, they suffer an additional stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} as their already present wounds are made much worse. On a Success, the creature only takes half damage. All the Bloodfeast gathered by this feature is raised into a bloody sphere flying above your head, which grants you and any other Bloodfeast consuming creatures within 15-ft of you a +1 bonus modifier to hit equal to each 5 Bloodfeast gathered, as the current yield of your sacrifice only makes your thirst more pronounced. This bonus can only reach up to a +3 and is reduced by one at the end of the round in initiative, the ball of blood dissolving when this bonus modifier becomes 0.

subclassFeature.name: Rituals of an Ailing Heart
entries: Through your clergy you've learned how to practice certain rites to absolve your fellow sinners of the corrosion that plagues their souls, even if you suffer for it. Starting at 6th level, as a bonus action on your turn you may spend 4 Bloodfeast to perform any of the following Ailing Rites:

items: {@b It's Going to be Okay.} You offer enchanted words of encouragement and kindness while ignoring how hollow they ring inside your own ears. When you do so, you instantly end the {@condition Charmed}, {@condition Frightened}, {@condition Poisoned}, {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Panicked|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} conditions that another creature within 30-ft of you may be suffering, yet their haunting thoughts become your own during this unassuming ritual. After you do so, you must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw against your own Spell Save DC or suffer {@dice 2d4} Psychic damage and be afflicted with the Conditions removed until the end of your next turn. You may also use this feature to change the targets of psychic-damage inducing spells such as {@spell phantasmal killer|PHB|Phantasmal Killer} to be yourself, ending their effect from the initial target and attempting to pass the same Wisdom Saving Throw or becoming the new target of the spell's effect. If a spell is transferred this way, its duration is not reset.

{@b Endure Further.} With a piercing touch to a willing creature within 5-ft, you sink your own blood into their body along a string of words to have them keep enduring the pains of battle. For up to one minute you maintain Concentration on the following effect: Your ailing mind slowly erodes from an overwhelming anxiety seeping in their blood, causing you to suffer your Proficiency Modifier as an amount of {@dice d6} die of psychic damage at the start of their turns, but granting them a bonus to AC for the duration equal to the amount of damage die taken, as your protection has them move involuntarily away from outside troubles.

{@b Light Concessionary.} You may listen to your kindred's sins and absolve them of such impure thoughts. During combat, you choose one willing creature within 30-ft. of yourself to start a rite of cleansing where they confess their sins to you by spending their reaction to do so. Upon spending their reaction, this creature gains half your Wisdom Modifier (Rounded Up) as a bonus to Wisdom Saving Throws for the next minute. You may use this feature once per day during a Long Rest without spending Bloodfeast as long as you perform no other heavy activity, if this feature is used in this manner you may have it target up to your Proficiency Bonus' worth of creatures and this feature's effects last until the next short rest. You may choose to hear more creatures confess than your limit, but you suffer a cumulative amount of Exhaustion for each creature above your maximum. Eg: One point of Exhaustion for the first, Two for the second, Three for the third and so on. A creature may benefit from this bonus only once per Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Kindred Domain: Ravenous Strikes
entries: You are starved with an obsessive might in battle. Starting at 8th level, when a creature takes Radiant or Piercing damage from one of your cantrips or weapon attacks, you can change its damage type to become Necrotic. Once you deal this damage you recover hit points equal to half its value, rounded down. You can't use this feature again until the start of your next turn and you may use this feature an amount of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining spent uses during a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: The Unforgivable Sin
entries: For so long you have held onto the scraps of sanity left from trying to keep everyone around you so pure, yet your disgusting desires can be pushed back no longer. When you reach 17th level you gain the following:

items: {@b All-Engulfing Hunger.} As an action you may unleash your pent up desires in a physical manner that destroys and degrades all around you, you spread an aura around 20-ft of you, taking the image of an unholy whirlpool of blood or any other gruesome description of your choice. Any creature who starts or ends their turn inside this aura has their blood shift and turn inside them, lashing out and lacerating them from the inside, having them suffer {@dice 2d4} necrotic damage and 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks. Other creatures who consume Bloodfeast are immune to this. This lasts for one minute or until you are knocked {@condition Unconscious}.

{@b Weight of the Kin.} When you would hit with any attack, you may add a number of {@dice d10} necrotic damage die for each cumulative 7 hit points you have missing, fuelled by the wish of finally having other filthy beings feel the same pain you've had to endure for so long. You may use this feature an amount of times equal to half your Wisdom Modifier, recovering uses on a long rest.

{@b A Holy Man's Breaking Point.} When you would be knocked {@condition Unconscious} or have your hit points reduced below 1, you may spend your reaction to instead cling onto your conscience by throwing away your raving concerns and inhibitions. You cannot regain hit points while in this state and it lasts for up to one minute or until another creature lands a Critical Hit on you or you are killed. Once per each creature's turn you suffer one point of Exhaustion if you take more than 20 damage during their turn. While in this state, All-Engulfing Hunger is always active and deals {@dice 3d6} necrotic damage per turn instead. Additionally, you gain one extra Action that you can use to Attack or Cast a Spell for this duration.

subclassFeature.name: Bloody Barber Specialization
entries: The work of the Bloody Barber is one that most people, the fools, struggle to grasp. Those who use of stitches and scissors to masterfully imbue life itself to the very concept of beauty are rare and few between, boasting knowledge of the arcane and sharp fashion senses, these are usually eccentric people who don't tend to band together with one another, instead wanting to have their craft flourish through their own merit.

In settings such as the Forgotten Realms, the art of the Bloody Barber has become one passed down through generation after generation, with renowned artificers taking a handful of pupils under their wing as they teach this necromantic art form. Most people might find the production method of the finest silk in the Sword Coast a reviling thing, but none can deny the quality of such fabulous clothing.

In others, such as Ravenloft, the Bloody Barber has become a nightmare inducing children's tale, one that was spread from Barovia and far into the mists, of the shady person that would abduct children of their homes and madly snap at them using their blood-red scissors, turning them into pretty little bows spread around the trees.

subclassFeature.name: Parlor's Bloodfeast
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you've found a way to harden and weave the very blood of other beings. Whenever you inflict a creature with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks, an equal amount of Bloodfeast is added to your party's pool. Bloodfeast is a party-wide resource used to fuel a number of skills, and when you use it to fuel your own skills. The party's Bloodfeast is reduced to 0 at the end of combat.

subclassFeature.name: Blood-Tinted Scissorblades
entries: Also at 3rd level, you've found a way to enhance your Weaver's Tools for devastating effect. You may create Blood-Tinted Scissorblades with your Bloodfeast, which gradually becomes stronger with the amount of blood you spend. The requirements you must meet for each rank and their effects are described in the table below:

entries.caption: Blood-Tinted Scissorblades Ranks
rows: 3rd

Your Weaver's Tools count as a martial melee weapon you are proficient with. They deal {@dice 2d4} slashing damage, can use Intelligence for attack and damage rolls, and have the Hemorrhaging (18-20) and Heavy properties.
I
3rd
Your scissorblades deal {@dice 2d4} slashing damage and have Hemorrhaging (17-20).
II
6th

Your scissorblades deal {@dice 2d6} slashing damage plus {@dice 1d6} slashing damage against targets afflicted with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. They count as a +1 weapon and a +1 spellcasting focus for artificer spells, and have Hemorrhaging (16-20).
III
12th

Your scissorblades deal {@dice 3d8} slashing damage plus {@dice 2d8} slashing damage against targets afflicted with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. They count as a +2 weapon and a +2 spellcasting focus for artificer spells. On a critical hit, the target suffers additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks equal to your proficiency bonus. They have Hemorrhaging (16-20).

subclassFeature.name: Fashionista's Supplies
entries: At third level, your ability with scissors isn't limited only to combat. You gain proficiency in Weaver's Tools or Expertise if you were already proficient with such. You also create Hardblood Accessories, small trinkets formed from blood and skill. You may do so once per turn by using your bonus action and spending three points of Bloodfeast, creating one of the following:

items: {@b Flourish of Bloodletting.} You deftly create a pendant you may attach to a weapon. When attached, it magically causes blood to coat its surface or ammunition and form jagged points that cause even more blood to pour out, the weapon gains the Hemorrhaging (18-20) property for one minute.

{@b Mistmaker Shoes.} You fabricate a pair of shoes that seem to stir with life. When equipped by a creature, it gains {@dice 2d4} temporary Hit Points. While those remain they also gain a 5-ft bonus to their movement speed.

{@b Roseate Shawl.} You weave a neck adornment with an intricate design that grants {@dice 4d8} temporary Hit Points to an equipped creature. While those remain this creature suffers a -1 penalty to their AC.

entries: When you create one of these items, you may grant them to an ally within 5-ft of you and have them equip the item instantly, additionally each ally may benefit only once per Accessory per combat, and if you attempt to give an ally two Accessories at the same time, the one created first becomes inert, providing no bonuses.

When a creature takes damage while they have Temporary Hit Points gained from this feature remaining, they are considered to have vulnerability against fire damage as it burns away the clothing, but any damage remaining after the clothing is destroyed is negated.

subclassFeature.name: Sewing Marcation
entries: Upon reaching 5th level, you've learned not only how to sew a magnificent piece of wear, but also how to implement devastating needlework to your attacks. Either when you are outside combat or at the beginning of your turns in combat, you may choose a creature within 60-ft of you to become a Sewing Target. The chosen creature loses this property at the beginning of your next turn, and Sewing Target's effects are as follows, depending if the target is hostile or friendly:
If the Sewing Target is a hostile creature:

items: When {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} is inflicted on this creature, they take damage equal to your half your Proficiency Modifier, rounded down.
Any {@skill Medicine} checks against this creature to remove {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} are made with disadvantage.

You may spend a use of your Flash of Genius as a Flash of Indignance instead, giving your next attack roll against the target advantage and dealing {@dice 1d4} additional damage of your weapon's damage type per each stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the Sewing Target. (To a maximum amount of {@dice d4} equal to your Intelligence modifier.)

entries: If the Sewing Target is a friendly creature:

items: You may spend an action and a use of your Flash of a use Genius as a Flash of Fabulosity instead, granting this friendly creature within 15-ft. of you an additional amount of hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus worth of {@dice d4}, which count towards the durability of a gifted Hardblood Accessory.

Your magnificent craftsmanship and overview not only gives the creature a stunning look, but also a confidence to exude an air of elegance. This creature has a bonus to their Charisma checks and Saving Throws equal to your Proficiency Bonus as long as they are within 120-ft of you and are wearing one of your Hardblood Accessories or another article of clothing produced by you.

entries: Designer's Note. You gain the ability to use the abilities which refer to Flash of Genius beginning at 7th level, where you would gain it. Before that, you can use this ability once per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Corteous Dress Making
entries: Upon reaching 15th level, you've created and recreated many pieces of wear, but now you've outdone yourself in a way that would leave even the dullest fashion sense in awe. Over the course of a long rest, you may create a Fashion Masterpiece, which counts as light armor that you are proficient with. When you create your Fashion Masterpiece, you may choose to give it up to three of the following traits:

items: {@b Blooming Rose Adornment.} You may spend 5 Bloodfeast to cause floral and thorn-like adornments of your clothing to magically lash out at creatures within 5-ft of you as a reaction to when you take damage. All creatures around must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer {@dice 4d10} slashing damage and be pushed back 5-ft, or take half the damage on a success.

{@b Reinforced Fabrics.} You may spend 3 Bloodfeast and a bonus action during your turn to soak your clothing in blood, making it more resilient. You gain +1 AC until the end of combat or when you are knocked {@condition Unconscious}. You may benefit from this up to three times per combat.

{@b Light Weaving.} You may spend up to 5 Bloodfeast at the start of your turn to make your clothes much lighter, gaining an additional 5-ft of movement per 1 Bloodfeast spent. You retain that bonus until the end of your turn.
{@b Fit for a Parade.} You may spend 4 Bloodfeast to restore your own blood, you may instantly spend two of your Hit Die and be healed for that amount.

{@b Jagged Shoulderblades.} You may spend 1 Bloodfeast before an attack to inflict an additional stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a hit as blood seeps into your gloves and aids your movements.

{@b Protective Padding.} You may spend 5 Bloodfeast as a reaction after you take damage to gain resistance against that damage type for the next three turns. If you use this feature while still benefiting from it, you lose the old benefits and gain the new, as your clothing can only reactively change its design to protect you when using its full focus. You cannot gain resistance against fire damage.

entries: You may only have one Fashion Masterpiece at any given time, if you attempt to create a new one while another already exists, you start seeing the failures in your old work, tearing it to pieces before being able to create again. You may choose to swap one of the Masterpiece's traits during a long rest, and it counts as a magical item which you must be attuned to, and you are automatically attuned to it when you create.

subclassFeature.name: Waxen Wings Font of Magic
entries: {@i Pain has given me pain, but I will now bring pain. I have had enough. Pain.}

subclassFeature.name: Volatile Manifestation
entries: There is a fire nestled deep within your soul, one that is let out when your emotions are flowing freely. As a bonus action, you can enter a Volatile State. It usually manifests as a blade and shield that reflect your personality and identity, but it can instead take the form of mystical appendages appearing from or around your body, such as wings. The state lasts for 1 minute. When you enter it, choose an Offensive Stance or Defensive Stance.

entries.name: Offensive Stance
entries: You produce a flame-wreathed weapon of your choice. Whenever you deal damage with a spell attack, add fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

items: {@b Sunset Blade.} When you cast {@spell Fleeting Emberblade|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you can expend a spell slot to empower it, applying 2 additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts per level of the slot. If the slot is 2nd level or higher, the spell's reach increases by 5 feet for every 2 levels of the slot (10 feet with a 2nd-level slot, 15 feet with a 4th-level slot, and 20 feet with a 6th-level slot). At 6th level, if the cantrip has already hit during this turn, you can make one additional spell attack as part of the casting; that attack applies half the additional Burn counts. You can make one more additional attack this way at 14th level.

{@b Make the Future.} As an action, you can expend a spell slot and move up to 15 feet in a line toward the nearest unoccupied space. Each creature in your path must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking {@damage 2d8} fire damage and suffering 3 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts per level of the slot on a failure.

{@b Rising Stigma.} As an action, you can expend a spell slot of up to 3rd level to gain a +2 bonus to AC for each level of the slot. This bonus lasts until the start of your next turn. For the same duration, you have advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist being moved or grappled. You then enter Defensive Stance.

entries.name: Defensive Stance
entries: You wrap magic around yourself like a cloak or shield. You gain a bonus to AC equal to your Charisma modifier, but your speed is halved.

items: {@b Brief Respite.} As a bonus action, you can expend a spell slot to summon translucent wings and move up to 15 feet directly backward without provoking opportunity attacks. The distance increases by 15 feet per slot level above 1st, to a maximum of 45 feet. If the slot is 3rd level or higher, a burst of flame fills the space you left. Each creature within 5 feet of that space must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts per slot level above 2nd.

{@b Face the Fear.} When you take damage, you can use your reaction and expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher to reduce the damage by half your proficiency bonus, rounded down. If you expend a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you also gain resistance to all damage except force and psychic damage until the start of your next turn.

{@b Razing Wing.} As an action, each hostile creature within 5 feet of you must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, a creature is pushed 15 feet away and suffers 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts. You can expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher to apply 2 additional Burn counts on a failed save, or half as many on a successful one. You then enter Offensive Stance.

entries: At the end of each of your turns in Volatile State, if you have not damaged a creature, affected a creature with one of your spells, hit with an attack, or taken a critical hit during that turn, the state wavers. Make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to 10 + your Charisma modifier + the number of times you have succeeded on this save during the current combat. On a failure, you take a number of d6s of psychic damage equal to the turns you have spent in Volatile State, and the state ends. The state also ends if you become unconscious or end it as a free action.

You learn the {@spell Fleeting Emberblade|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} cantrip. It does not count against your cantrips known. Once you enter Volatile State, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Volatile Passion
entries: At the end of each of your turns in Volatile State, you gain 1 Volatile Passion count. While you have Volatile Passion, you gain a bonus to attack rolls against creatures with Burn equal to half your Volatile Passion count, rounded down (minimum +1). When you hit such a creature, you also apply a number of Burn counts equal to this bonus.

If you have 3 or more Volatile Passion and apply {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} to a creature, each other hostile creature within 5 feet of it suffers half as many Burn counts, rounded down.

When your Volatile State ends without you ending it as a free action, you take {@damage 1d10} psychic damage per Volatile Passion count. If you had 3 or more counts, you can use your reaction when the state would end to extend it for 1 minute. You lose all Volatile Passion counts, still take the damage, and gain 1 level of exhaustion at the end of combat each time you extend the state this way.
While you are outside Volatile State, your Volatile Passion count is reduced by 1 at the end of each of your turns.

subclassFeature.name: Tempered Passion
entries: You can now gain 1 Volatile Passion count once per turn when you hit a target or successfully block an attack. You can expend Volatile Passion together with a spell slot of 5th level or higher to use the following abilities.

entries.name: Combusting Courage.
entries: You cast {@spell Fleeting Emberblade|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} and can expend up to 5 Volatile Passion counts to transform it into a hellish slash. The slash fills a 30-foot cone, increasing by 5 feet for every 2 counts expended. Make one spell attack roll and compare it with the AC of every target in the cone. On a hit, a target takes {@damage 8d8} fire damage plus {@damage 2d8} fire damage per count expended. Until the end of your next turn, targets with fire resistance lose it and targets with fire immunity instead have resistance.

entries.name: Waned Eventide.
entries: When a creature attacks you, after the attack misses or rolls damage, you can use your reaction and expend 1 Volatile Passion count to move 5 feet backward. The attacker is forced to move with you and suffers 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts. Until the start of your next turn, you can repeat this movement whenever another creature attacks you by expending another count.

entries.name: Cooling Heart.
entries: You regain {@dice 4d8} + your Charisma modifier hit points, plus {@dice 1d8} per Volatile Passion count expended. You can expend a number of counts up to your proficiency bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Culmination of a Fluttering Ego
entries: Your journey has reached a turning point. You will either be consumed by your own flame in self-destructive rage or embrace it as a controlled part of yourself. Choose Melting Pinion or Searing Wings, as you and your DM agree best fits your character development.

subclassFeature.name: Melting Pinion
entries: Your turbulent emotions eat at you whenever you use your power, but you keep clinging to your life and desires. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Passive Effect
entries: While you are in Volatile State, when you take psychic damage, you can use your reaction to scream. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, taking thunder damage equal to the psychic damage rolled on a failure, or half as much on a success.

entries.name: Wound of Sorrow.
entries: You can expend a spell slot of 7th level or higher to fire a blazing beam in a 120-foot-long, 10-foot-wide line. Each hostile creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking {@damage 10d8} fire damage and suffering 10 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts on a failure, or half as much damage and half as many counts on a success. You can expend up to 3 Volatile Passion counts to deal an additional {@damage 2d10} fire damage per count. Before firing, you can gain up to 5 Volatile Passion counts, taking {@damage 2d6} psychic damage per count gained. Before a creature that failed its save takes the damage, it loses fire resistance for 1 minute, or fire immunity becomes fire resistance for 1 minute.

entries.name: Defensive Stance
Supraheat.
entries: When you take damage, you can use your reaction to make the attack a critical hit against you. This damage cannot reduce you below 1 hit point. You then gain a pool equal to the damage taken, which you can spend until the end of combat to regain spell slots according to the Supraheat Spell Conversion table.

entries.caption: Supraheat Spell Conversion
rows: 1st-level spell slot
2nd-level spell slot
3rd-level spell slot
4th-level spell slot
5th-level spell slot
6th-level spell slot
7th-level spell slot
8th-level spell slot
9th-level spell slot

entries: You can use Supraheat a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Searing Wings
entries: When you enter Volatile State, you instead enter Balanced State. Both Offensive Stance and Defensive Stance are active at the same time, and you do not suffer the harmful effects of Volatile State.
Your fire damage ignores resistance and immunity to fire damage.

subclassFeature.name: Heartburn Martial Archetype
entries: Fighters who understand that a wildfire is not composed of one flame have forged their bodies into weapons of all-out war. Their fists bring the heat into battle as they sweep into the fray and extinguish enemies in their path.

subclassFeature.name: Kindling for the Mind
entries: A steady mind is as important as a strong body. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Athletics, Acrobatics, History, Investigation, or Survival.

subclassFeature.name: Inner Ardor

entries.name: Precise Ignition.
entries: When you make a melee weapon attack, you inflict 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count, plus 1 additional count if the unmodified attack roll is 15 or higher.

entries.name: Ardent Techniques.
entries: You learn three Ardent Techniques from the Novice Ardent Techniques table. You learn one additional technique at 7th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level. Whenever you gain a fighter level, you can replace one technique you know with another technique available to you.

You gain 1 Ardor Point whenever you hit a creature or succeed on an ability check. Your Ardent Technique save DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (chosen when you gain this subclass). You lose 1 Ardor Point for every minute in which you do not spend any Ardor Points.

entries.caption: Novice Ardent Techniques
rows: Red Kick
Attack

Make an unarmed melee attack against a creature within 5 feet. On a hit, it takes {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage plus fire damage equal to its {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count, and it suffers additional Burn counts equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.
Single Point Stab
Attack

Make an unarmed melee attack against a creature within 5 feet. On a hit, it takes {@damage 2d4} piercing damage and has disadvantage on concentration checks until the end of your next turn. The next time before then that it makes a Constitution, Intelligence, or Wisdom saving throw, its current {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} damage triggers. This can trigger once per turn.
Stalwart Stance
Bonus Action
Varies

Spend Ardor Points equal to your proficiency bonus. Until the start of your next turn, whenever a creature hits you with a melee attack, it suffers {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts equal to the points spent. You also gain a bonus to Constitution saving throws equal to half the points spent, rounded down, until the start of your next turn (or for 1 minute outside combat).
Passionate Cheer
Bonus Action
Choose up to a number of creatures within 120 feet equal to your proficiency bonus. Until the end of your next turn, each gains a {@dice 1d4} bonus to attack rolls and ability checks.
Burning Knifehand
Free Action

Your next attack has advantage if its target has 6 or more {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts and deals additional slashing damage equal to a number of d8s equal to half the target's Burn count. An unattended object or structure instead takes {@damage 6d8} fire damage and suffers 6 Burn counts.
Flaming Fists
Free Action
Until the end of your turn, your melee attacks inflict additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.
Warm Up
Reaction
When you make a saving throw or would suffer the charmed, frightened, or poisoned condition, gain a bonus to the saving throw equal to your proficiency bonus.
Flame Counter
Reaction

When you or a friendly creature within 5 feet is hit by a melee weapon attack, after damage is rolled, make a melee weapon attack against the attacker. On a hit, it suffers 1 additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count. This attack cannot be a critical hit.

entries: You are proficient with attacks made as part of Ardent Techniques. You gain access to the Advanced list at 7th level and the Master list at 15th level. A technique with an activation time of Attack can replace one attack made as part of your Attack action or an opportunity attack.

subclassFeature.name: Party Rapport Style
entries: Choose one of the following styles, which reflects how you support your companions in battle.

items: {@b Walls of Fire.} As a bonus action, choose up to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) hostile creatures within 60 feet. Each must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Ardent Technique save DC. On a failure, it must use all available movement to approach you and focus its attacks on you. A creature engaged with another creature has advantage on the save. While you are more than 20 feet from every friendly creature, you gain +1 AC for each hostile creature within 5 feet of you, to a maximum of +3.

{@b Great Mountain.} When a creature within 5 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by {@dice 2d8}, plus {@dice 1d8} for every 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts on the attacker, to a maximum of {@dice 3d8} additional reduction. The base reduction increases by {@dice 1d8} at 12th level and again at 18th level.

{@b Level-Headed Emotion.} Once per turn as a free action, choose a friendly creature within 60 feet. It gains a bonus equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to its next ability check, attack roll, or saving throw. You can expend your Second Wind when you grant this bonus to make it last until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Flame
entries: You gain access to the following Advanced Ardent Techniques.

entries.caption: Advanced Ardent Techniques
rows: Flowing Flame
Free Action
When your next attack hits, it inflicts 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count. Your following attack has advantage and inflicts twice its normal Burn counts.
Flame Cleave
Attack

Choose up to three targets in your reach, each within 5 feet of another target. Make one melee attack and damage roll and compare the attack with each target's AC. The attack gains +1 to hit and damage for every 3 total {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts among the targets.
Rush Down
Bonus Action
Move up to 15 feet toward a creature, then make two unarmed strikes against it without adding your ability modifier to the damage.
Gale Kick
Reaction

When a creature within 60 feet misses you with an attack, make a melee attack against it regardless of distance. On a hit, it suffers 4 additional {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts.

subclassFeature.name: Fire Tempered in Moonlight
entries: You gain resistance to psychic damage and proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

subclassFeature.name: Perfect Warfare
entries: You gain access to the following Master Ardent Techniques.

entries.caption: Master Ardent Techniques
rows: Perfected Death Fist
Action

Make a melee attack. On a hit, it deals an additional {@damage 2d10} fire damage plus {@damage 1d8} fire damage per {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count on the target. Each other creature within 5 feet of the target must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Ardent Technique save DC, taking the same fire damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.
Pinpoint Blitz
Action

Make four melee attacks against one creature. Each hit inflicts one more {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count than the previous hit. If the target has more than 5 Burn counts, these attacks gain +2 to hit and deal 2 additional fire damage per Burn count. If the first three attacks hit and are not resisted, the fourth gains +3 to hit instead and deals 4 additional fire damage per Burn count; on a hit, the target then loses all Burn counts.
Inner Gate Elbow Strike
Action

Make a melee attack. On a hit, it deals an additional {@damage 2d10} bludgeoning damage, plus {@damage 2d10} fire damage if the target has more than 5 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts. The target must make a Constitution saving throw against your Ardent Technique save DC. On a failure, it takes a penalty to attack rolls and saving throws equal to its Burn count until the end of its next turn. A creature without a nervous system or unable to feel pain is immune to this effect.
Perfect Palm Strike
Attack

Replace one attack of your Attack action with a melee attack that deals an additional {@damage 2d12} fire damage on a hit. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Ardent Technique save DC. Its AC is reduced by 2, plus 1 for every 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts it has (maximum reduction 6), or by half that amount on a success. Magical armor and natural armor recover after 3 of the creature's turns.
Cerulean Blaze Spread
Bonus Action
Choose a friendly creature within 10 feet. Until the end of your next turn, it gains your resistance to psychic damage and proficiency in Wisdom saving throws from Fire Tempered in Moonlight.

entries: Once per short or long rest, you can use one Ardent Technique without spending its minimum Ardor Point cost.

subclassFeature.name: Iron Lotus
entries: Once per long rest, when you or a friendly creature is knocked unconscious, you can use your reaction to enter Iron Lotus. The state lasts until you are knocked unconscious and grants the following effects:

items: If you have 0 hit points, you regain 1 hit point. You then gain temporary hit points equal to your current hit points.
You suffer 10 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts. These counts are removed only when you are knocked unconscious or when a friendly creature you can see dies.
Your attacks inflict 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} counts and deal an additional {@damage 1d10} fire damage against creatures suffering from Burn.
Your Ardent Techniques cost half as many Ardor Points, rounded up.
A hostile creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of you suffers 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count.

Whenever a friendly creature within 30 feet is knocked unconscious, you gain a cumulative +1 bonus to attack rolls and saving throws and temporary hit points equal to half that creature's hit point maximum.
You have advantage on rolls against effects that would make you charmed, frightened, paralyzed, restrained, or stunned.

condition.name: Butterfly
entries: {@i "Long ago, people believed that they would become beautiful beings with small wings when they died."}

A creature suffering from Butterfly is suffering two-fold, having a deep-seated lament cocoon around their heart and a grief for the departed flutter out as a pain that can hardly be avoided. For the sake of ease, the Butterfly Condition is also spread in two parts, starting out as Butterfly [The Living] when first applied to a creature and then turning into Butterfly [The Departed] at the end of the afflicted's turn.

entries.name: [ The Living ]
entries: Overflowing with lament for those yet to perish, a creature suffering from this Condition suffers an equal amount of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count as it's current Butterfly [The Living] at the end of their turns, then turning any remaining Butterfly [The Living] into Butterfly [The Departed]. {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} gained at the end of a creature's turn this way is applied after being halved as usual.

entries.name: [ The Departed ]
entries: With grief unto death, any attack that inflicts Butterfly against the creatures deals an additional amount of psychic damage equal to half it's current Butterfly [The Departed]. count, to a maximum value equal to the attacker's proficiency bonus. Butterfly [The Departed]. count becomes 0 at the end of the afflicted's turn.

items: You have disadvantage on {@skill Perception} checks, Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws and ranged attacks.
As a bonus action, you can yell at one of your allies to do better, granting them advantage on their next ability check, saving throw or attack roll, your choice

When you hit a creature that is {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning}, {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Tremoring}, or Both, you deal an additional {@damage 1d6} die of damage of equal damage to your weapon's damage type
You can substitute one of your attacks for a Sezionatura di Cervo.

condition.name: Escalating Duel
entries: The rush of an Escalating Duel is that of a hunt going through its crescendo, building up for a magnificent climax. You gain the following effects according to your current count:

items: {@b 1 Escalating Duel.} You deal an additional 1 damage on melee weapon attacks.

{@b 2 Escalating Duel.} You gain a +1 bonus modifier to hit and deal an additional 2 damage on melee weapon attacks. Additionally, you inflict your choice of a {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on hit.
{@b 3+ Escalating Duel.} You gain a +2 bonus modifier to hit and deal an additional 3 damage on melee weapon attacks.

entries: Additionally, you inflict 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on hit and may choose to trigger {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the first melee weapon attack you hit during your turn.

condition.name: Eye of Precognition
entries: You have 15 counts of Eye of Precognition. While you have counts of this, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet

When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

entries: Whenever you hit with an attack, you lose 1 count of Eye of Precognition. Likewise, you lose 3 counts whenever a creature misses an attack against you due to your AC bonus, and 5 counts whenever you take no damage after succeeding on a Dexterity saving throw.
Once you lose all counts of Eye of Precognition, you immediately gain 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

After completing a Long Rest, you immediately lose all counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} and gain up to 15 counts of Eye of Precognition, ensuring you have that maximum count of the Condition.

condition.name: Eye of Precognition - Overheat
entries: While you have counts of this, you gain the following characteristics:

items: You always roll an additional damage die of the weapon you are attacking with
Whenever taking Fire damage, take an additional damage die of the same value as your eye socket burns.

entries: Whenever you hit with an attack, you lose 1 count of Eye of Precognition - Overheat. Likewise, you lose 3 counts whenever a creature hits an attack against you due to your AC decrease, and 3 counts whenever you take additional Fire damage from a hostile source. Once you lose all counts of Eye of Precognition - Overheat, you immediately gain 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

After completing a Long Rest, you immediately lose all counts of Eye of Precognition - Overheat and gain up to 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, ensuring you have that maximum count of the Condition.

condition.name: Game Target
entries: You may choose to make the last creature you attacked on your turn become your Game Target.

When you hit your Game Target with an attack roll, once per turn, you may choose to convert all of their counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} into {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Tremor Scorch}. Furthermore, whenever you apply counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, to your Game Target, they suffer 1 additional count of each applied.

condition.name: Insight
entries: While you have Insight you gain a bonus modifier to unarmed attacks and Intelligence skill checks equal to half of your current count of the Condition. Additionally, you gain a bonus modifier to your Intelligence saving throws and skill checks equal to your current count. You may have a maximum count of the Condition equal to your proficiency bonus.

If you spend Ki to perform an ability that requires you to have a minimum amount of Insight, you lose one count at the end of your turns. Otherwise, your count is reduced by one per minute spent outside of combat.

condition.name: Severed Tendons
entries: A creature suffering from Severed Tendons has had their movement options sliced clean through, reducing their movement speed by 5-ft. per count of the Condition. Furthermore, this debilitation hinders them further the worse it gets, having the creature suffer a cumulative negative modifier to Dexterity skill checks and saving throws for each 2 count.

One count is removed per hour spent without gaining more count or upon recovering any amount of Hit Points. All counts are removed upon being the target of the Restoration or {@spell Greater Restoration} spells.

condition.name: Vengeance Mark
entries: During combat, the enemy that dealt the most damage to you or your allies this round gains a Vengeance Mark. This lasts until the end of the next round, or until you fall {@condition unconscious}. If no enemy has dealt damage this turn, the stack of Vengeance Mark is given to the enemy that last attempted to attack you or an allied creature. If two enemies dealt the same amount of highest damage, the stack of Vengeance Mark goes to the latest enemy that dealt this damage. Outside of combat, whenever someone rolls an ability check to hurt or damage your character or their reputation, they will also gain a point of Vengeance Mark until your next short rest. If combat is initiated right after an instance of this by rolling an initiative check, then the enemy with the highest initiative roll gains Vengeance Mark until the end of the first round of combat.

condition.name: Rhythm
entries: A creature with this Condition has been enraptured by the god-rending melody of your carnage, and can't help but want to partake in it as musician and instrument, dealing and suffering an additional amount of damage equal to your Charisma modifier whenever they deal or suffer damage ( respectively ) equal to your 3 times your Rhythm count that they currently have. Whenever a creature declines receiving Rhythm, they halve the counts of the Condition they currently have, rounded up. Additionally, if a creature with this Condition benefits from your Bardic Inspiration rolls the minimum value rolled is always equal to their current Rhythm count, being increased if it was lower.

A creature with Rhythm gain an additional count whenever they first kill a creature during a round, except for summoned creatures. Additionally, a creature with 3 or more count may spend one count to perform an additional weapon attack or cast an additional spell of 3rd level or lower during their turn.

condition.name: Corpus Ingredients
entries: You, however, do not limit yourself to using your own body as material, also acquiring one Corpus Ingredients count whenever you successfully deal damage to a creature within 15-ft. of you. You have a count limit equal to double your proficiency bonus, and due to a tendency to dutifully spend any leftovers on smaller projects during a short or long rest, you may only have up to your proficiency bonus worth of Corpus Ingredients after such.

condition.name: Nails
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Nails} has a number of them embedded in their flesh, drawing out blood and the faith of certain individuals in equal measure. At the end of their turns, a Nailed creature halves their {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Nail} count and gains the same value halved as {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count instead.

{@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Fanatical} creatures gain a +1 bonus modifier to attack rolls against Nailed creatures for each 15 {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Nails} they are currently suffering from, to a maximum of +3.

condition.name: Immolation
entries: A creature beset by {@condition Immolation|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is suffering from the holiest of flames, taking an amount of {@dice d4} radiant damage equal to their current {@condition Immolation|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count at the end of their turns, also halving its total count. When at one {@condition Immolation|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count, it extinguishes at the end of the creature's turn.

condition.name: Haste
entries: A creature that is going through {@condition Haste|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has a spring to their step, pushing themselves to move faster or are being carried through magical effects to become nimble as the breeze.

This creature gains 5-ft. of additional walking speed and, if already available flying speed for each {@condition Haste|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count they are benefitting from, to a maximum value of 5 times their proficiency bonus plus 5. All count of the Condition is lost at the start of the creature's next turn.

condition.name: Open Wound
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Open Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has a recent tear or puncture in their flesh that is still oozing with blood, and although they may not yet feel the pain from sheer adrenaline coursing through their body they already have difficulty in moving.

This creature has their movement speed reduced by 5-ft. per count of the Condition and upon reaching 2 counts, they lose that count and suffer from one count of {@condition Deep Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} instead.

Additionally, whenever a creature with Open, Deep or {@condition Fatal Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} suffers {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, they are converted to {@condition Tremor - Hemorrhage|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count instead. If they were already suffering from any of the two Conditions, their sum is converted as well.

condition.name: Deep Wound
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Deep Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has had a deep gash form in their body, great enough to assail them with pain constantly - And one that can be pushed to the edge with ease.

While suffering from the Condition, this creature has their movement speed reduced by 10-ft. and whenever they suffer a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} they also suffer 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. A creature suffering from this Condition cannot gain {@condition Open Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} counts.

condition.name: Tremor - Hemorrhage
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Tremor - Hemorrhage|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is one that is currently bleeding out from countless cuts that rove and worsen inside their being.

A creature with {@condition Tremor - Hemorrhage|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} counts suffers {@damage 1d4} damage whenever they perform any action ( Each Attack counts as a different Action, also including Bonus Actions and Reactions, but not Free Actions ) and then the Condition's count is reduced by one count. Creatures that have no blood are immune to this effect.

When a creature with {@condition Tremor - Hemorrhage|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} suffers {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} by other means, they take a number of {@damage 1d6} damage equal to the total count of the Condition they are currently suffering from, then losing all remaining counts of the Condition. The Condition is also lost after the creature is knocked {@condition unconscious}. If they are healed to their Maximum Hit Points they instantly lose all counts of the Condition, also losing 2 counts whenever they are healed by any amount of Hit Points.

condition.name: Fatal Wound
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Fatal Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} isn't long for this world, having a clear and brittle opening to the doorway that leads to their demise.

While suffering from the Condition, this creature has their movement speed reduced by 10-ft. and whenever they suffer a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} they also suffer 6 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. Furthermore, a creature has their minimum Critical Hit threshold increased by one, ex: They suffer a Critical Hit on an attack roll of 19-20. A Critical Hit against them triggers {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and then removes their {@condition Fatal Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Condition.
A creature suffering from this Condition cannot gain or have any Open or {@condition Deep Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count, which is instantly removed if gained or sustained.

condition.name: Fanatic
entries: Whenever you enter your Rage you may choose to instead enter a state of sheer {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Fanaticism}. While in that stage you have all the features you'd gain by being Raging, alongside the following:

items: Your faith burns brighter than anything, drawing holy wrath down the wounds poked into your foes. You deal an additional {@damage 1d6} radiant damage on and inflict {@condition Immolation|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count equal to the target's {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count on a melee weapon attack hit.

Your blind fanaticism may propel you to do grand things, but it also has you convinced of certain tribulations you simply must suffer entirely. Whenever you would be forced to make a saving throw or ability check, you may roll a {@dice d4}. On an odd result, you gain a bonus modifier equal to your proficiency bonus. On an even result, you get the same value as a negative modifier to the roll. If you are below half your Maximum Hit Points, you must always roll this {@dice d4}.

condition.name: Torn Memory
entries: Whenever you kill a {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature you gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus and one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count, as the already dissolving mental image of that which you have shattered lingers on in your aim. If you kill or knock a friendly creature {@condition unconscious} you gain one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, yet you may only gain one count per creature per combat.
During your turn you may spend {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} as a Free Action you may take once per turn for the following:

items: {@b Reload, Then Fire.} By spending one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} you may perform an additional attack as part of your Attack action during your next turn. This extra attack does not stack. Additionally, any ranged weapons you are wielding are instantly reloaded at the start of your next turn provided you have enough ammunition on your person.

{@b Designated Target Fire.} By spending at least three {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count you may spend your Action to perform a special attack, coating an 15-ft. radius within your weapon's range in a red haze that reeks of lingering sweat and charred hair. All creatures of your choice within that radius must pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer an amount of d10 piercing damage and a sum of 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the amount of {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} spent. Creatures who succeed take half that damage and count instead. Afterward you gain one {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count for each creature damaged through this, with an additional 8 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count if you have killed your {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature through this attack. These 8 count do not count toward your turn limit. You cannot gain an amount of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} in a single turn greater than double your proficiency bonus through this way.

condition.name: Stigmatized
entries: At the start of your turns you may choose to have a creature become {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, the centre of your everlasting hatred. You may only do so provided there is no creature already {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, or you can use your Bonus Action to switch the victim of your Stigma.

condition.name: Concussion
entries: A creature suffering form a {@condition Concussion|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has their senses flare up as if a worm was crawling and rattling the inside of their head, making any further breaks all the more painful. While suffering this Condition, they suffer the following:

items: Whenever the effects of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} are triggered, they count as if the triggering creature's Proficiency Bonus was its actual value plus one.
Whenever {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} is triggered, the damage die dealt are one step greater, such as d4s instead being d6s.
The afflicted creature loses one count of {@condition Concussion|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} at the end of their turns.

condition.name: Pink Petals
entries: A creature affected by Pink Petals feels their body become covered in greenish roots feeding petals that weigh down on their soul. They gain the following downsides:

items: For every 5 counts, take 1 extra point of cold damage from attacks that either deal cold damage or inflict counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
If you have 5 counts of this, gain an additional count of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever you suffer it.
When suffering a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, take additional {@damage 1d4} psychic damage equal to half the proficiency bonus of the attacking creature.

entries: A creature can only have a maximum of 15 counts of Pink Petals. They lose 1 count of it at the end of their turn.

condition.name: Pheromone
entries: A creature affected by Pheromone lets out a citric smell that infuriates nearby creatures. They gain the following characteristics:

items: Any creature within 15 feet of you who targets a creature other than yourself with a melee attack must first make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or your Bee Save DC (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier), your choice. On a failed save, the creature chooses you as the target or loses the attack.
Whenever you are hit by a melee attack, the attacker suffers 3 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries: A creature loses Pheromone at the end of combat or after 1 minute has passed while not in combat.

condition.name: Pheromone Mark
entries: A creature Marked by Pheromones is much more susceptible to being hurt by fire. For each 3 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} that they have, they take an additional {@damage 1d4} fire damage once per turn when attacked, to a maximum of {@damage 3d4}. They lose Pheromone Mark at the end of their turn.

condition.name: Fragility
entries: A Fragilized creature feels their interiors becoming brittle, and any blow could easily break them as the weakness sinks in, rendering attacks much more effective against them. A creature suffering from Fragility has the next damage type they take considered as if their resistance was one step down, with immunities becoming resistance, resistance becoming normal, and normal becoming a vulnerability. After taking damage like this, one count of Fragility is removed.

condition.name: Hyped-Up
entries: A creature that is Hyped-Up is in a musical frenzy, hitting extremely hard, but being hit just as hard in return, You gain the following characteristics:

items: Whenever you hit a creature with an attack, you deal an additional {@damage 2d4} psychic damage for each count of Hyped-Up you have.
Whenever you are hit by an attack, you must roll a {@dice d20}. On a roll of 5 or lower, you become {@condition Stunned} until the start of your next turn.

entries: You lose all counts of Hyped-Up at the start of your next turn. A creature cannot have more than 3 counts of Hyped-Up at once.

condition.name: Desperado
entries: A creature with Desperado knows that their resources are coming to an end and will not go down without a fight. You gain the following characteristics:

items: Any ranged attack that spends Ammunition deals an additional {@damage 1d10} Piercing damage.

You gain the Evasion ability. If you already have it, then when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Wisdom saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

entries: A creature loses all counts of Desperado at the start of their next turn.

condition.name: Target of the Prescript
entries: A creature who is the The Prescript's Target will soon feel the Living Will fall upon them.

Whenever a Target is dealt damage by a character that is aligned with the Will, such as a Living Will Warlock or Procuration Paladin, they suffer half their attacker's Proficiency Bonus in {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and the attacker may once per turn re-roll one of their damage die, taking the new result.
Other Conditions such as Will's Paper Slip also count as The Prescript's Target to any creature that isn't already benefiting from the equivalent Condition.

condition.name: Grace of the Prescript
entries: The blessings of the Living Will course through your veins like oxygen through your lungs, empowering your every movement and granting you a closer sense toward enlighten. You gain the following:

items: You gain a bonus modifier to your Attack Rolls and Saving Throws equal to half the count of Grace you currently have ( rounded down ).
You gain an amount of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the count of this effect at the start of your turns, with this value remaining until the end of your turn.

entries: This effect ends whenever you are knocked {@condition Unconscious}. You lose one count of Grace of the Prescript whenever you suffer {@condition Karmic Consequences|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. You may have 9 maximum counts of Grace.

condition.name: Karmic Consequences
entries: As negative Karma builds up from your inaction and disregard for what must be done, a crippling force presses down on your soul, slowly bringing you to nothingness. You suffer the following effects according to how many Karmic Consequences you are suffering from:

rows: You have disadvantage on Ability Checks.
You have disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Saving Throws.
Your maximum hit points are halved.
You are instantly knocked {@condition Unconscious}. This Condition lasts until your next short rest.

entries: Your Karmic Consequences count is reduced by one upon a short or long rest, and is reduced by 3 whenever the {@spell lesser restoration} spell is cast upon you, or reduced by 6 whenever the {@spell greater restoration} is cast upon you.

condition.name: Procuration [Hermes]
entries: This Effect is granted and defined by the To Become a Canvas, Slowly Painted feature of the Fatalism Domain.

condition.name: Sizzling Wound
entries: This state is granted and defined by the Masked Wounds feat.

condition.name: Needle
entries: A creature inflicted with counts of Needle suffers from a unique form of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. When you take slashing damage, gain 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and lose 1 count of Needle.
At the end of your turn, you lose 1 count of Needle and gain 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

condition.name: Curse
entries: A creature inflicted with Curse rolls a {@dice 1d4} on the start of their turn, getting one of the following corresponding effects until the start of their next turn:

items: On a 1, the inflicted creature has a -1 on attack rolls and ability checks
On a 2, the inflicted creature has a -1 to their AC.
On a 3, the inflicted creature has a -2 on attack rolls and ability checks.
On a 4, the inflicted creature has a -2 to their AC.

entries: After gaining one of these effects, reduce your Curse count by 1.

condition.name: Moonlit Azure Blade
entries: A creature with counts of Moonlit Azure Blade has honed their precision and instincts during the fight, connected as one with their blade. You gain the following effects:

items: At the start of your turn, you gain {@dice 1d4} Temporary Hit Points. If you have 2 counts, you gain {@dice 1d6} instead, {@dice 1d10} if you have 3, {@dice 1d12} if you have 4, and {@dice 2d6} if you have 5.
If you score a Posture Critical hit or a Critical Hit, you add {@damage 1d8} force damage to the roll. If you have at least 3 counts, it becomes {@damage 2d8} instead.

entries: You lose 1 count of Moonlit Azure Blade at the end of your turn and all counts at the end of combat. You can only have a maximum of 5 counts of Moonlit Azure Blade at once.

condition.name: Thermal Blades
entries: A creature inflicted with the Thermal Blades effect feels their blades have turned into searing hot weapons of burning incision. You gain the following effects:

items: If you hit a creature that has counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, gain {@dice 1d4} Temporary Hit Points. This becomes {@dice 1d6} at level 5, {@dice 1d8} at level 11 and {@dice 1d10} at level 17.
Whenever an attack of yours would inflict a count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, inflict the same amount of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target.

entries: You lose 1 count of Thermal Blades at the end of your turn and all counts at the end of combat.

condition.name: Blooming
entries: A Blooming is slowly being overtaken by roots growing around their body and a constant haze clouding their mind. While suffering this Condition, they are under the following effects:

items: Whenever they suffer {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, they suffer an additional count.
Their {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count cannot be reduced under 3 times their Blooming count.

entries: Upon reaching 5 counts of Blooming, the creature must pass a Wisdom saving throw or become Fully Bloomed until the start of your next turn, also losing all Blooming count. On a success they lose half their count instead, rounded up. While under this Condition, they suffer from the following:

items: Their {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count cannot be reduced.

Whenever they suffer damage, they suffer additional psychic damage equal to half their {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, for a maximum value equal to double your proficiency bonus.
The creature is {@condition Stunned} for the duration. After becoming Fully Bloomed, that creature gains Advantage against the effect for the next three turns.

condition.name: Bloodflame
entries: While you have {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you may easily coat your swings into a pure blaze, causing you to deal an additional {@damage 1d6} fire damage per count of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} and also inflict two times your {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on melee weapon attacks. You may have up to three counts of {@condition Bloodflame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} at any given time, losing one whenever you deal damage to a creature and at the end of combat.

condition.name: Headless Fowl [无头鸡]
entries: While in this state you have Disadvantage on any Saving Throws and Skill Checks, but may still move as your body acts upon its instincts looking for more fights. Whenever you inflict {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on another creature, you deal one more count of the condition and you deal an additional damage die on every melee weapon attack, with its damage type being the same as your weapon's. You must roll a Death Saving Throws at the end of your turn and automatically regain half your Maximum Hit Points if you pass three Death Saving Throws, however instead of taking damage when a creature would deal any to you, you instead fail one Death Saving Throw per creature, per turn. You may benefit from Fuel My Rampage while like this.

condition.name: Well-Fed
entries: A creature remains {@condition Well-Fed|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until the next short or long rest. At 6th level, it has Resistance against Fire damage and at 12th level, Cold damage as well.

condition.name: Lodged Arrow
entries: A creature with counts of {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Lodged Arrows} suffers the following effects:

items: When you suffer a count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, suffer 1 additional count per {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Lodged Arrows} stack.
Lose 1 AC per stack, to a maximum of 2.
You take an additional {@damage 1d4} piercing damage whenever an attack hits you if you have 2 or more counts of {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Lodged Arrows}.

entries: You can only have a maximum of 4 counts of {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Lodged Arrows}.

A creature with counts of {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Lodged Arrows} may use an action to remove the stuck arrows, taking {@damage 1d8} piercing damage and suffering 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for each arrow removed in the process. Otherwise, they lose all stacks of {@condition Lodged Arrow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Lodged Arrows} on a short or long rest.

condition.name: Smoke
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has smog crawl and tear at their lungs, weakening their entire body horribly. They suffer an additional 2 damage per {@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count they are suffering from whenever they would suffer any damage.

{@condition Smoke|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count is halved at the end of the afflicted's turns and fully removed upon ending a turn with a single count remaining, unless stated otherwise. There are few who can withstand this plume's effects, yet those who do can easily come to benefit from its vile use.

condition.name: Fragile
entries: A Fragilized creature is suffering from having their defenses torn asunder or having difficulties in moving away from harm's way. While Fragilized, you have a cumulative penalty to your Armor Class equal to the stacks of Fragilized you are suffering. All stacks are removed when your turn ends.

condition.name: Drowsy
entries: A Drowsy creature is more succeptible to sleep, with any following rolls of the spell being considered double the result. In addition they suffer a -5 to their {@skill Perception} checks, as they are just too sleepy.

condition.name: Addicted
entries: An Addicted creature is considered {@condition Charmed} and will obey your commands, as long as the music does not stop. On their turns, they focus on attacking any other creature that isn't addicted until they are dead, doing their best to achieve such goal.

If a creature that is Addicted listens to the song until its end, the effect of Addicted does not fade until it is dispelled through the {@spell remove curse|PHB|Remove Curse} spell or similar means, blindly following you in hopes of hearing the song again. Before that happens, though, an Addicted creature may attempt to retry the saving throw at the end of their turns.

condition.name: Enchanted
entries: A creature suffering from this condition takes an additional {@damage 1d6} of psychic damage whenever it takes damage, as it sees sights of a desired life it'll never have, degrading its mind. The condition lasts until the end of the creature's next turn.

condition.name: Semi-Conscious
entries: While Semi-Conscious, you stay awake and may perform actions and so on as usual, with the penalties of having your movement speed reduced in half, your AC reduced by -4 and your rolls having a -4 penalty. The condition ends after you've been healed by a third of your maximum HP, rounded up.

condition.name: Shimmering
entries: A creature with Shimmering generates 1 count of Bloodfeast whenever they are hit by an attack. Additionally, once per turn when they apply counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, they may choose to gain temporary Hit Points equal to the amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on the damaged creature, to a maximum of 10. This effect lasts until the end of the creature's next turn.

condition.name: Responsibility
