entries: A creature with Responsibility takes one additional dice of damage whenever hit by an attack, but deals two aditional dice of damage when they hit a creature with an attack. The new damage is always equal to the original. This effect lasts until your next short or long rest.

condition.name: Protecting Sword
entries: A creature with {@condition Protecting Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has a +1 bonus to its AC for every 2 counts of {@condition Protecting Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} it has.
A creature can have a maximum of 6 counts of {@condition Protecting Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, and it loses all counts when combat ends.

condition.name: Piercing Sword
entries: A creature with {@condition Piercing Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has a +1 bonus to its attack and damage rolls for every 2 counts of {@condition Piercing Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} it has. If the creature already benefits from a bonus to its attack and damage rolls, such as from a magic item, it instead adds {@damage 1d12} piercing damage to its damage rolls for every 2 counts of {@condition Piercing Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.
A creature can have a maximum of 6 counts of {@condition Piercing Sword|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, and it loses all counts when combat ends.

condition.name: Sharpened by Tears
entries: A creature that is Tear-Sharpened has been pierced by a weapon that carries an enormous amount of despair and regret. It gains the following effects:

items: It is vulnerable to piercing damage.
Whenever it hits an enemy with an attack, it rolls one additional damage die.
Whenever it or a friendly creature within 30 feet of it is hit by an attack, it can use its reaction to apply 6 counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} to the attacking creature.

entries: This effect lasts for 1 minute.

condition.name: Serpent Arm
entries: A creature with {@condition Serpent Arm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has 2 stacks of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for every stack of {@condition Serpent Arm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} it has.

{@condition Serpent Arm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} lasts until the end of the creature's next turn, when it loses all stacks. A creature can have a maximum of 3 stacks of {@condition Serpent Arm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.
Serpent Arm usually manifests as violet scales on thin, fast arms, making them move like whips.

condition.name: Deathrite Venom
entries: A creature with stacks of {@condition Deathrite Venom|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} suffers the following effects:

items: It has the {@condition Poisoned|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} condition even if it is immune to that condition.
Its AC is reduced by 1 for each stack of Deathrite Venom.
Its attack rolls and saving throws suffer a -1 penalty for each stack of Deathrite Venom.
Whenever it suffers a {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} critical or a critical hit, it takes an additional {@damage 2d8} poison damage and loses 1 stack of Deathrite Venom.

entries: A creature loses 1 stack of Deathrite Venom at the end of its turn. After losing all stacks, it is immune to Deathrite Venom for 24 hours.

condition.name: Accumulated Past
entries: Accumulated Past is a counter representing the amount of compressed time a Crushbound wizard has collected.
It dissipates by 1 count per minute outside combat until it reaches 0, and it cannot normally be gained outside combat.

condition.name: Dark Flame
entries: A creature ablaze with {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} feels its soul weaken while the fire eats away at it. Its AC is reduced by 1 for every 3 counts of {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} it has, to a maximum penalty of -3.

A creature afflicted with {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} loses 1 count at the end of its turn. {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} counts as {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

condition.name: Nerve Strike
entries: Whenever a creature with points of Nerve Strike moves or is forcibly moved, it takes force damage equal to one roll of the Burning Jade monk's Martial Arts die. A creature can have a maximum of 3 points of Nerve Strike and loses 1 point whenever Nerve Strike causes it to take damage.

condition.name: Deathrite Haste
entries: When a creature with points of {@condition Deathrite Haste|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is hit by an attack, it takes one additional damage die for every 30 feet the attacker traveled during the current turn, to a maximum of four additional dice at 120 feet. It then suffers a number of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} stacks equal to the number of additional dice. After the attack hits, it loses all points of {@condition Deathrite Haste|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, ending the condition.

condition.name: Strider Mao
entries: A creature with {@condition Strider Mao|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} gains 5 feet of speed for each point it has and loses all points at the end of its turn.

As a bonus action, the creature can jump a number of feet equal to five times its proficiency bonus without provoking opportunity attacks. It can use this ability once, only while its speed is greater than 0, and regains the expended use when it finishes a long rest.
A creature with Strider Mao takes on rabbit-like features, usually morphing its feet into paws or developing a fluffy tail.

condition.name: Deathrite Fissure
entries: When {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} is removed from a creature with points of {@condition Deathrite Fissure|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, its speed is reduced by 5 feet for each removed point. It recovers 5 feet of speed at the end of each subsequent turn. Its initiative is reduced by the same value and is restored by 1 at the end of each subsequent turn. After these effects are applied, the creature loses 1 point of {@condition Deathrite Fissure|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

condition.name: Immobilized
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is one who's physically suffering moving their limbs and joints. While enduring {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, they take a penalty equal to the number of {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} stacks they are afflicted with to all of their attack rolls, ability checks and saving throws. All {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} stacks are removed at the end of the afflicted's turn or after a minute has passed outside of combat.

condition.name: Panicked
entries: A {@condition Panicked|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature feels their heart nearly exploding constantly, as fears unimaginable crawl down their skin. As long as it is able to see the source of their panic must pass a Charisma saving throw on the start of their turn or have their movement reduced to 5-feet as they are nearly {@condition Paralyzed} from the horror. In addition to that, they suffer from a -2 penalty to their AC as long as they can see or hear the source of their Panic.

condition.name: Festive Fever
entries: Whenever a creature with points of {@condition Festive Fever|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} attacks, it adds one extra die to all of their damage dice for each point of {@condition Festive Fever|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} it has.
All points of {@condition Festive Fever|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} are removed at the end of the creature's turn.

condition.name: Volatile Passion
entries: A creature with {@condition Volatile Passion|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has a powerful will that can shatter if it falters.

While a creature has Volatile Passion, it gains a bonus to attack rolls against creatures affected by {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} equal to half its Volatile Passion count, rounded down. On a hit against such a creature, it also applies a number of Burn counts equal to that bonus.

optionalfeature.name: Fighting Style: Sacrifice
entries: As a Reaction when you see a friendly creature within 30 feet of you miss an attack roll, you may immediately use your remaining movement speed to jump towards them and make an attack roll against the creature they tried to hit if it is within reach. If you're successful, you deal damage to both creatures, but an additional {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage to the creature you hit. This damage cannot be diminished or prevented in any way, and they suffer any statuses as normal.

optionalfeature.name: The Disgrace
entries: {@i "I'll be damned before I let you ruin this! Not after toiling like a goddamn dog for decades, climbing up the ranks...!"}

What have you done? You should already know the answer to that question, after all it has been repeated in your head as often as you can recall. There's something you did, of your fault and folly, that has rendered you a complete and utter disgrace to those around you, a shame that would be best left erased. Yet still, your exhausted, spiteful fingers grip onto your remaining life like a starving animal does to its last meal.

This {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst} is recommended for characters who have screwed up phenomenally and even more-so as that failure being of their on fault. That single event is something that has defined them more than anything else in the past, even more-so if they were someone important before their horrid fall from grace. These are often seem as bitter and arrogant people.
Upon activation of your {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst}, you gain the following effects:

items: Hatred, spite and bitterness overtake your emotions to create a rage-fueled drive towards all your actions, granting you Immunity to becoming {@condition Frightened} or {@condition Charmed}.

You gain 4 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count at the start of your turns. Whenever you deal damage, you deal an additional amount of damage equal to half your current {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, to a maximum value equal to your proficiency bonus.
Whenever you would inflict {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you inflict an additional count.

Additionally, the anxiety to re-instate your greatness has you become even quicker on your feet as it grows. Each time an attack hits you, your AC increases by a +1 bonus modifier. You lose this bonus whenever you are missed with an attack.

optionalfeature.name: The Custodian
entries: {@i "Listen. We live in a binary world. The world that is luscious... and the world that is bristly. Are you aware of their differences?"}

Style, force and loyalty are words that radiate through your gait wherever you walk, exhaling a powerful aura that booms through the hearts of others, either shaking them to the core or having them fall under the protection of your beat.

This {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst} is recommended for characters who are great leaders and bolster both courage and imperativeness toward their fellows, taking care of any under them like a grand family that extends far beyond the bonds of blood. These are driven by and for their groups and factions as the first thing in their world, going to great lengths just to make sure they are happy and safe, also being reasonably vengeful at whoever wrongs them and their kin.
Upon activation of your {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst}, the following apply:

items: Describe how your presence extends like a bursting melody that has others quake in their boots. When first triggering this Burst, all hostile creatures that can see or hear you within a 360-ft. radius must pass a Charisma saving throw or become {@condition Frightened} of you for the next minute, also being able to retry this saving throw to end the Condition early at the end of their subsequent turns. While Frightened, a creature under this Condition suffers 2 {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count at the start of their turns, losing one count after each ability check, saving throw or attack roll.

You feel a surge of power at your fingertips - Confidence made manifest in pure, raw bravado. You gain unarmed weapons that you are proficient with in the shape of your fists and legs for the duration. These have the Finesse and Mesmerizing properties, dealing {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage on a hit. If you already had an Unarmed Strike option, you instead deal an additional {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage on your Unarmed Strike hits.

Your feet are stepping on air when it comes to being near those you care about. As a Bonus Action during your turns you may instantly move upwards to 30-ft. in a single leap, having to end your movement within 5-ft. of a friendly creature within that reach. If you are to occupy the same space as a hostile creature you may attempt a Shove attempt against them as part of the same Bonus Action, pushing them 5-ft. toward any direction and taking their space on a success or being forced to land within 5-ft. of that creature on a failure.

Whenever you hit a creature that has {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} with an Unarmed Strike, you deal an additional {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage against them and may choose to instantly push them back 5-ft.

optionalfeature.name: The Ward
entries: {@i "Anyhoo, has anyone here actually read 'The Cloudburst Blade?' If ya did, well... if I may have but 3-no, 4 hours of your time, good sir..."}

To be a ward is to be a waif in your life, you might still be under the graces of your master - your captor - your guardian, whatever they may be to you, and you may still somewhat believe in them but your heart, so carefully forged, has already seen through cracks that you might not be so keen to accept.

This {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst} is recommended for characters that are living a dichotomy of being attached to a reality that they hold immense fervour toward, but also having that reality being no more than a farce that could break under their feet at any moment. They are those who possess immense knowledge of specific topics but may seem sheltered to the outside world or have trouble accepting certain truths no matter how hard they stare them in the eye.
Upon activation of your {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst}, you gain the following:

items: The sheer energy pent up in you bursts out like a fire, granting you an additional 10-ft. of movement speed and having all your weapon or spell attacks inflict an additional 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

Your fervour is a dual-edged blade, both blinding you to what would leave most quaking but also obfuscating certain alluring dangers. You are Immune to being Frightened but suffer Disadvantage on saving throws against being Charmed.

You gain proficiency in the {@skill History} skill, or Expertise if you were already proficient. You and your DM may discuss a topic of particular interest to your character when first taking this Core Burst, then gaining Advantage on {@skill History} skill checks related to this interest after it is agreed by you and the DM. Additionally, you gain one of the following depending on your current relation to your guardian or symbol of affection:

{@b House of Glass Dreams.} If your relationship is of admiration or an otherwise positive outlook to this false idol, whenever you perform a Critical Hit or have success in a skill check or saving throw within sight of your idol, they may spend their Reaction to Praise you. When they do so, you may add a {@dice 1d8} bonus modifier to one roll of your choice until the end of your next turn and may only do so before you roll.

{@b House of Scattered Hopes.} If your relationship has been broken or is otherwise negative to this false idol, you suffer a {@dice 1d6} negative modifier to all rolls while you can see them within 160-ft. of you as a powerful heartache easily overtakes you. However, after this pain your broken hopes can still be picked up and become stronger through your turmoil. Whenever you have a Critical Success or have success in a skill check or saving throw you gain Confidence. You may spend one Confidence after you roll any of the aforementioned rolls to add an additional {@dice 1d6} to the final result, and may hold up to three Confidence count, which is only reset after a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Passion
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you inflict 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. Additionally, you gain advantage on {@skill Performance} checks whenever performing with ( or to impress ) other friendly creatures or against a hostile creature.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Skull Bursting
entries: Whenever you hit a Grappled creature you may choose to suplex them and cause them to become {@condition Prone}. When you do so, for the remainder of the duration this creature remains {@condition Prone} you may choose to re-roll any damage die against them, taking the greater result. You may do so once per die.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Needle Fractures
entries: You can sink the ink in this tattoo to create binding points in your muscles that take out the force of whatever hits you as a Reaction you may take whenever you suffer damage. When you do so, reduce the damage taken by your choice between your current amount of tattoos or proficiency bonus. You cannot reduce force damage this way and may use this tattoo an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining spent uses after a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Vicious Burns
entries: You learn the {@spell vicious mockery} spell. Whenever you causa damage to another creature using it, you may choose to fire damage instead of psychic and one {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for each damage die rolled. If you are not a spellcaster your DC for this spell's saving throw is 10 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus + any bonuses gained from being Attuned to a magical weapon.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Turtle Skin
entries: You may spend your Bonus Action to have the ink from this tattoo spread out and flow over your skin, creating a protective layer over it. As long as you aren't wearing armor or are wearing a Tattoo Set armor, you gain a bonus modifier to your AC equal to half your current magical Tattoo count until the start of your next turn. For each attack performed against you in that duration this modifier is reduced by one. You may use this tattoo an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, regaining spent uses after a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Mutual Discombobulation
entries: Once per turn you may choose to change one of your attacks as part of the Attack Action with a Headbutt. To do so you perform a melee Unarmed Strike that you are proficient in against a creature within 5-ft. of you. On a hit, you deal {@damage 2d10} bludgeoning damage and inflict half your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, then suffering half the damage dealt yourself and the same amount of the Condition's count. When you gain it this way, you only lose this count at the end of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Entrenched Ankles
entries: You gain 10-ft. move speed. Whenever you attempt to climb a surface, you can spend up to 10-ft. of walking speed at a time to successfully climb the same amount of feet spent by kicking and locking your feet into the surface, remaining there without falling at the end of your turns.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Threadmarks
entries: As an Action during your turn you may brace yourself for a violent sprint. When you do so, you gain 30-ft. of walking speed until the end of your turn and any damage dealt to you through Opportunity Attacks is halved. Whenever you move through another creature's space they must pass a Dexterity saving throw or be caught in your wild trample, being knocked {@condition Prone} on a failure and suffering an amount of d10 bludgeoning damage equal to your proficiency bonus, or half that value on a success. The DC for this is 8 + your Strength modifier + your proficiency bonus. When you do so you may choose to Grapple up to your Strength modifier's worth of creatures instead of Knocking them {@condition Prone}, then knocking them {@condition Prone} in a pile onto of any unoccupied space within 5-ft. of you at the end of your turn. You may use this ability an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, regaining spent uses after a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of an Thunderstorm
entries: Whenever you would be forced to attempt a Dexterity saving throw to resist the effects of a spell or attack that affects a radius, line or sphere that has a physical form ( Such as a {@spell fireball|PHB|Fireball}, {@spell lightning bolt|PHB|Lightning Bolt}, Ballista Bolt or Cannonball ) and pass, you may spend your Reaction to suffer no damage if you would take half and punch through the attack, redirecting it to instead hit another point of your choice within 60-ft. of you. When you do so, all creatures within this new area must attempt the same saving throw against the original DC. You may use this ability an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, regaining spent uses after a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Starburst
entries: Whenever you deal a Critical Hit against a target creature, you deal an additional 2 damage die equal to the attack's current damage. Additionally, you inflict an amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count against the hit creature equal to the amount of damage die rolled and when you perform this your fists burst into bright-light that covers an 30-ft. area around you. All hostile creatures within that reach must then pass a Constitution saving throw or be Blinded until the end of their next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Relocator Fighting Style
entries: Wielding certain weapons that are a menace from afar has become second nature to you, and you have learnt how to better grip and shove all on your way to shape the battlefield to your liking. Whenever you hit with a weapon that has the Reach property, you may move the target up to 5-ft. closer to you if they were within 10-ft. of you or push them away if they were within 5-ft. of you.

optionalfeature.name: Headshot Focus Fighting Style
entries: You are particular with where you aim your weaponry, focusing for a quick and clean kill whenever able. Whenever you target a creature that has a head with a ranged weapon attack, you may choose to Aim For the Head. When you do so, the following applies:

items: The Target's Armor Class is increased by their proficiency bonus.
You cannot hit the target unless you beat their AC, regardless of scoring a Critical Hit.
If you would Critically Hit yet miss the targets AC, you still roll damage, dealing half that amount as your shot grazes them.
You Critically Hit on this attack with a Critical Threshold reduced by 2, such as rolling an 18-20 on your dice, before any modifiers.

optionalfeature.name: The Veteran
entries: {@i "Thanks to that, I'm free to point the barrel at anyone I want. No matter where I fire it, this shotgun can blast anyone into fireworks like it hit them point blank, how wonderful is that?"}

Your life has been a warpath going from battle to battle, conflict to conflict. This might not be in the case of a literal war, but instead of various minor conflicts that have led you along to be hardened by them, granting you an askew view of your surroundings and the people that walk near you.

This Core Burst is recommended for characters who have been put through conflict for most of their lives be that by their own volition or otherwise. They are often found lurking over memories of their own path or attempting not to overlap their sights with something that isn't really there, but vary wildly in how they cope with their experiences.
Upon activation of your Core Burst, you gain the following effects:

items: You gain Resistance to psychic damage and the Frightened Condition.
You gain {@dice 1d4+1} Poise count at the start of your turns.
You gain Advantage on ability checks and saving throws against being Grappled or Blinded.
You are considered Proficient in the {@skill Athletics} skill if you weren't, and to have Expertise in said skill if you were.

entries: Additionally, choose one of the following to determine which feature you gain based on your own personality traits. If you see people still as a precious thing and value life greatly, gain this:

items: Whenever a friendly creature that you can see within 120-ft. of you is healed or protected by another creature, such as per the Protection Fighting Style, you gain Hope For Your Fellows until the end of your next turn. While clinging onto this Hope, you may reduce any damage you suffer by two die that equal double your proficiency bonus. ( Such as a +2 being 2d4, +3 being 2d6 and so on. ) Additionally you may, as a Free Action at the start of your turns, pass this Hope and its effects to a friendly creature within the same reach as first described.

entries: If you see people as resources to be spent toward your goal, gain this:

items: Whenever a friendly creature that you can see within 120-ft. of you suffers damage for the first time in the round, you gain one Poise count. Whenever a friendly creature within that same reach dies or first falls Unconscious during this combat, you gain Woe For Your Foes until the end of your next turn. While clinging into this Despair you may choose to re-roll once any individual damage die you roll on weapon attacks after first rolling them, having to take that result.

entries: And finally, if apathy towards life is all that fills you, gain this:

items: You may spend your Reaction when suffering damage to reduce your damage taken by a value equal to your current Poise count plus your proficiency bonus, as you only try to thread forward in the never-stopping march of life.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: For more information on Core Bursts, see the Fatalist Domain cleric.

optionalfeature.name: Scattering Aroma
entries: {@b Cost: 2 Sorcery Points.} As a Reaction to when you would be targeted for an attack, you may use your own magic to momentarily disperse the thoughts of your attacker, imposing Disadvantage on the attack. You may so after the creature rolls to hit but before the DM determines the result.

optionalfeature.name: Spreading Floral Breeze
entries: {@b Cost: 1-4 Points.} As a Free Action during your turn you may have your magic solidify roots sprouting from your shoulders or around your back that mimic your hands, acting in unison to deliver more at once. Your next weapon attack or cantrip spell attack until the end of your turn may target an additional different target for each Sorcery Point spent, provided the targets are still within reach.
If the cantrip you would cast can already target multiple targets, you just choose one more target for each Sorcery Point spent.

If you would deal additional damage with sources such as Divine Smite, that additional damage is divided evenly toward all targets, rounded down and with a minimum of one die or value of extra damage.
{@b Ex:} If you would deal an additional {@damage 5d8} fire damage from a magic weapon against four creatures, each suffers only an additional {@damage 2d8} fire damage.

optionalfeature.name: The Fatebound
entries: {@i "It must've been fate that brought us together. To think that I'd ever meet a husband like you..."}
Your heart beats to the tune of the fates, scattered to the waves until it stops. Even though volatile, you always make sure that when you crash, it will be glorious.

This Core Burst is recommended for characters who are marked by a certain detachment with everything else, those with a turbulent attitude toward their goals or characters who are ultimately fatalists.
Upon activation of your Core Burst, you gain the following in accordance to your current missing Hit Points:

items: While you are below half your Maximum Hit Points, deal an additional d6 damage whenever you damage a creature. This damage is of the same type as your original attack.
While below half of your Maximum Hit Points currently missing, gain a +1 bonus modifier to hit on your attack rolls. While below a quarter, gain a +2 instead.
Whenever you would gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, gain two additional counts of the effect.
Once per turn per creature, whenever you deal damage to a creature suffering from being {@condition Frightened} or {@condition Charmed} and you aren't, deal an additional 2d4 psychic damage as well.

optionalfeature.name: The Truthseeker
entries: {@i "Even if I don't have much happiness, I know where to go in the immediate future. And that's enough for me."}

You have always bene ticked off by the small rips at the seams of the world and the thoughts of what might move in the shadows. You may not always know how or why, but your heart yearns to understand the world and its many meanings.

This Core Burst is recommended for characters who just can't stand still when they've got the feeling that something is off, those with great intuition and those inclined to try to face the truth even if they may not be able to withstand it fully.
Upon activation of your Core Burst, you gain the following effects:

items: You gain Advantage on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Insight} checks.
You gain Advantage against resisting and perceiving Illusions of any kind, you also gain Advantage against Enchantment spells.
While you are above half your Maximum Hit Points, all damage you suffer is reduced by 1d4 as you feel like you can handle any erosion from seeing what you shouldn't.

While you are at or below half your Maximum Hit Points you feel the weight in your mind start to become heavy, yet a supernatural focus has been unlocked in your being. You suffer a -2 negative modifier on Wisdom and Charisma saving throws, but gain 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} at the start of your turns and whenever you trigger a Posture Critical, that damage cannot be reduced through any means.

optionalfeature.name: The Shackled

prerequisite.other: A Wisdom score of 18 or lesser

entries: {@i "I... I have to move forward... F-follow the shadow...!"}

You have a profound dependency or love for a particular subject, be that an object or a person. That is what keeps you going through anything so you can keep its safety and possible happiness guaranteed at any cost.

This Core Burst is recommended for characters that have developed a deep and ( although not always ) unhealthy obsession with something or someone, those who would split the word in two to complete what is requested for them or characters who are ultimately seeking some form of validation or to have others be proud of them.
Upon activation of your Core Burst, you gain the following effects:

items: Name a creature or object as your Desire when first activating your Burst. Whenever they suffer damage or are grabbed by another creature ( respectively ), you gain a cumulative +1 bonus modifier to hit and to damage on your next attack against the creature who harmed your Desire. This bonus is reset after dealing damage to them.

While your Desire is {@condition Unconscious} ( if it is a creature ) or is within a hostile creature's possession ( if it is an object ), you deal an additional 1d8 damage when dealing any damage while being within 15-ft of your Desire.
You gain a bonus modifier to your AC equal to half your proficiency bonus while within 15-ft. of your Desire.

You are permanently under the effects of the {@spell guidance} cantrip when tasked by your Desire ( if they are a creature ) to attempt something that would require a Skill Check or while using your Desire. ( if they are an object. )

entries: If your Desire is an object, you and your DM must agree that it is important enough for you to value it greatly. That item can be a weapon that has accompanied you through your journey and that has the possibility of being pried away from you, or a memento that keeps you steady through the hardest of times, such as a carved totem that reminds you of home or something of the sort.

optionalfeature.name: Random Targetting
entries: Sometimes an ability or feature may ask you to choose a random creature. To do so, refer to an order of the possible creatures to be chosen ( Such as groupings of hostile or friendly creatures, also making preferential use of the Initiative order if in combat ) and rolling an appropriate die for the number of creatures.

For a two or three creatures, simply roll a d4 or d6 respectively, with each creature having a "weight" of 2 on the roll, such as when rolling a d6 on a result of 1-2 creature A gets picked, while 3-4 would be creature B and a 5-6 results in creature C.

For creatures greater than that in an even number, simply roll an appropriate die, such as a d4 for 4 creatures, d6 for 6 and so on. In the case of odd creatures, roll the closest die rounded up, such as rolling a d8 if there are 7 creatures to be chosen. If the result is an unassigned number, simply re-roll until the result is a listed creature, or pick the last creature in order if this is repeated more than twice.

optionalfeature.name: Nailing Scissors
entries: Whenever you hit an attack roll with your scrap scissors, the target suffers 2 counts of {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. This count increases to 3 upon reaching level 9.

optionalfeature.name: Cursed Scissors
entries: Whenever you hit an attack roll with your scrap scissors, the target suffers 1 count of {@condition Curse|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. This count increases to 2 upon reaching level 9.

optionalfeature.name: Pinstack Scissors
entries: Whenever you hit an attack roll with your scrap scissors, the target suffers 2 counts of {@condition Needle|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

optionalfeature.name: Sharper Scissors
entries: Your Scrap Scissors deal an additional {@damage 1d8} slashing damage. This damage increases to {@damage 2d8} upon reaching level 9. If the Scrap Scissors are being held with two hands, the d8 becomes a d10 instead.

optionalfeature.name: Pushing Scissors
entries: After you hit a creature with your Scrap Scissors, they must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be pushed 5 feet back. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Frightening Scissors
entries: After hitting a creature with your Scrap Scissors, you can force them to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, or become {@condition frightened} of you for 1 turn. A creature affected by this can repeat their saving throws at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Molar Scissors
entries: Instead of attacking a creature, you may choose to grapple them with your Scrap Scissors instead. You may choose to perform an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) ability check instead of a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) ability check for the grapple, and you may perform the ability check with advantage.

optionalfeature.name: Divided Scissors
entries: Your Scrap Scissors can now be split into two separate blades for each hand. When separate, they each count as a {@item handaxe|PHB} you are proficient with, with the exception that they also have the finesse property. You may unite or separate them as a free action.

optionalfeature.name: Bleeding Scissors
entries: Whenever you apply counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} with your Scrap Scissors, you apply that many counts + 2 instead. Additionally, friendly creatures within 5 feet of you apply 1 additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count when they hit a creature with a melee attack.

optionalfeature.name: Critical Scissors
entries: Your attack rolls with your Scrap Scissors can score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20.

optionalfeature.name: Preserving Scissors
entries: Your attack rolls with your Scrap Scissors do not remove counts of {@condition Needle|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} from affected creatures.

optionalfeature.name: Aiding Scissors
entries: After you hit a creature with your Scrap Scissors, the next attack that targets them has advantage.

optionalfeature.name: Powerful Scissors
entries: Your Scrap Scissors gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it.

optionalfeature.name: Wounding Scissors
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with your Scrap Scissors and the attack deals more than half their hit points in damage, or was a critical hit, you may roll on the Lingering Injuries table to cause a wound on them.

optionalfeature.name: Singleton
entries: A spell may have a part of its text contain the "Singleton." keyword. This signifies that the spell has a special benefit to the first time it is cast until your next long rest, with this effect being written following the "Singleton." keyword itself If you cast multiple "Singleton." spells within the same long rest, their special effects trigger once per each individual spell.

optionalfeature.name: Saint's Touch
entries: Your mere touch is enough to take another creatures pain away, as you are one to be able to shoulder your fellows suffering. As an action on your turn, you may touch another creature within 5-feet of you and restore their hitpoints for a value equal to your Paladin level times five. When you do so, you take the same value in damage.
Starting at 11th level, you may also choose to remove one condition or non-magical disease from your target and suffer it yourself.

optionalfeature.name: Unrelenting Fighting Style
entries: After sinking your teeth in, it becomes only easier for you to lay waste to your targets. After hitting with an attack, you gain a +1 bonus to your next attack roll against the same target.

optionalfeature.name: Gluttonous Attack
entries: Beginning at 1st level, you've gained a knack for performing particularly violent gashes and being filled with vitality from the motivation of each blow struck. Once per turn, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d4} damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll, and you regain hit points equal to half the additional damage dealt. The attack must use a melee weapon with either the finesse or heavy property.

You don't need advantage on the attack roll if the target is below half its hit point maximum, isn't {@condition Incapacitated||incapacitated}, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll. The extra damage increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue table.

optionalfeature.name: Avenger Fighting Style
entries: You would never let any harm brought upon your dear companions go unpunished. After a friendly creature within 30-feet of you takes damage, you gain a +2 to the first attack roll against its source. This bonus is not added to damage rolls.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Broodmother
entries: Your patron grants you one of its dear children to protect and aid you in your ordeals. You gain the {@spell find familiar|PHB|Find Familiar} spell and may cast it as a ritual. The spell doesn't count against your number of spells known.

As an action, once per short rest, you may summon handfuls of tiny creatures resembling the visage of your patrons brood and scatter them around all 5-foot squares surrounding yourself. A creature besides yourself moving into the a space with these creatures must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or step onto one of the tiny creatures, squashing them. Upon sensing harm come to even a vestige of its brood, your patron manifests a great spider leg or otherwise fitting weapon that automatically hits the transgressing creature, dealing {@damage 3d8} piercing damage to them.
This damage increases by {@dice 1d8} at 6th, 12th, 15th and 18th level. Any given space containing these creatures lasts for up to one minute after being created or until they are squished.

optionalfeature.name: One Day Now, One Day Less
entries: You can't die, not yet, not now. There is more to be done. When you would suffer a failed Death Saving Throw, you may instead choose to have it become a success.

Whenever you do this, your Hit Points are permanently reduced by a value equal to half your hit die plus your Consittution modifier. This reduction cannot be lowered or restored by any means short of the Wish spell, as some scars will never heal, no matter how hard you try.

optionalfeature.name: Neverending Pain
entries: You won't be boggled down by what lowlifes such as your enemies attempt to afflict you with. By spending a Superiority Die and a bonus action, you may instantly end one condition afflicting you and you may, as a reaction to when you do so. you may perform a weapon attack against any target within your reach, dealing your Superiority Die in additional damage thats equal to the weapon's damage.

optionalfeature.name: Pressure Offload Point
entries: You take a swift palm or finger to a creature's pressure points, having them feel their tense body near instantly cool off. By spending 2 ki points you can target one creature within 5-feet of you with a jab to their pressure points, if the target is willing they fall under one of the effects of {@spell calm emotions|PHB|Calm Emotions} spell, ignoring its original saving throw. If the target is hostile, it must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw to dodge your apparent attack.
You choose which effect takes place.

optionalfeature.name: Resist and Bite Fighting Style
entries: What is one more scar for a body so used to carrying them? They'll only fuel the punishment delivered onto your enemies. As an action during your turn, you may forgo attacking to instead enter an enduring stance.

You release all the pain you've taken in a free action attack at one creature within reach on the start of your next turn, dealing an amount of additional damage die equal to the number of times you've taken damage during your enduring stance. If you would have additional attacks, also add one additional weapon damage dice for each of that you have foregone.

optionalfeature.name: Singing Spells
entries: As a free action when you cast a spell, you may spend one Sorcery point to start an oddly harmonious string of noises that form a sligthly off key melody as you go from slinging spell to spell. Choose one creature as the focus of your song, it takes an additional {@damage 1d4} psychic damage whenever it would take damage, as for it the song sounds much more distorted, as if a horrible droning had settled in their eardrum. You may spend an additional Sorcery point on the start of each of your subsequent turns to maintain the effect on the target or switch to another one.

optionalfeature.name: Chokehold Fighting Style
entries: Grappling a creature is only half the job to one such as you, one must still deprive them of the very air to weather them down! When you grapple a creature, you may forgo any number of attacks to automatically deal {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage + your Strength modifier per attack spent like this, as you squeeze down the creature.

optionalfeature.name: Fading Memories Pact Boon
entries: There are some moments during your day where foreign yet eerily beloved memories flash into your head, just when you're in the moment they seem all that much clearer, yet that has anything else you don't perceive pass by as if it were never there. During combat, you have a +1 to your rolls against or related to creatures directly engaged to you in combat, or those within 5-feet of you. In contrast, you suffer a -1 penalty to your rolls against or related to creatures who are not engaged to you during combat.

optionalfeature.name: Harmonize Spell
entries: For a two Sorcery points, you may better make use of your blood lineage through literally supplying that source onto your spells for better damage. When you cast a damage- inflicting spell, you may choose to take a number of your hit die in damage to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus, after doing so the cast spell deals the same amount of additional die in damage, the die size and damage is equal to the spell's. If the spell has multiple die listed, you choose which to add onto.

optionalfeature.name: Round Cleanup Fighting Style
entries: Its nice and all to deal with duels one on one, but you haven't ever been afraid of taking on an entire crowd at once. When you hit a creature, you gain a +1 to hit a different creature with an attack.

optionalfeature.name: Alluminum Defender
entries: Instead of using the Steel Defender statblock for your metallic companion, you can use the {@creature All-Around Helper|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|All-Around Helper} statblock below. The same rules apply to it, except it gains an additional Hit Die and additional maximum hit points whenever you gain a level. The Hit Die has the size shown in its statblock. Additionally, it gains one additional attack when you reach 8th level and another when you reach 12th level.
At 10th level, you can order the {@creature All-Around Helper|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|All-Around Helper} to use its Thorough Cleaning action.

optionalfeature.name: Unloved Gift Surprise
entries: Artificer Infusion Prerequisite:A gift box. Once per long rest, you long to feel unloved by someone. As such, you grab a perfectly good looking and ordinary gift box and tinker away with its insides to make a compact explosive device that triggers either when the box is opened, or at your merry whim, also letting some rocks slip inside to make it truly believable.

When you attempt to gift this item to another person, you have advantage on persuasion checks to do so. Additionally, as an action on your turn, you may toss the Gift to a space within 30-feet of yourself, and spend your bonus action to trigger the explosives inside. When triggered, all creatures within a 5-feet radius of the Gift must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or take {@damage 5d8} fire damage, or half on a success, also being covered in soot for good measure.
If a creature was surprised by this, it has disadvantage on this saving throw.

optionalfeature.name: Contractual Enactment
entries: Instead of entering a blind rage, your barbaric enactments of violence come elsewhere, from a contract or pact with someone or something from far away, far from what you'd initially think at least. By using a bonus action to start your contractual enactment, you unleash your given power like a congealed tempest, for the next minute you gain the following benefits: You have advantage on Charisma checks and Charisma saving throws. You may use Charisma for your attack and damage rolls.
When you make a melee weapon attack using Charisma, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll. This bonus increases as you level. You have your tongue and magical, chiding words as a natural weapon.

It has a range of 30 feet and deals {@damage 1d8} psychic damage. If you are able to cast spells, you can't cast them or concentrate on them while enacting. Your contractual enactment lasts for 1 minute.

It ends early if you are knocked {@condition Unconscious||unconscious} or if your turn ends and you haven't attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your enactment on your turn as a bonus action. Once you have enacted your contract the maximum number of times for your barbarian level, you must finish a long rest before you can enact it again.
You may rage 2 times at 1st level, 3 at 3rd, 4 at 6th, 5 at 12th, and 6 at 17th.

optionalfeature.name: Encroaching Fighting Style
entries: You arrive like a disease, silently waiting for your target to slip up and take their eyes away from a second, and then deliver your terrifying blows. You have a +2 to damage rolls against creatures that are {@condition Blinded||blinded} or otherwise can't see you, such as if they can't see through darkness.

optionalfeature.name: Disruptive Attack
entries: Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike swiftly and cause a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can reduce a value of damage you would take by {@dice 1d6} for a creature's opportunity attack after you provoke it. The next attack against the creature has advantage, in addition, if you have advantage granted by another creature to attack a hostile creature, for the first attack during your turn you deal an additional {@dice 1d4} damage.
The amount of the extra damage reduced and dealt increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue table. The die size remains the same.

optionalfeature.name: Hit Like a Train
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to put everything you have in a single blow. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to hit like a train. Doing so makes you forgo any extra attacks you would have during your turn, including opportunity attacks, but you gain advantage on this attack roll and deal {@dice 2d8} additional damage equal to your weapons damage type, as well as additional d8 for each attack you forewent for this.
However, attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Running Stream's Rush
entries: As your action during your turn, you may spend 3 ki points to enter a state of constant flow and movement. You may move up to your movement speed's worth in any direction, not provoking opportunity attacks until the end of your turn. Additionally, the first time you leave a creature's reach you may perform an unnarmed strike against them.

optionalfeature.name: Song of the Black Forest
entries: You can subtly deploy an enchatment through your song to better allow another to reach their end. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature suffers from {@condition Enchanted|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. {@condition Enchanted|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. until the end of their next turn.

A creature suffering from this condition takes an additional {@dice 1d6} of psychic damage whenever it takes damage, as it sees sights of a desired life it'll never have, degrading its mind. Your Song of the Black Forest die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level.

optionalfeature.name: Primeval Howling
entries: Upon reaching 3rd level, you can at times let all of the savage energy within you swell up in a guttural howl to strike the fear of nature into your foes' hearts. As an action, you may bellow out a mighty howl, all hostile creatures within 15-feet of you must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw whose DC is 8 +Your strength Modifier + your proficiency modifier or take {@damage 2d8} thunder damage and suffer a negative modifier to their Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma based rolls equal to half your proficiency modifier, rounded down. This lasts until the end of their next turn and they take only half the damage on a success.
After this Howl, you become winded, suffering the same negative modifier to your Strength, Dexterity and Constitution based rolls until the end of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Impose Balance
entries: Sometimes, your will falls in place with that of the very universe. As a reaction to when another creature would roll a dice within a 60-feet radius of yourself, after the result is shown, you may change it to become the inverse of what it should be, such as a 15 becoming a 5 or vice versa. A roll of 10 does not change.

optionalfeature.name: Penitent Fighting Style
entries: For Fighter, Ranger & Paladin. The pain adorns your body like the hilt of a blade, wield it to its fullest. Whenever you take one tenth of your maximum hit points of damage in a single turn, you gain a +1 to hit for your next attack and damage rolls.
This effect does not stack.

optionalfeature.name: Mind-Clearing Clap
entries: Sometimes, a clear head is all it takes to achieve peace, be it for yourself or a friend in need. As a bonus action during your turn, you may spend 2 Ki points to clap your hands and let the sound wash away your worries for a moment, or those of a friendly creature within 15-feet of yourself. After doing so, the target has advantage on their next Wisdom Saving Throw for the next minute.

optionalfeature.name: Aura of United Guardians
entries: You not only exude the best you can give in a fierce aura, but also can bring forth the best in the allies near you. You, as a bonus action during your turn, may consume one use of your Channel Divinity to initiate an Aura of Union between you and any friendly creature within a 10-feet raius of you. You and those creatures gain a bonus to damage rolls equal to +2 for each friendly creature within that area.
This area increases following the Paladin's usual area increase.

optionalfeature.name: Hard to Kill
entries: No one will be allowed to put you down, not until your body finally gives out. You gain the following benefits: Your Constitution or Wisdom score is increased by 1, to a maximum of 20. If you would be knocked {@condition Unconscious} by being reduced below one hit point, you instead stay half-awake in the {@condition Semi-Conscious|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} condition, which only ends after you've been healed by a third of your maximum HP, rounded up.

While {@condition Semi-Conscious|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you stay awake and may perform actions and so on as usual, with the penalties of having your movement speed reduced in half, your AC reduced by -4 and your rolls having a -4 penalty.

optionalfeature.name: Naturalist Master Fighting Style

prerequisite.other: {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} or Druid, Fighter, Ranger, or Sorcerer

entries: While you wield no weapon or shield in either hand, your natural weapons gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls against targets below half their hit point maximum.
You deal 2 additional damage of your natural weapon's damage type.

optionalfeature.name: Stalker in the Night Fighting Style

prerequisite.other: {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} or Rogue

entries: The shadows are an appropriate prowling ground for one such as you, who prefers to attack while unseen. If you deal damage from a weapon attack to a creature while you are hidden from it, you also inflict one {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count per damage die you deal.
In the case of inflicting more than 4 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count at once, you instead inflict Heavy {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed}.

optionalfeature.name: Royal Practice Fighting Style

prerequisite.other: {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} or Cleric, Fighter, or Paladin

entries: Few can truly call swordplay an art form in the way that you and your kindred can, evolving a single slash onto a bloody manifesto of your being.

Once per turn you may replace one of the attacks you'd perform from the Attack Action to a Flourishing Attack, of which you perform a Melee Weapon Attack against a target within reach. On a hit, you deal an additional 1 damage die that matches your weapon's and inflict 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count. On a miss, you whiff and embarrass yourself, suffering a -2 negative modifier to your Armor Class and Charisma related rolls until the start of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Cross Stitch Explosives

prerequisite.other: A spool of yarn

entries: You managed to create a densely packed mess of strings and needles that explode when pressed in the wrong way. Once per Long Rest you may create one {@item Stitchwrap Bomb|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Stitchwrap Bomb}, and a second one upon reaching 12th Level in Artificer. You cannot create more than what your Level permits at any given time, yet repair them at no additional cost.
See {@item Stitchwrap Bomb|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} for the deployable tool created by this infusion.

optionalfeature.name: Polished Needles

prerequisite.other: A sheet of metal

entries: Much like the wings of a butterfly, sometimes your projects should be pinned down to truly be observed. This has led to you creating specialized pins that you may craft so you have two at hand at any given time.

You create up to two {@item Rusty Iron Stake|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Rusty Iron Stakes} during a Long Rest if any are missing, and you gain a +1 bonus modifier to Attack and Damage Rolls using them upon reaching 5th level in Artificer, a +2 upon reaching 12th Level and a +3 upon reaching 18th Level.

optionalfeature.name: Sharpened Weapon

prerequisite.other: A simple or martial weapon

entries: The weapon gains the Hemorrhaging (17-20) property. If it already has that property, choose one of the following benefits:

items: The weapon's Hemorrhaging threshold is reduced by your proficiency bonus.
The weapon's Hemorrhaging threshold is reduced by 1, and the property inflicts 1 additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} count when triggered.

optionalfeature.name: Needled Lacing

prerequisite.other: A suit of armor or set of clothes; requires attunement

entries: With a lining of spikes or other jagged points, this piece of wear has become something that should be handled with care or have someone incur dire consequences.

When an attuned creature suffers damage from another creature within 5-ft, they may spend their reaction to have the item's pointy ends flare out as they are coated by spilled blood. The attacking creature must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC or suffer {@damage 2d4} piercing damage and 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count. On a success, they suffer half the damage and half that {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count, rounded down.

This damage increases by {@dice 1d4} and you deal an additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count when you reach 6th Level in Artificer ({@dice 2d4}, 3 Count) and once more when you reach 12th Level in Artificer ({@dice 3d4}, 4 Count).

optionalfeature.name: Overheated Fueling Mechanism
entries: You create a gadget you can attached to a melee or ranged weapon to have it coat its edges with a dosage of overheated fuel, which starts blazing when exposed to air. You may spend your Bonus Action to ignite, causing your weapon attacks to inflict 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count on hit until the end of your turn. You can use this an amount of times equal to Intelligence Modifier per Long Rest. This Infusion can also be used as an item, that being Uncommon and can be annexed to a weapon by Attuning to it. Instead of the users Intelligence Modifier, it uses their Proficiency Bonus to determine its maximum uses per Long Rest.

optionalfeature.name: Poisoned Spell
entries: {@b Cost:} 2 Sorcery Points

When a creature fails a saving throw against a spell you cast, you can spend 2 sorcery points to give it the {@condition Poisoned|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} condition until the start of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Favored Bullet
entries: You name one of your Magic Bullets as your favorite, exacerbating its effects when you cast {@spell Magic Bullet Fire|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, as shown in the Favored Bullet table.

entries.caption: Favored Bullet
rows: The 1st Magic Bullet
A creature hit by this bullet always takes force damage equal to your warlock level, regardless of whether it succeeded on or failed the saving throw.
The 2nd Magic Bullet

A creature that fails this saving throw becomes {@condition Paralyzed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} until the start of your next turn, except attacks made within 5 feet of it are not automatically critical hits.
The 3rd Magic Bullet
A creature that fails this saving throw deals only half the damage it rolls for the effect's duration.
The 4th Magic Bullet
A creature that fails this saving throw also suffers 4 counts of {@condition Dark Flame|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.
The 5th Magic Bullet
A creature that fails this saving throw has its AC reduced by your proficiency bonus until the end of your next turn.
The 6th Magic Bullet

All creatures within range suffer an additional {@damage 1d6} fire damage for every combined 3 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count among the targets, to a maximum of {@damage 8d6} additional fire damage.
The 7th Magic Bullet
Whenever you or a creature you hit with an attack suffers a critical hit, or rolls a 1 on a saving throw you impose, that creature is beheaded as though by a {@item vorpal sword|DMG|Vorpal Sword}.

entries: The Seventh Magic Bullet is the only exception: its favored effect is always active. If you are beheaded, you instantly die.

optionalfeature.name: Marksman's Repositioning
entries: Sometimes what you need is not the perfect shot, but something to distract opponents while you make a getaway. You learn the {@spell eldritch blast|PHB|Eldritch Blast} cantrip, and it does not count against your warlock cantrips known. When you cast {@spell eldritch blast|PHB|Eldritch Blast}, you can have each bolt deal {@damage 1d4} force damage instead. A target's attack and damage rolls are reduced by 1 for each bolt that hits it. Furthermore, your speed increases by 5 feet until the end of your turn for each bolt fired.

optionalfeature.name: Perfected Marksman's Weapon
entries: You have a near-perfect connection with the Marksman, allowing you to make full use of its Marksman's Weapon. When you first summon it, you can choose its appearance, such as a rifle or longbow, although it functions as a longbow that accepts any kind of ammunition. You are considered attuned to your Marksman's Weapon at all times, and this counts against your attunement limit.

The Marksman's Weapon becomes a +1 weapon when you reach 5th level in the warlock class, a +2 weapon at 11th level, and a +3 weapon at 16th level. It also counts as an arcane focus for your warlock spells, granting the same bonus to your spell attack rolls and spell save DC. This bonus does not stack with other magic items.

During a long rest, you can perform a ritual to feed another magic item to your Marksman's Weapon. The consumed item is destroyed, and the Marksman's Weapon inherits its properties. It can consume only wondrous items and other magic weapons, and it can retain the properties of a maximum of three consumed items at a time. If it consumes another, you must choose one of the previous three sets of properties to be destroyed. Once per turn as a free action, you can change your Marksman's Weapon into any previously consumed weapon, inheriting its properties and damage. If it has consumed a total of three +3 weapons, it permanently has a +4 bonus instead and is considered a legendary magic item.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Scary Faces
entries: You gain proficiency in {@skill Intimidation}, or expertise if already proficient. When you make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}), Charisma ({@skill Deception}), or Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check, you can use {@skill Intimidation} instead. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses when you finish a short or long rest. When making an Intimidation check against a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you can use Strength instead of Charisma.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Lockdown
entries: In place of one attack during the {@action Attack} action, you cause purple chains to burst from your tattoo toward a target within 20 feet. Make a grapple check against it. On a success, both your speed and the target's speed become 0 until the end of its next turn. If the target has {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, your speed is halved instead. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Goading Scowls
entries: While engaged in combat with a creature, when it attacks another creature, you can use your reaction to make your tattoos flash and goad it. It has disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than you until the end of its turn.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Bloody Knuckles
entries: When you cause a creature to suffer {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, it instead suffers {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} until cured. Heavily Bleeding deals {@damage 2d6} damage on the same triggers as Bleed and loses 2 stacks whenever triggered. The {@skill Medicine} check DC to remove it increases by 5.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Stitches
entries: When a creature within 30 feet targets you with a spell, it must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, purple chains wrap around its mouth, preventing it from speaking for 1 minute. It repeats the saving throw at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success. A creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has disadvantage on this saving throw. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Twisting
entries: As an action, you speak a command word and make your body rubbery for up to 1 hour or until you dismiss the effect. You can twist and bend through any opening greater than 1 foot in diameter, gain a +5 bonus to checks made to escape a grapple, and take only half damage from falling.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Ten Thousand Vendettas
entries: As a bonus action, you etch the names of a number of creatures equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, onto your body. Each suffers {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until it is knocked {@condition Unconscious||Unconscious} or dies.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of the Great Wielder
entries: After grappling a Large or smaller creature, you can wield it as a martial weapon with which you are proficient. Such a weapon is two-handed, and it is Heavy unless the creature is Tiny. A Tiny creature deals {@damage 2d4} bludgeoning damage, a Small creature deals {@damage 2d6}, a Medium creature deals {@damage 2d8}, and a Large creature deals {@damage 2d12}. Whenever an attack using the creature hits, the wielded creature takes half the damage dealt. Your speed is reduced by 10 feet while wielding a Medium creature and 20 feet while wielding a Large creature. A creature at 0 hit points instead deals only 1 bludgeoning damage.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Family
entries: If an ally within 30 feet of you also has active magical tattoos on their body, you may spend a bonus action to gain temporary hit points equal to your Unarmed Strike dice + your rage damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Remembrance
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you inflict 1 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Additionally, you gain advantage on {@skill History} checks made to remember events you participated in. You may inflict {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} this way up to two times per turn.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Loyalty
entries: When you hit a creature that has a stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} with an Unarmed Strike, other creatures will gain advantage on their first attack roll against it until the end of the affected creature's turn.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Fists
entries: When you hit a creature with an unarmed attack, you may perform another attack as a bonus action if the creature has a stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. Additionally, you can add your rage bonus to {@skill Intimidation} checks.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Arcana
entries: As an action, you can make your tattoos glow with a magical aura. For 1 minute, or until you dismiss it as an action, you shed bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like. You can take this as a reaction instead of an action when you enter your Rage. While you are glowing, you can spend a bonus action, or do this as part of your reaction when you rage, to force all creatures of your choice within 20 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your Tattoo save DC or become {@condition Frightened} of you until the start of your next turn. Creatures {@condition Frightened} this way take an additional dice of damage from your Unarmed Strikes whenever you hit them. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until your next long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Binding
entries: You can use a bonus action to force an enemy creature to make a Constitution saving throw against your tattoo save DC as magical shackles extend from your tattoos to hold them. If they pass, they take {@dice 1d6} bludgeoning damage as they break off the chains (this damage increases to {@dice 2d6} on 6th level, {@dice 3d6} on 10th level and {@dice 4d6} on 14th level). If they fail, both you and the creature can only use one action per turn until the start of your next turn. Extra attacks cannot be used as part of the same Attack action. This ability can only be used a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and you recover all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Punching
entries: When you make an attack action on your turn using an unarmed melee attack and successfully hit a creature, they must make a Constitution saving throw against your Tattoo save DC or gain one stack of {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. If you managed to hit all of your unarmed attacks made with your attack action this turn and they failed all of your saving throws, they gain 2 stacks of {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} per attack instead. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, and regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Kicking
entries: You can use an action to kick down an enemy's weak spot, leaving them vulnerable for further attacks. As a part of this action, roll an Unarmed Strike against the enemy. If it hits, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw against your Tattoo save DC or become {@condition Paralyzed} for a minute. The creature can reroll the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success. Once you successfully use this ability, you can only use it again after a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Payback
entries: When a creature hits you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you with an attack, you may, as a reaction, immediately move up to that creature without provoking opportunity attacks and hit them with a fortress-breaking punch, leaving a small crater on the floor. They must roll a Constitution saving throw against your Tattoo save DC or take {@dice 10d8} bludgeoning damage and gain one stack of {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. Additionally, you may add {@dice 1d4} to the next attack roll you make, and if it hits, add {@dice 1d4} force damage to the damage roll. On a successful save, they only take half the damage, but you still gain the attack and damage bonus. Once you use this feature, you can only use it again after a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Dominance
entries: A bright light shines from your tattoos, and zaps of electricity signify to all creatures around you the build up of strength you're about to commence when activating this tattoo. As a bonus action, which you may take together with your Rage bonus action, you begin for yourself a Test of the Big Brother. Until the start of your next turn, all enemies have advantage on attacks against you, and you gain vulnerability to all damage types. Once your second turn starts, if you're still alive, you pass the test, removing all the previous conditions. For two rounds, until the end of your second turn after this, you gain advantage on all of your ability checks, attack rolls and saving throws. Additionally, all creatures you attack gain vulnerability to your Unarmed Strikes for the duration.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Vengeance
entries: As an action, you get to dash in a straight line of up to 60 feet towards a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, leaving behind a purple trail of light and energy. This action does not provoke opportunity attacks. All other creatures of your choice in this line must roll a Dexterity saving throw against your Tattoo save DC or take {@dice 2d10} force damage, taking only half that damage on a success. Once you reach the target, you may roll an attack roll against it for each attack roll it has made in its last turn, with a minimum of two. After beating the creature to a pulp, it must make a Constitution saving throw, becoming {@condition Blinded} and {@condition Deafened} until the end of its next turn on a failure due to your thunderous pummeling. Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Wrath
entries: As an action, you accumulate powerful magical energy from your tattoos on your fists, charging up a devastating attack. You punch the ground, immediately shattering it like a crater as long as the material is non-magical. All creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you must roll a Constitution saving throw against your Tattoo save DC. On a failure, they take a number of {@dice d6} of force damage equal to the number of Magical Tattoos you have and are {@condition Stunned} until the start of your next turn. On a success, they take half the damage and suffer no additional effects. You can use this ability twice, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Hemomancy

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: You're particularly adept at controlling your own blood, and soon that of other creatures. You learn Sanguine Authority when you select this Blood Art, Hemorrhaging Gashes at 3rd level, and Exsanguinate at 5th level. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells. You can cast them by spending Blood Charges equal to the spell's level; Sanguine Authority costs no Blood Charges.

optionalfeature.name: Eyes on the Prize

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: As an action, you can spend 3 Blood Charges to focus your senses. You instantly detect the location of any creature with blood within 120 feet of you, seeing a faint afterimage as if it had been pinged by a submarine's radar. This sense is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.
If you extract blood from a creature you've downed within the next minute, you gain 2 Blood Charges instead of 1.

optionalfeature.name: In the Dark of the Night

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: You can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of red and black. You can spend 2 Blood Charges to touch a willing creature and grant it the same darkvision for 1 hour.

optionalfeature.name: Hungry for More

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: When you would be reduced below 1 hit point, you can spend 2 Blood Charges to remain at 1 hit point until the end of your next turn. This cost increases by 1 each time you use it during the same combat and returns to its original cost after a long rest. You also gain 1 level of exhaustion each time you use this feature.

optionalfeature.name: Blood Is Fuel

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: As an action, you can spend 4 Blood Charges to cast {@spell enhance ability|PHB|Enhance Ability} on yourself. You can also spend an equal number of Blood Charges and Hit Dice to gain temporary hit points equal to the total rolled on the expended Hit Dice. Hit Dice spent this way are regained only when you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Hardblood Armaments

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: As a bonus action, you can spend 1 Blood Charge to coalesce your blood into a Hardblood Armament. Choose whether it deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, then choose one of the following configurations:

entries.name: Brutality
entries: The armament deals {@damage 1d12} damage and has the heavy and two-handed properties.

entries.name: Swift Execution
entries: The armament deals {@damage 1d6} damage and has the finesse and light properties. You can create a secondary Hardblood Armament for two-weapon fighting; the secondary armament deals {@damage 1d4} damage.

entries.name: Rain Death
entries: The armament deals {@damage 1d6} damage and has the finesse and thrown (30/60) properties. It dissolves into mist after it hits or misses, and you can resummon it to your hand as a free action.
You must use a bonus action and spend 1 Blood Charge to change your Hardblood Armament's configuration. You are proficient with your Hardblood Armament.

During a long rest, you can bathe a magic weapon in the blood used for your Hardblood Armament. At the end of the rest, the armament gains that weapon's magical properties. The consumed magic item loses all its magical power, which flows into your Hardblood Armament. The armament is magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance to nonmagical attacks.

optionalfeature.name: Transfusion

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: As an action, you can spend a number of Blood Charges up to your proficiency bonus to heal a creature within 5 feet of you, including yourself. The creature regains {@dice 1d4} hit points per Blood Charge spent.

optionalfeature.name: Depraved Consumption

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: While you have fewer than half your maximum Blood Charges, you can use your action to consume a corpse within 5 feet. You regain hit points and Blood Charges based on the size of the creature:

entries.caption: Depraved Consumption
rows: Tiny
Small
{@dice 1d4 + 1}
Medium
{@dice 2d6 + 2}
Large
{@dice 3d6 + 4}

entries: You gain these benefits only if the corpse belonged to a creature that had blood and was not summoned, such as a rat produced by a Bag of Tricks.

optionalfeature.name: The Caring Hand

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: You can spend Blood Charges to generate twice as much Bloodfeast, to a maximum amount of Bloodfeast equal to your proficiency bonus.

optionalfeature.name: Quasi-Formed Bloodbag

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: You can spend 4 Blood Charges to afflict a creature within 30 feet with your blood.
