It must make a Charisma saving throw against a DC equal to 8 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus. On a failure, it becomes a Quasi-Bloodbag for up to 1 minute while you maintain concentration.

You can issue simple commands that don't cause the creature to harm itself directly. On its turn, it acts on instinct and bloodlust and attacks the closest creature. It retains its other abilities and repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature immune to being {@condition Charmed||charmed} automatically succeeds.

optionalfeature.name: Bloody Coating

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: As a bonus action, you can spend a number of Blood Charges up to your proficiency bonus to coat the weapon you are holding in Hardblood. For a number of turns equal to the charges spent, the weapon deals additional piercing damage equal to the charges spent and inflicts 1 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} count on a hit. A coated ranged weapon produces its own Hardblood ammunition.

optionalfeature.name: Higher Presence

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: You gain proficiency in Persuasion if you aren't already proficient, and you can spend 2 Blood Charges to cast {@spell command|PHB|Command}.

A Bloodfiend of lesser rank, or a creature whose level or CR is no greater than half your level rounded up, has disadvantage on the saving throw. A Bloodfiend of greater rank automatically succeeds. A creature whose level or CR is greater than half your level rounded up has advantage on the saving throw.

optionalfeature.name: Family Heirloom

prerequisite.other: Bloodfiend ancestry or a feature that grants a Blood Art

entries: You create a relic small enough to hold in one or both hands. While it is on your person, you can store excess Bloodfeast in it during a long rest, up to an amount equal to your level + your proficiency bonus. As a bonus action, you can retrieve any amount of that stored Bloodfeast.
If the heirloom is lost or destroyed, you can rebuild it during a long rest using 50 gp of fine materials.

item.name: First Seal Removed: Lævateinn
entries: A legendary sword acquired very deep underground after defeating a deadly guardian. Not everyone can wield it, and even less can unlock its full powers.

While attuned to it, you have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and you gain the following characteristics (if any of them require a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Burning Hot
entries: You gain Resistance to Fire damage.

entries.name: Follow-Up Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you may use a Bonus Action to attack an additional time, but you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative, and you don't inflict any Conditions.

entries.name: Wounding Inferno
entries: The first time you hit a creature with this weapon, they suffer 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, your choice.

entries.name: Slam Them Down
entries: You can use an Action to slam your sword into the ground, turning a 10-foot area around you into Difficult Terrain. All creatures within that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 3d6} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition Prone}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects.

entries.name: Looks Like I Gotta Unbox the Second Layer, too.
entries: Upon reaching level 10 in the Vengeance Fighter class or being a worthy wielder of the sword, this Greatsword becomes able to turn into {@item Second Seal Removed: Lævateinn|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. To do so, upon hitting a creature with an attack, you may choose to unseal the sword and release the casing on top of them. They must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 2d8} bludgeoning damage and become {@condition Frightened} until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

item.name: Lævateinn
entries: A legendary sword acquired very deep underground after defeating a deadly guardian. Not everyone can wield it, and even less can unlock its full powers.

While attuned to it, you have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, as well as an extra {@damage 2d6} Fire damage. You also gain the following characteristics (if any of them require a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Scorching Hot
entries: You gain Immunity to Fire damage.

entries.name: Armor of the Fire Giant
entries: As a Bonus Action, for 1 minute you gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class. Additionally, whenever a creature hits you with an attack roll, they take {@damage 1d8} Fire damage. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Follow-Up Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you may use a Bonus Action to attack an additional time, but you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative, and you don't inflict any Conditions.

entries.name: Wounding Inferno
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with this weapon, they suffer 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Melt Away and Die
entries: On a Critical Hit with this weapon, the target creature's skin blackens like charcoal, their veins glowing orange like lava. For the next minute, they suffer a {@dice 1d8} penalty on all ability checks and saving throws. If you score another Critical hit against the same creature, no matter when, they must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be immediately killed, their body melting away into nothing.

entries.name: Slam Them Down
entries: You can use an Action to slam your sword into the ground, turning a 20-foot area around you into Difficult Terrain filled with molten lava. All creatures within that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 8d6} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition Prone}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects. Any creature other than you that enters the area for the first time on their turn or starts their turn within the area immediately takes {@damage 1d6} Fire damage.

entries.name: Burn Through Any Opposition
entries: As an action, you can touch a nonmagical flammable object with this sword and cause it to ignite. If the object isn't being worn or carried, it is reduced to ash at the end of your turn. Additionally, as an action, you can touch a nonmagical wall, floor, or similar structure and melt a 5-foot cube of it, provided the material can be melted by heat.

item.name: Sealed Lævateinn
entries: A legendary sword acquired very deep underground after defeating a deadly guardian. Not everyone can wield it, and even less can unlock its full powers.
While attuned to it, you gain the following characteristics (if any of them require a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Burning Hot
entries: You gain Resistance to Fire damage.

entries.name: Follow-Up Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you may use a Bonus Action to attack an additional time, but you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative, and you don't inflict any Conditions.

entries.name: Slam Them Down
entries: You can use an Action to slam your sword into the ground, turning a 10-foot area around you into Difficult Terrain. All creatures within that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition Prone}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects.

entries.name: Time to Unpack!
entries: Upon reaching level 7 in the Vengeance Fighter class or being a worthy wielder of the sword, this Greatsword becomes able to turn into {@item First Seal Removed: Lævateinn|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. To do so, upon hitting a creature with an attack, you may choose to unseal the sword and release the casing on top of them. They must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage and become {@condition Frightened} until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

item.name: Second Seal Removed: Lævateinn
entries: A legendary sword acquired very deep underground after defeating a deadly guardian. Not everyone can wield it, and even less can unlock its full powers.

While attuned to it, you have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, as well as {@damage 1d6} additional Fire damage. You also gain the following characteristics (if any of them require a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Burning Hot
entries: You gain Resistance to Fire damage.

entries.name: Armor of the Fire Giant
entries: As a Bonus Action, for 1 minute you gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class. Additionally, whenever a creature hits you with an attack roll, they take {@damage 1d8} Fire damage. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Follow-Up Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you may use a Bonus Action to attack an additional time, but you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative, and you don't inflict any Conditions.

entries.name: Wounding Inferno
entries: The first time you hit a creature with this weapon, they suffer 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Slam Them Down
entries: You can use an Action to slam your sword into the ground, turning a 20-foot area around you into Difficult Terrain. All creatures within that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 4d6} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition Prone}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects.

entries.name: Burn Through Any Opposition
entries: As an action, you can touch a nonmagical flammable object with this sword and cause it to ignite. If the object isn't being worn or carried, it is reduced to ash at the end of your turn. Additionally, as an action, you can touch a nonmagical wall, floor, or similar structure and melt a 5-foot cube of it, provided the material can be melted by heat.

entries.name: Unsealed Phenomenon: Lævateinn
entries: Upon reaching level 15 in the Vengeance Fighter class or being a worthy wielder of the sword, this Greatsword becomes able to turn into {@item Lævateinn|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. To do so, upon hitting a creature with an attack, you may choose to unseal the sword and release the casing on top of them. They must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 4d8} bludgeoning damage and become {@condition Frightened} until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

item.name: Little Book of Vengeance
entries: Prerequisites: Be part of the Middle through a Subclass, Background or Feat.

This Book of Vengeance is awarded to all Little Brothers and Sisters of the Middle, and is connected to all other Books of Vengeance of the organization. Anything that is written in the book is shared among all Books of Vengeance, and no matter its size, it manages to magically contain every single page of vengeance. You can read its contents as a free action, and your DM will let you know whether there is any mission currently available for you to undertake and exact vengeance for the Middle.

Additionally, you can write down someone's name on the Book of Vengeance, and any other person that carries a Book of Vengeance will be able to read it and hunt that creature to earn the rewards below.
When you complete a quest from the Little Book of Vengeance, you gain the following benefits:

items: Until the next long rest, with every attack that you hit, you deal {@damage 1d4} extra damage of the same type as the attack.
Until the next long rest, you gain advantage on an ability check of your choice.

item.name: Young Book of Vengeance
entries: Prerequisites: Be part of the Middle through a Subclass, Background or Feat.

This Book of Vengeance is awarded to all Young Brothers and Sisters of the Middle, and is connected to all other Books of Vengeance of the organization. Anything that is written in the book is shared among all Books of Vengeance, and no matter its size, it manages to magically contain every single page of vengeance. You can read its contents as a free action, and your DM will let you know whether there is any mission currently available for you to undertake and exact vengeance for the Middle.

Additionally, you can write down someone's name on the Book of Vengeance, and any other person that carries a Book of Vengeance will be able to read it and hunt that creature to earn the rewards below.
When you complete a quest from the Young Book of Vengeance, you gain the following benefits:

items: Until the next long rest, with every attack that you hit, you deal {@damage 1d6} extra damage of the same type as the attack.
Until the next long rest, you gain advantage on two ability checks of your choice.
You gain a single point of Inspiration that can be used until your next Long Rest.

entries: {@note Little siblings usually take easier quests, suited for players from levels 1 - 5. Young siblings take quests from levels 6 - 10, Big siblings take levels 11 - 17 and Great siblings take quests from levels 18 and above.}

item.name: Golden HHair Coupon
entries: This is a golden ticket to utmost lusciousness, separating those with bristly hair from gods in humanoid form. This ticket is glistening gold, resembling the quality of shininess provided to follicles upon its use and has ancient engravings to allow use for any reputable and/or irreputable hair salon, filling the stylist with vigour and granting them the capability to cultivate the mane of dreams even if they wouldn't be able to cut a shrub with their fingers.

This item may be given to any hair stylist over the course of downtime or a long-rest for you to receive a luscious hair cut, consuming the item in the process. Any stylist must pass a DC 30 Wisdom saving throw or be compelled to give you the hair cut for free, as per the ticket demands. This process takes approximately 30 minutes, and afterward your Charisma score increases by 4, to a maximum of 24. Additionally, you permanently gain Proficiency in one Charisma skill of your choice and Expertise in another Charisma skill of your choice.

If you have not the access to a hair stylist at the given moment, you may read upon the faint engraving at this hair coupon's title, which at first seemed like a misprint doubling the "H" is actually fine print for "Haunted", indicating the capability of invoking a stylish poltergeist that will give you the hair cut instead of a living being in exchange for the ticket when it is folded neatly and then cut in two, as part of the phantom's ghastly ritual of utter lavishness.

entries.name: Cursed: Smells Like Chocolate.
entries: This item is a magnet to be stolen by lowly street dogs, as such any other creature has Advantage on {@skill Stealth} and {@skill Sleight of Hand|Sleight of Hands} to steal this item. When stolen, the thief permanently gains {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, even if they die and are revived. You deal an additional {@damage 1d10} bludgeoning damage on Unarmed Strikes against that creature.

item.name: Sunglasses of Surmountable Style
entries: A pair of golden trimmed and purple lensed sunglasses that radiates stylishness, being one of the few that most people can and should accept to be worn even during night. It is a symbol of class and power within certain families.

entries.name: Advanced Lusciousness
entries: Your Charisma score becomes 23 while Attuned to this item as long as it was lower than this value. Additionally, if you weren't proficient in the Persuasion or {@skill Intimidation} skills you still add half your proficiency bonus to skill checks of either.

entries.name: Curricular in Castigation.
entries: Let your heart beat and be beaten in the name of the family. At the start of your turn you may spend a Bonus Action to adjust your sunglasses and let them shine with a challenge to all - kill you or die trying. You gain Vulnerability to all damage types until the start of your next turn. At the start of your next turn and until its end any damage you deal to others has them be considered Vulnerable to that damage type. If you or a creature made Vulnerable this way would have Resistance to a damage type, they only take an amount of damage equal to the normal damage they would take plus half that same damage. If either were Immune to a damage type, they suffer that damage as if they were not Immune instead.

entries.name: Quality Eye Protection.
entries: You gain Advantage on rolls against effects that would cause you to be blinded. These glasses are just that good.

item.name: Chains of Loyalty
entries: A set of heavy, ostentatious golden chains that are usually rolled up around the wrists and forearms as a symbol of loyalty and the weight of family. To be used they are gripped in the hand and swung like a whip.
If you have any levels in a Middle subclass or the Sibling Background you are considered proficient in this weapon even if you normally wouldn't be.

item.name: Knuckles of Loyalty
entries: A set of heavy golden knuckledusters, housing enough weight to break a face and still retain their luscious shine.
If you have any levels in a Middle subclass or the Sibling Background you are considered proficient in this weapon even if you normally wouldn't be.

item.name: Premium Brand Top Sib's Hair Gel
entries: A premium brand of hair gel that leaves you cool to the touch.

Whenever you hit a friendly creature using this item, you may choose to instead of chucking the bottle full force at their head, having it be a glorious splatter of gel onto their hair. When you do so, you deal no damage and the creature gain a +1 to their Charisma modifier until the end of their next turn.

item.name: Adhesive of Moral Reinforcement
entries: A small sheet of powerfully adorable stickers that can be glued to others to fill them with great happiness.
This sheet holds 5 Stickers that may be spent in the following ways:

items: You may spend a single Sticker to glue it to another creature within 5-ft. of you as a Bonus Action, giving them positive reinforcement and {@dice 1d6} temporary Hit Points. While these Hit Points remain they may once per turn add an additional {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to an ability check, attack roll or saving throw before or after rolling the die, but before the DM determines a result.

You may spend two Stickers at once as an Action to attempt to make another creature within 5-ft. of you find some happiness in their life, instantly causing them to be affected by the {@spell calm emotions} spell with a DC of 10 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier. Irrelevant to this effect's result, the creature feels a little less sad from being recognized in some way.

You may spend three Stickers at once as an Action to overwhelm another creature within 5-ft. of you with resolve, granting them the effects of the {@spell heroism} spell for the next minute. The temporary Hit Points gained through this are instead {@dice 3d4} temporary Hit Points plus your Charisma modifier.

entries: After its effects, any Stickers glued remain through fire and rain, clinging to belongings like memories. Memories are important, after all.

item.name: Beating Box
entries: An overwhelmingly sturdy boombox that has been attached to a set of golden chains. Its beats are solid, ground-breaking and positively skull-crushing.
Bards are considered Proficient with this weapon.

While used by a Bard, this weapon counts as a musical instrument that may be used for Spellcasting and {@skill Performance} checks. Additionally under the same condition this weapon gains the Splash (1d6) property and may be used to deal thunder damage instead of bludgeoning, as a Bard best knows how to lay a beatdown with sound alone.

item.name: Tattoo Set of Confidence
entries: A set of intricate tattoos that make use of their wearer's confidence to harden muscles to protect the flesh from any damage the user would suffer. These are usually worn with leather or pelt-based clothing onto to further bolster their wearer's confidence in themselves.

This armor is a set of tattoos that glow whenever active, as such it cannot be doffed without specialized means yet may be covered by other clothing or even armor. While wearing armor over a Tattoo Set, you must choose to benefit from the effects of only one of the armors.

Due to the glow of these tattoos you have Disadvantage on {@skill Stealth} checks unless you are proficient in the {@skill Deception} skill or have expertise in the {@skill Stealth} skill, as you are more knowledgeable on how to mask such unnatural lights as a common part of the scenery or obfuscate that glow altogether.

item.name: Cursed Fireworks
entries: A modified lever-action rifle that acts as a shotgun. However, this modification is only the make-up for a much more devilish change that has been granted to this cursed creation.
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: A Pact With The Devil.
entries: This weapon's long range does not incur Disadvantage on attacks.

entries.name: The Power to Tear Open All Sides.
entries: Only one attack may be made using this weapon during your turn. When you do so, all creatures within 5-ft. of the original target are also targeted by the attack. You roll to hit only once and consider that result against the individual AC of each affected creature, also rolling damage only once for all.

entries.name: Iron sights on a Hazy Heart.
entries: This weapon is cursed to blow up the beloved persons in one's heart. If you are aware of two people who love each other platonically or romantically and deal damage to one while the other can see or hear, the other also suffers half the damage dealt as psychic damage. Whenever you Reload this weapon, if you have a beloved person yourself they suffer {@damage 3d8} piercing damage upon you firing the last bullet in this weapon's magazine. You may choose to otherwise suffer that damage yourself.

item.name: Beak-Shaped Necklace
entries: A mysterious necklace made with small pellets reminiscent of gunpowder bullets and a sharp beak from an unknown bird at the center. Whenever you make a ranged attack that spends ammunition, you gain 5 feet of movement for ammunition spent this way until the start of your next turn. If all attacks you made hit, you gain advantage on ranged attack next turn.
Additionally, your attacks that inflict counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} deal an additional {@damage 1d6} piercing damage.

item.name: Staticky Two-Way Radio
entries: A strange communication device that never seems to reach anyone, it only transmits a buzzing static sound. Whenever you make a ranged attack that spends ammunition, you gain 5 feet of movement for each ammunition spent this way until the start of your next turn. If all attacks you made hit, you gain advantage on your first ranged attack next turn.
Additionally, your attacks that inflict counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} deal an additional {@damage 1d6} cold damage.

item.name: Pink Petals
entries: A vine covered in a bundle of pink petals that produce an aroma which brings with it feelings of melancholy and nostalgia. Whenever you would inflict counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} inflict 1 count of {@condition Pink Petals|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} as well. Inflict 1 additional count of {@condition Pink Petals|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} if the creature already has 5 or more counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

item.name: Still-Warm Coffee
entries: A cup of coffee that never loses its warmth, no matter how many days it spends out in the cold. This item holds no nutritional value, but drinking from it brings a powerful boost. As a bonus action, you can drink from this beverage to give yourself {@dice 1d10} temporary hit points. If you have all of your Hit Points, you also gain advantage on your first attack each turn for 1 minute.
If you drink more than 1 Still-warm Coffee before a Long rest, you suffer 1 point of {@condition Exhaustion} when its effects wear off.

item.name: Royal Jelly Perfume
entries: A strange bottle of perfume made from an extract of monstrous bees. As a Bonus Action, you can spray yourself with the perfume bottle to gain {@condition Pheromone|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, which lasts for 1 minute or until the end of combat if you enter one while it is still active. Whenever a {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning} enemy hits you, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by {@dice 1d8}.

Additionally, at the end of your turn, the creature that dealt most damage to you during the last round suffers from {@condition Pheromone Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} If no creature dealt damage to you, choose 1 hostile creature at random.

item.name: Harmonics
entries: A strange, bloodied instrument infused with dark magic and put together with scraps of a dark machine. Whenever a creature is knocked {@condition Unconscious} or suffers a Critical Hit, every creature that is not {@condition Deafened} within 30 feet of you suffers 1 count of {@condition Fragility|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

If you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you applies counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} while there are Fragility creatures within 30 feet of you because of this effect, all friendly creatures within 30 feet of you lose 1 count of {@condition Fragility|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, and the attacked creature suffers an additional 3 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

item.name: Walking Bass
entries: A serrated instrument infused with dark magic and put together with scraps of a dark machine. At the start of your turn in combat, you may choose to gain 1 count of {@condition Hyped-Up|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} as a free action. Whenever you hit a creature with an attack, but before you apply damage, roll a {@dice d20}.

On a roll of 16 or higher, you and 1 random friendly creature within 30 feet of you that isn't {@condition Deafened} gains 1 count of {@condition Hyped-Up|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} If it was an attack that inflicts counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} it happens on a roll of 11 or higher instead.

entries.name: Curse
entries: You love the sound of your own music too much, so you can't go without listening to it during the chaos of combat. If you spend more than 2 turns without Hyping yourself up, you hear discordant notes inside your mind, taking {@damage 2d6} psychic damage that cannot be reduced in any way.

item.name: Desperado
entries: A skull steel case filled with empty rounds of Ammunition that somehow empower you by their presence alone. You gain 10 feet of movement and a +1 to all Ranged attacks that spend Ammunition, as long as you already don't have a +3 from external sources.

At the start of your turn, if you only have 6 or less pieces of ammunition remaining, gain 1 count of {@condition Desperado|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. At the end of your turn, you can spend a Bonus Action to make an additional Ranged attack against a creature within range as long as you have counts of Desperado Additionally, you always recover all spend Ammunition when searching for it after a fight as long as it wasn't destroyed.

entries.name: Not My First Rodeo
entries: As a Reaction to when a creature moves or uses an Action, Bonus Action or Reaction within reach of one of your ranged weapon attacks, you can immediately make a Ranged attack against them. If it hits, they must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Dexterity modifier) or become {@condition Stunned} until the end of their next turn. Once you use this ability, you can only do so again after the next dawn if the creature failed the saving throw.

item.name: Pink Bouquet
entries: A magical bouquet of flowers empowered by the energy of a Domain of Pleasure's Spring season. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a ranged attack, you deal an additional 5 ({@damage 1d10}) piercing damage until the end of your next turn. Whenever you knock a hostile creature unconscious with a ranged attack, you gain an additional 10 feet of movement for 1 minute.

Additionally, whenever a friendly creature within 30 feet of you inflicts counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a creature, that creature also suffers 1 count of {@condition Pink Petals|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} the creature is already Sinking they suffer an additional count of {@condition Pink Petals|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} and 1 count of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
At the start of your turn, choose a creature within 30 feet of you that is Sinking, they lose 10 feet of movement until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Spring's Genesis
entries: As an Action, all terrain within a 100-foot radius centered on you becomes fertile, and immediately grows patches of grass and pink flowers. If there were already seeds planted on the ground, they germinate immediately and yield fruits.

If you do this in an area already taken over by nature, the plants grow beyond their natural abilities and the area becomes thick and overgrown with plant life, turning into difficult terrain. Any ice or snow present within the area immediately thaws and melts, and any fire burning outside of a container is extinguished.
Once you use this ability, you can only do so again after the next dawn.

item.name: BongBong Orange
entries: This slimy, yet delicious bubble dropped from a verminous creature is extremely healthy and, sadly, addictive. As a Bonus Action, any creature may eat this or feed it to a willing creature. The creature regains {@dice 6d4 + 6} hit points. They must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 14) or become addicted to the substance and unable to heal from anything else or eat anything else until their next Long Rest. This DC increases by 2 each time this item is consumed before a Long Rest.

item.name: Bolt Rifle
entries: A powerful weapon made to take targets down from afar, possessing a bolt-action mechanism to fire rounds at unparalleled speed and force.

item.name: Heavy Gauntlet
entries: A metallic glove made specially to allow for heavy punches instead of the usual defense a gauntlet provides.

entries.name: Special
entries: Heavy Gauntlets are meant to facilitate the use of your hands while being donned, yet still have their limitations. While donning a Heavy Gauntlet, you can still use that hand to cast Somatic components or interact with objects, but the metal makes it impossible to wield another weapon over it.

item.name: Heavy Revolver
entries: A steel-made revolver capable of causing heavy damage, but remaining unwieldy due to it's unwieldy kickback.

item.name: Single-Stroke Katana
entries: A sleek sword meant to end fights quickly after it's drawn from its sheath.

item.name: Basillisoup Ladle
entries: A large pole made by the clerics who follow the Lifestew, it dons a beak-like apparatus at its end that contains everflowing soup. It's scalding hot and exceedingly tough to handle by someone who knows not the ways of the stew.

entries.name: Stir the Stew.
entries: You may spend your bonus action to magically reheat the stew inside the ladle, having it become piping hot for this turn. When you do so, it deals an additional {@damage 1d8|d8} fire damage and inflicts a total of 3 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. This lasts until the start of your next turn, where it becomes Warm, dealing regular damage and 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} only. After another turn, it becomes cold, dealing cold damage instead.

entries.name: Force-Feed.
entries: As an action during your turn, you may perform a melee weapon attack against a prone creature to force-feed it. On a hit, you deal an additional {@damage 1d8|d8} of fire damage and inflict 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on that creature.

item.name: Little Harbinger Bird
entries: {@i "The bird fights its way out of the egg. The egg is the world. Whoever will be born must destroy a world."}

A tiny round bird that could fit in your hand. Its feathers are umbral in pigmentation, devouring light as if the world itself was temporarily erased in its space - Despite that, it has bright white dots for eyes that calmly peer into others' souls. This bird will herald the dawn of change wherever it goes.

entries.name: Canary in the Coalmine
entries: The Bird acts a Familiar linked to you as per the {@spell find familiar|PHB|Find Familiar} spell, using the {@creature eagle|MM|Eagle} stat block, except it is Tiny and has an amount of Hit Points equal to 10 times your level. You also cannot see or hear through its senses, but it is able to reliably use a bunch of chirps, cute gestures and a psychic connection to perfectly convey what it saw to you when necessary. If killed or if it has missing hit points, the Bird can be brought back or be healed through a ritual you may perform over the course of 10 minutes or a short or long rest; Once hatched, a fledgling of apocalypse can hardly be forever stopped.

entries.name: The First Trumpet
entries: The Harbinger Bird is attentive, realizing details as small as itself with ease, and its makes use of its shockingly strident singing to echo out alarm when danger approaches. The Bird always knows whenever a creature with hostile intent enters a 120-ft. area of yourself or prepares to deliver a particularly powerful attack on their next turn, such as a Dragon's Breath weapon. It does so by chirping a song that can be heard by creatures within 30-ft. of you or, if you order it to be sneaky about it, by pecking you softly at a rhythm.

entries.name: Wade Through the Worlds
entries: Once per long rest you may order the bird to step through the worlds of darkness and light as a Bonus Action. When you do so, choose between Dark and Light:

items: {@b Wade to Darkness.} The bird distorts a 60-ft. radius around you, extending the pure blackness of its body to cover it as per the effects of the {@spell darkness|PHB|Darkness} spell, except it does not require Concentration and you may end it as a Free Action and you plus a number of creatures of your choice can see through this magical darkness.

{@b Wade to Light.} The bird's eyes flash and dispels all illusions, reveals all {@condition Invisible} creatures and repels all magical darkness within a 30-ft. radius around you, establishing order once again for you to benefit from.

item.name: Feather of the Plagued
entries: People often mistake the dark coloration of this long raven feather and its namesake as some sort of ill-omen bringing filth and pestilence, yet the reality is that the feather itself seems to seek the broken and sickly to grant them respite. Upon attuning to this item, you can almost feel a welcoming presence comforting you whenever you take a long rest, one that you could only describe as gentle. When taking a short rest, you may instead of rolling your Hit Die to restore hit points, you may simply choose to restore your hit points as if you had rolled the maximum value for half of your total Hit Die.

In addition, when taking a long rest you heal double the amount of Exhaustion points you have, you also have advantage on any checks to resist disease and sickness that you might have contracted. In addition to this, you gain resistance to any damage taken whose origin is magical and have advantage on spell Saving Throws. The feather's black coloring slowly turns paler as it is attuned to.

On the twelfth time it is attuned to, counting only attunements from different cretures, it turns fully white, not granting any benefit on further attunements. In addition, all creatures who once have benefitted from its effects start seeing life itself as a disease to be cured, becoming hostile to nearly all creatures. If they were dead, they are revived and dug out of the earth if buried, filled with that one notion to flock around the feather and destroy all in their path so the world may begin anew.

All of the once-attuned gain a +3 bonus to all of their rolls, resistance to all damage types except Radiant damage, of which they gain immunity. Their alignment is also changed to Lawful Evil and will do anything in their power to protect the feather. This occurs for all of the previously attuned except for the 12th creature to have attuned to this item, who instead retains their alignment and any damage they would deal to the other previously-attuned is instead considered as if they had vulnerability, disregarding the damage type inflicted.
In addition, the 12th gains the ability of destroying the feather through cremation in sanctified incense.

item.name: A Crow's Favorite Candy
entries: This little of dark candy tastes like licorice and most likely is licorice, with the odd fact that there is an intense kindness emanating from it. When consumed, you feel a warmth around you as if an angel's wing was curled over your shoulder, protecting you from wordly pains. You gain 7 temporary hit points and gain resistance to non-magical Slashing, Piercing and Bludgeoning damage for the next minute.

item.name: Good Intent
entries: An old, ornate walking cane carved out of an ancient tree, dark purple in its color. When held close to ones chest, a burning desire is felt. It sports the head of a crow at its top and a razor-sharp talon at its bottom.

When attuned, this weapon counts as a +1 arcane focus and any spells cast through it that deal necrotic damage also have that damage count as radiant damage for the purposes of overcoming resistence, vulnerability and immunity. Additionally, if your roll on a spell attack is equal to 20 before any modifiers, the target creature(s) cannot recover a value of hit points equal to the damage dealt for the next week, as they feel an overwhelming dread looming over them.

item.name: Ravenous Clipped Wings
entries: A pair of bladed tonfas that curve inwards, resembling wings in the middle of beating. Both of them emit the constant smell of iron, and its wielders often report feeling a greater appetite. The weight of each tonfa belies their sleek design.

This weapon is considered to have a +1 to your attack and damage modifiers, in addition, whenever you score a critical hit against a creature while using the Ravenous Clipped Wings, you heal for half the damage dealt. Additionally, when you take the attack action, you may spend one charge to perform a Ravenous Wingbeat attack. Ravenous Wingbeat.

You deliver a violent attack onto a victim, draining them of their nutrients and absorbing all of them into yourself. Perform a melee weapon attack against any target within your reach, on a hit, you heal for half of the damage dealt. You may then spend any further attacks you would have had to automatically hit the same target, shering into their flesh with the Wings toothed blades, dealing a further {@damage 1d4} slashing damage and healing for that damage dealt.
This weapon has 3 charges, and you regain all uses on a long rest, additionally it recovers one charge every time you'd gain a point of exhaustion because of starvation.

item.name: Red Spider Fang
entries: A ornate rapier that seems to be made from some sort of ebony metal. Its guard is like webbing held by six spider legs curling inwards toward the hand. Whenever a particularly vicious strike is dealt, its wielder can swear the legs move, and they feel the fleshy, wet feeling of a bright red eye opening on the hilt against their palm.

You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, or a +2 instead against creatures that are below you on the initiative order by a difference of 3 or higher. In addition, whenever your roll to hit's result is a 16- 20 before any modifiers, you inflict one Paralyze on the target. Paralyze deducts an amount to the afflicted's initiative score equal to each stack of Paralyze is on a given creature.
All stacks are destroyed on the end of the afflicted's turn.

item.name: The Last Drop
entries: This silver laden goblet has no discernible features on its surface, with no special engraving apart from lattice-like scratches resembling a wine racket. Its contents are a nearly overflowing amount of deep red wine, which never seems to overflow, not even when the cup is fully turned does the liquid fall. When consumed, you become instantly attuned to The Last Drop as the overly sweet taste overtakes your senses and you feel an emptiness in your heart slowly form.

While attuned, you have a constant longing for more wine, as you feel it is the only thing you may do to acknowledge that your life had any successes. At the beginning of a long rest, you must pass a DC 14 ( Plus however many times you've already consumed from the Last Drop ) or consume more of the liquid, which never empties. For each time you drink, you feel a heavier weight placed upon your heart, until you can't handle it anymore, eventually wasting away.

For each time you've consumed, you lose one hit die until this condition is cured. If you have no hit die left to lose, you start taking an amount of typeless damage equal to your hit die, for an amount equal to however many "negative" hit die you have. This condition may only be cured with the {@spell greater restoration|PHB|Greater Restoration} or {@spell remove curse|PHB|Remove Curse} spells, or similar means.
Upon curing, you restore one of your destroyed Hit Die, and regain one more on each further long rest.

item.name: Bandages of Inner Healing
entries: "Life can be hard, but thats okay." This looks like a completely normal roll of bandages, yet there's something about holding them that makes you feel calmer. A full roll has 3 uses, and the bandages may be applied to a creature within 5-feet reach as an action. When applied, the target creature is healed for {@damage 2d8+4} hit points and it feels weirdly soothed.

If the target creature is in a state of mental distress ( At the DMs discretion ) or has taken psychic damage in the last minute, the bandages can sense that hurt, healing an additional {@dice 2d8} damage and causing the creature to let out part of the weight on their shoulders, albeit momentarily. The creature gains resistance to psychic damage for one minute, and must pass a DC 15 Wisdom Saving throw or start crying, taking a -1 penalty to hit for the duration. As tears fall, they are magically soaked in by the bandages, which feed on the pained's tears and grow into more cloth for the roll, regaining one of its uses.

item.name: Thorns Of Regret
entries: A warhammer bearing an immeasurable weight not in the physical sense, but to its wielders mind. Its malformed head bears spikes that tear into its target's flesh, yet so does its handle, so that its wielder may quickly learn the weight of their own actions. You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, but you take half the damage dealt on each hit, in addition, you gain the Regret condition until the end of your next turn.

Metallic Ringing. While afflicted with Regret, your attacks become more unhinged. On a roll of 18-20 before modifiers, your attack deals an additional {@damage 1d8} thunder damage as the metal makes sounds reverberate inside the targets head in an unbearable droning.

Regret. A creature with Regret feels the weight of their sins on their mind, yet it must be beared, lest the mind break fully. For the duration of Regret, the creature has disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws, but the dulling of its mind renders more focus to the body, gaining advantage on Constitution saving throws.

item.name: Little Wings
entries: A cloth patch of a pair of small wings with a pale blue color that can easily be sewn into clothes. Rumours say it was made by a small child with sorcerous abilities who simply wanted to rid the world of evil, so they ran as much as they could to work on that dream, despite their little legs. To attune to this item, you must sew it into a piece of clothing you are wearing.

Fluttering Wings Once per long rest, you may tap the patch as a bonus action to activate it. While active, tiny spectral wings hover over your shoulder and you gain a fly speed equal to your walking speed for one minute. You cannot, however, stay afloat in air, as your wings are to weak to fully carry you.
You fall 10-feet per round spent in the air. Additionally, if the Wings are inactive and you would take fall damage, they activate by themselves to negate that damage, even if they were used before.

item.name: Teeth of Perseverance
entries: A simple looking necklace sporting sharp teeth as its main piece. When attuned to it, you feel your determination towards your goals being slightly amplified, as if it were easier to focus on such. Once per day, when you would fail a roll, you may spend your reaction to re-roll the dice, possibly turning a failure into a success, as you feel the necklace feel almost alive, it's sharp tooth pecking at your chest to motivate you onward.

item.name: Pale Dagger
entries: This pale dagger seems meek and brittle, yet it will never break. When it senses its wielder taking particularly grievous wounds, its blade turns a deep red and seeks punishment.

When a creature scores a critical hit against you, you can use your reaction to make an attack against that creature with advantage. If the attack hits, it is considered a critical hit and deals an additional {@damage 4d4} piercing damage.

item.name: Shard from Beyond
entries: attunement) 1 lb. (435 kg) {@dice 1d6} piercing - reach This spear seems to always change its shape slightly when looked at for a second time, as it still seeks its form much after it's left a forge. When attuned to, its wielder can feel the spear always trying to explore the back of its thoughts, so it may finally find what it wants to be.

While unformed, its black surface nearly seems like a child's scribbles, with crude little drawings detailing it. You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Moment of Clarity.

While attuned, if either your Intelligence or Wisdom scores are higher than 14, you may sometimes reach a special synchrony with the spear. Whenever you roll an 18 or higher to hit, before any modifiers, the spear coalesces into a more tangible form, becoming smoother and more well finished. It remains like that for a minute, and for the duration it deals {@damage 1d8} piercing damage and gives a +2 bonus to hit and to damage rolls instead of a +1.

item.name: Lureberries
entries: A green berry that always emits a vibrant light when its squeezed. Seems incredibly appetizing and its hard to control the urge to simply eat it. These berries can have many uses depending on who gets their hands on them, even more-so for adventurers.

As such, it may be sold for 100 GP per berry, or used for one of the following concotions: Lureblade Oil. By grinding a berry to a fine paste, you may coat the liquid on a weapon as a bonus action. For the next ten minutes, you may use your bonus action to raise the blade and shake it, causing the liquid to shine in a bright light.

Any creature besides you must pass a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Blinded||blinded} and {@condition Deafened||deafened} until the end of their next turn, as they can only focus on the bright light. Creatures who have resisted against or suffered the effects from Lureberries have advantage against this check. Lying Flytrap Phial.

During a long rest, you may use a Lureberry and 20 GP in other ingredients to brew them into a potion called the Lying Flytrap Phial. To do so, you must be proficient in Alchemist's Supplies and have a set for use. When consumed, this potion grants its consumer the effects of heightened resistance to any sort of enchantment, for the next ten minutes they have advantage against any Charisma saving throws and to resist Enchantment spells.

item.name: Hungry Hand Puppets
entries: The child always loved playing the dragon, it was in their blood afterall. It was a shame when they decided that their chivalrous friends would no longer touch their hoard, and they didn't know how much of a dragon lied beneath their skin. A pair of fluffy mittens that almost look like little cotton balls if not for the chattering teeth at its sides.

It fully covers the fingers, forcing it so a puppet-like mouth is the only type of shape your hand can take as you wear this. While attuned to the pair of mittens, the palms protude sharp teeth that gash and gnaw, and you always feel a tinge of elation to all you do, as if a filter were placed upon your perception of the world, making it all feel more chivalric. This weapon is considered to have a +1 to your attack and damage modifiers, in addition, it can hold up to 5 charges.

It regains one charge each time you deal damage to an enemy. You may spend charges to perform one of the following actions: Feast for the Chivalrous. As part of your action, you may spend 5 charges to indulge in a great feast.

Until the end of your turn, this weapon's damage die is changed to a d12, and you heal for half the damage dealt, as the mouthes in your gloves grow to gnaw away at your foes. Whirlwind of Om-Nom-Nom. By spending 5 charges and your action, you may perform an attack on each creature of your choice within a 5-feet radius of yourself.
You heal 2 hit points for each hit creature.

item.name: Forestkeeper's Bell
entries: attunement) 1 lb. (435 kg) {@dice 1d12} thunder - versatile(d12),reach A massive silver bell held at the end of a quarterstaff. Its sound, when played near a creature can be made to reverberade so loud it hurts.

Rumours say that this bell was crafted by a lone druid who'd tend to the animals every single day, playing the bell twice when the critters grew old and perished. After centuries of this, the souls of the animals laid to rest grew to miss their old friend, and the ringing of that peaceful bell, still holding on for the chance another creature could come and play it for them. Don't Leave Us.

When you become attuned to this weapon, the spirits of various critters hold onto you for their comfort. If you attempt to unattune from this weapon, you must pass a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, you take 2 points of exhaustion as you feel a shortness of breath overtake you, as if you were being clung to tightly.

We'll Help. If you would be reduced below one hit point, you instead mantain one hit point until the end of your next turn, as the spirits of wildlife keep you wide awake for a last chance of success, lest they are left alone because of the claws of death once more.

item.name: The Red Axe
entries: versatile(d10), Hemorrhaging(15-20) A true lumberjack doesn't mind how tired he is, nor what kind of wood he cuts into. There will never be greater elation than feeling the warmth of freshly cut sap dig into their fingernails as they once again fell another, nor when they hear the logs roll over. This handaxe reeks of blood yet it looks incredibly well preserved, almost hypnotic.

When you attune to this weapon, you cannot unattune from it, save for the effects of the {@spell remove curse|PHB|Remove Curse} spell. Sanguine Desire. While attuned to this weapon, all your senses feel heightened, mere passing moments of joy turn into elation, small annoyances into heavy grievances and so on.

As such, you gain advantage on any {@skill Performance} checks, as they become much more genuine, yet your clouded judgement has you suffer disadvantage on any {@skill Insight} checks. Additionally, there is a bloodlust that instills in you, feeling completely natural. When you reduce a creature below 1 hit point during combat, this weapon gains a cumulative +1 bonus to hit and to its damage rolls, to a maximum of +3.

You cannot deal non-lethal damage with this weapon, nor use any other weapon to attack while attuned to the Red Axe. Additionally, in the same turn when you kill a creature, you must spend all your remaining attacks to slash at the body, all to satiate your bloodlust.

item.name: Flesh Pipe
entries: This flute reeks of the smell of damp blood. Its appearence is rather common, made from some silverish metal and with intricate details of musical notes littering all of its surface. When played, its instinctual for you to play a hauntingly beautiful tune.

Song from the Heart. As an action, once per day you may start playing a melody that makes the body curl inside itself, unraveling minds from its sheer beauty. This song lasts for up to one minute, with concentration rules applying to it.

At the start of your turn, all creatures within 60-feet of you that can hear must pass a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw or be afflicted by the melody, becoming {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to it. An {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature is considered {@condition Charmed||charmed} and will obey your commands, as long as the music does not stop. On their turns, they focus on attacking any other creature that isn't addicted until they are dead, doing their best to achieve such goal.

If a creature that is {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} listens to the song until its end, the effect of {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} does not fade until it is dispelled through the {@spell remove curse|PHB|Remove Curse} spell or similar means, blindly following you in hopes of hearing the song again. Before that happens, though, an {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature may attempt to retry the saving throw at the end of their turns. Feed the Machine!

As a bonus action during your turn while playing Song from the Heart, you may start casting a spell through the flute, any corpses within 30-feet of yourself start convulsing and caving into themselves, adding unto the bloody melody. {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creatures gain a cumulative +1 to their attack and damage rolls, alongside gaining 5 temporary hit points per corpse that joins the melody, losing all these bonuses on the song's end. Additionally, the Saving throw for breaking free from {@condition Addicted|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} increases by 1 per corpse that has been forced into the song.

item.name: Saw Guitar
entries: This weapon has the {@itemProperty Hemorrhaging|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} property (18-20).

A fully metallic guitar featuring a buzzsaw as its base, rendering it useful in the act of both shredding a chord or shredding another creature to bits. Despite being in its lonesome, this guitar always sounds as if it were plugged to an amplifier. While attuned, if you are proficient with any string instruments, you are considered proficient with the Saw Guitar.

Additionally, you may choose for Charisma to be your main modifier using this weapon instead of Strength, it also counts as a bardic focus. You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and it may hold up to 8 charges. You may spend them to use the abilities described below.

Charges are restored by {@dice 1d4+1} at dawn, or by 1 whenever your bardic inspiration is used by another creature. The abilities below have a range of a 30-feet radius with you as its center, and only willing creatures of your choice may be affected unless described as otherwise. Please work harder!You may spend your action and 3 charges to turn your playing into a resolute, low-tone solo, droning in the background of the fight.

Until the end of your next turn, all willing creatures listening to you feel an urge to push themselves to no end. They suffer a penalty of -2 AC, yet gain a +2 to hit with their attacks. Additionally, you gain a +1 bonus to your own AC per creature affected by this.

Lets make music! As an action, you may spend 4 charge and start playing a frenetic solo, contagiating any willing creature so they give their maximum. Until the start of your next turn, all creatures affected by this deal a critical hit on one value less, such as a roll of 19 before any modifiers being considered a critical hit.

Additionally, affected all creatures deal an additional {@dice 1d8} dice of slashing damage. Harmony of Despair. When a friendly creature reduces a creature below one hit point within this weapons range, you may spend 6 charge and use your reaction to start harmonizing the sounds of tearing flesh with your guitar.

The creature downed automatically takes a hit as its flesh begins to be cut, as if the buzzsaw were on them, and all hostile creatures within reach must pass a Charisma Saving throw against your Spell Save DC or take {@dice 3d8} + your Charisma modifier in psychic damage, as the harmony cuts through their mind. If any creature would be knocked below one hit point by Harmony of Despair, the same creatures must repeat the Saving Throw, taking the same damage on failure. This repeats for a maximum of two times.

item.name: Manatek Charger
entries: A round contraption thats painted in a smooth white finishing. It passively has lightning arch around it when fully charged, and may be used for a boost on ranged weapons by simply attaching it near the ammunition's shooting method. During a long rest, you may attach the Charger onto a ranged weapon, while attached, the weapon ignores the loading condition and needs no ammunition, as the Charger generates ammunition made of pure arcana.

Once per day you may spend your action to do have the Charger create copies of the ammunition fired from your weapon, acting as a volley. When you take this action, you may choose to target up to three creatures on your next attack and then attack with your attached weapon. If special ammunition was used for this, it retains its properties.

item.name: Grinder Mk4
entries: handed This polearm ending in a circular shape with a smiling face drawn on it has spikes protuding from its head, as a saw lays concealed inside. As a reaction taken when you deal damage to a creature using this weapon, you may turn on the grinder, forcing the creature to pass a Constitution Saving Throw whose DC is equal to your 8 + Strength modifier + your Proficiency Bonus or take an addiitonal {@damage 4d4} slashing damage.

item.name: Galaxy Egostone
entries: A waystone, guiding one heart to another in their connected galaxy. This twinkling, dark-colored geode is finely engraved to nearly look like a coin, its center exposing the shining white core of the outer-space mineral. This Egostone, when attuned, also absorbs a little of the attuned creature's mana to fully connect to them, and the attuned must speak aloud a new command word for it.

This attunement does not break save for the creature who attuned unattuning or the spell {@spell dispel magic|PHB|Dispel Magic} be cast unto it. An Egostone is meant to be exchanged with another, so two souls may always be able to see eachother. With an action, you may speak the stone's command word, when you do soo a magical illusion showing its attuned creatures whole body and 20-foot area around them or from their shoulders up appears, and you can hear everything around 30-feet of them clearly.

When you speak, you may choose to let the creature hear you and consequently everything else within a 10-foot radius of the stone, where the creature will telepathically hear everything inside their head.

item.name: Vial of Unicorn Tears
entries: One always must think to themselves how a product was taken from nature, yet this one? This one will bring tears to yourself. When consumed, you are healed for {@damage 8d8+8} hit points as the unicorns purity washes over all of your body, a sense of innocence and care swealling in your heart.

After you are healed by this, you must pass a DC 18 Charisma saving throw or start crying uncontrollably as the memories of what caused such a creature to cry flood your mind's eye. While crying, you have disadvantage on attack rolls and to maintain concentration. Evil-aligned creatures have advantage against this saving throw.

item.name: Departure in the Shade
entries: An ebony colored pistol with fancy white engravings at its sides. Holding it gives a sense of determination to follow ones duty, yet when held alone you can sense a feeling of longing for its other wing. This Weapon has its own ammunition that is created magically when you reload, which you can do as a bonus action.

Reloading this way grants you 12 bullets for both Departure and Homecoming. You have a +2 to attack and damage rolls using this weapon, in addition to the following: TwinWings. This weapon's properties shown below are only active if you are attuned to both Departure in the Shade and Pale Homecoming.

In addition to those abilities, while attuned to both any damage you deal with this weapon also counts as radiant damage for the purposes of overcoming resistance and vulnerability. Absorbing the Light. The damage inflicted by this weapon fuels souls to keep on fighting for peace.

Every time you deal damage with it, this weapon and Pale Homecoming gain 1 collective charge. Upon delivering a critical hit against a hostile creature, you gain 2 charges instead. All charges . dissipate at the end of combat or after one minute.
You start combat without charges. Calm in the Shade. When you spend your bonus action with this weapon, you may spend a number of charges to heal yourself.

You're healed by {@dice 1d8+1} per 2 charges spent, to a maximum of 8 charges spent. Gravekeeper's Duty. As part of your attack action, you may trade one of your attacks to cast the {@spell spare the dying|PHB|Spare the Dying} spell without expending a spell slot by using 2 charges.

item.name: Pale Homecoming
entries: special. An ivory colored pistol with ornate black engravings at its sides. Holding it makes you feel at peace with yourself, yet when held alone the weapon also emits a sense of loneliness.

This Weapon has its own ammunition that is created magically when you reload, which you can do as a bonus action. Reloading this way grants you 12 bullets for both Homecoming and Departrure. You have a +2 to attack and damage rolls using this weapon, in addition to the following: TwinWings.

This weapon's properties shown below are only active if you are attuned to both Pale Homecoming and Departure in the Shade. In addition to those abilities, while attuned to both any damage you deal with this weapon also counts as necrotic damage for the purposes of overcoming resistance and vulnerability. {@condition Shimmering|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Light. As part of your Attack action, you may spend charges to switch one of your attacks to instead shoot a friendly creature within reach.

This shot does not deal damage, instead healing them for an amount of {@dice 1d6+1} for each 2 charges spent. Fear Not Death. As a reaction to when a creature within 30-feet of you becomes {@condition Frightened} or {@condition Charmed}, you may spend 4 charges and 6 ammunition to offload a hail of magical bullets that restore their mental state, ending the condition instantly.

item.name: The Life Story of a Gravekeeper
entries: This is a hefty and worn logbook of a nameless gravekeeper who had been collecting the stories of theri graveyards inhabitants for years now. When attuned, you feel the amalgamated spirit of so many tales swerve around in the book. Once per day, you may peer into the book to get a gleamse of its wisdom, granting you a d8 bonus to one skill check until your next long rest.

item.name: Sharpshooter's Smoking Pipe
entries: An ornate smoking pipe made out of dark wood and blue engravings, it never seems to need any tabbacco, instead puffing out clouds of celestial smoke when puffed on, resembling the stars in the sky. When an attuned creature uses their bonus action to smoke from this pipe, they feel their heart feel colder, as if hugged by frost. They also learn instinctively the exact location of a creature of your choice that you have seen in your life.

You only know where they are at that given moment, yet if within your attack range, you gain advantage to hit this creature until the end of your turn after smoking. If you use this while attuned to Seven Bullets, its loses its range property, instead being able to be aimed at any target discovered from the pipe ignoring cover, as a magic portal appears near the target to fire at them.

item.name: Seven Bullets
entries: loading. This rifle inlaid with blue accents reeks of faint traces of contractual magic. When you would be about to attune to this weapon, it speaks to you inside your head as if possessed, explaining its curse and asking if you do want to use its bullets.

If you say no, you become unable to attune to it for the next 24 hours, if you say yes, you become attuned to it. It does not ever speak again, yet those who plead for it to go away say that they can hear the rifle laughing. You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and it also has the following effects: Magic Bullets.

When you shoot with this weapon, a magic portal opens at its barrels end, turning a bullet into a line of destruction. When you target a creature, all other creatures in a line from it to you are caught in the bullets wake. When you roll to hit, your roll counts as if you were attacking all creatures in this path, dealing the weapons damage if it would hit their AC.
Devil's Six. When you hit another creature with this weapon, its critical hit threshold is reduced by 5. Number of Divine Deliverance.

Every time you shoot with this weapon, wether you hit or miss, add a +1 to a counter. After this counter reaches 7, the counter resets and Seven Bullets binds your fingers and arms in tight chains, spectral in their appearence and freezing to the touch. They manipulate you to take a shot aimed at your closest loved one, such as a spouse, best friend and so on.

This shot ignores range, instead automatically hitting any creature fitting that criteria as long as they are within a 3-mile radius. If there would be no creature that counts for this available in the area or otherwise, Seven Bullets targets you instead. The damage for this attack is doubled.

item.name: Forgotten Saint's Spear
entries: This spear is still warm to the touch, despite being made of what seems to be congealed blood and dry sinew. When it pierces another creature, it drinks blood as if that would bring back the Old God it used to be wielded in service of. You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and when you hit a creature using this weapon and its roll before modifiers is within the range of 17-20, the target suffers a stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} that cannot be removed unless the creature takes fire damage, as the Spear grows sharp thorns inside their flesh, those being torn off and stuck inside when you reel the spear back.

item.name: Heaven's Thorn
entries: This seems like the torn off branch of a tree, yet on closer inspection, its made of muscle tissue and sinew. It never rots, and when attuned to, you feel a need to be gazed back upon whenever you look another creature in their eyes. You hear echoes from time to time coming from the Thorn, echoes saying that it came from Paradise.

While attuned to Heaven's Thorn, it always crawls up to your shoulders by itself during combat, as if it were alive. Whenever a creature that was engaged with you disengages or suffers from blindness, the Thorn performs an attack against it. This attack has a reach of 10-ft., a +8 to hit and deals {@damage 2d10} piercing damage plus {@damage 4d8} radiant damage as it pierces the target with its thorns, absorbing any blood spilled.

item.name: Waykeeper's Ledger
entries: This ledger is bound by a dark leather that feels like a tree's bark when you run your fingers across. A pen made out of obsidian and inlaid with silver is chained to it. This item does not attune to a person, instead, its attunement process during a long rest is made through marking down an area for up to a 25-ft. cube using the Ledger's pen.
Any creature that passes through this area has its given name, a near-photographic sketch of its face, if it has one, and the time they passed magically etched on the Ledger.

item.name: The Path of Freedom
entries: The Path of Freedom is a lantern held with a dark metallic cage, and its light is constantly covered by a black cloth. Whenever it is revealed, the light comes from a shimmering golden orb that swirls inside itself as if liquid was present inside, and the distorted sounds of a forest may be heard. While attuned and while holding the lantern in one hand, you may spend your bonus action to raise it toward a creature that can see within 60-feet of you.

They must pass a DC 18 Charisma Saving Throw or be enthralled by its swirling light, using their reaction to immediatedly move double their movement speed up to the closest empty space close to you, as if they used the Sprint action. If they are within reach when their reaction ends, your next attack is done with advantage and is considered a critical hit on a roll of 15 or higher before adding any modifiers.

item.name: Coat of Evil Seeking
entries: This dark coat has a feathered collar and many golden, blazing eyes along its length. While attuned to this item, you have an AC of 14 +Your Dexterity Modifier ( Max. of 3 ) + Your {@skill Perception} Modifier ( Max. of 2 ). In addition, while donning it you cannot be surprised and have advantage on {@skill Insight} checks to detect evil intent from other creatures, with the addition of a faint dark aura appearing around the creature you made the check against, if its alignment is in fact evil.

On a critical failure in such an {@skill Insight} check, you determine they are evil no matter what, the armor activelly meddling with your thoughts to find any source of evil that could come from the creature, and the dark aura appearing all the same.

item.name: Greatsword of Justice
entries: This sword's blade is a great rectangle of a darkened metal. Its wrapped in several bandages that somehow never shred as its swung around, and can't be dislodged by any means. You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, additioanlly when you hit a creature they gain one stack of Sin Sin until the end of combat.

When you hit a creature with Sin Sin you gain an additional +1 to your attack and damage modifiers for each 2 stacks of Sin on the creature, to a maximum bonus of +3. If a Creature has 5 or more stacks of Sin, you may, as an action, perform Justice, you perform an attack with advantage against the target, and they take an additional d8 radiant damage per stack of Sin on them, then removing every stack of Sin they had.

item.name: Blind Judge's Scale
entries: This item cannot be attuned to by regular means, instead, during a period of 10 minutes you may drip a vial of blood extracted from a creature to fill its bowl, the creature becoming attuned to the Scale. This attunement lasts for one day. For the duration, a creature attuned to the Scale has their biases sharply weighted in directions they usually wouldn't.

The DM or Player (Whoever controls the character) may choose between having the creature do the inverse of what it usually would regarding its decisions, such as a politician who once plead for executing a person changing their mind and instead letting them free, or instead rolling dice to determine their choices, the die size being in accord to the number of options directly in their mind.

item.name: Red Hunter's Hood
entries: A pair of a flowing crimson hood, blood-red in its color, and a metalic facemask with grafitti resembling the toothy grin of a predator. When attuned to this item, you feel constantly reminded of your grudges and the monsters that lurk around the world, unpunished. Once per long rest, you may declare a creature your quarry, your thoughts scarcely being able to leave the thought of the creature for the rest of the day.

You gain disadvantage to Intelligence skill checks unrelated to the creature, their place or region of residence and anything that wouldn't be pertinent to hunting this quarry. This lasts until your next long rest, yet you also gain a +2 to {@skill Perception}, {@skill Investigation} and {@skill Survival} rolls to locate or perceive your quarry, additionally can always know their location if you have inflicted the {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} condition on them, as you see a red outline of their body if you are within a 300- feet radius of them. You also gain a +2 to hit this creature with weapon attacks, and gain the following bonus action, which you can also take as part of your attack action: Hunter's Advance.

You lunge at your target with eviscerating strikes, aimed right at their arteries. Until the end of your turn, your attacks deal 1 stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on hit. You may use this bonus action a number of times equal to half your proficiency modifier, regaining expended uses on a long rest.

item.name: Crimson Switchblade
entries: Special This weapon possesses an ingenous design with a retractable blade for ease of porting, possessing both a defensive and offensive mode. It usually sits in its defensive state, granting you a +1 bonus to your AC while wielding it with two hands. Switch.

As a bonus action during your turn, you may switch this weapons mode, raising it to the air, unlocking its restraints and turning the blade outwardly, forming a great scythe. The weapon loses its original traits and gains the Two- Handed, Heavy and Hemorrhaging(15) properties, dealing {@damage 2d8} slashing damage on a hit. In addition, you deal +2 weapon damage on hits against creatures below their hit point maximum.

item.name: Primal Claws of Scarring
entries: A pair of gauntlets made out of cobalt, their blue hue gleams against moonglight, and the fingertips end in claws sharp enough to rival most greatswords. You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and additionally you gain the following bonus action: Cobalt Scar. After spending your bonus action during your turn, you may choose to pounce on any creature that is below its maximum hit points as long as it is within a 30-foot radius of yourself.

item.name: Beast Hunter Pistol
entries: This old, rickety handcannon holds many runes and magic circles inside so that any bullet will be blessed into tearing into monster's flesh. Any bullet fired by this gun is considered silvered and inflicts 1 Stack of {@condition Fragile|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} on a hit.

item.name: Cowl of Nurturing Balance
entries: This flowing shawl meant to be worn over the shoulders is inlaid with silver resembling the scales of a carp. Touching its surface feels like caressing a cloud, yet it feels just as fragile. While attuned to this item, you feel a harmony come from the depths of your soul and resonate with the positiveness of whatever is around.

When you would use a hit die to heal yourself, you are instead healed by the full amount. Additionally, when you would cause or benefit from healing, you heal an cumulative +2 hit points per dice that would be rolled in the healing process.

item.name: Robes of Entropic Balance
entries: This flowing open robe is inlaid with a refined bronze mixed with ruby dust to form the pattern of fish scales, with its cloth being soft to the touch yet surprisingly resistant, painted in a dark brown color. While wearing this item, your AC is 12 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier ( Max. 3 ). This item has 6 charges, and regains all expended ones at dawn.

As a reaction to when you would take damage or be targeted with a damaging spell effect, you may spend 2 charges to activate the latent ki powers embedded in the cloth. Redirect Despair. You suffer no damage nor effects from the source of this reaction, instead it is redirected into the flow of the universe.
You may choose to redirect the damage or spell to target one creature within 60-feet of yourself instead.

item.name: Yang's Blessing
entries: This light-colored earring of a teardrop represents all the positivity in the world. While attuned, when you or another friendly creature you can see would take damage, you may choose to, as a free action, share of your blessing so the pain is highly diminished, making it so the damage taken is reduced to a mere 1, instead of whatever else it would be. This feature may be used a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, regaining uses at dawn.

If this item is attuned at the same time asYin's Blessing, its feature may be used an amount of times equal to your proficiency modifier instead, additionally, you may spend one of its uses to make use of Impose Balance, as described below Yin's Blessing.

item.name: Yin's Blessing
entries: This dark-colored earring of a teardrop represents the entropy in the world. While attuned, when you take damage you may roll {@dice 1d8} as a free action. On a roll of 8 instead of taking the damage you would take, you instead are healed by the exact amount, as the energies of destruction and creation are swapped at the last moment.

You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, regaining expended uses at a long rest. If this item is attuned at the same time asYang's Blessing, the effect of this item activates on a roll of 4 or higher instead of just 8. Additionally, you may spend 2 charges to make use of Impose Balance, as described below.

item.name: Yearning Desire
entries: heavy This greatsword yearns for humanity, to become akin to a humanoid. This desire shall never be granted, forever remaining just a desire. Instead of metal, it seems to be made of bone, muscle and sinew, yet it is sharper than anything else you've ever seen.

You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and it holds 5 charges, which you can spend to: Yearning, Calling. The sword absorbs and funnels a victims blood on hit in hopes that will make it feel more alive, yet ends up only funneling the life force into you. After dealing damage to a creature withYearning Desire, you may spend 1 charge to heal yourself for half the damage dealt.

Learn of Inner Humanity. You raise the sword with a clamour, bringing it down to cut a creature in two. Before you attack, you may spend 2 charges to cause your next attack to be considered a critical hit on a roll of 14-20, before modifiers.
