Broken Speech. It likes to speak, although its false murmuring could never make it be considered truly sentient. By spending 1 charge, you may have the sword mimic the speech of any person you've heard within the last week.

This gives advantage to any checks to see through the lie that is this fake voice. Its intonation at parts is fully wrong, though, enough for close people to notice. If a creature tries to see through the lie and is closely familiar with the fake voice's origin, it has advantage on checks to discern the truth.
You gain one charge every time you kill a creature whose CR is equal to or higher than your level.

item.name: Crown of the Priest of Stars
entries: All the Lights in the Sky are Stars, and so are your friends. This crown is actually a visor that covers the eyes partially, yet its true magic lies in the fact that it can release a pleasant symphony that alleviates the troubles of the wearer's beoved. While attuned to this item and while you aren't {@condition Unconscious||unconscious}, you and all friendly creatures within a 15-foot radius of you restore a number of hit points equal to your proficiency modifier at the start of your turn as a magical wave emanates from the crown.

An {@condition Unconscious||unconscious} creature cannot benefit from this feature. If you take force damage while wearing this item, the crowns resonance is disrupted, causing the wave to instead deal force damage of an equal value of what would be healed. This lasts until the end of your second next turn.

item.name: Feather of Three Saints
entries: This greatsword weights more than the skeleton of a dragon, slices like the teeth of a Hydra and has been through conflict that would put beings from the Astral Sea to shame. To attune to this weapon, you must have the will of a true monster, not a simple warg hunting its food nor the malice of those that would rather take entire settlements, instead you require a will strong enough to bend the entire world and make it into something new. To attune to this item, you must have at least a Strength or Dexterity score of 20 and an Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma score of 20.

Otherwise, attuning to this weapon fails and you suffer a level of exhaustion from the futile attempt. This item holds 20 charges, which you may use to fuel the abilities described below. It restores {@dice 1d8+3} expended charges at twilight.

You also have a +4 bonus to hit and for damage rolls while using this magic weapon. ShimmeringWings. As part of your attack action, you may spend 1 charge per attack hit to change the attacks damage type to what the target has vulnerability against.

Ordeal ofTwilight. As a bonus action on your turn, you spend 4 charges to slam the greatsword onto the ground and unleash a wave of magic covering a 60-feet radius around you. All creatures of your choice must pass a DC 20 Wisdom Saving Throw or suffer disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than you.

Creatures that fail this check by a difference of 5 or more also become Panicked for one minute. The Futility of Humanity. As a reaction to when you take over 30 hit points of damage, you may spend 6 charges to give this weapon theVorpal trait until the end of your next turn, also lowering your critical hit treshold by two.

Final Judgement. As an action on your turn, you may spend 12 charges to invoke a giant stone scale behind you. All creatures of your choice in a 120-foot radius must pass a Charisma Saving Throw or take {@damage 6d8} force damage per each creature they have killed in the last week, or half the damage on a success.

item.name: Hatchling of Punishment
entries: A small, round little bird that resembles a little dove. It has a penchant for pecking people and perching on peoples heads. While attuned to a Hatchling of Punishment, you gain a +1 to Wisdom Saving Throws, as the Hatchling's incessant pecking keeps you annoyed, but focused with whatever task at hand.

As a reaction you may forgo this bonus on yourself and give it to a friendly creature within 15-feet of you. Also while attuned, once per day you may use your action to Enact Punishment. Enact Punishment.

Some people have pushed things too far and they need to get their due. You perform an attack against a creature within melee attack reach, gaining advantage if this creature dealt damage to you on the last turn. On a hit, you deal an additional {@damage 4d8} piercing damage as a force compels you to use the beak of your weapon to stab the culprit a few additional times.
This action may only be used when you are below half your maximum hit points.

item.name: Hatchling of Protection
entries: This tiny, fist-sized bird is a big ball of dark feathers that still fail to cover the various golden. slightly incandescent eyes across its body. Those, of course, only being rivaled in quantity by the sharp teeth in this bird's mouth. It cannot fly, but will gladly use its big wings to climb up and hoist a ride on its owner's shoulders.

It really wishes to keep all safe and sound. While attuned to a Hatchling of Protection, you gain a +1 bonus to {@skill Perception} skill checks and your passive {@skill Perception}, as the Hatchling's watchful gaze always helps you find your way. Also, while attuned you may spend your reaction when an ally would be targeted by an attack to Draw in Interlopers.

Draw in Interlopers. You ready yourself for a fight as the Hatchlings eyes and yours glow in a golden light. The attacking creature must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw or be compelled to attack you instead until the end of their next turn.

The DC for this is whichever your class would have for their features or Spellcasting. If there is none, the DC is 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. You must be in range of the attacker's attack to use Draw in Interlopers.

item.name: Hatchling of Justice
entries: While this little bird is quite lanky for its size category, it can still be carried over the shoulder with ease, as most of its length comes from its crane-like neck. Its body is covered by dark feathers, and its head by bandages of a gift long given. It gives tips on how to be impartial and fair always and yearns for justice.

While attuned to a Hatchling of Justice, you gain a +1 bonus to your {@skill Insight} checks, as the Hatchling aids in guiding your judgements. As an action, once per day, you may perform a Peacekeeping Gift. Choose up to four willing creatures beside yourself.

A spectral white pinion falls and lodges itself in any place that it can addorn, such as on one's hair or pauldron, and you become linked for a quick moment. In this quick moment, the health values of all creatures in this ritual is summed up and then divided equally for each creature, becoming the result of that. If this value would exceed one's maximum hit points, they gain the excess as temporary hit points.

This cannot affect creatures who are {@condition Unconscious}. Woundrous Pets & Friends A "Wondrous Pet" is the mechanical term this document uses to refer to, well, pets! A Pet in this way is a magical being that while attuned, will always remain within a 60-feet radius of its perceived owner.

They do not require food nor sleep, but will gladly partake in either joy. A Pet does not partake in combat initiative, instead it is treated like any other magic item when called upon for an active or passive ability it grants. Additionally, it has no stat block of its own, instead only providing static benefits to its master.

Much like the {@spell find familiar|PHB|Find Familiar} spell, a pet may be commanded with a free action to move and to enter or exit an extradimensional space where it is kept safe. It automatically enters that space if it would be immediately in harms way, instead remaining safe. If the {@spell dispel magic|PHB|Dispel Magic} spell is cast on the Pet, it vanishes for one minute, and then rematerializes after this time.
During its vanishing, you cannot benefit from its abilities.

item.name: Mask of Teething Maws
entries: This black, metalic facemask covers the bottom of nose, the mouth and both cheeks in a giant row of teeth that when attuned, fuses to the wearer's face, leading to their stomach when opened. While attuned to this item, you feel a constant peckishness about you, and you may actively indulge in that desire for food with a natural Bite attack you gain. You are proficient with this bite attack, it is considered a melee attack which deals {@damage 1d8} piercing damage and you are healed by half the damage dealt after a hit using it, as you tear off and consume part of a targets flesh.

You do not heal from undead and construct creatures. As an action during your turn, you may gorge yourself on a dead body of a creature of Medium or Large size within 5- feet of yourself. When you do so, you rapidly consume it as a whole, recovering {@damage 3d8+4} hit points, with a bonus {@damage 2d8+2} hit points if it was a large creature.

This item has 3 stages of power, and it is natively in its 1st stage. It evolves or dissolves into another stage as the value of SMILE SMILE reaches certain numbers. SMILE is a counter for each dead body consumed using the Mask of Teething Maws, of which you gain 1 point when you consume a dead body, and lose 1 point for each week you go without consuming a dead body.

STAGE I. You feel a ravenous hunger at most times, yet can barely push back from the urge to bite down the first thing you can see. If suffer from a negative modifier to all your rolls equal to the amount of negative SMILE points you have, if you haven't eaten.
STAGE II. Hunger's need turns to desire, gluttonous joy. Your Bite natural attack grows in strength, gaining a +1 to hit and for its damage roll, also now dealing {@damage 2d8} piercing damage.
Additionally, your movement speed is increased by 10-feet. You reach STAGE II with 4 SMILE points. STAGE III.

The elation from consumption of another's being is unbearable. Your Bite attack changes once more, becoming disjointed and destructive, you have a +2 to hit and a +3 to damage rolls using it, alongside dealing {@damage 3d8} piercing damage. Aditionally, your movement speed is increased by 20- feet, and once per day you may cast the Sickening Sludge spell without spending a spell slot.

You can cast it more times by spending 2 SMILE points. You also may spend 1 SMILE point to gain an additional 5-feet to your movement speed until the end of your turn or spend the same value for a +1 for your attacks hit and damage modifier, also for the same duration. You reach STAGE III with 10 SMILE points.

item.name: Divine Tears of Rage
entries: This round spherical object resembles an ornate egg with gold, platinum or silver bands wrapping around itself. In reality, it is the congealed wrathful tear of a divinty, whose rage may explode once more for even more destruction. As an action, you can prime this weapon and throw it in any space you can see within a 60-foot radius of yourself.

You prime this item by removing a latch that is an ornate symbol of its divinity atop the sphere. All creatures within a 15-foot radius of the sphere must pass a DC 22 Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 10d8} radiant damage, or half on a success. On a failure whose final roll is 17 or below, the creature also has one of their limbs fully dissolved in light, roll a d10 to determine which.

A result of 1-2 is the right leg, 3-4 is the left leg, 5-6 is the right arm, 7-8 is the left arm, 9 is nothing lost and 10 the head or other relevant central organism, resulting in instant death. If a creature that failed that way has more than a limb or a completely different anatomy, the DM decides the roll and if a part can even be broken or not.

item.name: Robes of a Priest who Wished to Cure Sin
entries: These robes smell like a long forgotten summer dream. They are of a dark color, embroidered in the imagery of wings and feathers. If an evil-aligned creature attempts to attune to this item, the attunement fails as the Robes reject it.

While wearing this armor, your AC is 12 + your Dexterity modifier + 2. Additionally, you have the following traits: To Don Penance. Whenever you take 12 or more points of damage in one attack, you gain a +5 bonus to your Concentration checks as the pain keeps you even more focused on your goals.

Sticks and Stones. If you would take less than 10 damage in a single attack, lower that damage to 1 instead. This value is increased to reducing any damage below 24 if you are also attuned to Paradise Lost. ..

item.name: Paradise Lost
entries: A ceptre made from materials unfathomable to mere mortals. It resembles a limb carved out from an angels wing, entwined with the intestines of divinity itself. A red orb stands at its end, radiating holy power.

While attuned to this item, your spells gain a +3 modifier to hit and your Spell Saving Throw DC is increased by 3, in addition, this item can hold up to 20 charges. You gain one charge each time you deal a cumulative 20 points of damage through spells cast using Paradise Lost, also gaining one charge when healing {@condition Unconscious||unconscious} creatures and 3 charges when reviving dead creatures. You may spend your charges to perform the following miracles: Minor Miracle of Life.

As an action, you point Paradise Lost at a creature within 60-feet of yourself and spend any number of charges to heal them for an amount of d4+1 hit points per charge spent. Minor Miracle of Pain. As an action, you point Paradise Lost at a hostile creature within 60-feet of yourself and spend any number of charges to deal an amount of d6+1 necrotic damage per charge spent.

Miracle of Semi-Omnipresence. You may spend 5 charges to cast the {@spell Step Through Heaven's Door|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} spell without spending a spell slot. When cast like this, if you do so within the next minute, spend 2 charges to cast the spell again and being teleported to your original space, or the nearest unnocupied space.
Punishment of the Bad Apple. You may spend 15 charges to cast the {@spell Paradisiac Rapture|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} spell without spending spell slots. Punishment of Debauchery.

You spend 15 charges to cast the {@spell Fear of God [Cleric Only]|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Fear of God} {@spell Fear of God [Cleric Only]|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Fear of God} spell without spending a spell slot. When cast this way, all sources of damage caused by this spell deal an additional two dice of damage. Greater Miracle of God's Love.

As a bonus action during your turn, you may spend a number of charges to restore a spell slot whose level equals half the charges spent, to a maximum of spending 10 charges to regain a 5th level spell slot. When you do this, you may choose to regain multiple uses of the same level of spell slot, such as spending 12 charges to regain three 3rd level spell slots. Whenever you do this, you feel your devotion deepen greatly.

item.name: Collar of the Beast
entries: A collar made out of pure gold, its insides are full of intricate runes that lock up and slowly syphon the mana of the attuned, only to release it all back at a moment of true peril. This item can only be attuned by full casters. While attuned, this item is in sealed mode and latches itself to the attuneds neck, and while it isn't cursed it may only be removed by a spellcaster who knows at least fifth-level spells during a long rest.

Also while attuned, the wearer is rendered more fragile by the collars syphoning, taking their Proficiency Modifier's worth of additional force damage on each time they take damage. The attuned also gains a Release Counter, which starts at 0 every long rest and is increased by an equal value to the damage taken by the attuned. When the Release Counter reaches a value equal to your Proficiency Bonus times 50, the Collar enters its Released Beast state, which lasts for one minute.

The counter always resets to 0 on a long rest. Released State. After entering this state, you are granted your Proficiency Bonus times 20 temporary hit points and gain your Proficiency Bonus * 2 as a temporary increase to your Strength, Dexterity, Constitution scores and your Spellcasting score, to a maximum of 10.

Additionally, the overflowing mana releases can easily be manifested into Natural Weapons which take the shape of your choice, you may use your Spellcasting modifier to attack with this weapon and it has the Reach property, dealing {@damage 3d4} force damage on a hit. You also take your Proficiency Bonus times two less damage on each time you would take damage.

item.name: Band of Penance
entries: This leather sash contains various spikes on its inner fold, containing belts to be fastened to a creature's thigh or arm, feeding them a constant, righteous stream of pain. You may spend your Action to don or doff the Band of Penance, becoming Attuned to it. While Attuned, you suffer 1 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count at the end of your turns. This value increases by one for each day that you spend Attuned to the Band, also becoming Heavy {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} after reaching 6 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} per turn. While {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding}, you gain Advantage on Wisdom Saving Throws, and while Heavily {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding}, you gain a +4 bonus to Constitution and Wisdom Saving Throws. When you doff the Band and become Unattuned, you still suffer appropriate {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count at the end of your turns, reducing that value by 2 per day spent unattuned as your wounds slowly close.

item.name: Devouring Bloodstone
entries: A sphere of solidified blood that feels extremely rough to the touch, often rippling into small spikes while touching another surface. Inside it is a living hunger shivering to be sated.

As an Action you may toss the Bloodstone at an {@condition Unconscious} creature corpse within 30-ft of you, dealing {@damage 4d12} piercing damage to the creature if it is still living. If causing a creature to die or targeting a dead corpse, the Bloodstone quickly devours it until there is no trace left, generating Bloodfeast according to the creatures size, as follows:

entries.caption: Bloodfeast Generated
rows: Tiny
{@dice 1d4} - 1
Small
{@dice 1d4 + 1}
Medium
{@dice 1d6 + 2}
Large
{@dice 2d6 + 3}
Huge
{@dice 4d8 + 4}
Gargantuan
{@dice 8d8 + 6}

entries: A summoned creature or one with no blood cannot generate any Bloodfeast.

item.name: Hemobar
entries: A bar of compressed and dried blood meant to quench the thirst of Bloodfiends and Vampires alike. It is textureless and tasteless, functioning as a Ration yet barely palatable. You may spend an Action to consume a Hemobar and gain one Bloodfeast, yet must pass a DC 13 + Times you've consumed a Hemobar until your next Short or Long Rest Constitution Saving Throw to benefit from another one, suffering one point of Exhaustion on a failure.

item.name: Goblet of the First Kindred
entries: A goblet of pure gold, emblazoned with rubies and other red jewels and intricately detailed with the figures of the first Bloodfiends to ever exist. An endless amount of crystalline blood sprouts from the cup, yet it never seems to spill, with the liquid defying gravity when turned upside down. Spilling Blood, Sharing Familial Bonds. Whenever a creature consumes from the Goblet, their eyes turn a deep red and their canines sharpen to the point of easily cutting flesh. The creature is turned into a Bloodfiend and cannot be restored by any means except the destruction of the Goblet. Destroying the Goblet of the First Kindred. To destroy the Goblet, you must burn the current First Kindred of a family to ashes and sink the Goblet inside them, then fixating it to the blades of a windmill using silvered stakes. After doing so, you must have the windmill for twenty four hours, to where the Goblet will have melted and its contents irrevocably spewed.

item.name: Helmet of Mambrino
entries: A golden crown and visor meant to be worn as a helmet, covering the eyes in many jingling parts. It is finely crafted and rumoured to grant invulnerability to its wearer. Might Before the Tall Things. Not even a living mountain could get past you! While attuned to the Helmet, you think you are invulnerable to damage and that you automatically pass all Saving Throws. You also become immune to the {@condition Charmed||Charmed} and {@condition Frightened||Frightened} Conditions. Cursed. The Helmet of Mambrino digs teeth-like appendages onto its wearer's face after being attuned with an imperceptible pain. If not through a {@spell remove curse|PHB|Remove Curse} spell or greater, a forced attempt to remove the helmet will cause you to suffer {@damage 6d8} slashing damage and become permanently {@condition Blinded||Blinded} as you lose your eyes.

item.name: The Helmet of Begon
entries: The crown of an ancient king, known for granting invulnerability to its wearer. It is made of pure gold and hangs various ornaments in its visor, ostentating its might. Might Before Giants. While attuned, you gain Resistance against all types of damage except for Force damage. You also become Immune to all non-magical damage and magical piercing, bludgeoning and slashing damage.

item.name: Mask of the Parade's Prince/Princess
entries: A simple carnival mask made out of linens and metals. It has a deep fragrance of fresh blood when close to the face, and is said to have belonged to the single most beautiful vampire in the world. While Attuned, your Charisma becomes 23 if it was lower and you have Advantage on {@skill Persuasion} Saving Throws as the Mask's allure hides any undesirable traits of your body and makes all other beauty make itself known.

item.name: Pendant of the First Drop
entries: This golden necklace contains the rumoured first drop of blood ever shed by a First Kindred, crystalized and engraved in their grand visage. While Attuned, you gain a bonus +1 modifier to Attack Rolls and Saving Throws for every 5 Bloodfeast you have consumed to fuel an ability until the start of your next turn, to a maximum bonus modifier of +4.

item.name: Pincushion of Exploding
entries: An unassuming pincushion of a red, velvety color. It is packed to the brim with various used pins, often being used as makeshift weapons by barbers. You may prime the Charge as an Action, throwing it to a point within 30-ft of you, exploding in a hail of pins when it hits a surface and forcing all creatures within 10-ft of it to pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer {@damage 4d4} piercing damage and 4 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count, or half of both on a success. The DC for this Saving Throw is 14 + your Dexterity Modifier, or your Artificer Spell Save DC if applicable.

item.name: Poet's Everbeating Heart
entries: A still beating heart of a prominent poet whose real name has blurred within the passing of time. It has been mutated through various arcane processes, growing a mouth and teeth that bite and latch onto you when Attuned. While Attuned, you become immune to the effects of a Vorpal weapon and gain Resistance to Psychic damage, as the heart constantly whispers tales to you. Whenever you start your turn within 15-ft of a {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} creature, the heart beats faster, causing your blood to rush violently. When this happens, you deal an additional {@dice 1d4} damage of your weapon's damage type per {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} creature within reach whenever you hit a creature with a weapon attack, to a maximum bonus of {@dice 6d4}.

item.name: Rusty Iron Stake
entries: This weapon has the {@itemProperty Hemorrhaging|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} property.

A grimy iron needle that has rusted over with dried blood over its length. It is unusually large, reaching the size of a rapier. Special: Pinned. When you hit a creature with this item, you may choose to stick it to their body. While stuck, any melee weapon attacks against the creature are considered to have the Hemorrhaging(16-20) weapon property and it may only be removed by the creature spending their Bonus Action to do so, also causing them to suffer {@damage 1d6} piercing damage and suffering 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count.

item.name: Shard of Crystalized Blood
entries: A shard of crystalized blood, easily shatterable within one's hand. You may spend your Bonus Action to shatter the Shard under your palm, causing it to melt and meld into your body, instantly causing you to recover up to your {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count's worth of d4 + 1 hit points, to a maximum of {@dice 10d4 + 10} hit points. After doing so, your wounds close and heal, ending the Condition automatically.

item.name: Vampiric Noblesse Clothes
entries: Finely crafted clothes that help you hide your bloodthirsty nature with an otherworldly sense of style. While wearing these clothes, other creatures have Disadvantage on {@skill Insight} checks for perceiving you as a Vampire, Bloodfiend, Shapechanger and otherwise, instead usually assuming you are only a flamboyant noble.

item.name: Vial of Pristine Blood
entries: A glass vial of certain blood collections mixed with a number of special reagents to make it pure. When consumed with a Bonus Action, you are healed and gain Bloodfeast according to the Vial's rarity, as presented below:

entries.caption: Vial of Pristine Blood
rows: Common
50 gp

Uncommon

Legendary
Priceless
Gods

item.name: Stitchwrap Bomb
entries: A carefully built bomb wrapped by various spools of red thread that was drenched in blood, forming sharp crystals all around to be used as pins. When triggered, the triggering creature must pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer {@damage 3d4} piercing damage and 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} Count, or half on a success as the pins go off and latch onto the target's face. On a failure, if the triggering creature is of Large or smaller size it must roll a d4. On an even roll they have their eyes stitched, becoming {@condition Blinded||Blinded} until they suffer slashing damage. On an odd roll, they have their mouth stitched, becoming unable to speak until they suffer slashing damage.

item.name: Aromatized Incense Burner
entries: An ornate box full to the brim with incense, in its metallic surface there are various etchings resembling holy symbols to preserve a veil of sanctity over it. As an action, a creature may start burning the incense, which lasts for a minute. It spreads a fine mist in a 60-feet area around itself, spreading to fit around corners and walls. This haze isn't enough to impair visibility, yet emits a strong herbal scent that is unpleasurable for Vampires, Bloodfiends and other blood-sucking creatures, having them feel nauseous and generally repulsed, granting advantage on any creatures insight checks to recognize their fiendish nature. This mist lasts for 1 minute or until dispersed by a strong wind or magical effect.

item.name: Battle Torch
entries: A concealed torch that usually looks like a crude cudgel from its metallic casing. Its continual flame is hidden by a simple set of plates that can be opened up by holding a lever in its handle; it is done so since the flame is enchanted to quickly cover an area when blown on. While unlocked, the torch emits light like any normal torch.

item.name: Serrated Hand-axe
entries: This weapon has the {@itemProperty Hemorrhaging|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} property.
A crude lead-made hand-axe with sharp points sawed off of its edge. These nearly pierce skin on simple touch.

item.name: Stake
entries: This weapon has the {@itemProperty Hemorrhaging|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} property.
A simple wooden stake that was carved until deep wounds could be punctured with its use.

item.name: Stake Crossbow
entries: A more complex heavy crossbow with a mechanism for firing stakes, forgoing any kind of arrows in the process. When a stake is fired using this weapon, it always inflicts one stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed}.

item.name: Carmilla
entries: A whip made out of dry rosevines, holding it prickles your hands in its thorns, that although don't pierce through your skin, constantly reminds the weapon of its neverending hunger. At its tip, there is a wilting rosebud. This weapon is considered to have a +3 to your attack and damage modifiers, it also always inflicts one stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} on a hit. In addition to that, Carmilla deals additional piercing damage to the creature it hits equal to how many stacks of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} the creature has. Hunger of Four-Hundred Roses. When you roll a 20 before any modifiers to attack while using Carmilla, the creature hit takes 20% of their maximum health in additional piercing damage, rounded down, as the rose in its tip starts blooming, and blood seeping down through the vine's length.

item.name: Bonecrusher Hammer
entries: This large hammer has its tip laid with spikes and a grip that facilitates both throwing and swapping it for a primary weapon. When you hit an attack with this weapon, the target suffers one stack of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Rupture}.

item.name: Grappling Dart
entries: A long rope with a weighted hook at its end, meant to be thrown and pulled afterward. When you hit a creature with this weapon you may spend your Bonus Action to attempt Shoving them 5-ft closer to you. When you do so you gain your Proficiency Bonus' worth as a bonus to your {@skill Athletics} check to do so and the creature takes an additional {@damage 1d4} piercing damage if successfully pulled. After being thrown you may spend a Free Action to instantly pull the Dart back into your hands.

item.name: Styptics Bag
entries: A grab bag of healing herbs laid out and pressed against bandages for easy use to stop bleeding. You may consume this item to instantly end the {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding} Condition.

item.name: Vial of Silver Water
entries: A charm of holy water mixed with silver dust for an even stronger purifying effect. It can be worn around your body, having its own AC that equals yours + your Dexterity Modifier and 10 hit points. While worn, creatures with a weakness to radiant damage, silvered weapons or that are bloodfiends suffer a -1 modifier to all Saving Throws as long as they are within 60-ft of you.

item.name: Vein Splitter
entries: This weapon has the {@itemProperty Hemorrhaging|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} property.

This easily concealed blade can be worn as a brooch and easily be mistaken as one, having a mechanism to fully unsheathe its sharpened blade quickly when needed. You have advantage on {@skill Stealth} Checks to keep this weapon concealed.

item.name: Sanctified Canister
entries: A vial of holy water that has been primed and pressured to explode on hard contact with a surface. Instead of performing an attack with this weapon, you instead throw it to a space you can see within its thrown range, causing any creatures within a 10-ft radius of that point to perform a DC 15 + Your Dexterity Modifier Dexterity Saving Throw or suffer its damage. If thrown at a long range, this Saving Throw is performed at advantage.

item.name: Emblazoned Hunting Shawl
entries: A Shawl fashioned for quick donning and practical movement while in a hunt. Its hem is lined with sharp emblems, either of holy symbols for protection or those resembling an old hunting order. This Shawl has six Vein Splitters spread around his hem, which you can spend to throw as part of your attack action. A Vein Splitter thrown this way is lost when thrown but inflicts {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} as per Hemorrhaging as long as it hits a creature who isn't immune to the condition. As an action while wearing this armor you may swiftly spin around, forcing all creatures within 5-ft of you to pass Dexterity Saving Throw whose DC 8 + Your Proficiency Modifier + Your Dexterity Modifier or suffer a number of d4 slashing damage plus the same number in {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} stacks, or half on a success. This number is equal to half the amount of Vein Splitters still attached to it, rounded up. You may replace up to your Proficiency Modifier's worth of Vein Splitters to the hem of the shawl by using a separate Vein Splitter or by spending 20 gp per replaced part.

item.name: Firing Gauntlet
entries: A gauntlet made out of various heat-resistant metals. While worn, you can use it for unarmed attacks. Fire Breathing Hand. Once per Long Rest you may extend your hand in place of one of your attacks (as part of the Attack Action) and emit a 15-ft cone of flame from it, causing any creature within reach to pass a Dexterity Saving Throw or take {@damage 3d6} fire damage and suffer 4 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count. The DC for this Saving Throw is 8 + Your Dexterity Modifier + Your Proficiency Bonus.

item.name: Charred Mask
entries: This old metallic mask was owned by a man who lost everything, and in his desperation to eviscerate the mire of his mistakes, nothing remained except for it. While attuned, you have a -2 penalty to Wisdom Saving Throws and any Wisdom based Skill Checks. You also gain Immunity to Poison damage and Resistance to Fire damage. When you kill a non-summoned or magically created creature you gain {@dice 1d4+2} Temporary Hit Points as the Mask urges you onward until the purge is done. Furthermore, you are immune to the {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} Conditions.

item.name: Talisman of Enwrapping Dissonance
entries: As a bonus action, make a ranged weapon attack against a creature you can see within 60 feet. The talisman disintegrates when used. On a hit, it triggers the target's {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and distributes the amount of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} it had as evenly as possible among creatures of your choice within 5 feet of it. You choose which creatures receive any remainder. If the original target had no {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, it instead suffers 3 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

item.name: Talisman of Quick-Wits
entries: This talisman is worn around the wrist or attached directly to skin or bone. When you roll initiative, you can allow it to burn away and add {@dice 1d4} to the roll as revitalizing energy sharpens your focus.

item.name: Cursewrought Blade
entries: This gigantic squared blade is engraved with runes that fester along its length. While attuned, potent ritual magic courses through your arms like a counterweight, allowing you to carry a weapon with the Heavy property in your other hand. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. A creature hit by it suffers 2 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If you hit a creature with this weapon after hitting the same creature with a weapon that has the Heavy property, the attack deals an additional {@damage 1d6} slashing damage.

itemProperty.name: Unarmed
entries: A weapon with the Unarmed property is usually light enough to be worn over the hands as more of an accessory than a tool. While wielding those, you count any attacks done with them as unarmed weapon attacks.

feat.name: Ink Thicker Than Blood

prerequisite.other: You aren't of a Middle Subclass

entries: You've found yourself a place in a greater family and it shows in your skin with pride and pomp. When you take this Feature, consider how your character was first introduced to the Middle, how they came to join and how they look up to their older Siblings. Nevertheless, you gain the following:

items: Your choice of your Strength or Charisma scores increase by 1, to a maximum value of 20.
You instantly gain a 3rd level Tattoo of the Middle, as per the Path of Grievance's rules. You gain an additional one upon reaching 6th level, another at 10th and a final one at 14th level.

During combat, the enemy that dealt the most damage to you or your allies this round gains a {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. This lasts until the end of the next round, or until you fall unconscious. If no enemy has dealt damage this turn, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is given to the enemy that last attempted to attack you or an allied creature. This applies after any other Middle Subclass characters application, going toward the creature that dealt the second most damage if applicable. Outside of combat, whenever someone rolls an ability check to hurt or damage your character or their reputation, they will also gain a point of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until your next short rest. If combat is initiated right after an instance of this by rolling an initiative check, then the enemy with the highest initiative roll gains {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until the end of the first round of combat.
Whenever you hit an enemy with a stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, they gain 1 stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries: When first you take this Feature you gain a {@item Little Book of Vengeance|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} from another Sibling that acts as a courier for you.

feat.name: Masked Wounds
entries: {@i "I keep it covered because it hurts to even look at."}
You've been horribly disfigured in one way or another that left part of your body ever-aching, and you've procured a means to mask such a painful memory. You gain the following:

items: Your Constitution modifier increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You always have a means to procure a way to mask your wound, instantly recovering one roll of your Hit Die in Hit Points during a short rest.

Whenever your current Hit Points are reduced to or below half their Maximum Value, you enter a {@condition Sizzling Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} state, as your pain soars to an unbearable amount, causing your mind to fully focus on drenching that wound in blood to quench the aching.

entries: While in this state your AC is reduced by 2 and you deal an additional 1d6 fire damage when dealing damage, also inflicting {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half your proficiency bonus. If the attack already deals fire damage, inflict a count equal to your proficiency bonus instead.
This state lasts until your next short rest or you recover all your Hit Points.

feat.name: Guided by the Will
entries: {@i "According to the city's will, its volition... The City's will matches the will of the people living in it."}

You are a follower of the Living Will and may have your orders appear to you in a small slip of paper at any given moment, standing by for the next goal. You are able to receive Prescripts in the following ways:

items: As a Free Action during your turn you may draw a Prescript, as per the Follower of an Order Prescripts and the Magicked Prescripts Tables. Upon completion, you gain one {@condition Grace of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} which remains until your next short or long rest. Upon failure, you suffer one {@condition Karmic Consequences|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} You may do this up to an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest, rounded down.

You may choose to draw from the Crawling Prescripts table upon finishing a long rest. Upon its completion, you gain three {@condition Grace of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. Upon a failure you suffer three {@condition Karmic Consequences|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} instead.

entries: Additionally the Will benefits you in certain moments of need. Once per turn you may spend one {@condition Grace of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count to re-roll your damage die or a saving throw. You must do so before the DM determines it a success or a failure in the latter case.

prerequisite.other: You have no levels in a Living Will subclass.

feat.name: Hearts Cast Aside
entries: {@i "Qui si spoglia l'elmo e la corazza... e getta via la spada Durindana."}

Sometimes, your emotions become so turbulent that the only thing you manage to do to claw away from your aching heart is to sever what ties it down. While at half your maximum Hit Points or lower, you may spend your Bonus Action to grip a Magical Item that you are Attuned to in one of your free hands, instantly shattering the item into pieces and inciting a mad fury to beat from your heart, drawing more power to yourself. This power is according to the item's rarity, as follows:

entries.caption: Hearts Cast Aside
rows: Uncommon
You gain a +1 bonus modifier to all your Attack Rolls until the end of combat.
Rare
You gain a +1 bonus modifier to all your Attack Rolls and to your AC until the end of combat.
Very Rare
You gain a +2 bonus modifier to all your Attack Rolls, to your AC and to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution until the end of combat.
Legendary

You gain a +3 bonus modifier to all your Attack Rolls, to your AC, Saving Throws and an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to ability checks to all Ability Checks until your next Long Rest. Furthermore, when you would be reduced to one Hit Point you instantly gain half your Maximum Hit Points as Temporary Hit Points. When you gain these Hit Points, you may also let out a guttural scream, causing all creatures within 30-ft. of you to attempt a Strength saving throw or be pushed 10-ft. and become {@condition Frightened} of you for the next minute, or only be pushed back 5-ft. on a success.
Artifact
You gain the same effects as when you would Shattering a Legendary item. Additionally, while having Temporary Hit Points from this feature all damage you deal ignores Resistances and Immunities.

entries: You may use this ability once per Long Rest and the item is cannot be restored through any means other than a {@spell wish} spell. You may use this ability an additional time per Long Rest after reaching 16th-Level. If you attempt to shatter an Artifact, it is instead cracked and loses all its properties for {@dice 1d6} months. You gain the same value rolled in Exhaustion points after your next Long Rest, as your aching heart fails to cease its fervent beating.

feat.name: Retaliator
entries: {@i "Non trova pace il cor, né quiete il petto, se non vendica l'ira e'l suo disdegno."}
The world might beat and beat and beat you, but you never back down, not fully. You always end up striking back with all your might, granting the following benefits:

items: Your choice of your Strength, Dexterity or Constitution Attribute Score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Whenever you suffer damage from another creature within your attack reach you may spend your Reaction to perform a weapon attack against them. You may also instead use a damaging cantrip to do so instead of a weapon attack.

feat.name: Trench Warfare Expert
entries: {@i "Looks like my past self has faced some tough battles, too."}
You've become used to combat in cramped spaces as you have gone through your life, benefitting the most while dragging others to your zone of command. You gain the following:

items: Your choice of your Strength, Dexterity or Constitution score increases by one, to a maximum of 20.
You gain Advantage on melee weapon attacks made within enclosed spaces or while being Flanked.

entries: Enclosed spaces count has having walls or similarly impassable objects covering at least two opposite spaces around a 5-ft. radius of you. Large or greater creatures count as walls for the purposes of this feature.

feat.name: Dismantle Prosthesis

prerequisite.other: Racism?

entries: {@i "The Second Smoke War was a conflict between humans and humans who no longer looked the part."}

The war caused a divide between the people and whatever the hell the other things were calling themselves. The names don't matter, not to you, what matters is knowing how to tear them bolt by bolt, limb by limb. You have the following when concerning Constructs:

items: You gain 1 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} at the start of your turns for each Construct within 30-ft. of you. You gain an additional count for every Construct corpse within that same reach. The maximum amount gained this way is equal to your proficiency bonus.
You inflict 2 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count against Constructs whenever you deal weapon damage to them.
You have Advantage on {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Perception} and {@skill Survival} skill checks to track or perceive Constructs.

You have Disadvantage on {@skill Insight} checks against Constructs, as your bias will always tell that those machines are built to produce lies. The same Disadvantage applies to Charisma skill checks ( except for {@skill Intimidation} ) against them, due to your tendency towards them being near impossible to conceal.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: You may talk with your DM about changing the creature type for any other that might fit! Consider "Faction-Aligned" characters as a choice as well so that they may fit as a suitable target, such as the enemy side of whatever war you may have come to participate in. In general, we recommend using Rangers' Favoured Enemy for a rule-of-thumb of what can categorize as an apt creature type to be chosen by this feature, including choosing two kinds of humanoids.

feat.name: Red Eyes of the Hunter
entries: Your eyes have taken to dark places and those who are difficult to navigate, all in search of prey. While you are actively tracking a creature or an object, your irises shine in a piercing red, and you can see through non-magical darkness. You gain proficiency in the perception skill, or Expertise if you were already had proficient in it.

You may use {@skill Perception} in place of {@skill Survival} or {@skill Investigation} skills when attempting to track a creature or object. Additionally, you gain Darkvision if you didn't have it already, seeing in shades of red, seeing up to 60-feet in darkness as if it were bright light and darkness as if in dim light.

prerequisite.other: 4th Level, at least a +4 modifier to Perception

feat.name: Chained Wrath
entries: Your anger and rage only festers as you wait to unleash it, nearly bursting as any fight breaks out. Upon the start of a combat, you may choose to have your initiative be considered one for the rest of combat. If you do so, your first melee attack always has a bonus to hit damage equal to the number of creatures who acted before you, and double that number for its damage modifier.

prerequisite.other: Proficiency in martial melee weapons or unarmed attack, or Barbarian

feat.name: Shield and Sword
entries: Your studies have led you to a place where you can allow yourself not only to go unhurt, but punish those who would dare attack you. As part of your reaction when you cast the {@spell shield|PHB|Shield} spell, if the attack that would hit you was turned into a miss, you may also cause a burst of arcane swords to pierce out off of your shield, instantly dealing {@damage 2d12} force damage back to the attacker.

prerequisite.other: Know the Shield spell and have 3rd level spell slots available.

feat.name: Caving Mole
entries: The instincts and will of worms have gotten to you, and you have decided to join the moles in the dirt for their eternal dig, be it through frivolous use of your magic or the repeated stomping of your fists against even rock. You gain a burrowing speed of 25-feet, additionally, you may choose to leave a 5-foot by 5-foot tunnel in the wake of your digging. If you stay too long underneath the earth, you start losing track of what might be happening outside, as such you suffer from the {@condition Blinded} and {@condition Deafened} conditions if you finish your turn fully burrowed, losing these conditions upon re-emerging.

prerequisite.other: Strength or Spellcasting score equal or greater than 16, 4th level.

feat.name: All-Devouring Maw
entries: Guts of iron, razor sharp teeth... You've got them all. You may eat anything and everything without a hassle, you gain a +5 to Constitution Saving Throws when ingesting poison, alcohol or any similar sort of effect inducing substances.

Additionally, you may use your action to consume even unnusual objects for a meal, such as swords and other kinds of weapons. Each consumed weapon counts as a full ration eaten. Additionally, once per day you may bite down a magic item to temporarily disrupt its energies, nearly leaving a dent in both it and your teeth.

For the next ten minutes, as long as the magic item is a tiny object, it loses all magical properties. Any ongoing effects coming from the item are immediately stopped, and they don't resume when the magic returns.

prerequisite.other: Consitution score of 15 or higher.

feat.name: Throes of Rejection
entries: There is a wound within you that will never heal, and every small "no" you hear only pokes at the scabs. As such, when you are neglected by a creature during a social interaction, you may channel this frustration in further actions. Whenever you are rejected, you gain one Frustration Dice.

Those are d4s and you may have up to your proficiency modifiers worth of them at any given time, and you may spend them when you fail skill checks to use your frustration to seek success, although scuffed. However, you have a disadvantage equal to one roll of your Frustration Dice against any creature who had caused you to gain one within the last week. Hemorrhaging Weapon Property.

A serrated weapon causes a stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever you hit with it, provided the roll equals the value presented alongside the property before any modifiers. {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} A bleeding bleed creature is well, creature is well, bleeding bleed ! You take {@dice 1d4} damage when you performany action ( Each attack is considered a different action, this also includes Bonus Actions and Reactions, but not Free Actions ), and then is reduced by one count. You may heal or have {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} fully removed if you or another creature passes a succesful medicine check on you.

The DC for this is 10 + The number of counts you currently have. If you have only one count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, it will not be removed upon taking damage and must be removed through a medicine check.

feat.name: Primed and Ready to Go
entries: At the start of any battle, you're a force to be reckoned with due to your absolutely explosive starts. You gain the following benefits: Your Strength or Dexterity scores increase by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain a +2 bonus to hit and in damage rolls, yet that bonus is reduced by one each time you use Action Surge, SecondWind. or or Indomitable Indomitable, as you become more winded for the fight in general, with this bonus being restored after a long rest.

prerequisite.other: 4th-level Fighter.

feat.name: Repose of the Butterflies
entries: The dead follow you, not as putrid remains reanimated to slave away at your will, but as gentle spirits which follow your guidance. When you gain this feat, you also gain the following: Your Charisma or Wisdom score increases by 1. When you cast the {@spell spare the dying|PHB|Spare the Dying} spell, you may instead choose to free the soul of a creature from its body and transform it into a White Butterfly, which uses the Tressym sheet for itself.

When freed this way, the fragile butterfly may be used instead of the creatures original body for reviving it. The butterfly created by this retains the memories and personality of its last life, with the change that it is now in a constant state of serenity. It may choose by itself if it would rather fly away and disappear into whatever afterlife might exist in its world or stay with you.
You may ask the butterfly one question per day, with them responding with their voice emanating inside your head.

prerequisite.other: Know the Spare the Dying spell.

feat.name: Vorpal Instinct
entries: There is no greater rush than when you sever a creature's head from its body. When you would kill a creature through a melee weapon attack, you may choose to viscerally decapitate it, casting fear into your foes hearts. As you do so, choose one creature within 30-feet of yourself, it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw or become {@condition Frightened} of you until the end of your next turn.

A creature that is immune to being {@condition Frightened||frightened} instead only gains advantage against this check. The DC for this Wisdom Saving Throw is 8 +Your Strength or Dexterity modifier ( Choosen when you take this feat ) + your Proficiency Bonus.

prerequisite.other: Proficiency in Martial Melee Weapons.

feat.name: The Fair Justiciar
entries: Your tenets will be followed, as that is the true justice! Whenever a creature you can see and hear breaks one of your subclass' tenets, you may spend your reaction to fuel your desire to correct such behaviour. You gain half your proficiency modifier as a bonus on any Charisma based skill checks, {@skill Insight} checks and attack rolls against that creature for the next minute.
You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining expended uses after a long rest.

prerequisite.other: 3rd Level Paladin

feat.name: Body Sculpted in War
entries: After adventuring for a while, you've gained a great many deal of scars from your various encounters. Your skin is most likely hoarse to the touch after receiving so much damage, yet knowing your body is etched in the history of your exploits gives some pride, respite or an acknowledgement that you were there. You receive the following benefits: Your Constitution score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Your scars ache from time to time, yet you endure it. As a free action during your turn, you may choose to take 1 bludgeoning damage from them. You may do this a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier, restoring expended uses on a short or long rest.

So much fighting has allowed you to better resist getting wounded once more. You may spend your reaction when taking any damage type besides force and psychic to gain resistance to that damage type until the start of your next turn. You may do this a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier, regaining expended uses on a long rest.

prerequisite.other: 8th level.

feat.name: United Hunt
entries: Nothing creates a bond like a good hunt between a tight-knit crew, and you know that. Afterall, slaying a beast together will be much more effective. As someone who knows how to make the most of it, you gain the following benefits: Your choice of your Strength, Dexterity or Constitution modifiers increase by 1, to a maximum of 20.

You gain a +1 to hit against creatures that have been hit by a friendly creature before you in a combat round. When you receive or give help in skill checks to perceive or track a creature, add a furhter +2 bonus to the dice rolled.

prerequisite.other: Proficiency in Martial Weapons.

feat.name: Never Erring Paragon
entries: No temptation shall ever come to pass in your life, as your mind is a temple, sacred and well-kept. You gain the following benefits: Your Wisdom score increaes by 1, to a maximum of 20. You have advantage against being deceived or coerced into performing actions you do not wish to do, or speaking what you do not want to speak.
You gain advantage on saving throws against being {@condition Charmed||charmed} or {@condition Frightened||frightened}.

prerequisite.other: 14 or higher Wisdom.

feat.name: Awe-Inducing
entries: Some have called you a terrific presence to be around, yet others are able to truly acknowledge your grandiosity, that feeling that makes one's heart stop and beat at your beck and call. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your Charisma score increases by 1, to a maximum of 22.

When your presence would cause a creature to become {@condition Frightened||frightened}, it instead becomes Reverent for the original duration. At the start of each of its turns while it can see you, a Reverent creature must succeed on a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw or have its speed reduced to 0 for that turn. It also has disadvantage on ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws while it can see you, and the DC of its concentration checks increases by 7.

prerequisite.other: Be able to cause the Frightened Condition, 16th level.

feat.name: See Things Through
entries: Things don't always go your way, but you're fine with that, because you never quit right away. You gain the following benefits:

items: One ability score of your choice increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.

When you fail an ability check, you can use your reaction to reroll it with a -2 penalty. You can do this only once per roll and a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

prerequisite.other: 4th level.

feat.name: Guardian's Aura
entries: The soul of a true defender is the one you show, and with a touch of magic you can push that energy into a barrier for a friend. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your Constitution score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.

As an action, choose a friendly creature you can see within 60 feet. For 1 minute while you maintain concentration, that creature gains a +2 bonus to AC. Other creatures have disadvantage on attacks against it unless no other conscious creature friendly to it is within 30 feet.

prerequisite.other: 8th-level, Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma score that is 16 or greater.

feat.name: Turned Kindred
entries: You were turned into the next generation of {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} by your sire. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your Charisma score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries.name: Blood Arts
entries: You learn two Blood Arts from the {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} ancestry:

entries.optionalfeature: In the Dark of the Night|TheUndertomesProjectMoon

entries.name: It's in the Blood
entries: When a creature with blood drops below 1 hit point because of your actions, you gain 1 Blood Charge. You can also use an action to extract blood from a corpse that has been dead for less than 1 day. You can hold up to 10 Blood Charges and spend them to fuel your Blood Arts.
You take a penalty to saving throws against enchantment spells cast by your sire equal to your sire's Charisma modifier.

prerequisite.other: Not a {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} or Bloodbag

feat.name: Bloodarts Master
entries: You have become learned in the manipulation of blood. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries.name: Blood Arts
entries: You learn two Blood Arts from the {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} ancestry:

entries.optionalfeature: In the Dark of the Night|TheUndertomesProjectMoon

entries: You can take this feat more than once.

prerequisite.other: You know at least one Blood Art; 4th level

feat.name: Turned Bloodbag
entries: You were turned into a Bloodbag by your sire. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your Wisdom and Intelligence scores each decrease by 1, to a minimum of 5.

entries.name: Blood Arts
entries: You learn two Blood Arts from the {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} ancestry:

entries.optionalfeature: In the Dark of the Night|TheUndertomesProjectMoon

entries.name: It's in the Blood
entries: When a creature with blood drops below 1 hit point because of your actions, you gain 1 Blood Charge. You can also use an action to extract blood from a corpse that has been dead for less than 1 day. You can hold up to 10 Blood Charges and spend them to fuel your Blood Arts.
You take a penalty to saving throws against enchantment spells cast by your sire equal to your sire's Charisma modifier, and you have disadvantage on those saving throws.

prerequisite.other: Not a {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend}

feat.name: Stakehunter's Instincts
entries: You're experienced at hunting the beasts of blood that haunt the realm. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your Strength or Dexterity score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency with {@item Serrated Hand-axe|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Serrated Handaxes}, Stakes, and {@item Stake Crossbow|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Stake Crossbows}.
You gain a +2 bonus to ability checks made to perceive or track Vampires, {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiends}, or another creature that subsists solely on blood.

feat.name: Break and Enter
entries: Sometimes your targets cower beneath some shoddy door, box or wall; They really don't know what's coming. You can use your action to attempt to topple and destroy a non-wieldable nor worn object or wall by performing an {@skill Athletics} check against a base DC of 14 plus the modifier shown in the table below according to its material:

entries.caption: Material DC Modifier
rows: Wood
Stone
Metal

entries: You cannot break a wall that is thicker than 10-ft, and objects made of a material that is not listed above may have its modifier assigned as the one closest, as per the DM's discretion.
When you break a cover, you may spend your reaction to move to 5-ft around a creature who was benefitting from it and perform a melee weapon attack against them.

prerequisite.other: 4th level; proficiency in Athletics

feat.name: Impaler
entries: To truly make use of a weapon that you drive into a foul beast, you must know to twist it. When you deal piercing damage to a creature through a melee attack you may spend your bonus action to twist the blade or weapon used, dealing an additional d4 of piercing damage equal to half your Proficiency Bonus and inflict that same amount in {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleed} stacks. You may use this feature up to a number of times equal to your Proficiency Modifier, regaining spent uses on a short or long rest.

feat.name: Targeted Relief
entries: There's some sort of monstrous being that really ticks you off, to a point where their losses outright give you life. When you take this feat, choose one from the following creature types: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead.

When a creature of this type is reduced to 0 hit points for the first time in an hour, you may become invigorated with satisfaction, giving you an {@dice 1d4} bonus to skill checks, attack rolls and saving throws until your next turn, or up to one minute when outside of combat. This does not work on summoned creatures such as those created from magic items such as a Bag of Pests or spells like the Summon Elementals spell.

prerequisite.other: 4th level

feat.name: Filthy Blood
entries: You've experimented with yourself to a point where your blood is a toxic substance or it has always been this way for a reason or another. When a creature would hit you with a bite attack, any bite-adjacent attacks (Such as a peck or any melee attack that would cause your blood to be absorbed) or when it triggers a Critical Hit against you while within 5-ft of you, that creature must pass a Constitution Saving Throw whose DC 14 + Your Constitution Modifier + Your Proficiency Score or become {@condition Poisoned||Poisoned} for one minute, being able to retry this Saving Throw at the end of their subsequent turns, yet also taking {@damage 2d4} poison damage on any further failures after becoming {@condition Poisoned||Poisoned}.

prerequisite.other: Constitution score of 14 or higher

feat.name: Not a Trace of Gasoline
entries: Allows you to overextend the perceived fuel of your gauntlet into one devastating punch. Your Fire Breathing Hand Action fires out a 30-ft long cone of flame instead, with its DC being increased by half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down, dealing {@dice 4d8} damage instead of {@dice 3d4} and inflicting a total of 8 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burn} count.

prerequisite.other: Proficiency with Firing Gauntlets; 6th level

feat.name: Never Again.
entries: During your life, there was a moment or another where you believe you should've said goodbye, that you could've said something different, and to this day you feel like so much could have been better if you did.

You've learned from your previous mistakes. When your party would be split in separate groups, such as you going to check out a tavern while others sneak around the back, you may give your fellows a pep-talk or any form of encouragement that you'll see each other soon. When you do so, they gain a Longing Die that they may use in any roll before you reunite.

This Longing Die is initially a d6. At 8th level this Longing Die becomes a d8, and upon reaching 16th level it becomes a d10. Whenever a creature adds a Longing Die to their roll, it becomes one step lesser, such as a d6 becoming a d4. When a Longing Die is rolled as a d4, it is then lost.

prerequisite.other: Charisma score of 15 or greater

_.special: a set of fancy clothes bearing purple all over them
at least two sets of golden chains
another 5 gp's worth of beer and other party drinks

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
items.entry: {@skill History}, {@skill Intimidation}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: One type of gaming set and one musical instrument

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of fancy clothes bearing purple all over them, a Family-gifted boombox, at least two sets of golden chains, a wallet containing 10 gp, and another 5 gp's worth of beer and other party drinks

entries.name: Feature: Middle Finger to the World
entries: Your family has gotten your back no matter what happens, but that can hardly matter when you are adventuring nigh and high with other folk, so they provide you the best they can when you're away from them. You have a 25% discount on any magical tattoos you'd purchase for yourself or trusted creatures.

Additionally, whenever you are within Middle controlled territory you have advantage on {@skill Intimidation} rolls and other siblings will easily provide food and shelter for you and any friends you bring along.
Alternatively, with your DM's permission ( or if you are playing with '24 Backgrounds in general ) gain the {@feat Ink Thicker Than Blood|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Feat.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The vast majority of those adopted into the Middle are colourful figures who are a living party unto themselves, with many was to show that. Despite the seeming union of the faction as a whole, there are those who are around for power rather than just the ones who are looking for true loyalty and camaraderie. Nevertheless, a great knowledge for their extensive grudges is a must for any of them.
The Middle is defined by some form of relation to the rest of the gang, be that a quirk toward them or a way you particularly enjoy being part of the whole thing.

entries.caption: Familial Quirk
rows: I spend an embarrassingly massive amount of gold on cute stickers to award to others.
I look up to others easily and feel afraid of disappointing them.
Blasting loud music is the same as breathing to you, screw what others say.
I write every. Single. Little. Slight. In the book. No exceptions.
I spend excessive time every single day taking care of your luscious mane of hair.
I tend to butt heads with your siblings often in good humour, making sure everyone has enough strength to carry their chains.
I are a collector of trivia and information about each persons tattoos, usually recognizing people by their ink before their faces.
I always look cool to your younger siblings and you don't know why. After all, its simply your job to take care of them.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: I meet any slight with immediate retribution in the form of violence.
I tend to give others a second chance, even if it is after giving them a well-deserved punch.
If my neck-line isn't invisible from the sheer weight of my chains, I am not stylish enough.
I can't calm down without a good beat in the background.
I live my life by the book, both in vengeance and in my lifestyle, preferring to have my routines be sacred and unchanging.
I can't deal with technicalities and hedge-cases that are complex, so I just always default to the worst case scenario on the basis of a single coin flip.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: The reason I joined the family is freedom, I want to do whatever the hell I want whenever I want! (Chaotic)
Loyalty to your fellow is the most important thing in life. Breaking away from that is unforgivable. (Lawful)
I enjoy loud music. Environments with clear regulation are also favorable. (Neutral)
This is all about having a good time for me, what's truly right is making sure our little siblings are fine while the oldest to try and deal fairly with whatever comes our way. (Good)
Taking care of those close to you is important. (Any)
So what if I want to take some things for myself first? Family is about making sacrifices, after all. (Evil)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: Some asshole stole something precious from me. I want it back.
At first I was nothing more than just related to someone from the Middle, but after certain events that took them away from me I decided to enter in their honour.
I want to become a Great Sibling.
Some freakish calamity overtook the branch of the Middle that I am a part of, and I'm still picking myself up from the floor after that.
Out of all my siblings there are a handful some that I consider the closest to me.
My Book of Vengeance is to become the most well-written and well-executed Artifact in the history of the Middle.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: In the end I see that the Middle really is just a bunch of nobodies clinging to one another. They're as expendable to me like any other joe, the only difference is that they're loyal.
I lose my cool way too quickly at the slightest transgression.
I can't find it in myself to forgive anyone who has wronged me, and much less so whenever someone crossed one of my loved ones.
I believe that rules exist for a reason, and must not be broken in any circumstance.
Doubts about joining have began clinging to me after joining and I don't know what to do.
I expect loyalty to be repaid with absolute obedience.

_.special: all the items of the background you are faking
a crumpled paper that reminds you of what you wish to become (or what was chosen for you to become)

items.entry: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: One of your choice

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: All the items of the background you are faking, and a crumpled paper that reminds you of what you wish to become (or what was chosen for you to become)

entries.name: Feature: Facsimile
entries: You've trained yourself to become something that you are not. Your walk, your manner of speech, even the abilities you openly display have been trained to craft a delicate persona that you perfectly maintain. When you choose this Background, choose another Background.

You gain a +1 bonus modifier on rolls using the Skill Proficiencies of the other Background. If this background would give you a bonus to rolls, you gain half the value you would add to those rolls, to a minimum of +1. This is always rounded down.

If it gives you protection or information of some sort, you cannot get it for sure, but have enough knowledge on the topic and an ability to weasel your way inside, gaining Advantage on checks related to that goal.
You add double your {@skill Deception} modifier to checks regarding maintaining your persona.

entries.name: Persona.
entries: Fakers can come in all shapes and sizes, and they'll convince you that they are something else. They aren't just liars or schemers, instead they are someone pretending to be what they ultimately are not at all given moments. To aid with a choice of who to become, you may roll on the following table or make up a Persona of your own:

rows: I was born poor and alone, always wanting to protect others, and so I used my strength to do just that, no matter if some betrayed me or not. (Folk Hero Background)
I am no one, but I have a dream. A dream to reach the highest- reaching factions and stand shoulder to shoulder to them all. (Urchin Background)
I have lost what once was my heart, yet its ghastly beat remains reverberating in my chest. I'll take my time to grow back into strength and take my dazzling revenge. (Soldier Background)
My friends, I always thought I'd protect them, that I'm a hero, but I'm not so sure anymore. I can't help but to run away from where I should be, like any weeping coward would. (Charlatan Background)
I am looking for my lost child, as I have been for so long and will keep doing so even if I need to tear the world apart to reach them. ( Far Traveler)
I have beckoned people towards a just cause, to a brighter future. I truly believe what I preach, even if most around me don't feel the same yet. (Sage Background)
My family is dead, my road thus far has been that of blood-shed, pain and suffering to those left in my wake. I will never go back to what once was. (Criminal Background)

I followed someone who I truly believed in to the bitter end, and my place in the world was lost in the process. Nevertheless, I am one who has earned and embodied my position even as I look toward the future. (Acolyte Background)

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Now, one such as you has varied characteristics that even you might forget at times, as your Persona's have been superimposed onto you. Roll in your chosen background's Tables.

background.name: Nobleblood Fiend

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
items.entry: {@skill History}, plus one from among {@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, and {@skill Performance}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: One type of gaming set

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: One of your choice

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of {@item Fine Clothes|PHB|fine clothes}, an emblem of your noble household (such as a {@item Signet Ring|PHB|signet ring}), and a purse containing 25 gp

entries: You were born into, sired by, or raised among {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} noblesse. You've enjoyed the banquets of blood shared among your kindred and formed relationships with other highborn families throughout the region. You likely uphold the {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} code, living in secrecy like your peers. Or perhaps you've fled from it all, unable to restrain your darker urges any longer. Who sired you? What is your relationship with them and with others in your Estate? How do you navigate the rules that keep your kind hidden?

entries.name: Feature: Faces from High Places
entries: You've mingled with other noblesse in the past-whether those interactions were cordial or contentious. Regardless, you know proper etiquette and how to gain an audience in noble courts. Provided the host is not overtly hostile, you can find temporary shelter and sustenance at another {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} noble's estate. Additionally, you are well-versed in the hierarchies and names of noble {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiends} within your known sphere, granting you a +2 bonus to {@skill History} checks to recall such information.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: I can barely fathom the apparent humanity of lower beings.
I cannot bear to see a peon attempting to speak up to their master, it's sickening.
People look at me in awe whenever I go, yet they have no clue that behind my charm lies a thirsty monster.
I constantly speak in an old-timey manner, more befitting of the good old days of my Sire.
Despite my nature, I attempt to be the best I can, to truly prove I am beyond some monster.
The desire for power is greater than my hunger for power, as my very Sire should beware of my burning desire.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: Control. Hierarchy is everything, all should know their place. (Lawful)
Supremacy. Superiority of the Kindred should be imposed unto all lesser than us. (Evil)
Peace. I simply wish the best for my estate and its inhabitants, despite what they may be. (Good)
Elation. I crave the moments where I can host a great banquet for my kin. (Chaotic)
Order. I was raised into this, and I'll take heed to the code as I will, yet my life is my own to live. (Any)
Solitude. My near kin and subjects should be left well alone from all the outside bickering. (Neutral)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: My kindred are my everything.
Who needs soldiers when an army of Bloodbags will suffice?
I keep many a friend close during any given situation.
There is a heirloom that I covet more than anything.
I serve a horrid Sire, yet that won't be for long...
I don't make bonds, preferring to live alone in my own Estate, with at most one servant or two.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: I proudly believe that everyone is beneath me.
I always attempt to skirt around the Code's lines.
The world should see what its true master is.
My Kindred are only tools to me, and nothing else.
The blood I once consumed slightly isn't enough anymore.
I have long abandoned my Estate, I have better things to do.

_.special: an emblem of your noble household (such as a signet ring)

background.name: Renegade Fiend

items.name: Skill Proficiencies:
items.entry: Choose two from among {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Stealth}, {@skill Survival}, {@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Performance}, and {@skill Investigation}

items.name: Tool Proficiencies:
items.entry: {@item Thieves' Tools|PHB|Thieves' tools} and one type of gaming set

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: One of your choice

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: A set of {@item Traveler's Clothes|PHB|traveler's clothes}, a map of the region, a trinket that once belonged to your Sire, and 15 gp

entries: The {@race Bloodfiend|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Bloodfiend} 'Code' was always more of a suggestion to you. Why should you hold back from embracing your true nature-or hide your very existence from the world? Isn't it a basic right to be yourself?

Of course, many despise you for your so-called free will. But that's fine. You don't care for them either, nor for their rules. You've broken away from your Sire and any remaining kindred, determined to live on your own terms.
What pushed you to sever ties with your kin? Do you regret your actions? What was your most notorious breach of the Code?

entries.name: Feature: Faces from High Places
entries: Most people avoid alleyways at night-and you're the reason why. When you enter a new city, you quickly learn the streets, discovering where to stalk a mark or avoid prying eyes. While in urban environments, you gain a +2 bonus to {@skill Stealth} checks made to avoid guards or hunting parties, as well as to silently pursue a target through alleyways.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: Megalomania is just another way to say confident!
To live alone is bliss, why would I need others?
I often overcompensate my lack of humanity with hip and popular slang to mask the old accent.
